title: G1b playback arm regresses 24% on Demo 2 under every clip-hiding mechanism
description:
Found by strides-kyu.3. The shell restructure is free; CONCEALING the clip's <video> is not.

Demo 2 (portrait 4K, 59.94fps — the only test clip whose sampling is throughput-limited), playback
arm (`{"sequentialSampling":{"enabled":false}}`), 5 trials per variant, paired back-to-back against
a throwaway worktree at ab5d185, real GPU (ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro):

  base ab5d185 (old layout, visible)      62 [57..63]
  kyu.3 layout, wrapper left `relative`   61 [56..63]   restructure is FREE
  kyu.3 layout, `fixed` but ON SCREEN     63 [57..64]   `position:fixed` is FREE
  L0  fixed offscreen + inert             47 [46..57]   -24%   (shipped)
  L3  1x1 overflow:hidden window          47 [40..59]   -24%
  L2  -z-20 behind an opaque backdrop     39 [37..47]   -37%
  L1  opacity-0 + -z-10                   34 [33..39]   -45%

Pre-registered gate is +/-10%. Every rung of design.md D2's escalation ladder fails it, and the
ladder's ordering is INVERTED — L0 is jointly the best concealed option, descending is monotonically
worse. "Descend on failure" has nowhere to go, so this is not fixable by picking a rung.

WHY IT WAS NOT CAUGHT EARLIER
- G1a passes. It measures an IDLE element with no competing per-frame work; the hidden element does
  still present frames (Demo 2 116 vs visible 118). The failure is proportional, not binary: fewer
  SAMPLES once something contends for the frame budget. D8's "PRIMARY instrument … decisive in
  seconds" is necessary but not sufficient and must always be run with G1b's playback arm.
- Demo 1 (landscape 4K, 25fps) reads 47 -> 47 at every rung — 40ms/frame is enough slack to absorb
  the added per-frame cost. Any gate that measures only Demo 1 reads green through this entire
  failure. Demo 2 must be in the matrix.

BLAST RADIUS (bounded)
Default WebCodecs path untouched: Demo 1 53 -> 53, Demo 2 99 -> 99, bit-identical, `sampling.path`
asserted `'sequential'` vs `'playback'` per arm. The loss lands only where canUseSequentialDecode
returns false — WebM and webcam recordings. That is exactly the population D8's own correction
identified as the one the original G1 was blind to, and the population D1's observational guard
exists to protect.

THE ONE DIRECTION THE DATA SUPPORTS
Keep the element genuinely ON SCREEN while its own analysis is in flight, and conceal it only once
that clip reaches a terminal phase. Both "visible" controls above measure at or above baseline, so
this is the shape that works. It changes what the reader sees during analysis, which is a product
decision — kyu.3 deliberately did not make it. Note it composes with D1's presentation-scoped
looping (kyu.5): "presented" and "must stay visible because it is being sampled" would become two
reasons for the same element to be on screen.

Not yet ruled out and worth measuring before designing anything: whether a genuinely visible but
very small on-screen element (scaled down, not clipped — distinct from L3, which clips a full-size
element) keeps full throughput. If it does, it is a far cheaper answer than a visible-during-
analysis surface.

Repro: node scripts/ab-person-selection.mjs --arm 'playback={"sequentialSampling":{"enabled":false}}'
--clips demo2 --trials 5 --port <free>
close_reason:
RESOLVED by measurement — the cause is on-screen vs off-screen, not any concealment technique, and a genuinely visible element keeps FULL throughput down to at least 60 CSS px.

Demo 2, playback arm, 5 trials/arm, same session, real GPU (ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro), sampling.path='playback' on all 30 trials, commit bf95a1a:

  visible-full (control, 264x470 = 124,256 px painted)   61 [56..62]   —
  visible-full (repeat, 321x570 = 182,756 px)            61 [49..62]   0.0%   PASS
  tiny-120     (67.5x120 = 8,100 px)                     62 [56..63]  +1.6%   PASS
  tiny-60      (33.75x60 = 2,025 px)                     62 [56..63]  +1.6%   PASS
  L0 shipped   (offscreen + inert, 0 px on screen)       49 [48..52] -19.7%   FAIL
  L0 repeat    (end of session)                          47 [46..55] -23.0%   FAIL

NO THRESHOLD. Painted area varies 61x across the three passing arms (2,025 -> 124,256 px) with throughput flat at 61-62. The discontinuity is binary: on screen or not.

The negative control held at the end of the session (47 [46..55], matching this ticket's independently-measured 47 [46..57]) and the positive control reproduced at 61 twice at two different sizes and offsets — so the session COULD resolve the known failure, making its inability to find one in the tiny arms a real null rather than a blind instrument.

RESOLUTION: keep the analysing clip's element genuinely on screen. The navbar strip thumbnail (60-120 CSS px) can simply BE the live element while that clip's analysis is in flight, reverting to the static poster once it reaches a terminal phase. No product compromise, no visible-at-size surface needed. Folded into strides-kyu.4.

title: Fix poster review findings: decoder fan-out and webcam frame-0
description:
Code review of strides-kyu.2 (commit 70b9a8a) returned two ship-blocking findings plus two test gaps against that ticket's own stated acceptance criteria.

## MUST-FIX 1 — N concurrent detached 4K decoders (CONFIRMED)
useClipPoster.ts:41 -> posterFrame.ts:202-231. `useClipPoster` is per-ClipSlot with NO cross-clip serialization, so every clip reaching status:'ready' opens its own detached <video> with preload='auto' over its full blob, CONCURRENTLY, during sampling.

This is the exact hazard the module it borrows from serializes against by construction — extractFrames.ts:474-478: 'Sequential by construction rather than by caller convention: Demo 1 is 3840x2160 and Demo 2 is 2160x3840, so N concurrent detached decoders is not an acceptable amount of memory to hold (design R3).'

Repro: FileUpload sets `multiple` and fires onSelected once per file (FileUpload.tsx:33-35), wired straight to addClip (MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:218). Pick 4 files -> 4 addClip in one tick -> 4 ClipSlots mount -> 4 queueMicrotask(load) in one flush -> 4 simultaneous deriveClipPoster, each minting a 4K decoder and seeking it, while clip 1's MoveNet/WebGL sampling loop runs against the shared detector.

kyu.2's live verification was single-clip only, so acceptance criterion 2 ('does not disturb analysis') is UNVERIFIED for the multi-clip path this feature exists to serve.

Fix direction: a module-level promise chain in posterFrame.ts, matching extractSessionEvidence's posture. Serialize by construction, not by caller convention.

## MUST-FIX 2 — every webcam clip posters at frame 0 (CONFIRMED)
posterFrame.ts:126-130. `choosePosterTimestamp` returns 0 for non-finite duration. POSTER_TIMESTAMP_FRACTION's own doc (posterFrame.ts:37-42) says zero is precisely what must be avoided: 'the first frame of a real clip is routinely a fade-in, a black leader, or the runner not yet in shot.'

MediaRecorder WebM reports duration: Infinity — already asserted in-repo at EvidenceGallery.tsx:93-94. useVideoSource.ts:53 copies video.duration verbatim into metadata.durationSec. So: choosePosterTimestamp(Infinity) -> 0 -> seekTo(video, 0) short-circuits to 'already-there' (extractFrames.ts:147), skipping even the presentation wait -> drawImage of frame 0. For a self-recorded run that is the user still walking back from the camera.

Systematic for one of the app's four input modes, and silent. **posterFrame.test.ts:123 tests this case as 'falls back to the first frame' — the test locks in the defect rather than catching it.** Fix the test's intent too.

Fix direction: when duration is unusable, still target a small fixed offset rather than 0 (the existing cap is a natural candidate), degrading gracefully if that seek cannot complete. Do not simply widen the clamp.

## SHOULD-FIX 3 — both MultiClipVideoSession release sites are untested
MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:130 and :187 are exactly what kyu.2's acceptance criterion 5 ('released on clip removal and session reset') names, and MultiClipVideoSession.test.tsx has zero references to poster or releaseClipPoster. Replace either call with a no-op and the suite stays green. useClipPoster.test.ts covers the HOOK's cleanup — a different site, and specifically the one both code comments say they deliberately do NOT rely on. So 'release does not lean on React cleanup ordering' is asserted in prose and nowhere in code. sameClipSession's new `previous.poster === next.poster` line (:67) is likewise uncovered.

## SHOULD-FIX 4 — 'derives once per source' is load-bearing and unasserted
useClipPoster.test.ts never asserts deriveClipPoster's call COUNT (only not.toHaveBeenCalled at :67). ClipSlot reports up on every render and the parent re-renders on every progress tick. It is correct today because all three effect deps are useVideoSource state set once per load — the reviewer traced and confirmed this — but a future change making `metadata` a per-render object would re-decode a 4K clip on every progress tick with no failing test.

## NOT findings — verified correct, do not 'fix' these
- The `clipIds.length > 1` guard at :130 is correct, not a leak. When false, setClipIds refuses the removal, the slot stays mounted, and useClipPoster keeps owning and re-reporting that poster; releasing there would blank a live thumbnail.
- All four release paths fire, including the decode that resolves after teardown. No leak path found.
- The detached decoder is torn down on every path; the object URL is created after both null guards so no path creates one it does not revoke.
- The non-disturbance claim holds transitively — no caller-owned element is reachable.
- sameClipSession still terminates.
- The purity boundary is genuine, not nominal.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Poster derivation is serialized across clips BY CONSTRUCTION, not by caller convention
- [ ] Multi-clip poster path live-verified: 3+ clips added in one file-picker interaction, sampling.detectedFrames still in normal range, numbers recorded
- [ ] A clip with unusable duration (MediaRecorder WebM, duration===Infinity) no longer posters at frame 0
- [ ] posterFrame.test.ts:123's assertion is rewritten to express the intended behavior, not the defect
- [ ] MultiClipVideoSession.test.tsx covers release on clip removal AND on session reset — verified load-bearing by confirming the suite fails when either call is stubbed out
- [ ] useClipPoster.test.ts asserts the derive call COUNT across many re-renders
- [ ] tsc -b, npm test, eslint all clean
notes:
=== ACCURACY NOTE on finding 2's severity — the fix is right, the premise was overstated ===

The review claimed every webcam clip posters at frame 0. Measured during the fix: on Chromium 151, `recorder.start()` with NO timeslice — which is exactly what `WebcamCapture.tsx:203` calls — produces a WebM reporting a FINITE duration. The Infinity case reproduces through `recorder.start(100)` (chunked), which this app does not do.

So finding 2 did NOT reproduce through the app's actual webcam path on that browser/version. It is still a real hazard: the in-repo comment at EvidenceGallery.tsx:93-94 asserts MediaRecorder WebM reports Infinity (measured at some earlier point, possibly a different engine), MediaRecorder duration reporting is a well-known long-standing cross-browser quirk, and `useVideoSource.ts:53` copies `video.duration` verbatim with no guard.

The fix is correct and costs nothing — an unusable duration now targets a 1.0s offset and falls back to frame 0 only if that seek cannot complete. But it is DEFENSIVE hardening against a case not currently observed in this app on this engine, not the repair of a live user-visible defect. Recording this so the next reader does not over-trust the finding's framing.

Finding 1 (decoder fan-out) is unaffected by this note — it was reproduced live, 3 concurrent decoders pre-fix vs 1 post-fix, in the app's real multi-file path.
close_reason: Closed

title: Reconcile the poster spec with the shipped detached-decoder implementation
description:
Wave 1 ran strides-kyu.1 (spec) and strides-kyu.2 (implementation) in PARALLEL. They disagree about how a poster is captured. This is a parallelization cost, not a mistake by either agent — neither could see the other's output.

## The disagreement
`openspec/changes/navbar-clip-shell/specs/video-input/spec.md` 'Poster frame for a loaded clip' says:
  'Deriving the poster SHALL NOT disturb the element's playback: it SHALL NOT seek, play, pause,
   mute, or otherwise write to the video element's playback state. IT CAPTURES WHATEVER FRAME THE
   ELEMENT HAS ALREADY DECODED.'
and its scenario 'A poster appears once a frame is decodable' keys on 'its element has decoded its first frame'.

The shipped implementation (commit 70b9a8a, `src/video/posterFrame.ts` + `useClipPoster.ts`) instead mints a DETACHED <video> from `videoSource.sourceBlob` with its own object URL and decoder, seeks THAT to 10% in (capped at 1s), draws, and tears all three down. `useClipPoster` reads status/sourceBlob/metadata and never `videoRef`.

## Resolution: amend the SPEC, keep the implementation
The spec's real invariant is 'never write to the canonical element's playback state'. The implementation satisfies that MORE strongly than the spec's own mechanism does — it cannot reach the canonical element at all, which is a structural guarantee rather than a discipline. The spec's literal mechanism is also worse in practice:
- The canonical element's already-decoded frame at 'ready' is frame 0, which on real clips is routinely a fade-in or black leader. A strip of black squares is worse than no strip.
- During sampling it is whatever mid-analysis frame happens to be up — non-deterministic, and different every run given this repo's documented frame-timing jitter.

The implementation was live-verified with a paired baseline arm (real GPU, code genuinely stashed for the control): sampling identical at 99/99/0 on Demo 2, Demo 1 detected 53 frames matching CLAUDE.md's documented anchor exactly, wall clock differing ~100ms in both directions. Zero measurable analysis cost.

## What to change
In `navbar-clip-shell/specs/video-input/spec.md`, requirement 'Poster frame for a loaded clip':
- Permit deriving the poster from a separate, short-lived decoder built from the retained source blob, and REQUIRE that the canonical element's playback state is never written to. Keep 'SHALL NOT seek, play, pause, mute, or otherwise write' scoped to the CANONICAL element.
- Adjust the scenario 'A poster appears once a frame is decodable' so it does not mandate capturing from the canonical element.
- KEEP unchanged: no serialization of the poster itself (data URL / blob / object URL / storage); release on removal and reset; the pure sizing/aspect math rule; the null-until-available lifecycle and neutral-placeholder consumer rule.
- Note that an object URL for the transient DECODER is permitted and must be revoked — it is not a serialization of the poster.
- Re-run `openspec validate navbar-clip-shell --strict`.

Also worth adding as a scenario, since it is the stronger guarantee the implementation actually provides: poster derivation never obtains a reference to the canonical element at all.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Spec permits the detached-decoder mechanism and forbids writing to the canonical element's playback state
- [ ] The 'no serialization of the poster' rule survives verbatim in intent, with the transient decoder's object URL explicitly carved out and required to be revoked
- [ ] Release-on-removal/reset and the pure-math rule survive
- [ ] `openspec validate navbar-clip-shell --strict` passes
- [ ] No src/ changes — the implementation is correct as shipped
close_reason: Spec amended to match the shipped detached-decoder implementation. video-input 'Poster frame for a loaded clip' now scopes the no-write rule to the canonical element and permits a derivation-owned transient decoder; added scenarios for 'never reaches the canonical element' and 'transient decoder torn down on every path'; carved the decoder's object URL out of the no-serialization rule while keeping the poster itself covered. design.md D5 rewritten with a revision note recording the parallel-execution cause and the paired-baseline evidence. proposal.md + tasks.md destaled; tasks 2.1-2.6 checked off. Verified choosePosterTimestamp clamps non-finite duration to 0, so D5's webcam duration===Infinity objection is handled. openspec validate --strict passes. Commit e276dd1. No src/ changes.

title: Build the pure per-metric annotation-geometry layer
description:
The core of Epic B. Turn each metric's exemplar into a canvas-free description of what to draw. No rendering in this ticket.

## The coordinate transform (video-native -> output canvas)
  outputSide = max(1, round(min(crop.side, maxOutputSidePx)))   // maxOutputSidePx default 640
  s  = outputSide / crop.side
  cx = (kp.x - crop.x) * s
  cy = (kp.y - crop.y) * s
Note s is round(min(side,640))/side, NOT 640/side — the rounding is in the numerator only, and computeCropRect returns FLOAT sides, so s is not exactly 1 even when side <= 640. No explicit point-mapping helper exists today; the forward transform is only implicit in the 9-arg drawImage at extractFrames.ts:327-337. The exact INVERSE already exists at movenet.ts:88-95 (`toVideoSpaceKeypoints`) — same algebra, opposite direction.

## toDrawOps cannot be reused as-is — three concrete reasons
`toDrawOps(frame): DrawOp[]` (skeletonGeometry.ts:121-164) emits `PointDrawOp {kind,name,x,y,opacity}` / `EdgeDrawOp {kind,from,to,x1,y1,x2,y2,opacity}`, with DETECTED_OPACITY 1 / INTERPOLATED_OPACITY 0.35 and edge opacity = min of endpoints. Reuse the MODEL, but it needs a variant because:
  1. coordinates are video-native with no transform hook (:130)
  2. it draws all 22 SKELETON_EDGES, not the exemplar's cropKeypoints subset — a kneeFlexion crop would get the whole skeleton, nearly all of it outside the crop
  3. no frame-level opacity multiplier: a ghosted pair needs base skeleton at 1.0 and ghost at EVIDENCE_GHOST_OPACITY 0.5, composed with each point's own detected/interpolated opacity

## Per-metric marks (researched from the calcs, not guessed)
- trunkLean: hip-mid -> shoulder-mid segment; VERTICAL ray up from hip-mid; ANGLE ARC at hip-mid between them. This is literally what atan2(dx,-dy) measures (trunkLean.ts:164-173). Two instants, each with its own arc.
- kneeFlexion: hip -> knee -> ankle chain; reference ray = hip->knee extended past the knee; ANGLE ARC at the KNEE vertex. CAUTION: the reported number is 180 - interiorAngle, so the drawn arc is the SUPPLEMENT of the value. Label accordingly. The ghost (extension trough) is legibility context only and carries no measured value (kneeFlexion.ts:69-81) — must not be captioned as measured.
- overstriding: ankle <-> hip-mid; VERTICAL plumb line at hipMid.x; HORIZONTAL caliper plumb->ankle. Not an angle.
- footStrikePattern: knee -> ankle shank; VERTICAL plumb at the knee; HORIZONTAL caliper knee.x->ankle.x, plus the +/-0.05*torso midfoot band as guide lines. Do NOT draw a shank-vs-vertical arc labelled with the value — the quantity is a horizontal offset, not an angle. ONE instant.
- stepWidth / stepWidthCm: ankle + both hips; VERTICAL midline at hipMidX, PER FRAME (a ghosted pair has TWO midlines, not one); HORIZONTAL caliper midline->ankle per instant. For stepWidth the left_hip->right_hip segment IS the normalizer and is drawable in-frame.
- armSwingSymmetry: shoulder -> elbow -> wrist, one side; HORIZONTAL line through the shoulder in each frame; TWO VERTICAL BARS for wrist.y - shoulder.y. Drawing only the two wrist positions would be WRONG — the quantity is a difference of two SHOULDER-RELATIVE offsets (armSwingSymmetry.ts:117).
- bounceCycle (verticalOscillation, verticalOscillationCm, verticalRatio): midpoint marker + HORIZONTAL line at each instant's midpoint-y. See the honesty rule below before adding a caliper label.
- verticalRatio stridePair: hip-mid marker; VERTICAL tick at each hip-mid x; HORIZONTAL caliper between ticks.
- cadence: emits nothing, by design (cadence.ts:118-129, and independently METRICS_WITHOUT_EVIDENCE at evidenceFrames.ts:97).

## HONESTY RULE — the drawn quantity is usually NOT the card's number
Do not label a mark with the metric's reported value unless they are genuinely the same quantity. They usually are not:
- bounceCycle amplitude is a whole-clip least-squares spectral fit with a c+d*t+e*t^2 trend removed (bounceInstants.ts:20-30). The pixel gap between the two ghosted midpoints is NOT the reported amplitude. verticalOscillationCm is further removed still — its fit is over integrated metre deltas from one winning run.
- verticalRatio's value is a quotient across two DIFFERENT exemplars; each image shows one factor.
- armSwingSymmetry's value is a ratio BETWEEN the two images.
- Every torso/hip-width-normalized ratio (overstriding, footStrikePattern, stepWidth) divides by a CLIP-MEDIAN body scale (bodyScale.ts:41, :68) — numerator drawable, denominator not.
- trunkLean and overstriding deliberately select the EXTREME instants (exemplars.ts:44-54) while the card reports a MEDIAN, so the drawn geometry is by construction not the reported number.
Caption marks as what was measured AT THIS INSTANT. This is the same discipline that keeps the spec's ideal-posture prohibition meaningful.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A pure, canvas-free module turns an EvidenceFramePlan into annotation draw ops in output-canvas coordinates
- [ ] The transform is exercised by unit tests including a fractional crop.side (s != 1)
- [ ] Joint layer reuses the skeletonGeometry DrawOp model and preserves detected-vs-interpolated opacity, composed with the base/ghost multiplier
- [ ] Only the exemplar's own keypoints are drawn, not all 22 skeleton edges
- [ ] Per-metric marks match the table above; kneeFlexion's supplement relationship is handled explicitly
- [ ] No mark is labelled with the card's reported value where the drawn quantity differs; metrics with no honestly drawable mark get joints only
- [ ] Zero canvas/DOM references in this module (it must run in jsdom)
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean
notes:
=== CORRECTIONS from the strides-ac9.1 spec pass (source-verified) — these override the description ===

1. **stepWidth's normalizer is HIP WIDTH, not torso length — and this row is the most dangerous, not the safest.**
   The description's per-metric table calls stepWidth safe on the grounds that 'the left_hip->right_hip segment IS the normalizer and is drawable in-frame'. That is WRONG. stepWidth divides by `estimateHipWidth`'s CLIP-MEDIAN `hipWidthPx` (stepWidth.ts:224, bodyScale.ts:56-68 — deliberately a separate function from estimateBodyScale per bodyScale.ts:46-55).
   The hip segment visible in the picture is THAT FRAME'S hip width. The value used the CLIP MEDIAN. So a reader who measures the drawn segment and divides gets a different number than the card shows — a drawable-LOOKING denominator that is not the one used. Draw the segment, but do NOT label the quotient.

2. **trunkLean's sign flips with direction of travel.** trunkLean.ts:171-173 multiplies by travelDirection. On a right-to-left runner the sign of the tilt visible on screen is the OPPOSITE of the sign the card reports. An arc labelled with the card's value would point the wrong way — not merely be imprecise. This is now a spec scenario in the inline-annotated-evidence change.

3. armSwingSymmetry's reported value is computed at armSwingSymmetry.ts:271, not :117. (:117 is the per-side half-swing excursion, which is the drawable part.)

4. stepWidthCm has NO clip-median denominator — it divides by per-frame `frame.pixelsPerMeter` (stepWidthCm.ts:248). Still not drawable (a MediaPipe world-landmark calibration is not a visible length), so same no-label rule, different reason.

Read `openspec/changes/inline-annotated-evidence/design.md` D2 for the verified per-metric table — prefer it over the description's table where they disagree.
=== DECISION YOU MUST MAKE — grafted metrics resolve annotation off the WRONG detector's frames ===
From the strides-ac9.6 code review. CONFIRMED mechanism, not yet user-visible, and it lands squarely in this ticket.

`resolveOutwardSigns`'s doc claims it is 'stepWidth.ts:222-223 verbatim, not an approximation'. True for the PRIMARY-pass stepWidth. NOT true for **stepWidthCm** and **verticalOscillationCm**, which arrive by graft from the background MediaPipe scale pass.

scalePassGraft.ts:43-50 records that grafted exemplars carry the SCALE PASS's instants while 'the only frames any consumer holds are the primary pass's', and EvidenceGallery.tsx:204 duly hands planClipEvidence `input.frames = clip.analysis.robustFrames` (MoveNet) alongside the grafted heuristics. So instantPlan resolves those exemplars' joint positions AND hip polarity off a MoveNet frame snapped within tolerance — never the MediaPipe frame the metric actually measured.

Concrete failure: front-view clip, MoveNet primary, scale pass 'agreed' (so dropGraftedExemplars does not fire). stepWidthCm selects a right-foot strike where MediaPipe put right_hip 4px right of left_hip -> outwardSign +1, a positive 'own side' offset. MoveNet's frame at the nearest sampled timestamp puts the hips 2px the other way — a coin flip at that separation, and near-frontal instants are exactly where step-width strikes live. The plan then carries {left:+1, right:-1}, the INVERSE of what the metric used, and your caliper labels a crossover strike as landing on its own side — contradicting the card's own crossover caveat (stepWidth.ts:273-277) in the same viewport.

Live-reachable: this repo's measurements record verticalOscillationCm planning an exemplar post-graft on all three test clips.

Not introduced by ac9.6 — it widened a documented, accepted seam that previously carried only a coarse crop box, where a few pixels are invisible. ac9.6 is the first to push a POLARITY through it.

DECIDE, and record the decision: (a) draw no signed/oriented mark for grafted metrics, (b) draw joints only for them, or (c) accept it with a stated argument for why the divergence cannot flip a sign in practice. Do NOT let this be discovered at draw time. Whichever you pick, correct resolveOutwardSigns' 'verbatim' doc comment to name the graft exception.
close_reason: Annotation layer shipped as src/results/evidenceAnnotations.ts. planEvidenceAnnotations(plan, maxOutputSidePx) emits flat ops carrying layer ('joint'|'measurement'), instant ('base'|'ghost'|'pair') and a composed opacity, ALL in output-canvas space via a single toEvidenceOutputSpace call site that a hygiene test pins. Dispatch is on exemplar KIND, not MetricId (bounceCycle is shared by three metrics, stepWidthStrike by two). Grafted-metric divergence resolved as option (a): polarity suppressed, geometry kept — verticalOscillationCm stays op-for-op identical to verticalOscillation, stepWidthCm's caliper draws as the unsigned span it honestly is. resolveOutwardSigns' 'verbatim' doc corrected. Ghost multiplier composes as pointOpacity x frameMultiplier, all four combinations asserted. No numeric labels anywhere, per the honesty requirement. Two deviations from the ticket, both recorded in design D12: the midfoot band is DROPPED (its half-width is a clip-median torso length and a band around the knee reads as a target zone, which this change's own spec forbids), and no caliper is emitted without a per-instant side (filed as a follow-up rather than inferred from cropKeypoints array order). 78 files / 1118 tests, tsc + eslint + openspec --strict green, nothing under src/heuristics/ touched.

title: Thread keypoints and measurement sign into the evidence plan
description:
Plumbing prerequisite. Nothing in Epic B can draw a joint or an oriented caliper until this lands.

## Gap 1 — the plan drops the keypoints
`EvidenceFramePlan` (evidenceFrames.ts:139-154) retains only `{metric, kind, side?, quality, label, base:{timestamp,opacity}, ghost, crop, demotedFromPair}`. No RobustPoseFrame, no keypoint positions, and `cropKeypoints` is consumed inside `planExemplarFrames` (:404-429) and then DROPPED.

`robustFrames` is also not threaded into the extractor at all: `ClipEvidenceInput = { sourceBlob, plan }` (extractFrames.ts:121-124), and EvidenceGallery has `input.frames` in scope (:57, :92) but passes only `{sourceBlob, plan}` (:218).

Three viable seams. PREFER THE FIRST — `planExemplarFrames` already holds both RobustPoseFrames at :401-410, so resolving there keeps everything in the pure, unit-testable half exactly as the module already does for crop rects:
  a) resolve positions (or DrawOps) into EvidenceFramePlan during planning  <-- preferred
  b) carry cropKeypoints forward and re-resolve at draw time
  c) add frames to ClipEvidenceInput and resolve in extractFrames.ts

Resolution itself is exact: `base.timestamp`/`ghost.timestamp` are the SAMPLED frame's own timestamp (evidenceFrames.ts:438-445), so `findNearestFrame` returns exactly that frame object. Note `resolvePoint` (keypoints.ts:23-30) treats 'detected' AND 'interpolated' as resolvable; only 'unrecoverable' is null — preserve that distinction, the thumbnails should show it.

## Gap 2 — the sign is missing
`travelDirection` (±1) and `outwardSign` determine the SIGN of every offset metric — overstriding.ts:177, footStrikePattern.ts:192, trunkLean.ts:171, strideLength.ts:182, stepWidth.ts:222-223. NEITHER is carried on `MetricExemplar` nor `EvidenceFramePlan`.

Consequence: a caliper or arrow claiming 'ahead of the hip' vs 'behind', or 'own side' vs 'crossed over', CANNOT be oriented from the plan today. Without this, an overstriding mark can be drawn pointing the wrong way on a right-to-left runner and nothing will catch it.

Thread whichever of these the annotation layer needs. Keep it canvas-free — jsdom has no canvas.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Both instants' keypoint positions are resolvable by the draw layer, with detected-vs-interpolated status preserved
- [ ] travelDirection and/or outwardSign are available wherever a signed mark is drawn

title: Restructure the shell: clips leave the body, picker owns the zero-clip state
description:
The structural move, and the riskiest ticket in the epic. Everything else in Epic A depends on it.

Today `MultiClipVideoSession` renders a 2-col grid: every clip as a full `ClipSlot` stacked in a sticky left column (MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:179-201), results in the right column. This ticket removes clips from the page body.

After this ticket:
- Clip video elements are MOUNTED BUT NOT LAID OUT IN THE BODY — they become hidden hosts that the modal (next ticket) reveals.
- Zero clips renders a full-page picker.
- The results column becomes the page's main content rather than one half of a grid.

## HARD CONSTRAINT — the whole reason this is its own ticket
Sampling reads frames off a live, PLAYING <video> element (`useVideoAnalysis` per clip, mounted in ClipSlot.tsx:51). Clip video elements MUST remain mounted and playable while analysing. Hiding must be visual only. Do NOT conditionally render them, do not move them behind a mount gate, and do not use `display:none` without verifying frame sampling still advances — a display:none video can be throttled or refuse to play in some engines. Prefer keeping the element in flow but visually clipped/offscreen, and VERIFY LIVE.

Type checks and unit tests will NOT catch a break here. Verify in headless Chromium on real GPU per CLAUDE.md's live-browser harness: analysis must still reach 'Analysis complete' with a normal `sampling.detectedFrames` count on Demo 1 and Demo 2.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Clips no longer occupy a body column; results are the main content
- [ ] Zero clips renders a full-page picker
- [ ] Clip video elements stay mounted and analysis still completes — VERIFIED LIVE in headless Chromium on real GPU, not by unit test alone
- [ ] `[analysis-diagnostics]` sampling.detectedFrames on Demo 1 is within normal range vs. the pre-change baseline (record both numbers in the ticket)
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean
notes:
=== strides-kyu.3 IMPLEMENTED — but G1b's playback arm FAILS on every ladder rung. Needs an epic decision. ===

Branch: worktree-agent-ab4188c1e2747b18b, based on feat/layout-redesign (ab5d185). 4 commits, NOT pushed, NOT merged.

## What landed
- ClipPicker extracted out of VideoInputPanel as a pure, DOM-identical refactor (committed and
  verified alone first, so a selector break bisects to one commit).
- Decision 1: a genuinely EMPTY session. clipIds seeds []; removeClip's refuse-below-one guard and
  its mirrored poster-release guard both gone; canRemove removed from ClipSlot; reset goes to [].
  Every clip, the first included, is created by addClip with a pendingLoad. Side effect: deletes the
  bug where three files picked from the old first slot produced ONE clip, last file wins.
  Picker-vs-results gate is anyClipVideoReady, not clipIds.length.
- Layout collapsed: <main> loses the 2-col grid, sticky column and results scroll-box.
- Hiding: rung L0 on the video host only — fixed; top:0; left:-200vw; full size; inert.
  hidden={status==='empty'} untouched. Loading line, load-error alert + Try again, queued hint and
  Remove all stay in the body and visible.
- handleTryAgain now focuses the heading (the errored clip's <video> is offscreen + inert, so focus
  would have been lost to <body>).
- Decision 2: "Analyze"/"Analyze again" does NOT move. ResultsView.tsx changed not at all.

## THE BLOCKER — G1b playback arm, Demo 2, -24%, on EVERY rung
Demo 2 only (portrait 4K 59.94fps, the only test clip whose sampling is throughput-limited), 5
trials/variant, paired back-to-back vs a throwaway worktree at ab5d185, real GPU:

  base ab5d185 (old layout, visible)      62 [57..63]
  this layout, wrapper left `relative`    61 [56..63]   <- the RESTRUCTURE is free
  this layout, `fixed` but ON SCREEN      63 [57..64]   <- `position:fixed` is free
  L0  fixed offscreen + inert             47 [46..57]   -24%   (shipped, jointly best)
  L3  1x1 overflow:hidden window          47 [40..59]   -24%
  L2  -z-20 behind an opaque backdrop     39 [37..47]   -37%
  L1  opacity-0 + -z-10                   34 [33..39]   -45%

The cost is CONCEALMENT, not any one technique. The ladder's ordering is inverted — L0 is the BEST
concealed option and descending is monotonically worse, so "descend on failure" has nowhere to go.
Escalated rather than accepted or tuned away.

Two findings beyond the number:
1. G1a PASSED while G1b failed, so G1a alone is NOT sufficient (D8 calls it "the PRIMARY instrument
   … decisive in seconds"). It measures an idle element with no competing per-frame work; the real
   failure is proportional, not binary — hidden still presents frames (Demo 2 116 vs visible 118),
   it just yields fewer SAMPLES once something contends for the frame budget.
2. Only a throughput-limited clip can see it. Demo 1 (25fps) reads 47 -> 47 at every rung; 40ms/frame
   is enough slack. Demo 2 has 16.7ms. A gate measuring only Demo 1 reads green through this.

Blast radius is bounded: default WebCodecs path untouched (Demo 1 53->53, Demo 2 99->99,
bit-identical, sampling.path asserted per arm). Loss lands only where canUseSequentialDecode says
no — WebM/webcam clips, the exact population D8's own correction said the original G1 was blind to.

The only mechanism the data points at: keep the element genuinely ON SCREEN while its own analysis
is in flight, conceal it only afterwards. That changes what the reader sees during analysis — a
product decision this ticket has no mandate to make. NOT attempted.

## Gates that passed
G1a: hidden vs visible over a fixed 2s window — Demo 1 51 vs 50, Demo 2 116 vs 118; inert moves
neither (2x2 measured). readyState 4, paused false, box non-degenerate throughout.
G1b sequential arm: Demo 1 53->53, Demo 2 99->99, bit-identical.
G5: Demo 1 7 images / 5 sections, Demo 2 5 / 4 — per-metric breakdown matches CLAUDE.md
cell-for-cell, zero extraction-failed.
tsc -b clean; eslint clean; 1083 unit tests pass (baseline 1079); npm run test:e2e green with ZERO
e2e edits.
Human-eye: zero clips -> full picker, all four inputs; Demo 1 -> results own the page, no stray 4K
video at narrow/wide x light/dark (video box measured offscreen at x=-2878); .txt renamed .mp4 ->
error alert + Try again visible and working WITH the picker beside it; Remove works and removing the
last clip returns to the picker; 40 Tab stops never enter the hidden host; R2 (Demo 1 as the FIRST
clip through pendingLoad under StrictMode) gets a live blob: src and completes — no corruption.
close_reason: Restructure landed and is FREE — measured. Clips out of the body, results own the page, empty session modelled (clipIds seeds [], removeClip guard dropped), ClipPicker extracted with byte-identical DOM (zero e2e edits). Decision 1: genuinely empty session. Decision 2: Analyze stays in ResultsView. Decision 3: ResultsView.tsx untouched. G1a passes at L0 (Demo 1 51 vs 50 control; Demo 2 116 vs 118), inert costs nothing. G5 matches CLAUDE.md cell-for-cell. R2 StrictMode first-clip-via-pendingLoad verified clean. 77 files / 1083 tests, tsc + eslint + e2e green. The CONCEALMENT half fails G1b's playback arm by -24% on Demo 2 under every ladder rung — escalated as strides-kyu.13 (P0) rather than tuned; L0 shipped as jointly least-bad.

title: Focus-area taxonomy and cited feedback points (why / cue / non-point / one thing)
description:
## Description
Build the pure data layer that turns 13 metrics into **feedback points by body region**. It contains no UI.

1. **`src/guidance/focusAreas.ts`.** `FocusAreaId = 'rhythm' | 'arms' | 'posture' | 'knees' | 'landing' | 'footPath'` in tour order, plus the final 'oneThing' stop, which is a tour concept, not an area. Each area has a label (1–2 words) and its metricIds:
   - rhythm: cadence, verticalRatio, verticalOscillationCm, verticalOscillation
   - arms: armSwingAmplitude
   - posture: trunkLean
   - knees: kneeDrive, kneeFlexion
   - landing: overstriding, footStrikePattern
   - footPath: stepWidth, stepWidthCm, swingFootLateralExcursion

   A pure helper `focusAreaView(area, fusedMetrics, tiers)` returns: the headline metric (the first measured and not excluded, in a documented preference order), the supporting metrics, and `measured: boolean`.
2. **`src/guidance/feedbackPoints.ts`.** For each area:
   - A `why` line: ≤ 14 words, with `{ text, url, evidence: 'trial' | 'association' | 'mixed' }`.
   - A `cue`, used only where an intervention has evidence. Reuse the existing `METRIC_GUIDANCE[*].tryLine` wherever one exists (cadence, verticalOscillationCm, verticalOscillation, overstriding). Keep the existing `tryLineApplies` rule (src/results/guidedGroups.ts) to decide whether the cue applies to this value.
   - A `nonPoint` where the evidence says not to change. Foot strike: "Most runners land heel-first; no evidence says to change it." (Anderson 2020 / Larson 2011.) Step width: "Your own width is usually your most economical." (Arellano 2011.)
   - Knees **never** cue "lift your knees" (Folland 2017).
   - Every URL must come from docs/prd/runner-led-results-research.md or existing metricGuidance links, and must be **re-verified** (open it and confirm it states the claim). Pin each URL in a test the same way metricGuidance.test.ts does. If a claim can't be verified, drop the line. Do not soften it into something unsourced.
3. **`selectOneThing(areas)`.** Picks the applicable cue with the strongest evidence, in this priority order: cadence > overstriding > bounce (VO family) > others. If none applies, it returns `{ kind: 'nothingToChange' }`. A cue for a value inside its cited band is never selected.
4. **Word-budget test.** A stop's visible furniture (label + why + cue or nonPoint) is ≤ 25 words.
5. **The openspec change `add-runner-tour`.** Create it with proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md and `specs/runner-feedback/spec.md`, covering: the cited-or-absent rule for why/cue lines; never grading; the non-point rule; the one-thing rule.

## Expected file paths
- src/guidance/focusAreas.ts (+ test)
- src/guidance/feedbackPoints.ts (+ test)
- src/guidance/types.ts (only if a shared type belongs there)
- openspec/changes/add-runner-tour/** (proposal, design, tasks, specs/runner-feedback/spec.md)

## Notes
Read docs/agent-notes/guided-results-view.md first: the band rules, the "most is not best" rule, tryLine direction, and word-budget history. The user previously found the page "significantly too verbose".

title: Adopt-your-gait intro beat for the model runner
description:
## Description
Add the "adopt your gait" intro beat to ModelRunner, as an `intro` prop or a `useRunnerIntro` hook.

- The runner starts fully neutral: grey and dashed.
- Measured parameters are then applied one at a time, in focus-area order, over about 4 s total. Each parameter tweens from neutral to its measured value, its segment turns solid, and its value flashes as a small label for about 500 ms.
- There is a "Skip" affordance, and the intro is skipped entirely under reduced motion.

title: ModelRunner SVG renderer: measured vs neutral, focus annotations, 30fps, pause, reduced motion
description:
## Description
Add `src/runner/ModelRunner.tsx`, the SVG renderer for the model-runner core.

Props: `{ params: BoundRunnerParams, camera: CameraPreset | CameraState, focus?: { metricIds: MetricId[], annotation?: 'angleArc' | 'bracket' | 'offset' }, playbackRate?: number, label: string }`.

- **Drawing.** Measured parts are solid. Neutral parts are dashed grey. The focus area's measured parts are accented and carry a value annotation: an angle arc for lean/knee, a vertical bracket for bounce, a horizontal offset for overstride/step width. Joints are dots.
- **Animation.** Use a requestAnimationFrame loop capped at 30 fps. Phase advances at `cadence/120` cycles per second × `playbackRate`. Pause when `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'` or when the element is offscreen (IntersectionObserver).
- **Camera.** Changing the camera tweens over about 600 ms. Under reduced motion it cuts instead.
- **Controls.** An inline pause/play button is always visible, and the choice persists for the component's lifetime. This fixes the WCAG 2.2.2 gap in strides-au2. Under reduced motion the runner holds a still mid-stance pose unless the reader presses play.
- **Accessibility.** The SVG is `aria-hidden`. A visually hidden text alternative names which parameters were measured.
- **Caption.** The caption reads "Model built from your numbers". Never "reference" or "ideal" (strides-v2d).

Extend the `add-model-runner` spec with the rendering requirements.

## Expected file paths
- src/runner/ModelRunner.tsx (+ .test.tsx)
- src/runner/runnerAnnotations.ts (if needed)
- src/index.css (only if a token is needed; prefer Tailwind utilities)
- openspec/changes/add-model-runner/specs/model-runner/spec.md

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: A1 (model-runner core).

title: Model-runner core: gait kinematics, metric→parameter binding, camera presets
description:
## Description
Build the pure (React-free) model-runner core in `src/runner/`. This is the contract every later runner ticket builds on, so it ships with thorough unit tests.

1. **`gaitModel.ts`.** `poseAt(phase: number, params: RunnerParams): Joint3D[]`, where `phase` is in [0,1) for one full gait cycle (two steps, L then R). It covers the 19 joints of `COMMON_KEYPOINT_NAMES` (src/pose/types.ts), and the loop is seamless at phase 0/1. The model is procedural (sinusoids/splines per joint), with fixed body proportions documented as illustrative.
2. **`runnerParams.ts`.** `bindRunnerParams(metrics, tiers)` returns `{ value, source: 'measured' | 'neutral', metricId? }` per parameter. The binding is exactly one metric per DOF:
   - cadence → cycle rate
   - verticalOscillation (ratio of torso; fall back to verticalOscillationCm against model torso length) → pelvis vertical amplitude
   - trunkLean → torso pitch
   - armSwingAmplitude → arm swing amplitude
   - kneeDrive → peak swing thigh angle
   - kneeFlexion → peak swing knee bend. Read src/heuristics/kneeFlexion.ts to confirm whether this is a swing or contact angle and bind accordingly.
   - overstriding → foot landing offset ahead of the hip, in torso lengths
   - footStrikePattern → ankle angle at contact
   - stepWidth → lateral foot placement
   - swingFootLateralExcursion → swing-foot lateral arc

   A metric whose tier is 'excluded' (src/results/metricConfidence.ts:73) or that is null leaves its DOF **neutral**. Neutral constants are documented as illustrative and are **never** a band midpoint.
3. **`camera.ts`.** An orthographic projection with yaw, pitch, zoom and a focus target. Presets: `wholeBodySide`, `upperFrontQuarter`, `torsoSide`, `legsSide`, `footSide`, `feetFront`. Also `interpolateCamera(a, b, t)`.
4. **The openspec change `add-model-runner`.** proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md, and `specs/model-runner/spec.md` with the honesty rules from the PRD: one metric per DOF; neutral parts flagged so the renderer can draw them dashed; no per-side or variability display; no "ideal" runner. Must pass `openspec validate add-model-runner --strict`.

## Expected file paths
- src/runner/gaitModel.ts (+ .test.ts)
- src/runner/runnerParams.ts (+ .test.ts)
- src/runner/camera.ts (+ .test.ts)
- src/runner/types.ts
- openspec/changes/add-model-runner/**

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: strides-t1e (spec housekeeping must land before new deltas).
- Parallel with: the tour epic's feedback-content ticket.

## Notes
- MetricResult carries no per-side or per-stride data (src/heuristics/types.ts:296-342). Do not invent asymmetry.
- Do not touch src/heuristics/** or any measurement code.
design:
# Plan: strides-ps19.1, the model-runner core (`src/runner/`, openspec `add-model-runner`)

Orchestrator decisions on the planner's open questions (all defaults accepted):
Q1 footStrikePattern binds contactShankOffset exactly; foot pitch at contact = shank angle.
Q2 swing arc outward, documented illustrative. Q3 no stepWidthCm fallback. Q4 segment measured if ANY param listing it is measured.
Q5 head edges always neutral. Q6 `tierOf` fn param defaulting to `metricTier`. Q7 keep `metricValue` + `clamped`. Q8 upperFrontQuarter yaw 45°.

## 1. Design summary
`src/runner/` holds three pure, React-free modules. Nothing under `src/heuristics/**` is read except type imports (and read-only imports of guidance constants in tests).
- `gaitModel.ts`: forward kinematics driven by periodic cosine-eased keyframe curves and sinusoids. Output is 19 `Joint3D` in `COMMON_KEYPOINT_NAMES` order. Units are torso lengths (shoulder-mid to hip-mid = 1).
- `runnerParams.ts`: binds each DOF to one metric, or holds it at a neutral constant.
- `camera.ts`: orthographic camera with yaw, pitch, zoom and a target; presets; `interpolateCamera`.

Core rule: every parameter is stored in its metric's own unit. Each bound DOF reproduces its metric's own definition when that formula is applied to the model's joints, so binding is identity + clamp (VO_cm is the one exception, divided by model torso length 50 cm). Testable honesty rule: "measuring the model returns the bound value".

### Exact types (`src/runner/types.ts`)
```ts
import type { KeypointName } from '../pose/types'
import type { MetricId } from '../heuristics/types'

export interface Vec3 { x: number; y: number; z: number }
/** x = direction of travel, y = up, z = runner's RIGHT (right-handed). Torso lengths. */
export interface Joint3D extends Vec3 { name: KeypointName }

export type RunnerParamId =
  | 'cadence'            // steps/min
  | 'pelvisBounce'       // hip-mid vertical peak-to-peak, torso lengths
  | 'torsoPitch'         // deg, + = forward of vertical
  | 'armSwing'           // peak-to-peak (wrist.y - shoulder.y), torso lengths
  | 'peakThighAngle'     // deg, hip->knee forward of down-vertical, swing peak
  | 'peakSwingKneeBend'  // deg flexion (180 - hip-knee-ankle interior), swing peak
  | 'landingOffset'      // ankle ahead of hip-mid at contact, torso lengths
  | 'contactShankOffset' // ankle ahead of same-side knee at contact, torso lengths
  | 'stepWidth'          // ankle lateral from midline at contact, hip widths, + = own side
  | 'swingFootArc'       // lateral (ankle - knee) range in early-to-mid swing, hip widths
export type RunnerParams = Readonly<Record<RunnerParamId, number>>

export type RunnerMetricId =   // explicit 11 of 13; verticalRatio and stepWidthCm never bind
  | 'cadence' | 'verticalOscillation' | 'verticalOscillationCm' | 'trunkLean'
  | 'armSwingAmplitude' | 'kneeDrive' | 'kneeFlexion' | 'overstriding'
  | 'footStrikePattern' | 'stepWidth' | 'swingFootLateralExcursion'

export type BoundRunnerParam =
  | { source: 'measured'; value: number; metricId: RunnerMetricId; metricValue: number; clamped: boolean }
  | { source: 'neutral'; value: number }
export type BoundRunnerParams = Readonly<Record<RunnerParamId, BoundRunnerParam>>

export type CameraPreset =
  | 'wholeBodySide' | 'upperFrontQuarter' | 'torsoSide' | 'legsSide' | 'footSide' | 'feetFront'
export interface CameraState { yawDeg: number; pitchDeg: number; zoom: number; target: Vec3 }
/** SVG orientation: x right, y DOWN, torso lengths x zoom, origin = target; larger depth = nearer. */
export interface ProjectedJoint { name: KeypointName; x: number; y: number; depth: number }

export type SkeletonEdge = readonly [KeypointName, KeypointName]
export type { MetricId }
```
- `MetricId` has 13 members (`src/heuristics/types.ts:67-80`).
- The bound param carries `metricValue` and `clamped` (ps19.2/.3 label the true number and need to know when the drawing hit a geometry limit).

### Neutral constants (illustrative, no claim attached)
Ranges are drawable-geometry limits, not plausibility judgments.

| param | neutral | clamp range | not a band midpoint / central value |
|---|---|---|---|
| cadence | 160 spm | [120, 220] | zone midpoints 158 / 168.5 / 178.5 |
| pelvisBounce | 0.14 (7.0 cm at 50 cm torso) | [0, 0.5] | VO_cm band 6.0–9.5, midpoint 7.75, central 7.7 |
| torsoPitch | 4° | [−15, 35] | trunkLean band 1.8–21.4, midpoint 11.6, central 10.3 |
| armSwing | 0.30 | [0, 0.9] | unbanded |
| peakThighAngle | 40° | [10, 85] | unbanded |
| peakSwingKneeBend | 90° | [50, 150] | kneeFlexion band 71.3–129, midpoint 100.15, central 94.1 |
| landingOffset | 0.30 | [−0.3, 0.7] | unbanded |
| contactShankOffset | 0.08 | [−0.3, 0.4] | unbanded; ≠ ±0.05 midfoot boundary (`types.ts:953`) |
| stepWidth | 0.30 | [−1.5, 1.5] | unbanded |
| swingFootArc | 0.15 | [0, 0.8] | unbanded |

(Verify these band numbers against METRIC_GUIDANCE yourself; the test enforces it.) Each neutral differs from `makeHeuristics()` fixture defaults (`src/results/__fixtures__/metricResult.ts`). `MODEL_TORSO_LENGTH_CM = 50`.

## 2. Metric → DOF mapping
| metric (unit, sign; source) | param | conversion | realization |
|---|---|---|---|
| cadence (spm) | cadence | ×1 | `cyclesPerSecond = cadence/120`; no geometry |
| verticalOscillation (ratio hip p2p / torso; `types.ts:362`) | pelvisBounce | ×1 | hip-mid y = H0 − (B/2)·cos(4π(p − 0.19)) |
| ↳ fallback verticalOscillationCm, only when VO excluded/null | pelvisBounce | ÷ 50 | same |
| trunkLean (deg, + toward travel; `trunkLean.ts:117,158-168`) | torsoPitch | ×1 | shoulder-mid = hip-mid + (sin λ, cos λ, 0) |
| armSwingAmplitude (ratio, mean p2p (wrist.y − shoulder.y)/torso; `armSwingAmplitude.ts:37-38,168-170`) | armSwing | ×1 | closed form §4 |
| kneeDrive (deg hip→knee off down-vertical, swing peak; `kneeDrive.ts:159-185,224-229`) | peakThighAngle | ×1 | thigh keyframe at swing peak |
| kneeFlexion (deg, 180 − interior, swing peak median) — SWING angle: `kneeFlexion.ts:213,160-166,243-245,259,292`; `kneeDrive.ts:162-164` | peakSwingKneeBend | ×1 | knee keyframe q=0.62 |
| overstriding (ratio (ankle.x − hipMid.x)/torso at footstrike; `overstriding.ts:247-249,305-307`) | landingOffset | ×1 | contact solve §4 |
| footStrikePattern (ratio (ankle.x − knee.x)/torso at footstrike; `footStrikePattern.ts:133-139`) | contactShankOffset | ×1 | contact solve; foot pitch at contact = shank angle |
| stepWidth (percent of hip width; `stepWidth.ts:106-110`) | stepWidth | ×1 (check unit: percent vs fraction — convert to hip widths) | frontal leg tilt α §4 |
| swingFootLateralExcursion (percent of hip width, median P80−P20; `swingFootLateralExcursion.ts:146-153`) | swingFootArc | ×1 (same unit check) | lateral bump §4 |

Each metric id appears in exactly one param's candidate list. Out-of-range → clamp, `clamped: true`.

## 3. File-by-file
Nothing outside `src/runner/` and `openspec/changes/add-model-runner/`. No new deps.
1. `src/runner/types.ts`.
2. `src/runner/gaitModel.ts` — exports `MODEL_PROPORTIONS`, `MODEL_TORSO_LENGTH_CM = 50`, `GAIT_PHASES` (left-leg q; right = q+0.5: leftContact 0, rightContact 0.5, midStance 0.19, stanceEnd 0.38, peakSwingKneeBend 0.62, peakThigh 0.85, swingArcStart 0.5, swingArcEnd 5/6), `poseAt(phase, params): Joint3D[]`, `cyclesPerSecond(params)`. Private keyframe interp + contact solve. File doc: proportions illustrative.
3. `gaitModel.test.ts`
4. `src/runner/runnerParams.ts` — `RUNNER_PARAM_SPECS: Record<RunnerParamId, { metrics: readonly { metric: RunnerMetricId; scale: number }[]; neutral: number; range: readonly [number, number] }>` (priority order); `NEUTRAL_RUNNER_PARAMS`; `bindRunnerParams(metrics: Pick<FormHeuristicsResult, RunnerMetricId>, tierOf = metricTier): BoundRunnerParams` (skip candidate if value null or tier 'excluded'; caveated binds); `runnerParamValues(bound): RunnerParams`; `paramForMetric(id: MetricId): RunnerParamId | null`; `RUNNER_PARAM_SEGMENTS: Record<RunnerParamId, readonly SkeletonEdge[]>`; `segmentSource(edge, bound)`. Reuse `SKELETON_EDGES` from `src/results/skeletonGeometry.ts:8` (do not duplicate; check it includes heel/foot_index edges — if not, define the foot-triangle edges locally and note it).
5. `runnerParams.test.ts`
6. `src/runner/camera.ts` — `CAMERA_PRESETS`, `CAMERA_FRAME_HALF_HEIGHT = 2`, `resolveCamera`, `projectPoint`, `projectPose`, `interpolateCamera`.
7. `camera.test.ts`
8. `openspec/changes/add-model-runner/` via `openspec new change "add-model-runner"`; proposal/design/tasks/specs/model-runner/spec.md (ADDED only).

No existing 3D/projection code; `motionStoryGeometry.ts` is 2D and not reused.

## 4. Joint-geometry model
Frame: x travel, y up (ground y=0), z runner's right. Hip-mid x=0, z=0. `p = phase - Math.floor(phase)`. Left q=p, right q=frac(p+0.5).

Proportions (torso=1, illustrative; adjust only with doc): hip width W 0.40; shoulder width 0.75; thigh T/shank S 0.85/0.85; upper arm U/forearm F 0.60/0.55; elbow flexion β 80°; heel (−0.15 along sole, −0.10 normal); toe (+0.45, −0.10); ears (fwd −0.05, up 0.42, lat ±0.12); nose (fwd 0.12, up 0.38). Tune PELVIS_HEIGHT H0 once so neutral lowest foot point ≈ y=0, hard-code.

Curves: periodic cosine-eased keyframes `v = a + (b−a)(1−cos πu)/2` (exact at keys, C1, no overshoot, monotone in key values).
- Thigh θ(q) (deg fwd of down-vertical): keys [0, θc], [0.38, −22], [0.85, peakThighAngle].
- Knee κ(q) (flexion; shank σ = θ − κ): [0, κc], [0.19, 40], [0.38, 22], [0.62, peakSwingKneeBend], [0.90, 15]. Clamp floor 50 > all other keys and κc ≤ 45, so max = bound value.
- Foot pitch φ(q) (+ toes up): [0, σc], [0.19, 0], [0.38, −35], [0.62, −20], [0.90, 5].
- FK from hip: knee = (T sinθ, −T cosθ); ankle = knee + (S sinσ, −S cosσ); u=(cosφ, sinφ), n=(−sinφ, cosφ); heel = ankle − 0.15u − 0.10n; toe = ankle + 0.45u − 0.10n.

Contact solve (θc, σc, κc from L=landingOffset, F=contactShankOffset): σ* = asin(clamp(F/S)); θ* = asin(clamp((L − S sinσ*)/T)). If κ* = θ* − σ* ∈ [0°,45°] and no asin clamped, use it. Else κc = clamp(κ*,0,45), solve θ with L exact: θ = asin(clamp(L/R_k)) − φ_k, R_k = |T + S·e^{−iκ}|, φ_k = arg(T + S·e^{−iκ}); σ = θ − κ (foot-strike gives way). NOTE landingOffset is ankle vs hip-MID; the hip joint is at hip-mid in x (z offset only), so fine in sagittal plane.

Step width: rotate leg chain (knee, ankle, heel, toe) about hip's x axis by constant α: z_out' = −y·sinα, y' = y·cosα. α = asin(clamp((stepWidth − 0.5)·W / d_c)), d_c = T cosθc + S cosσc, so contact ankle outward offset from midline = stepWidth·W. Left z = −, right z = +; hip joints at z = ∓W/2.

Swing arc: outward z shift on ankle, heel, toe only (not knee): side·E'·bump(q), bump = (1 − cos(2π(q−0.5)/(1/3)))/2 on q ∈ [0.5, 5/6], else 0. E' = swingFootArc·W / cos(π/5) (P80−P20 of sampled raised-cosine ≈ cos(π/5) of peak — verify numerically in test; tolerance ~0.05 hip widths).

Pelvis: all joints + (0, H0 − (B/2)cos(4π(p − 0.19)), 0).

Torso/head: rigid in torso frame, up t=(sinλ, cosλ, 0), fwd f=(cosλ, −sinλ, 0), pivot hip-mid. Shoulders = shoulder-mid ± (0,0,0.375).

Arms (world frame so lean doesn't change wrist-vs-shoulder): elbow = shoulder + U(sinθa, −cosθa, 0); wrist = elbow + F(sin(θa+β), −cos(θa+β), 0). Drop = R·cos(θa + φ), R=|U + F e^{iβ}|, φ=arg(U + F e^{iβ}). θa_L(p) = (c − φ) + A·sin(2π(p − 0.15)), c = 48°, A = asin(armSwing / (2R sin c)). p2p = armSwing exactly. Right arm(p) = left(p+0.5).

Joints each binding may move (all others bit-identical; tests assert):
| param | allowed |
|---|---|
| cadence | none |
| pelvisBounce | all, y only, same Δy per phase |
| torsoPitch | shoulders, elbows, wrists, ears, nose |
| armSwing | elbows, wrists |
| peakThighAngle | knees, ankles, heels, foot_index |
| peakSwingKneeBend | ankles, heels, foot_index |
| landingOffset, contactShankOffset, stepWidth | knees, ankles, heels, foot_index |
| swingFootArc | ankles, heels, foot_index (z only) |

Segments per param (measured if ANY listing param is measured): pelvisBounce: hip–hip. torsoPitch: both shoulder–hip + shoulder–shoulder. armSwing: four arm edges. peakThighAngle: thighs. landingOffset, stepWidth: thighs + shanks. peakSwingKneeBend: shanks. contactShankOffset, swingFootArc: shanks + foot triangles. cadence: none. Head: always neutral.

Camera: yaw ψ: right r=(cosψ,0,−sinψ), toward-camera c=(sinψ,0,cosψ), up y. Pitch e (camera above): c' = c cos e + y sin e, up' = y cos e − c sin e. d = P − target: x = zoom·(d·r), y = −zoom·(d·up'), depth = d·c'. Yaw 0: runner moves screen-right. Yaw 90: front view, runner's left on screen right. interpolateCamera: clamp t; yaw shortest wrapped path; pitch/target lerp; zoom geometric.

| preset | yaw | pitch | zoom | target |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wholeBodySide | 0 | 0 | 1 | (0, 1.6, 0) |
| upperFrontQuarter | 45 | 5 | 1.7 | (0, 2.4, 0) |
| torsoSide | 0 | 0 | 1.8 | (0, 2.2, 0) |
| legsSide | 0 | 0 | 1.4 | (0, 0.9, 0) |
| footSide | 0 | 0 | 3 | (0.25, 0.25, 0) |
| feetFront | 90 | 0 | 2.4 | (0, 0.35, 0) |
Derive targets from model constants (H0) where possible.

## 5. Tests by AC
Seamless loop: poseAt(0) vs poseAt(1) within 1e-9 (neutral + range corners); poseAt(1−1e-9) within 1e-6 of poseAt(0); 1.25≡0.25, negative phases; 19 joints in order, finite at corners; segment lengths constant; mirror symmetry pose(p) == pose(p+0.5) with L/R swapped and z negated.
Monotone & isolated (one `it` per binding): sweep 5 values low→high with others neutral; realized quantity (metric's own formula on model) strictly rises and ≈ bound value (1e-6 closed form; ~0.2° angle cases; ~0.05 hip widths swingFootArc); over 24 phases joints outside allowed set unchanged. Plus a contact-conflict case (F > L/2).
Null/excluded → neutral: defaults all measured; each metric null → neutral = NEUTRAL value; viewFit 'unsuitable' → neutral; caveated binds; VO fallback cases; clamp sets clamped; verticalRatio/stepWidthCm change nothing; no metric in two params; neutrals differ >1% from every band midpoint/centralTendency in METRIC_GUIDANCE (read-only import); segmentSource cases.
Camera: yaw 0 and 90 projection; target→(0,0); pitch case; interpolate endpoints, yaw wrap 350→10 via 0, zoom 1→4 gives 2; continuity over t steps for every preset pair; presets finite/zoom>0, focus joints within ±CAMERA_FRAME_HALF_HEIGHT; resolveCamera both forms.
Gates: `npm run lint`, `npx tsc -b`, `npx vitest run src/runner`, `openspec validate add-model-runner --strict`.

## 6. openspec change (capability `model-runner`, ADDED only)
proposal.md (Why: PRD "Why a model runner"; What Changes; New capability model-runner; Impact: new src/runner/*, no measurement/threshold/UI change, no dep).
design.md D1 units=metric units; D2 kneeFlexion swing finding w/ line refs; D3 footStrike binds shank offset; D4 contact-conflict rule; D5 neutral table "never a band midpoint or central value; illustrative"; D6 VO_cm fallback vs 50 cm torso; D7 segment rule; D8 camera conventions + presets; D9 no IK, feet illustrative.
tasks.md: types; gaitModel+tests; runnerParams+tests; camera+tests; gates; validate. (Archive happens in the tour epic's verify ticket.)
spec.md ADDED Requirements (SHALL + WHEN/THEN scenarios):
1. The model runner is a seamless procedural gait cycle over the nineteen pose joints. (phase 0 = phase 1; mirrored half-cycle)
2. Every degree of freedom is bound to exactly one measured value or held at a documented neutral constant. (measured binds; null neutral; excluded neutral; caveated binds; cm fallback; one metric never drives two DOFs)
3. Neutral constants are illustrative and never a target. (not band midpoint/central; no ideal/second runner; no per-side or variability param)
4. A bound parameter changes only its own part of the runner, in the direction of its value. (more lean pitches torso further, legs unchanged; measuring the model returns the bound value)
5. Neutral parts are identifiable per segment.
6. An orthographic camera turns, zooms and interpolates continuously. (side yaw 0, front yaw 90, six presets, continuous)
7. The core is pure and leaves measurement untouched.

## 7. Risks
Overstride vs foot-strike conflict (landing exact, knee floors straight, foot-strike gives way; D4). Thigh peak conflict documented. Feet illustrative (no IK). swingFootArc approximate. ps19.2 labels `metricValue`, treats `clamped` as "drawn at the limit". ps19.2/.3 must integrate phase over time (phase += dt·cyclesPerSecond·rate). Reduced motion uses poseAt(GAIT_PHASES.midStance).

- [ ] Driving each measured parameter from low to high changes the intended joint geometry monotonically (for example, more trunkLean gives a larger torso pitch), and does not change unrelated joints. One test per binding.
- [ ] A null or excluded metric yields `source: 'neutral'`.
- [ ] Projection is correct for yaw 0 (side) and 90° (front); camera interpolation stays continuous.
- [ ] `npm run lint`, `npx tsc -b` (or the repo's typecheck) and `npx vitest run src/runner` pass.

title: Yield to the event loop between frames on the sequential sampling path
description: The sequential sampler's per-frame loop runs as one unbroken microtask chain (Chrome trace: RunMicrotasks tasks of 3.9 s and 3.1 s on a Galaxy S21), so the UI cannot paint or respond until a batch ends. Insert a macrotask yield (scheduler.yield() where available, else MessageChannel/setTimeout 0) per frame or per ~16-50 ms of work. Sequential decode is frame-exact, not real-time, so results must stay bit-identical - gate with ab-person-selection --evidence md5. Do NOT touch the playback (rVFC) path: it is real-time and loses samples to added latency.
notes: Implemented on branch perf/6i6.1-yield-sequential-frames (b4ee9a1) in worktree /private/tmp/claude-501/perf-android; not merged. Desktop A/B bit-identical (3 clips x3 trials --evidence + 4-clip run). Galaxy S21: 3-4 s RunMicrotasks chains gone; remaining >500 ms tasks are warm-ups (MoveNet first inference 5.7 s, MoveNet new-resolution 1.8 s, MediaPipe first inference 2.3 s, MediaPipe creation ~2.9 s).

title: Downscale decoded frames before pose inference
description: Detection dominates (p50 64 ms/frame on 4K vs 43 ms on 1080p on a Galaxy S21) although MoveNet's input is 192 px: the cost is likely uploading a full 4K canvas into WebGL each frame. Changes inputs, so needs a pre-registered accuracy A/B on all public clips + private fixtures (keypoints, metric values, tiers, person selection, evidence crops which use native-pixel keypoints). Measure the speed effect on the phone first with a probe.
notes: Speed probe 2026-10-13 on Galaxy S21 (one run each, phone thermal noise likely large): long side bounded at 1280 px. MoveNet detect p50 4K landscape 43.8 -> 34.4 ms, 4K portrait 63.0 -> 37.1 ms, 1080p 31.2 -> 32.4 ms (unchanged); MediaPipe scale pass 4K 56.3 -> 39.5 ms. Roughly 20-40% per 4K frame; per-frame floor ~30-35 ms (MoveNet) and ~40 ms (MediaPipe) remains. Modest, not transformative; still needs the accuracy A/B.

title: Reduce time to fused results by scheduling scale passes after primary clips
description: nextActiveClipIndex waits for each clip's MediaPipe scale pass before allowing the next clip's primary MoveNet pass, so the three-clip demo serializes primary and optional scale work. Evaluate a scheduler that completes all primaries first, shows the fused base metrics, then runs optional scale passes one at a time without GPU contention. Measure time to first useful results, final results, and metric equivalence.
acceptance_criteria: Measured time-to-first-fused-results and time-to-final on the 3-clip demo vs T0 baseline. Per-clip analysis fields identical to single-clip runs. npm test/tsc/eslint green.
notes:
Epic strides-e4c T4. Two candidate schedules to evaluate: (a) this bead's own - all primaries first, then scale passes one at a time (no GPU contention, better time-to-first-results); (b) overlap clip N+1 primary with clip N scale pass on the SEQUENTIAL path only (lower total wall-clock, but GPU contention; CLAUDE.md shows cold/warm process flipping one detection, so metrics may move). Never two scale passes at once (one stateful MediaPipe instance with timestamp-restart logic). Playback path (WebM/webcam) keeps current serialization. Seam: isDoneWithSharedDetector / nextActiveClipIndex in src/results/multiClipAnalysis.ts. Prefer (a) unless (b) is bit-identical and materially faster; report if any field moves.
PLAN (2026-10-05) - DECISION: schedule (a) all primaries first, then scale passes one at a time; playback-path clips keep today's rule. (b) overlap rejected: no time-to-first-results gain over (a) (both ~9.3 s vs 14.3 s fused on the 3-clip demo), only ~2-3 s on the last cm graft, and GPU contention risks moving detections (cold/warm flip re-partitions tracks). No hybrid flag.
Mechanism: useVideoAnalysis gains a 4th param scalePassAllowed=true (guard + dep on the scale-pass effect; a pass already started is never cancelled when the flag flips off). title: MoveNet emits a bystander instead of a large, fully visible runner on IMG_9117 (2.0-2.73 s)
description: On private side clip IMG_9117, the single-pose detector returns the orange-vest worker (behind a parked SUV, x 754->1500 of 3840) for ~0.7 s while the runner is fully visible in the foreground at x<800 with a ~900 px tall box (keyframe at 2.3 s confirms). Detection flips to the runner at 2.733 s. ~43 of ~140 runner frames lost - the whole entry phase. Reproduces with personOfInterest.enabled=false and when the clip is trimmed to start at 2.0 (runner in frame on frame 1), so it is not a stale lock from earlier frames. Mechanism unknown. Hypotheses: MoveNet single-pose centre weighting (it favours the person nearest image centre), the pose-detection package's own internal smart-crop tracking, and acquisition/re-verification never firing because the worker's confidence stays high. Found during strides-2qt.
notes: FIX ATTEMPT 2026-10-02: NO-SHIP (pre-registered gate iii failed; nothing committed). Uncommitted work kept in worktree .claude/worktrees/agent-af315baec8ea8f95d (challengerCheck config + movenet.ts dispatch + 12 tests + openspec change challenge-a-locked-bystander with full measurement in design.md). FINDINGS: (1) On IMG_9117 the check switches to the runner at 2.333 s (ratio 5.16) but after the 3 settle-in crop calls the crop->full-frame reset hands single-pose MoveNet the full frame and it picks the WORKER again at 2.40; gate-refused frames are still returned, reacquisition gives up and installs the worker as anchor at 2.583; runner only recovered at 2.75. This CONTRADICTS the spike's counterfactual (forced full frame every call picked the runner from ~2.2) - unresolved, must be reconciled before another attempt. (2) The PUBLIC clips side-landscape (walker behind the fence, runner enters right edge) and multiperson have the SAME lock-on bug: the check switches once and gains +38 / +23 detected frames, segment start 1.80->1.467 and 2.133->1.433. On multiperson, cadence/verticalOscillation/verticalRatio go caveated->null with the extra frames (cf. CLAUDE.md cold 103 vs warm 127 frames, cadence null when warm - possibly the same phenomenon, unverified). (3) The check is not a strict no-op: multipose MoveNet's BoundingBoxTracker + one-euro filters (detector.js:420-431) advance on every check, drifting later re-verification output on clips with zero switches (front-approach kneeFlexion 106.103->106.795). Gate (i)'s negative control was wrong: side-landscape is not single-person in effect.

title: MetricScale: show a value inside a cited band, accessible without the graphic
description:
Build the scale component that shows where one measured value sits inside a cited reference band.

- src/guidance/MetricScale.test.tsx

BEHAVIOUR
- Renders a horizontal track spanning the metric's scale domain, the reference band shaded within
  it, and a marker at the measured value.
- Labels the domain ends and the band bounds in the metric's own unit.

  silently render as "at the maximum".
- Multi-zone bands (cadence and verticalRatio have five published percentile zones) render every

   band bounds.
2. NO VERDICT IN COLOUR. No red/green/amber semantics, no check or cross, no word grading the
   runner. The band is drawn in a neutral or brand-tinted fill that means "this is where most
   runners are", not "this is where you should be". A test must assert no element carries a
   class matching /\b(bg|text|border)-(red|green|emerald|rose|amber|yellow)-/ .

Tailwind v4, tokens from src/index.css (--color-brand-400..800, --font-sans, --font-display). Follow
the repo idioms: `border-2 border-black dark:border-white`, accent stripe
`border-l-4 border-l-brand-600 dark:border-l-brand-400`. Dark mode via paired `dark:` variants —
there is no class toggler. Give it a BEM-ish root class (e.g. `metric-scale`) since those double as

BOUNDARIES

- Zero edits to src/heuristics/, src/pose/, src/video/, ResultsView.tsx, MetricsPanel.tsx.

title: src/guidance/: the twelve-entry metric guidance record with cited bands
description:
Build the pure data layer that every other ticket consumes: one guidance entry per MetricId, carrying its reference band (or an explicit absence), its research links, its remediation links, its display rank, and its capture hint for when the metric could not be measured.

FILES
- src/guidance/types.ts        — MetricGuidance, ReferenceBand, GuidanceLink, and the evidence-direction union
- src/guidance/metricGuidance.ts — the twelve-entry Record<MetricId, MetricGuidance>
- src/guidance/metricGuidance.test.ts

No React in this ticket. Pure TypeScript.

THE ASSIGNMENT IS DECIDED — take it verbatim from scratchpad/reference-ranges.md and the openspec
design.md. Do not re-derive it and do not add to it.

BANDED (5), in this display rank:
  1 cadence              Garmin 5-zone percentiles: <153 / 153-163 / 164-173 / 174-183 / >183 spm
  2 verticalRatio        Garmin bands HALVED to per-stride: <3.05 / 3.05-3.70 / 3.75-4.30 / 4.35-5.05 / >5.05 %
  3 verticalOscillationCm 6.0-9.5 cm (Malisoux 2023 P10-P90), midpoint 7.7
  4 trunkLean            1.8-21.4 deg observed, mean 10.3 (Folland 2017 n=97)
  5 kneeFlexion          85-125 deg (Fukuchi 2017 speed-stratified + Hanley 2021)

NOT BANDED (7): verticalOscillation, overstriding, footStrikePattern, stepWidth, stepWidthCm,
kneeDrive, armSwingAmplitude. Each still carries research links, remediation links where they exist,
and a note. Three carry a mandatory note whose substance is in reference-ranges.md: overstriding
(no torso-length normalisation exists in the literature; the only defensible statement is relative),
stepWidth/stepWidthCm (crossover is NORMAL at speed; the injury link is modelling-only and rests on
a documented citation error), footStrikePattern (~8 in 10 distance runners are rearfoot; attach no
valence).

Note the cadence entry must ALSO carry the overstriding remediation links, because the evidenced
intervention for overstriding is a 5-10% cadence increase (Lenhart 2014 frames reduced step rate as
overstriding explicitly). That is deliberate, not a copy-paste error.

A band's unit MUST match the MetricResult.unit of its metric. cadence is 'stepsPerMinute',
verticalRatio is 'percent' (a 0..1 value the panel renders as %, so mind the factor of 100),
verticalOscillationCm is 'centimeters', trunkLean and kneeFlexion are 'degrees'.

ACCEPTANCE (all pinned by tests)
- Every one of the 12 MetricIds has an entry; exhaustiveness is enforced by the Record type AND by
  a test that iterates the MetricId union.
- Every banded metric's band names a source with a title, a URL, a population and a sample size.
- Every URL is https, and is one of the URLs verified in reference-ranges.md / remediation-research.md.
  Pin that set as a literal in the test so an unverified URL cannot be added silently.
- Every band's bounds lie inside its own scale domain.
- The seven unbanded metrics have band === null. A test names them explicitly, so adding a band to
  one is a deliberate, visible change.
- Display ranks are unique and dense.

BOUNDARIES
- Zero edits to src/heuristics/, src/pose/, src/video/, ResultsView.tsx, MetricsPanel.tsx.
- No invented numbers. If you think a metric deserves a band that reference-ranges.md does not list,
  STOP and report.

VERIFY: `npx tsc -b && npm test -- src/guidance && npm run lint`
close_reason: Closed
