title: Sub-floor bounce fit adopts red noise as a retimed rhythm — blocks strides-b4f
description:
BLOCKS strides-b4f. The two-pass sub-floor bounce fit (openspec change
detect-retimed-clips-below-the-gait-floor, src/heuristics/bounceSpectrum.ts) works on its target but
cannot ship: the sub-floor band is exactly where RED noise concentrates its power, and the gate it
reuses was calibrated against WHITE noise.

THE MEASUREMENT. 300 seeded random walks (v[k] = v[k-1] + U(-0.5,0.5)) -- a series with no rhythm at
any frequency -- at this corpus's own sample counts:

  288 @30fps (side-portrait scale pass): adopted 275/300 (91.7%), R2 p50 0.519 p95 0.788,
                                         cycles p50 1.82 p95 3.73, spr p50 0.126 p05 0.033
  280 @30fps (side-portrait primary):    adopted 277/300 (92.3%), R2 p50 0.522 p95 0.788,
                                         cycles p50 1.95 p95 3.81, spr p50 0.130 p05 0.037
  138 @30fps (2x control scale pass):    adopted 224/300 (74.7%)
  106 @60fps (side-landscape primary):   adopted  37/300 (12.3%) -- span too short for a cycle

WHY THE GATE DOES NOT PROTECT. verticalOscillationMinFitR2's own doc states its calibration is a
"2000-seed pure-noise floor, p95 ~ 0.22 at n=50" -- a WHITE-noise floor. Integrated white noise is
red noise (~1/f2), so its power sits in exactly the band pass 2 searches. The doc's existing warning
is about n; the regime that actually breaks it here is the FREQUENCY BAND.

NO THRESHOLD SEPARATES THEM. park-side-portrait's genuine primary detection sits inside the
red-noise distribution on every field SpectralFitSuccess reports:
  sinusoidR2      0.7561  vs noise p95 0.788   -> inside
  observedCycles  3.81    vs noise p95 3.81    -> exactly at p95
  secondPeakRatio 0.0354  vs noise p05 0.037   -> inside
Same shape as the 4K area floor (#57): the endpoints overlap, so DO NOT re-derive by picking a
cycles minimum or a higher R2 -- 33-38 of 300 pure-noise walks reach 3 cycles.

IT REACHES THE USER. verticalOscillationCm.calibrate fits a CUMULATIVE INTEGRAL of per-frame deltas
-- a random walk by construction. On park-side-portrait the background MediaPipe scale pass adopts
0.15 Hz (the grid's own bottom edge) at R2 0.398 / 1.515 cycles and reports 46.41 cm of vertical
oscillation against a 0.4938 m torso -- 0.94 torso lengths, ~5.5x the primary pixel path's implied
8.5 cm, against a 6-13 cm literature band. The A/B confirms the card renders:
evidence.clips[0].metrics.verticalOscillationCm.status moves no-evidence -> planned. The same
mechanism fires on the ffmpeg -itsscale 2 negative control's scale pass (0.31 Hz, R2 0.630, 2
strikes instead of 5), invisible there only because stepWidthCm is view-excluded on a side view.

ALSO ESTABLISHED: "observedCycles >= 1 prunes low grid points to inertness" -- the stated safety
argument for capping MAX_RETIMING_FACTOR at 8 -- is FALSE on this corpus. At 0.15 Hz over a 10.1 s
window the winner completes 1.515 cycles and clears the rule. Exposure grows with clip length; the
two short clips are safe only because their spans cannot complete a sub-floor cycle.

DIRECTIONS THAT MIGHT WORK (none measured): an F-test on the fit's 2 sinusoid degrees of freedom
against its residual DoF -- the n-invariant upgrade verticalOscillationMinFitR2's own doc already
names, and which would replace both that key and cadenceMinFitR2 together; a red-noise (AR(1)) null
model instead of a trend-only baseline; cross-validating the primary and scale passes' independent
series against each other, since on park-side-portrait they disagree 0.39 Hz vs 0.15 Hz while a
genuine rhythm should be common to both; or not extending the two-pass to the metre series at all,
which sacrifices the family-coherence property the change was designed around.

The behaviour is pinned executably by a deliberately-failing-when-fixed test in
src/heuristics/bounceSpectrum.test.ts ("KNOWN DEFECT: a rhythmless random walk is adopted as a
sub-floor rhythm"). Full tables:
openspec/changes/detect-retimed-clips-below-the-gait-floor/design.md D4.
acceptance_criteria: A rhythmless random walk is adopted as a sub-floor rhythm on a rate consistent with the gate's stated false-positive budget rather than on 75-92% of seeds, WITHOUT losing the genuine 0.39 Hz detection on park-side-portrait.mp4; and the background scale pass on that clip no longer reports 46.4 cm of vertical oscillation. Or: the direction is measured to be unsalvageable and recorded as such, the way #57 closed the 4K area floor.
notes:
2026-09-09 — MEASURED. The cheap fix (confine the two-pass to the pixel path, since only the metre
series is a cumulative integral) is REFUTED. Both series are red; the colour gap between the two
consumers is too small to build a fix on.

AR(1) phi and log-log spectral slope, after stripping BOTH the quadratic trend and the winning
sinusoid(s) — one trial per clip, fresh Chromium, real GPU, identity-verified server:

  clip             series            n    span    phi      slope
  side-landscape   hip (PRIMARY)     106  1.75s   0.8073   -1.460
  side-portrait    hip (PRIMARY)     280  9.77s   0.9358   -1.485
  front-approach   hip (PRIMARY)      99  1.64s   0.7954   -1.544
  side-portrait    cm (integral)     288  10.10s  0.9800   -1.332

  CONTROLS, same timestamps, same detrend, rhythm-free by construction:
  white noise                                -0.15..-0.28   +0.22..+0.62
  random walk                                 0.861..0.955  -1.69..-1.78

The primary hip series sits ON the random-walk control, not the white one, on all three clips.
The hypothesis that fitSpectralSinusoid's c + d*t + e*t^2 trend terms whiten hip position is
refuted outright.

⚠️ NAIVE MEASUREMENT IS CONFOUNDED — do not repeat it. Quadratic detrend ALONE gives phi 0.88-0.98
on every series, but at 60 fps a clean 2.9 Hz sinusoid by itself produces lag-1 ~0.95. The rhythm
must be removed before the colour is measurable.

FALSE-POSITIVE RATE on real footage, surrogates resampled onto the original timestamps and run
through the real fitBounceSpectrum:
  side-portrait primary, phase-surrogate (colour preserved)   93/200 = 46.5%
  side-portrait primary, shuffled (whitened, same values)      0/300 =  0.0%
  side-portrait primary, synthetic random walk               269/300 = 89.7%
The whole effect is temporal correlation; nothing else.

CORROBORATED THREE WAYS, so this is not a simulation artifact:
1. Direct refit of the sub-floor band on side-portrait's REAL primary residual, trend and genuine
   0.39 Hz rhythm both removed -> f = 0.150 Hz, R^2 = 0.5682. Clears the 0.30 gate by 0.27.
2. Adopted-frequency histogram over the 93 adoptions: 0.15:19 0.17:24 0.19:33 0.21:11 0.23:5 0.57:1.
   ZERO of 93 land within +/-0.04 Hz of the real 0.39 Hz. They pile at the grid floor.
3. The SHIPPED pipeline already falls for it on real footage: side-portrait's scale-pass hip
   POSITION series (not the integral) adopts 0.150 Hz at R^2 0.3981 against a keyframe ground
   truth of 0.40 Hz.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO strides-b4f's RECORD:
- The 75-92% figure is a LONG-CLIP rate. The same synthetic random walk reads 12.0% on
  side-landscape (1.75s) and 4.0% on front-approach (1.63s). 20-32% of short-clip trials are killed
  by insufficient-cycles, NOT by the R^2 gate — a clip shorter than 1/0.15 = 6.67s structurally
  cannot reach the sub-floor grid. So the two short clips are protected by SPAN, and any A/B that
  reads only side-landscape and front-approach reads green straight through this defect.
- Being less red is not safer at short span: front-approach's real residual adopts at 14.5% where a
  pure random walk adopts at 4.0%, because an extreme red winner self-rejects at the grid floor.

AN F-TEST DOES NOT FIX THIS. Against a random walk a low-frequency sinusoid genuinely explains large
variance, so the F statistic is large too. An F-test fixes the gate's n-dependence, not its
noise-colour assumption. Removed from the candidate list.

CROSS-PASS AGREEMENT IS NOT A VALIDATOR EITHER. Per-clip winners
(primary / scale-pass hip / scale-pass cm): side-landscape 2.900/2.880/2.880; side-portrait
0.390/0.150/0.150; front-approach 3.020/3.140/3.120. The cm integral agrees with ITS OWN pass's hip
series to within one grid step everywhere, so the disagreement is between PASSES, not between the
two series' colour. On the only clip with a genuine retiming it would reject the CORRECT detection
along with the wrong one, because the pass that fell for the noise casts the second vote. It is a
disagreement flag, not a validator.

REMAINING DIRECTION: an AR(1) red-noise null. Estimate phi from the residual, build the theoretical
AR(1) spectrum, require the peak to clear that null rather than a fixed R^2. Standard practice in
spectral analysis; the 95% level is conventional rather than tuned. It should discriminate here by
construction: the null is HIGHER at 0.15 Hz than at 0.39 Hz (~1/f^2), so the genuine peak faces a
LOWER bar than the grid-floor pile-up.

SCOPE IT TO THE SUB-FLOOR ADOPTION DECISION ONLY. In-band behaviour then stays bit-identical and
cadenceMinFitR2 / verticalOscillationMinFitR2 are untouched, holding blast radius at zero for the
two clips that work today.

WHAT COULD NOT BE MEASURED: there is no long clip in the corpus WITHOUT a genuine sub-floor rhythm,
so the direct experiment ('a normal 10s clip adopts noise X% of the time') is unavailable. The 46.5%
is measured on side-portrait's residual after removing its real rhythm — the best available proxy,
corroborated three ways, but not the same experiment.

2026-09-09 FIXED on worktree-agent-aaeb4382f5af42645 (d1386c1 + 7e19a39, base 14b438d).

THE FIX: src/heuristics/redNoiseNull.ts. Sub-floor adoption now requires the family gate AND
significance against an AR(1) red-noise null fitted to the sub-floor band's OWN periodogram, at a
conventional 95%. AR(1) shape by a robust L1-in-log scan over phi; level by the median of the
flattened values; chi2_2 quantile corrected for the INDEPENDENT frequencies the span resolves
(bandwidth x span). spectralFit.ts gains fitSpectralSinusoidWithBandPower, which hands back the
grid search's periodogram; fitSpectralSinusoid is a thin wrapper and its return object is unchanged.

RATES through the shipped fitBounceSpectrum, 300 seeds each, before -> after:
  random walk 288@30fps  91.7% -> 4.3%
  random walk 280@30fps  92.3% -> 5.7%
  random walk 138@30fps  74.7% -> 3.7%
  random walk 106@60fps  12.3% -> 0.0%
  colour sweep phi 0/0.3/0.6/0.9/0.99: 0/0/0/33.3/91.0% -> 0/0/0/4.0/6.0%
The after column sits at the 5% the null is stated at, across the whole colour range.

GENUINE DETECTION SURVIVES. side-portrait unchanged from a96bffa on every metric: overstriding
0.478109 @ 1.0, footStrikePattern 0.0972584 @ 1.0 (sampleSize 4), verticalOscillation 0.171343 @
0.907373, verticalRatio 0.0299206 @ 0.604915, cadence null with the retiming caveat.
verticalOscillationCm is the ONLY thing that moved: scale-pass 46.41 cm -> null (fitFailureReason
below-quality-gate), evidence status planned -> no-evidence. torsoMeters 0.4938,
medianPixelsPerMeter 205.1, scaleCoverage 0.931 unchanged -- the scale is still measured, only the
noise fit is refused.

BLAST RADIUS ZERO. side-landscape identical on all 183 fields and front-approach on all 167,
against base 14b438d AND against a96bffa; md5 of the elapsedMs-stripped report sections identical
on all three commits. ffmpeg -itsscale 2 negative control bit-identical to base: cadence 87.6 @
0.9056, no retiming caveat.

0.95 NOT TUNED -- the literature's conventional level, fixed before the genuine detection was
tested, which clears it by 3-15x. No second constant; verticalOscillationMinFitR2 and
cadenceMinFitR2 untouched; pass 1 never consults the null.

THE THEORETICAL VARIANCE-NORMALIZED NULL DOES NOT WORK HERE, and that is the one thing worth not
re-deriving: it ties the null's level to the series' TOTAL variance, and fitSpectralSinusoid's own
c+d*t+e*t^2 detrend guts the f->0 end that dominates a red series' variance. Measured: 33.7% of
random walks still adopted. Estimating the level from the band itself (Mann & Lees' robust
background) takes it to 3.5%. Same reason phi is read off the SPECTRUM, not off a residual.

Gates: tsc clean, eslint clean, vitest 1540 passed (baseline 1527, +13), openspec 10/10 strict.

2026-09-09 — CORRECTION (repair round). One claim in this bead's DESCRIPTION is UNVERIFIED and
should not be read as measured fact: "The same mechanism fires on the ffmpeg -itsscale 2 negative
control's scale pass (0.31 Hz, R^2 0.630, 2 strikes instead of 5)", attributed to a96bffa.

Why it is unverified: a96bffa was never re-run on that control. The live verification drove the
control at base (14b438d) and at d1386c1 only, and both landed in-band at 1.44 Hz — which is the
expected outcome either way and therefore tests nothing about what the pre-null commit did on that
clip's scale pass. The claim also contradicts a96bffa's own design table (D5), which recorded that
control as bit-identical to baseline on every user-visible value.

It is left in place rather than deleted because it was written in good faith and may well be true;
it simply has no measurement behind it. Nothing about the merge decision turns on it: the shipped
null refuses that scale pass's sub-floor fit regardless, and the control is bit-identical to
baseline on every captured field on the shipped commit (design.md D8.5).

Closing it properly would mean checking out a96bffa and driving the -itsscale 2 control through the
Upload tab while capturing the [analysis-diagnostics:scale-pass] line — ~10 minutes of harness time
that buys only a historical detail.

title: Detect retimed (slow-motion) clips and recover their footstrike timing
description:
Enables the whole vertical-oscillation family, cadence and correct footstrike timing on retimed footage, and fixes actively-wrong output on park-side-portrait.mp4.

PROBLEM. park-side-portrait.mp4 is ~7-8x slow motion. Its on-screen step frequency is ~0.43 Hz
(~26 spm) against spectralFitMinFrequencyHz = 1.2, so the shared hip-bounce fit finds no candidate,
sinusoidR2 collapses to ~0.005-0.05, and cadenceMinFitR2/verticalOscillationMinFitR2 (0.30)
correctly reject it. Diagnosed under strides-aha; the gate is behaving correctly.

THE DAMAGE IS NOT JUST MISSING DATA. Because the fit fails, footstrikes.ts:253 routes to the
ankle-difference FALLBACK detector, which reports 13 strikes over a window that physically contains
4-5. overstriding (-0.008) and footStrikePattern (-0.240) on that clip are computed from those wrong
instants AT CONFIDENCE 1.0 and are fused into the panel. MAD 0.4516 vs side-landscape's 0.1238.
This is the mechanism behind the strides-5hj P1 cross-clip disagreement.

THIS IS A REAL-USER FEATURE, NOT DEMO HOUSEKEEPING. iOS renders slow motion when a clip leaves
Photos, so an upload from the camera roll arrives with the retiming BAKED INTO stts: 30 fps nominal,
unity-rate elst, stretchFactor 1.00003, no capture rate anywhere. Confirmed on all three demo clips
(TAG:encoder=Lavc62.28.100 libx264, handler_name=Core Media Video, zero com.apple.quicktime tags).
CONSEQUENCE: detectSlowMotion's existing container predicate (nominalFps >= 100) STRUCTURALLY CANNOT
FIRE on real user input. It is already in src/ with zero callers; CLAUDE.md's 'spike-branch only'
note is stale. Content-side detection is the only mechanism that can ever work here.
The in-app recording path (getUserMedia, WebcamCapture.tsx:142) cannot produce slow motion at all.

THE KEY ASYMMETRY - only cadence needs the slowdown factor. Verified against the metric modules:
cadence is the only MetricId whose value is a rate (stepsPerMinute). overstriding, footStrikePattern,
stepWidth, trunkLean, kneeFlexion, kneeDrive are spatial and measured AT an instant;
verticalOscillation and armSwingAmplitude are unit:'ratio'; verticalOscillationCm and stepWidthCm are
distances; verticalRatio uses fit.frequencyHz only for a gate, not its value. So correcting the fit
fixes contact timing and every spatial metric with NO factor required, on any device.

SCOPE (option A, agreed with the user 2026-09-09):
1. Two-pass fit. Normal band first; ONLY on failure retry on a widened diagnostic grid. A confident
   fit below the human running floor (~2 Hz) means the clip is retimed. Self-limiting by
   construction: the wide grid is never consulted for a clip whose normal fit succeeds, so the two
   working clips cannot be destabilised.
2. Publish every factor-independent metric normally on a detected clip. This is what converts
   park-side-portrait from actively wrong to correct.
3. Withhold cadence alone, with a reason naming the retiming. No factor needed on any device.

OUT OF SCOPE, deliberately: inferring the factor to report cadence (strides-yg8-style follow-up;
candidate route is peak ankle-relative-to-hip velocity in torso-lengths/sec, which scales exactly
with k through an observable that is NOT cadence, cross-checked against the discrete capture-rate set
4/8/16/32); asking the user to confirm the speed; motion-blur-vs-displacement detection.

DO NOT widen the shipped band globally. Measured under strides-aha: with the floor at 0.30 Hz this
clip resolves cadence ~26 spm at R^2 ~0.95 - a confidently-displayed wrong number replacing an honest
null, and it would silence verticalOscillationCm's fit.frequencyHz x 60 == cadence.value tripwire by
making it agree with the wrong answer. Do not touch cadenceMinFitR2 or verticalOscillationMinFitR2.

VALIDATION, buildable with no new footage - note plain 'ffmpeg -itsscale 8' gives a 7.5 fps file,
which is NOT the iOS shape; the correct formula is -itsscale (source_fps / 30), verified to yield
r_frame_rate=30/1:
  negative control  ffmpeg -itsscale 2 on park-side-landscape (60fps) -> 30fps, 2x slow, 87 spm,
                    still in band. Detector MUST NOT fire. Real footage, container-faithful.
  positive, exact   syntheticGait.ts at a sub-floor frequency on a 30 fps lattice. Known truth.
  positive, real    park-side-portrait.mp4.

BLAST RADIUS. On the detected clip this flips detectFootstrikes from the fallback to the bounce-phase
path, moving overstriding, footStrikePattern, stepWidth, stepWidthCm and transitively verticalRatio,
plus every evidence.* exemplar those emit. Needs a full three-clip --evidence A/B; the other two
clips must be bit-identical outside elapsedMs.

FIDELITY UPSIDE. At ~8x, each playback frame is ~4 ms of real time against ~16.7 ms on the 60 fps
clips - 4x finer resolution on the contact instant. Relevant to the standing +0.11 s footstrike lag
(strides-24s closed after three correction strategies failed; strides-pr1 shipped a disclosing
caveat). A correctly-handled retimed clip is plausibly the best instrument in the corpus for that.
acceptance_criteria: On park-side-portrait.mp4 the hip-bounce fit resolves via the two-pass path and detectFootstrikes uses the bounce-phase detector rather than the ankle-difference fallback, yielding a strike count consistent with the 4-5 contacts the footage physically contains rather than 13. Every factor-independent metric publishes; cadence alone is withheld with a reason naming the retiming. The ffmpeg -itsscale 2 negative control does NOT trigger detection. A three-clip --evidence A/B shows side-landscape and front-approach bit-identical outside elapsedMs.
notes:
2026-09-09 implementation + verification (agent worktree agent-aaeb4382f5af42645, branch worktree-agent-aaeb4382f5af42645, base 14b438d). PRIMARY PATH WORKS AND IS VERIFIED: park-side-portrait pass 1 fits 1.24 Hz @ R2 0.0231, pass 2 fits 0.39 Hz @ R2 0.7561 (secondPeakRatio 0.0354, 3.81 cycles) against a keyframe-derived ground truth of 0.40 Hz (contacts 1.4/3.9/6.4/8.9 s, uniform 2.5 s, FOUR contacts). detectFootstrikes flips ankle-fallback -> phase, 13 strikes -> 4, alternating L/R/L/R, uniformly 2.567 s apart, attributeSides evidence -322.12 (not close to a tie). overstriding -0.008 -> +0.478, footStrikePattern -0.240 -> +0.097, verticalOscillation null -> 0.171 @ 0.907, verticalRatio null -> 0.0299 @ 0.605, cadence stays null with the retiming caveat. side-landscape and front-approach 0 fields moved outside elapsedMs (two instruments). ffmpeg -itsscale 2 negative control bit-identical to baseline, cadence 87.6 spm, detector does not fire. Q1 ANSWERED: side-portrait DOES carry real-world scale (torsoMeters 0.4938, medianPixelsPerMeter 205.1, scaleCoverage 0.93) -- only the fit failed.

BLOCKED, do not merge: strides-mc1. The sub-floor band is where RED noise lives and the gate it reuses is a WHITE-noise calibration -- a rhythmless random walk is adopted on 75-92% of 300 seeds at this corpus's sample counts, and on real footage park-side-portrait's background MediaPipe scale pass adopts 0.15 Hz @ R2 0.398 and would render 46.4 cm of vertical oscillation against a 0.494 m torso (the A/B confirms the card renders). No threshold on any SpectralFitSuccess field separates the genuine detection from noise -- it sits at the noise p95 on all three. Full tables: openspec/changes/detect-retimed-clips-below-the-gait-floor/design.md D4.

sample count, and stays at the null's 5% across a colour sweep from white to phi=0.99 where it
previously climbed to 91%. park-side-portrait's genuine 0.39 Hz detection is untouched to every

evidence status planned -> no-evidence). side-landscape and front-approach identical on all
183/167 fields against base 14b438d, md5-confirmed; ffmpeg -itsscale 2 negative control
bit-identical to base at cadence 87.6 @ 0.9056 with no retiming caveat.

  overstriding        -0.008 @ 1.0 (WRONG, from phantom strikes) -> +0.478109 @ 1.0
  footStrikePattern   -0.240 -> +0.0972584
  verticalOscillation null -> 0.171343 @ 0.907
  verticalRatio       null -> 0.0299206 @ 0.605
  cadence             null, now with the retiming caveat rather than 'too irregular'

BLAST RADIUS ZERO ON WORKING CLIPS. side-landscape 183/183 and front-approach 167/167 fields
identical to base 14b438d; section md5s equal across all three commits. Structural, not lucky: pass
1 clears the gate there so pass 2 is never formed. The -itsscale 2 negative control (real footage,
30fps, 87 spm, in-band) is bit-identical and the detector stays silent.

THE HARD PART WAS strides-mc1. The sub-floor band is where RED noise concentrates power and the gate
reused there is a WHITE-noise calibration. Rhythmless real series were adopted on 46.5% of
colour-preserving surrogates vs 0.0% whitened; the scale pass rendered 46.4 cm of vertical
oscillation against a 0.49 m torso. Fixed with an AR(1) red-noise null (Gilman 1963, Mann & Lees
1996, Torrence & Compo 1998) at the conventional 0.95, scoped to sub-floor adoption only.
Rhythmless adoption 91.7% -> 4.3%, flat at the nominal 5% across phi in {0,0.3,0.6,0.9,0.99}, while
the genuine detection clears by 3-15x and is unchanged to every digit.

THE R^2 GATE WAS KEPT ALONGSIDE THE NULL, against the implementation brief, and review proved that
was right: on the RED side the null does 100% of the discriminating, but on white/pink the null
OVER-fires at 2-2.6x nominal and R^2 is the only thing holding the line. Dropping it as instructed
would have raised false positives from ~0% to 10-13% on low-phi series.

MATHS INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED IN REVIEW: Poisson-kernel normalization 1.00000000 by 2e6-point
quadrature for every phi; pointwise chi-squared-2 calibration across 15,000 simulated fits through
the real fit; independent-frequency count = the exact Rayleigh count; PHI_MAX/PHI_GRID_STEP shown to
be numerics by manipulation (<=0.3pp).

KNOWN AND DISCLOSED, not defects: a ~5% residual IS the 95% level and exposure grows with clip
length; per-clip multiplicity exceeds 5% because verticalOscillationCm.calibrate fits once per
integration run; the declared reach to 0.15 Hz is NOMINAL - power collapses below ~0.25 Hz, though a
150-240 spm runner at 8x lands at 0.31-0.5 Hz in the 95-100% band; armSwingAmplitude stays null on a
retimed clip since armSwing.ts fits the shipped band directly. All recorded in design.md D8.

1541 tests, tsc clean, lint clean, openspec 10/10.

title: Chromium's currentTime is on the MEDIA clock on park-side-landscape — the evidence seek's edit-list term may be wrong
description:
Measured 2026-09-05 while implementing strides-5t4 (seek to the frame midpoint). evidenceSeekOffset.ts subtracts the container's elst media_time from every evidence seek, on the premise that HTMLVideoElement.currentTime is edit-list-adjusted while the WebCodecs robustFrames[].timestamp is raw media time. On src/video/demo-clips/park-side-landscape.mp4 that premise does not hold.

EVIDENCE (fresh headless Chromium, real GPU, identity-verified dev server):
1. video.duration reads 3.883333 = 233/60, the FULL media duration - not 3.884, the elst segment_duration/1000. If the edit list were applied and the first two frames trimmed, duration would be the latter.
2. A PURE Chromium seek, no app code at all, to currentTime = 2.0 draws media frame 120 (PSNR argmax 21.345 dB, clean unimodal peak, runner-up 119 at 20.195). The edit-list-applied model predicts media frame 122.
3. Both app footStrikePattern evidence images corroborate: seeking 3.049999666666667 drew media frame 182 = floor(3.049999 * 60) exactly, and 3.399999666666667 drew 203. The edit-list-applied model predicts 184 and 205.

CONSEQUENCE: the -512/15360 term moves this clip's evidence seek TWO FRAMES EARLY. After strides-5t4's midpoint the drawn frame is 2 frames from the instant the metric actually measured, not 0.

WHY THIS IS NOT A CONTRADICTION OF THE ORIGINAL #69/#68 MEASUREMENT: that +2-frame drift was ground-truthed on the retired Pexels Demo 1 clip and on e2e/fixtures/multiperson-track.mp4. multiperson-track.mp4 and park-side-landscape.mp4 are DIFFERENT FILES on an identical timing lattice (md5 5da45ab1fbc9d4af89e7d6d7a9416d73 vs 106dcee831466d7e5a38e606043b3ffa; both 15360 timescale, elst media_time 512, 60 fps, 233 frames, identical stretchFactor). A reading on one is not a reading on the other, and nobody has measured park-side-landscape's offset directly until now.

WHAT TO DO: re-measure the seek offset per clip across the whole corpus with the pure-Chromium probe (seek to a known currentTime, PSNR the drawn frame against ffmpeg-reconstructed candidates - note ffmpeg does NOT apply the edit list, -ignore_editlist 1 changes nothing, so its select='eq(n,N)' index IS the media frame index). Determine whether Chromium's edit-list handling varies by file, by codec/container detail, or whether the original measurement was misindexed. Then decide whether editListSeekOffsetSeconds should stay, narrow, or go.

DOES NOT BLOCK strides-5t4: the midpoint's effect is +1 frame regardless of what the offset is, the two terms are independent by construction (separate fields, separate derivation, separate override), and the frame the midpoint now lands on is the keyframe-confirmed first-contact frame. Fixing the offset later composes cleanly.
notes:
2026-09-05, added by the strides-5t4 review pass.

IF THIS TICKET LANDS, strides-5t4's ACCEPTANCE CRITERION GOES STALE - do not read the
change as a regression when it does.

strides-5t4's criterion is 'both footStrikePattern cards draw frames 183 and 204 on
park-side-landscape.mp4', and that is met TODAY partly because the edit-list term shifts
the seek back two frames. If this ticket correctly zeroes that term, the drawn frames
become 185 and 206. That will read as a regression against 5t4's own wording and will not
be one.

The durable statement is 5t4's design.md D9: 'the drawn frame is two frames from the
instant the metric measured'. Zeroing the term takes that to zero. The remaining residual
after that is the footstrike sampling-instant lag (strides-pr1, shipped as a caveat rather
than a correction), which is a different quantity and is not this ticket's to fix.
RESOLVED 2026-09-06 — REFUTED. editListSeekOffsetSeconds is CORRECT on all four clips and STAYS unchanged. The report was a frame-numbering error, not a behaviour.

MEASUREMENT: 31 pure-Chromium seeks (no app, no dev server), 4 clips, PSNR argmax against ffmpeg-reconstructed candidates. Targets were frame-interval midpoints under each model, so the two predictions sit exactly 2 frames apart; >=1 whole-microsecond and >=1 non-whole-microsecond target per clip. 30/31 matched the edit-list-applied model exactly; the 31st is a deliberate frame-BOUNDARY target (121/60, read back 2.016665) that landed one frame low on the known microsecond truncation. NOT ONE matched the media-clock model.

ROOT CAUSE: ffmpeg's select='eq(n,N)' indexes CODED PICTURES, not timeline slots. On all four clips the lowest sample composition timestamp equals the elst media_time exactly (512/1024/2002/512) — the ordinary ctts B-frame priming edit, which discards no picture. So ffmpeg frame N sits at composition time (media_time + N*delta)/timescale, not N*delta/timescale. Counting media_time as trimmed frames mis-numbers every picture by exactly the quantity in dispute, so a correct conversion reads as a 2-frame error the other way.

Re-indexed, this ticket's own three readings CONFIRM the term: currentTime=2.0 -> edit-list model predicts 120 (not 122), measured 120; the two app seeks predict 182 and 203, measured 182 and 203.

NON-DISCRIMINATORS (do not re-derive): video.duration cannot decide this — the edit segment spans the whole media, so 3.884 is just 3883.33ms rounded into the 1000Hz movie timescale and both models predict 3.883333. And '-ignore_editlist 1 changes nothing' is not evidence ffmpeg ignores the edit list: it does shift packet PTS (first packet 0 vs 512) then re-bases output start time either way, so select='eq(n,183)' reports pts_time 3.05 in both modes — that is frame 183's PRESENTATION time; its composition time is 3.083333, which is what the sampler reports.

BY FILE / BY CONTAINER DETAIL / MISINDEXED? -> MISINDEXED. park-side-landscape and multiperson-track (controlled pair, identical lattice, different files) agree on every shared target; so do the 60000-timescale and variable-rate clips.

strides-5t4's acceptance criterion (frames 183 and 204) is CONFIRMED, not stale. Its design D9 claim 'the drawn frame is two frames from the instant the metric measured' is WITHDRAWN — the residual is zero. Looked at the frames: 183/204 are touchdown, 185/206 (what removing the term would draw) are mid-stance.

Shipped: openspec change 'pin-the-evidence-seek-clock-conversion' (one ADDED results-view requirement), evidenceSeekOffset.ts doc correction (comment-only, no behaviour), CLAUDE.md resolution, correction note beside 5t4's D9. A/B: no metrics./sampling./personSelection./view./evidence. field moved.
close_reason:
REFUTED by measurement. The edit-list term is CORRECT on every clip and stays unchanged. The report was a frame-numbering error, not a behaviour.

31 pure-Chromium seeks (no app, no dev server), 4 clips, PSNR argmax against ffmpeg-reconstructed
candidates, with targets placed at frame-interval midpoints under each model so the two predictions
sit exactly two frames apart, and at least one whole-microsecond and one non-whole-microsecond
target per clip. 30 of 31 matched the edit-list-applied model exactly; the 31st was a deliberate
frame BOUNDARY target that landed one frame low on the already-known microsecond truncation. NOT ONE
matched the media-clock model.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE FALSE REPORT: ffmpeg's select='eq(n,N)' indexes CODED PICTURES, and on all four
clips the lowest sample composition timestamp equals the elst media_time exactly (512 / 1024 / 2002
/ 512) - the ordinary ctts B-frame priming edit, which DISCARDS NO PICTURE. So ffmpeg frame N sits
at composition time (media_time + N*delta)/timescale, not N*delta/timescale. Counting media_time as
trimmed frames mis-numbers every picture by exactly the quantity being converted, so a correct
conversion reads as a two-frame error in the opposite direction. Re-indexed, the bead's own three
readings confirm the term rather than refute it.

'By file, by container detail, or misindexed?' - MISINDEXED. park-side-landscape and
multiperson-track are the controlled pair (different footage, identical 15360/512 lattice) and agree
on every shared target, as do the 60000-timescale clip and the VFR one.

CONSEQUENCE FOR strides-5t4: its acceptance criterion does NOT go stale. Frames 183/204 stand, and
the note I added here on 2026-09-05 warning they would become 185/206 is withdrawn - it was
predicated on this bead being correct.

SHIPPED, despite no behaviour change: openspec change pin-the-evidence-seek-clock-conversion adding
'An evidence seek converts the sampled timestamp onto the presentation clock'. The conversion had no
requirement of its own and the midpoint requirement forward-referenced one that did not exist -
which is how an unpinned load-bearing fact got a P1 filed against working code. Plus a doc
correction in evidenceSeekOffset.ts: the module called the edit-list shape a 'trim', which is the
wrong mental model and the one that produced this report.

Gates: tsc clean, lint clean, 1511 tests, A/B elapsedMs-only (correct - no behaviour changed).

title: multiperson loses cadence/verticalOscillation/verticalRatio at the fresh operating point, and 174 spm was CORRECT
description:
Measured 2026-09-04 settling strides-je4.

GROUND TRUTH, hand-measured on e2e/fixtures/multiperson-track.mp4 (60.000fps, static camera):
volt-shoe colour tracking + connected components over the whole clip; stance = the shoe blob whose
x is stationary while the body advances 14.7 px/frame. Stance plateaus at x = 1588 (f99-109),
1278 (f120-130), 971 (f141-150), 657 (f162-171), 337 (f183-194), ~30 (f204-215).
Contact ONSETS: frames 100, 120, 141, 162, 183, 204 -> intervals 20, 21, 21, 21, 21.
Cadence = 3600 / 20.8 = 173.1 spm; +/-2 frames on each endpoint gives 166.7-180.0 spm.
Independent cross-check: contact-to-contact x spacing 310/307/314/320/307 px (mean 311.6) divided
by body speed 14.7 px/frame = 21.2 frames per step. Agrees.

So the PRE-FIX arm's cadence 174 spm is right to 0.5%. carry-exact-decoded-frame-timestamps
turns it into null (frameCoverage 0, sampleSize 0), along with verticalOscillation 0.2196 and
verticalRatio 0.0348. All three had viewFit primary, so pre-fix they render as CAVEATED cards
(confidence 0.0196, 'Low confidence'); post-fix they render as EXCLUDED. That is user-visible.

BUT THE FIX IS NOT WHAT BREAKS THEM. A --reuse-browser control on the PRE-FIX commit (cee2706),
5 trials, multiperson first: trial 1 (cold) = detected 103, cadence 174, segmentCount 3;
trials 2-5 (warm) = detected 127, cadence NULL, segmentCount 2, verticalOscillation NULL,
verticalRatio NULL. So the pre-fix build already loses all three on 4 of 5 warm trials, and
CLAUDE.md says a real user's browser is warm. The fix moves the fresh regime onto that same
operating point.

STILL OPEN: why does the hip-bounce fit fail with MORE frames? Post-fix the winning segment gains
frames 99-127 at clip-open (start 2.133 -> 1.65 s), where the runner is entering frame. Untested
hypothesis: those 29 frames drag sinusoidR2 below cadenceMinFitR2. Not measured - would need a
probe on the fit, or a personSelection window override.

ALSO NOTED, same run: post-fix multiperson footStrikePattern reports confidence 1.0 from
sampleSize 9, but the ground truth above has only ~6 contacts inside the winner's window
(app 1.65-3.9 s). The ankle-difference fallback over-triggers (the hip fit failed, so it is the
fallback that ran). Pre-fix reported 4 against ~5 in its shorter window. Neither is clean, and the
value flips sign 0.1117 -> -0.1739 with confidence rising 0.8 -> 1.0.
notes: 2026-09-05: the change that SURFACED this (carry-exact-decoded-frame-timestamps) has been backed out, but this bug is NOT withdrawn and is not caused by it. The confound test proved the pre-fix build already loses these three metrics on 4 of 5 --reuse-browser trials: cold trial 1 reads detectedFrames 103 with cadence 174, warm trials 2-5 read 127 with cadence/verticalOscillation/verticalRatio all null. CLAUDE.md's own Determinism section records the same split and states a real user's browser is warm — so a real user is ALREADY getting the null. The hand-measured ground truth (173.1 spm, range 166.7-180.0, from shoe-colour tracking over all 233 frames with contact onsets at frames 100/120/141/162/183/204) stands on its own and is the durable value here: it says 174 was CORRECT, so the warm-regime null is a genuine loss of a genuine number. Untested hypothesis for why more frames make the hip-bounce fit WORSE: the added clip-open frames drag sinusoidR2 below cadenceMinFitR2.

title: Decide whether carry-exact-decoded-frame-timestamps' 340-line metric movement is acceptable
description:
STOP CONDITION from strides-e6y's pre-registered A/B gate, 2026-09-04. Needs a human decision before carry-exact-decoded-frame-timestamps merges.

The gate said: every metrics.* row identical at 6 significant figures, every sampling.*/personSelection.*/view.* row exactly identical, no change in which exemplars are planned; a 6th-digit flip on the VO family only was allowed. It was written on the premise that '333ns cannot move a spectral fit'.

MEASURED: scripts/ab-person-selection.mjs --arm 'base={}' --clips demo1,demo2,multiperson --trials 2 --evidence, fresh process per trial, real GPU, identity-verified server. before vs after diffs on 340 LINES. Examples: multiperson sampling.detectedFrames 103 -> 136, personSelection.segmentCount 3 -> 2, rejectedOtherSegment 74 -> 45, cadence/verticalOscillation/verticalRatio non-null -> NULL; demo2 kneeFlexion 106.103 -> 162.269, cadence 181.2 -> 182.4. Exemplar selection moves on every clip.

THE INSTRUMENT AND THE RESTRUCTURING ARE BOTH EXONERATED by a three-way control:
  pre-fix vs pre-fix (40 min apart):                12 lines, elapsedMs only
  post-fix vs post-fix:                             20 lines, elapsedMs only
  helper NEUTRALISED to return the old lossy value, new imports + mediaTimescaleHz field retained, vs pre-fix:  12 lines, elapsedMs only
  that same tree vs the real helper (timestamp VALUES the only difference):  340 lines
So the movement is caused purely by the <=500ns correction.

MECHANISM: timestamps do not only feed least-squares fits, they feed DISCRETE GATES. movenet.ts:954 passes timestampSec*1000 into the detector; its person-of-interest continuity check (movenet.ts:1011) bounds a speed = distance / gap-since-previous-committed-call; retroactivePersonSelection gates on maxContinuityGapSeconds / maxCenterSpeedSidesPerSecond; TF.js's keypoint smoothing filter derives its alpha from dt. Each is continuous in dt but decides something discrete, so a nanosecond-scale change flips frames sitting near a threshold and the track re-partitions.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: which arm is more CORRECT. The new timestamps are provably exact (bit-identical to mp4Demux's own cts/timescale over every sample of park-approach.mp4). That makes the post-fix arm the one with correct inputs, but nobody has checked whether e.g. multiperson losing cadence entirely is an improvement or a regression. That is the decision.

OPTIONS: (a) accept, on the grounds that exact inputs are correct by construction and the gate's premise was simply wrong; (b) accept but re-baseline every expected value CLAUDE.md records; (c) investigate the multiperson cadence -> null case specifically before merging.

Evidence files were written to a scratchpad and are not preserved; re-run the A/B to reproduce.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-09-04 by a dedicated measurement session. Decision still HUMAN — nothing closed here.

METHOD. Both arms inside the worktree only (HEAD 5a290fc vs HEAD~1 cee2706, identical otherwise),
worktree's own derived port 5331, dev server started and identity-verified by each run, fresh
Chromium per trial, real GPU (ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro). Rules pre-registered in writing
before any measurement. rtk proxy diff reproduced the 340 diff lines EXACTLY.

WHERE THE 340 LINES LIVE: 125 moved fields — demo1 ZERO, demo2 30, multiperson 95. The fix is a
bit-identical NO-OP on the side-view reference clip, every metric and every evidence field.

Q1 kneeFlexion demo2 106.103 -> 162.269: CANNOT SEPARATE by hand measurement (pre-registered
threshold: needed better than +/-28 deg; the swing-leg ankle is occluded at peak flexion on this
front view and thigh/shin project to only ~80-120 px, giving ~+/-39 deg). Auxiliary evidence is
decisive about what it is NOT: both arms carry viewFit 'unsuitable' -> metricTier 'excluded', so
neither number is ever rendered. And the instability is PRE-EXISTING — on cee2706 alone, toggling
the tracking crop moves it 106.103 -> 177.686. Value tracks interpolatedFraction monotonically
(0.667->106, 0.5->103, 0.286->162, 0.200->178). Full mechanism recorded on strides-90l.

Q2 multiperson cadence 174 -> null: PRE-FIX FAVOURED. Hand-counted footfalls (volt-shoe tracking;
onsets at frames 100/120/141/162/183/204, intervals 20/21/21/21/21) give 173.1 spm, range
166.7-180.0. 174 is correct to 0.5%. Filed as strides-e45 with the caveat below.

Q3 multiperson detectedFrames 103 -> 136: POST-FIX FAVOURED, all three pre-registered conditions
met. The winner's span moves 2.133-3.9 -> 1.65-3.9 s, i.e. it GAINS frames 99-127. Keyframes at
frames 90/96/102/108/114/120/126/132 and full frames at 100 and 128 show the runner fully visible,
unoccluded, large, in clean side profile throughout — the pre-fix arm was discarding 29 real
frames. Not a stitched bystander: segments[0].medianAreaPx 29883.1 -> 30592.1 (+2.4%, gate was
<25%), separationRatio 17.98 -> 33.60 (rises), and the only other near-field person is the walker
parked at x~150 while the runner is at x 1200-1700. Downstream: trunkLean sampleSize 107 -> 136
with interpolatedFraction 0.0748 -> 0.0368.

CONFOUND TEST — the decisive result. --reuse-browser on the PRE-FIX arm, multiperson, 5 trials:
  trial 1 (cold): detected 103, cadence 174,  segmentCount 3, seg0 101 frames from 2.133
  trials 2-5 (warm): detected 127, cadence NULL, segmentCount 2, seg0 123 frames from 1.75,
                     verticalOscillation NULL, verticalRatio NULL
Post-fix FRESH matches pre-fix WARM on every structural field: detectedSamplesIn 204 == 204,
segmentCount 2 == 2, separationRatio 33.60 vs 33.54 (0.2%), and the SAME three metrics null.
It differs quantitatively: detectedFrames 136 vs 127, seg0 133 vs 123 frames, start 1.65 vs 1.75.
Per the pre-registered rule this is PARTIAL (null-set matches, frame count gap 9 > +/-5): the two
operating points are qualitatively the same and quantitatively different. So the three nulls are
NOT introduced by this change — the pre-fix build already produces them warm, and CLAUDE.md says a
real user's browser is warm.

RECOMMENDATION FROM THE MEASUREMENT SESSION: merge as built, plus strides-e45. The pre-registered
overall rule did not cover 'Q2 favours pre-fix while Q3 favours post-fix' and is reported as
unusable for that combination rather than silently replaced.

NOT MEASURED / GAPS: (1) the worktree is 20 commits behind main, so its demo1 is the RETIRED
Pexels clip — main's park-side-landscape.mp4 and park-side-portrait.mp4 were never exercised by
this A/B and should be before merge; (2) why the hip-bounce fit fails with MORE frames was not
isolated; (3) per-frame detected/missing lists need a dev probe this session was not permitted to
add, so Q3 was answered from segment spans plus keyframes rather than a frame-by-frame diff.
close_reason: Decision made 2026-09-05: the 340-line movement is NOT acceptable as a side effect of an image fix. carry-exact-decoded-frame-timestamps is backed out; commit preserved on local branch wip/exact-decoded-frame-timestamps (35a6427). The deciding evidence arrived AFTER this bead's own investigation: re-running the A/B on the three SHIPPING clips (the investigation ran on base cee2706, whose demo1 key was the retired Pexels clip) showed side-landscape moving 84 fields — the most of the three, not the bit-identical no-op recorded here — losing 13.2% of detected frames and demoting verticalRatio from normal to caveated. Combined with the fix only correcting one of the two footstrike images, the trade did not hold. The investigation's own findings STAND and are not withdrawn: multiperson's +33 frames are a keyframe-confirmed genuine improvement, kneeFlexion's swing is product-invisible and pre-existing (reproduces on the pre-fix commit alone under a tracking-crop toggle), and multiperson's cadence loss is not created by this change (pre-fix already loses it on 4 of 5 warm trials) — that last one is preserved as strides-e45. Superseded by strides-5t4's half-frame seek, which fixes the reported bug with zero metric movement.

title: Fusion tie-breaks to clip 1, silently hiding an equally-confident clip that contradicts it
description:
Measured 2026-09-04 on commit f7b02e8, fresh-process, real GPU, 2 trials, zero spread except elapsedMs.

The three bundled demo clips disagree materially on two metrics, and fuseHeuristics.ts:17 uses strict '>' so equal confidences resolve to the LOWEST clip index. The losing clip's reading is discarded with no user-visible trace.

  metric              side-landscape   side-portrait   both conf
  overstriding        +0.512135        -0.00809497     1.0
  footStrikePattern   +0.115103 (heel) -0.239589 (fore) 1.0

That is a 0.52 torso spread on overstriding and 0.355 on strike pattern, between two SIDE-view clips of the SAME runner, both at confidence 1.0 (the ceiling). The fused demo session shows clip 1's answer only.

Because 1.0 is the ceiling, an equally-confident later clip can NEVER displace clip 1 - the tie is structurally unwinnable, not merely unlucky.

This is the mechanism behind the user report 'overstriding seems wrong (50% of torso for my three demo clips)': it is ~51% on ONE clip, and the fusion presents that as the session answer.
acceptance_criteria: A session whose clips disagree materially on a metric does not present one clip's number as if uncontested. Either the disagreement is surfaced to the reader, or the tie-break stops being index-order, or confidence stops saturating at 1.0 so a genuine ranking exists.
notes:
2026-09-05 — PARTIALLY SHIPPED. Deliberately left OPEN; see the gap below.

USER DECISION: surface the disagreement (not 'fix confidence', not 'change the tie-break'). Shipped
on feat/bundle-three-clip-demo (66ddef7, a69a6da, archived dcfe92c).

THE RULE: surface where the losing clip lands in a different CATEGORY of a band the metric already
owns and already ships. No magnitude threshold, no new constant. Renders as, after the existing
proxy caveat and 'Combined from clip 1 of 3.':
  'The clips disagree: clip 2 read a forefoot strike. Nothing here settles which clip is right.'

Verified live on the real three-clip demo, read out of the DOM. Standard A/B is a NEGATIVE CONTROL
only and is structurally blind to this change - single-clip fusion returns results[0] by reference
before pickMetric runs - and came back elapsedMs-clean, proving no computed value moved. 1511 tests.

COVERAGE: 1 of 12 metrics. footStrikePattern only, because it owns classifyFootStrike and uniquely
renders that WORD as the card's value. Declined with reasons: stepWidth/stepWidthCm (own a
zero-width 'value < 0' boundary - fires on noise), cadence (isNearGridEdge answers 'near the limit
of measurability', not 'what kind of value'), and eight metrics with no value-keyed branch at all.

⚠️ WHY THIS TICKET STAYS OPEN. The acceptance criterion is 'A session whose clips disagree
materially on a metric does not present one clip's number as if uncontested.' The OVERSTRIDING card
still reads 51.2% of torso with no trace that another clip read ~0% - and that is the number in the
original user report. overstriding owns no interpretive band, so the shipped rule cannot see it, and
covering it would need exactly the constant the design refuses to invent. Split out as strides-yg8,
which carries the two candidate routes.

ALSO STILL HIDDEN, a second shape the rule structurally cannot see: cadence disagrees by ABSENCE -
side-portrait resolves none at all - so fusion silently shows side-landscape's 174 spm. That is 'one
clip resolved', out of scope by the criterion as written.

The upstream cause remains strides-aha (side-portrait's hip fit below cadenceMinFitR2, so it runs
the ankle-difference fallback while side-landscape runs the fitted phase). Fixing that may make the
disagreement largely evaporate, which would change which route in strides-yg8 is worth building.
strides-2po still depends on this ticket.

title: Sizing spike: recover the 35-40% frame loss on the playback sampling path (WebM/rotated-MP4 fallback)
description:
SPIKE (no production code). sampleClip.ts:153 self-throttles: any frame presented while a detection is in flight is discarded, not queued. Playback path captures ~60-65 of 99 on Demo 2 vs 99/99 on the WebCodecs sequential path. canUseSequentialDecode (webCodecsSupport.ts:74) gates the good path with 8 conditions; looksLikeIsoBmff rejects WebM outright, and webcam recordings are WebM.

Question: which direction — (a) teach the pipeline WebM demuxing, (b) record MP4 via MediaRecorder where supported, (c) reduce loss on the playback path itself, (d) something else — and what would each cost.

Findings recorded in notes as they land.
notes:
MEASURED BLOCK 1 (headless Chromium 151, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro, dev server 5262 identity-verified, commit fd1b513).

PREMISE RE-CONFIRMED, 4 trials/arm, fresh process per trial, scripts/ab-person-selection.mjs:
  demo2 (99 src frames):  sequential totalSamples 99 (no spread) | playback 59 [58..59]  -> 40.4% loss
  multiperson (233):      sequential 233                          | playback 192 [191..193] -> 17.6% loss

Q1 MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported (verbatim):

multiperson (0.0196 vs 0.7810) and ~40% worse on demo2. It would also help nobody on Firefox
(bug 1631143 open, explicitly deprioritised) and nobody on Safari before 18.4.

  T1 (P1, small) Recover playback-path frames by slowing the clip, not by queueing.
      video.playbackRate in sampleClip.ts, ideally adaptive (measure detection latency, target

      rotation dependency. Cost: 3.3x analysis wall clock at 0.25x, which is why it should be
      adaptive. ACCEPTANCE GATE MUST BE METRIC CONFIDENCE, NOT FRAME COUNT — on demo2 the same
      change moves cadence and verticalOscillation from normal tier to caveated.
  T2 (P2) Recalibrate fit-R2 confidence against sample count. Blocks T1 shipping on demo2.
      Spectral-fit R2 falls as samples rise on that clip; today's formula rewards sparse sampling.
  T3 (P2, medium) Replace mp4box with mediabunny; add WebM, honour rotation, close the de-dup.
      +8.2 kB gzipped net for all four containers. Gives (a) and gate 6 and the standing
      'mp4box de-dup' backlog item in one move. sampleClipSequential.ts already draws every
      VideoFrame to a canvas, so rotation is a transform on an existing draw call.
      MUST carry evidenceSeekOffset in its acceptance criteria — admitting rot90-style clips flips
      their evidence seek offset from 0 to -0.0333 s.

      fps 401.5 for a 2.94 s recording, and containerTiming reports nominalFps null. Inert today
      (zero non-test consumers of DemuxedTrack.fps/.durationSec) but a landmine. Also fix
      webCodecsSupport.ts's stale 'enabled: false by default' doc comment.
  T5 (P3, one line + a test) The (b) reorder, AFTER T3 lands. Once WebM demuxes, recording MP4
      stops being load-bearing and becomes a small quality preference (H.264 hardware encode,
      Safari parity). Doing it before T3 buys the D7 penalty for no compensating gain.

HONEST RISK: the strongest result here (T1) rests on 3 trials x 2 clips, and its direction on
cadence confidence is OPPOSITE on the two clips. demo1 was not run. Nobody should build T1 without
first running all three clips x at least 3 playbackRate rungs, and T2 may turn out to be the real
ticket with T1 riding on it.

NO FOURTH OPTION. Every demux-free route (MediaStreamTrackProcessor on a live track, on
videoElement.captureStream(), or new VideoFrame(videoElement) inside requestVideoFrameCallback)
rides the PRESENTATION pipeline, is clock-bound, and drops frames by specification —
mediacapture-transform normatively sets maxBufferSize to 1; Chromium's captureStream is a
wall-clock snapshot poller that ignores playbackRate entirely; rVFC fires per presentation, and
Firefox caps it at 25 fps. Documented, not measured. VideoDecoder fed by a demuxer is the only
frame-complete, faster-than-real-time route.

title: SPIKE: measure the real model-fetch seam in a browser before building against it
description:
Gate for the progress/cache work. Determines whether byte-accurate progress and client-side caching are achievable per asset, or only for the assets we serve ourselves.

Method: drive the app in headless Chromium with real GPU per CLAUDE.md's harness section (--headless=new --enable-gpu --ignore-gpu-blocklist, derived dev-server port, nonce identity guard — never SwiftShader), and read the network via CDP/Playwright response events. Capture on a COLD profile so cached responses do not mask the headers.

Confirmed feasible already, from node_modules, so do not re-derive: pose-detection's detector.js:495-520 sets fromTFHub=false when config.modelUrl is not a string, and passes it straight to loadGraphModel — so an io.IOHandler IS a real escape hatch. tfjs's own LoadOptions.onProgress is a fraction of FILES not bytes (tfjs-core/dist/io/weights_loader.js:74) and is useless here. MediaPipe accepts BaseOptions.modelAssetBuffer as a Uint8Array or ReadableStreamDefaultReader (@mediapipe/tasks-vision/vision.d.ts:27). FilesetResolver exposes no WASM progress hook at all — that asset is indeterminate no matter what this spike finds.

Surface: frontend. Blocks the MoveNet half of the progress/cache work.
design:

reading — see section 5B below):

`access-control-allow-origin: *` headers observed on that response are the CHALLENGE PAGE's
headers, not the model's, and must not be quoted as fact. Browsers clearly get through (CLAUDE.md

  movenet-singlepose    4,821,969          4,821,245         0/3  FULL RE-DOWNLOAD

  MoveNet is UNCACHEABLE BY THE BROWSER FOR TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS, both measured:

   (b) the signed URL DIFFERS ON EVERY REQUEST - cold vs warm differ in X-Goog-Date
       (20260903T192505Z vs 20260903T192707Z) and X-Goog-Signature on all 7 files. The HTTP
       cache key is the URL, so there is not even an entry to revalidate.
   => the epic's "re-fetched on every page load" premise is CONFIRMED, and no header or CDN
      change could ever fix it; only an app-owned cache can.
  The MediaPipe WASM is ALREADY cached for a year, immutable, at zero further transferred bytes.
  The .task 304 above is VITE DEV behaviour; production max-age=600 means a returning visitor
  past 10 minutes revalidates, and on any etag change re-downloads 9.4 MB.

=== 3. PER-ASSET GO / NO-GO ON CUSTOM-io.IOHandler BYTE PROGRESS ===

  MoveNet SinglePose Lightning - GO. CORS-readable across the 3-origin redirect chain, exact
    Content-Length, body arrives as a ReadableStream in 8/118/22 chunks: loaded/total is honest.
  MoveNet MultiPose Lightning  - GO. Identical; 17/128/94/35 chunks.
  pose_landmarker_full.task    - GO (and needs no IOHandler; MediaPipe takes
    BaseOptions.modelAssetBuffer directly). Same-origin, exact Content-Length, 150 chunks.
  tasks-vision WASM            - NO-GO, as predicted. FilesetResolver exposes no progress hook and
    the fetch happens inside the Emscripten loader. Even if reachable, content-encoding: br makes
    Content-Length 3.8x smaller than the streamed byte count, so a naive loaded/total reads ~376%.
    Indeterminate. It is also already year-cached and only 3.2 MB on the wire - the least worth
    instrumenting of the four.

=== 4. FALLBACK IF MoveNet WERE UNINSTRUMENTABLE ===
  Not needed - MoveNet is the best-instrumented of the four. Stated anyway, in priority order:
   (a) File-level progress WEIGHTED by model.json's weight manifest (model.json is fetched first,
       is small, and declares every shard's size), giving byte-accurate progress without touching
       the shard fetches. tfjs's own onProgress is a fraction of FILES and must not be used.
   (b) Failing that, a 7-step determinate bar keyed on file completion (3 + 4 files) - honest
       about its granularity rather than fake-smooth.
   (c) Failing that, an indeterminate "Downloading pose model" state - still strictly better than
       today, where a loaded clip reads Ready while blocked on an unmentioned 14.5 MB fetch.

=== 5. CONTRADICTIONS / EXTENSIONS TO THE TICKET BODIES ===

  A. THE HEADLINE THE TICKETS DID NOT HAVE: MoveNet's fetched URL is PER-REQUEST SIGNED (see
     2(b)). Load-bearing for strides-utn.4 - a cache keyed on the fetched URL MISSES 100% of the
     time. Key on the stable tfhub.dev URL (or the kaggle path), never on response.url.

  B. THE SHELL reCAPTCHA READING IS FULLY REFUTED IN A BROWSER. tfhub.dev -> kaggle -> signed
     GCS, 200 on all 7 files, cold and warm, no challenge. The "no-cache, no-store,
     must-revalidate" seen from curl was the challenge page's; the real header is
     "private, max-age=0".

  C. THE EPIC UNDERSTATES THE PAYLOAD. It names the 9,398,198-byte .task as the big asset.
     MoveNet is bigger: 14,522,593 body bytes (4.82 MB singlepose + 9.70 MB multipose) at app
     MOUNT, before any clip is touched - and MULTIPOSE ALONE (9.70 MB) exceeds the .task. Cold
     total across all four assets is 27.1 MB. MultiPose is fetched only because
     personOfInterestConfig.enabled is true (movenet.ts), so it is 9.7 MB a
     {personOfInterest:{enabled:false}} run does not pay.

  D. content-encoding CHANGES WHAT PROGRESS MEANS, and only for the WASM. For MoveNet and the
     .task, Content-Length == streamed bytes exactly. For the jsdelivr WASM it is 3.8-4.1x off.
     A shared fetch/progress utility (strides-utn.3) must decide PER RESPONSE whether to trust
     Content-Length; it cannot assume.

  E. THE WASM DOES NOT NEED A CACHE. public, max-age=31536000, immutable; measured
     fromDiskCache:true / 0 transferred bytes on the warm run. Adding it to an app-owned cache
     would be strictly WORSE: CacheStorage stores the DECODED body, so a 3.12 MB wire payload
     occupies 11.76 MB of quota.

  F. CacheStorage IS A VIABLE BACKING STORE - measured, not assumed. caches.open/put/match
     round-tripped all three storable assets byte-identically from the app own origin,
     INCLUDING the cross-origin CORS ones:
       movenet group1-shard2of2    455,912 ->    455,912   type "cors",  content-length preserved
       vision_wasm_internal.wasm 11,756,954 -> 11,756,954  type "cors"
       pose_landmarker_full.task  9,398,198 ->  9,398,198  type "basic"
     navigator.storage.estimate(): quota 10,759,035,392 bytes (~10.76 GB). The full model set
     (~35.6 MB decoded, or ~23.9 MB leaving the WASM to the browser) is ~0.2-0.3% of quota.

  G. THE .task OWN COMMENT IS WRONG IN A SECOND WAY. mediapipePoseLandmarker.ts:17-23 says
     self-hosting "rides our own deploy caching". Production is max-age=600 (confirmed), 6x
     worse than the 3600s Google bucket it replaced. The self-hosting decision is still right
     (the bucket "latest" tag floats), but that caching rationale is false - and is the reason
     strides-utn.3 exists.

=== 6. REPRODUCTION ===
  Throwaway probes, scratchpad only, nothing added to src/:
    measure-model-fetch.mjs - cold+warm capture via CDP Network.* on ONE persistent Chromium
      profile; starts the derived-port dev server, runs assertServesThisCheckout +
      assertHardwareRenderer, drives Demo 2 to completion, waits for the scale-pass console line.
    probe-cors.mjs - in-page fetch(mode:cors) + ReadableStream byte count + CacheStorage
      put/match round-trip + navigator.storage.estimate(), on the app own origin.
  Port: resolveDevServerPort() from scripts/lib/harnessProvenance.mjs => 5236
  Launch args: ['--headless=new','--enable-gpu','--ignore-gpu-blocklist'] via launchPersistentContext.
  Production headers: curl -sS -o /dev/null -D - -L https://cazzer.github.io/strides/models/pose_landmarker_full.task

Ends with an explicit per-asset go/no-go on the custom-IOHandler byte-progress approach, and a stated fallback if MoveNet turns out to be uninstrumentable. Findings recorded on this bead and in the openspec design doc. NO production code ships from this ticket.
notes: SPIKE COMPLETE 2026-09-03. Full measurement table, cold+warm readings, per-asset go/no-go and the contradiction list are in this issue's DESIGN field. Headline: MoveNet singlepose+multipose are BOTH a GO for custom-io.IOHandler byte progress (CORS-readable across a tfhub->kaggle->signed-GCS redirect chain, exact Content-Length, ReadableStream bodies). The .task is a GO and needs no IOHandler. The tasks-vision WASM is a NO-GO and stays indeterminate. title: Overstriding under-reports because it samples mid-stance, and no correction is available from current signals
description:
Successor to strides-24s, which is CLOSED on its own criterion (its proposed remedy was measured and rejected). The problem it named is not fixed.

WHAT IS WRONG. detectFromBouncePhase puts touchdown at the fitted hip-bounce low point minus T/4. On Demo 1 the emitted instants land +0.10 to +0.12s after keyframe-confirmed onsets (4.08/4.74/5.40/6.06) on all four strikes. The hip travels ~1800 px/s while the planted foot is stationary, so 0.11s of lag removes ~216 px = ~0.52 torso lengths from the ankle-to-hip offset — LARGER than the 0.326 torso lengths the card reports. Hand-measured from keyframes, the same strike reads ~0.65 torso at true touchdown against 0.36 at the sampled instant. The reported number is roughly half the true overstride.

WHY IT IS NOT CORRECTABLE TODAY (strides-24s spike, pre-registered gates, all failed):
- Duty factor is not recoverable from ankle-x stationarity: 20% of strikes resolvable overall, 0% on Demo 2, where 8 of 9 candidates have no sustained low-speed run at all. Ankle-x velocity also passes near zero at the swing-arc reversal, so it is necessary but not sufficient for stance.
- The closed form is not even the mechanism: measured stances land essentially at T/2, so lag=(stance-T/2)/2 predicts a near-zero correction, and applying it made the residual LARGER on both available data points.
- The dominant term (W1: hip low point trails geometric midstance) has consistent SIGN but a 37x magnitude range across clips (0.0045-0.1673s), and spans 0.058s within a single clip against a 0.02s tolerance. Not a modelable constant of the runner.

WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND WORTH PROTECTING: the bias is SYSTEMATIC WITHIN A CLIP — measured spread 0.020s against the superseded ankle detector's 0.340s. Every consumer depends on that property, so this must not be 'fixed' by reverting to the ankle-difference detector, which was worse in exactly the way that matters.

OPTIONS, none yet chosen — this needs a product decision, not a threshold:
(a) DISCLOSE. Caveat overstriding (and the other fore-aft consumers) that the measurement is taken at a sampled instant which trails touchdown, so the value is a lower bound. Cheap, shippable today, and stops the card overstating its own precision. Risk: the MECHANISM is general but the MAGNITUDE is measured on one clip, so the wording must not quote a number.
(b) NEW SIGNAL. Acquire footage with independently confirmable ground contact (markers, or a known high frame rate), or an orthogonal contact cue such as vertical foot position / shoe deformation from a rear or dead-front angle. This is the same footage gap the dynamic-valgus investigation named as its top ask.
(c) ACCEPT AND DOCUMENT. Leave the number as is, recorded in CLAUDE.md as a known systematic under-report.

⚠️ DO NOT fit a constant offset to Demo 1's four contacts. strides-da8's proof was against exactly that, strides-24s repeated the prohibition by name, and the spike now shows the quantity a constant would encode varies 37x across the corpus.

⚠️ GROUND TRUTH IS n=1 CLIP. Four contacts, one runner, one camera, and no confirmed toe-off anywhere — even the spike's stance readings are unverified against anything. Any claim about the magnitude of this bias on other footage is extrapolation.
acceptance_criteria: Either the card stops implying a precision it does not have (option a), or a signal is acquired that makes the correction measurable and it is validated on more than one clip. Explicitly NOT satisfied by a constant offset fitted to Demo 1.
notes:

Built and measured a fourth correction strategy strides-24s did not evaluate: re-sample
overstriding's own forward-reach signal at its interior local maximum within a bounded backward
window (W=0.5 step periods), instead of correcting the detected instant's timing. Pre-registered
gates, adjudicated mechanically:

title: Overstriding measures collapsed-pose frames as footstrikes (both ankles within 3px)
description:
User-reported: the Overstriding card's evidence shows a trailing swing leg, not a footstrike. Confirmed by measurement — the metric is sampling instants where the pose has collapsed.

MEASURED, Demo 1, primary MoveNet pass, real GPU (temporary [overstride-probe] in computeOverstriding, added-measured-reverted):

  t      side   ratio     hipMid   leftAnkle        rightAnkle       ankle separation
  4.200  right  +0.5102   457      683 interp       670 interp       13 px
  4.840  left   +0.2936   1520     1643 detected    1161 detected    482 px
  5.520  right  +0.3579   2665     2340 detected    2815 detected    475 px
  6.160  left   -0.7215   3711     3409 detected    3406 detected    3 px

Two of four strikes sit on frames where BOTH ankles collapse onto one point (3 px and 13 px apart) against ~480 px on the two healthy frames. At a genuine footstrike the ankles are near maximal separation — that is the entire basis of the ankle-difference detector this module falls back to — so a 3 px separation is a degenerate pose, not a contact.

Keyframes pulled at app 6.16 (ffmpeg 6.08, this clip's 0.08 s edit-list shift applied) confirm it: the runner is nearly out of frame right, both detected ankles land on the TRAILING swing foot (x~3407) while the planted foot is at the frame edge (x~3800+), and the hip is at 3711. The reported -0.7215 means 'the foot landed 72% of a torso length BEHIND the hip', which is anatomically impossible for a footstrike. The 4.200 strike is the mirror case: both ankles interpolated and 13 px apart, yielding the maximum ratio (+0.5102).

⚠️ THE REPORTED VALUE IS CURRENTLY CORRECT BY ACCIDENT. With n=4 the median averages the middle two, and the two collapsed strikes happen to be the min and the max, so they are discarded: median = (0.2936+0.3579)/2 = 0.32574, which matches the shipped value exactly. One fewer healthy strike, or two collapses on the same side of the median, and the number moves. Same shape as strides-h6r (small-n median is not outlier-robust) — that ticket is stepWidth, this is its overstriding twin, and here the contaminated samples are already present rather than hypothetical.

⚠️ Confidence reads 0.875 ('High confidence' on the card) with usableStrikeCount 4, so the sample presents as healthier than it is: half its strikes are degenerate.

NOT the +0.11 s footstrike lag. That lag is real and reproduced here on all four strikes (detected 4.20/4.84/5.52/6.16 vs keyframe-confirmed onsets 4.08/4.74/5.40/6.06, so +0.12/+0.10/+0.12/+0.10), but it does not cause this: at the true onset 6.06 the left foot is even further behind. See strides-24s.

DIRECTION: reject a strike whose two ankles are implausibly close (they should be near maximal separation at contact), and/or whose measured ankle sits behind the hip by more than gait allows. A per-strike plausibility gate is the missing piece; detectFootstrikes' phase path (footstrikes.ts:615-648) predicts one instant per step from the fitted bounce and never checks that the pose at that instant looks like a contact.
acceptance_criteria: On Demo 1, overstriding's usable strikes exclude the collapsed frames at t=4.20 and t=6.16; the reported value is derived only from poses where the ankles are plausibly separated; and the evidence exemplar is drawn from a surviving strike.
notes: CORRECTION to the close reason: the n=2 vacuous-extreme follow-up is strides-9uj, not 'strides-erx' — that id was written from memory and does not exist. Carried forward from this ticket: strides-24s (P1), strides-9uj (P2), strides-dbh (P3).
close_reason:
Now fully satisfied. Its third acceptance criterion — 'the evidence exemplar is drawn from a surviving strike' — was met at the metric layer but not the rendered layer, which is why this was deliberately held open. strides-ddj (c4e55b3 + f00efd6) closed that gap: the card renders t=4.84, one of the two surviving strikes. Criteria 1 and 2 were already met in 7ad694b + fb99506 — usable strikes exclude the collapsed frames at t=4.20 and t=6.16, and the value 0.3257433216584835 is derived only from plausibly-separated poses at sampleSize 2, frameCoverage 0.5, confidence 0.25.

Carried forward, NOT fixed here: strides-24s (P1) — the sampled instants are ~0.11s late, so the reported value understates the true overstride at touchdown by roughly half; strides-erx — at n=2 the extreme-pair framing is vacuous; strides-dbh — the sibling MIN_*_SAMPLE_SIZE sweep.

title: Re-extract only the metrics whose plan actually changed
description:
Follow-up to strides-3ui (D5 of openspec/changes/hold-evidence-through-reextraction/design.md).

Reuse is now decided per CLIP: if the recomputed plan is structurally identical to the cached one, the whole clip is reused and no decoder opens. When the plan DOES move — Demo 1, where the scale-pass graft takes verticalOscillationCm from metric-excluded to planned — the entire clip is still re-extracted, including the nine metrics whose plans did not change.

This is no longer user-visible: since strides-3ui the previous pass's images stay on screen for the duration, so the cost is wasted decode work rather than a blank. Worth doing anyway on a 4K clip.

Shape: split a clip's plan into extract-these / reuse-those, run the extractor on the first, and merge with the cached MetricEvidence for the second. Touches extractSessionEvidence's batch contract (ClipEvidenceInput is currently one whole ClipEvidencePlan per clip), which is why it was kept out of the flicker fix.
acceptance_criteria: A graft that changes one metric's plan re-decodes only that metric's instants; the other metrics' cached images are reused by reference. Verified on Demo 1, where verticalOscillationCm moves from metric-excluded to planned.
notes:
Related: strides-8zv (pending-evidence placeholder) plumbs the evidence PLAN out of useSessionEvidence's startRun, where it is currently computed and discarded except into cacheRef (:329). That exposed plan is the same input a per-metric re-extraction diff would need, so land 8zv first and this ticket gets materially cheaper.
Epic strides-e4c (T0 baseline 2026-10-05): every single-clip run extracts evidence twice — the pre-graft pass runs to near completion and is discarded (1.7-3.8 s wasted seek+draw; side-landscape 3761 ms), and the kept pass queues behind it. Scope widened: (1) abort a superseded extraction promptly (check signal between seeks, not only between items), (2) re-extract only metrics whose plan changed. Gate: evidence canvases pixel-identical; time to evidence-settled vs baseline.
Implemented on branch perf/zm8-evidence-reextract @ 570887d (unmerged, unpushed; based on db1b4b1). (1) extractFrames checks the abort signal before every seek (was per image). (2) ClipEvidenceInput gains reuse (held metrics passed through by reference, never seeked) + onMetricExtracted (finished metrics reported as they finish, never after an abort). (3) useSessionEvidence cache is per metric (serialised plan entry + blob); in-flight runs harvest finished metrics so the graft-superseded primary pass's work is reused, and only moved plan entries re-decode. Objective 3 (skip planning grafted metrics on the first pass) not done: with harvesting the first pass's unchanged-metric work is no longer wasted, and the cm metrics are typically excluded on the primary plan anyway. Live gate (pixel hashes, evidence settled@, reusedImages on kept pass) left to the e4c verifier.
Review follow-up e040ad4 on perf/zm8-evidence-reextract: cache/harvest only complete metrics (failed/partial re-decode next pass); abort check after seekTo in drawInstant; perf 'images' counts decoded only; extracting state shows held images for metrics with nothing on screen (same-clip-set only, carried wins).
VERIFIED LIVE (2026-10-05, verifier) at int perf/e4c 5a2afbb (bfbf436 + e4c.3 + dt9 + zm8) vs ref c39a7a8, real GPU ANGLE Metal M4 Pro, fresh process per trial, derived ports, identity verified. A/B gate (4 clips x3, --evidence) BIT-IDENTICAL: stripped md5 577597202f4c7675a92b2fbfd0ade236 both sides, rtk proxy diff empty. Evidence pixel check (scratch driver, sha256 of getImageData per main canvas keyed by card aria-label+order, 4 single uploads + demo3, 2 trials x both checkouts): 43/43 canvases identical across ref x2 + int x2 (8/8/6/9/12), none missing, ref stable trial to trial. Session medians ref->int: evidence settled landscape 14497->11939, portrait 9538->7840, approach 6401->5342, multiperson 7707->6590; demo3 all-complete 14186->13030, last scale 15254->13984, all-settled 25531->23930. zm8-specific, kept pass ref->int (seeks/decoded images/reusedImages, total ms): landscape 13/8/- 6098 -> 9/6/2 4237 (trial range 9-11 seeks, reused 1-2: whether the pre-graft pass's second VO/VR pair finished before the abort is a race); portrait 14/8/- 1852 -> 6/4/4 760; approach 12/6/- 1682 -> 8/4/2 1016; multiperson 15/9/- 1809 -> 11/7/2 1290; demo3 clip1 13/8 -> 13/8/0.
