Recorded live via getUserMedia + MediaRecorder (fake device fed a y4m of the park clip): video/webm;codecs=vp9, 2.65MB, 205 samples, sampling.path 'playback' — the rVFC sampler, exactly the branch that must not shift. resolveEvidenceSeekOffsetSeconds returned EXACTLY 0 on both extraction passes, annotation lands on the runner. Per-clip MP4 offsets for contrast, all exact: Demo 1 -0.08 (2/25), Demo 2 -0.03336666666666667 (2002/60000), multiperson -0.03333333333333333 (512/15360).

CONTRACTS ALL PASS: [analysis-diagnostics] same six top-level keys ~5.5kB with no canvas/blob/dataUrl/exemplar/crop on all four clips; vite build's shipped JS has zero dev-only prefixes; no toDataURL/toBlob export path; no fillText/strokeText/measureText/font in any annotation or extraction module and zero text visible across ~15 images; anchor 4.421467928439415 cm with fit 1.52 x 60 = 91.2 == cadence 91.2; subjectAgreement 52/53. Wall clock +1.4% on both demo clips over 6 trials/arm against pre-epic baseline 2a3f009 — no regression, extraction settles after 'Analysis complete'. Two-clip provenance 10 images / 7 sections with every 'From clip N of 2.' matching sourceIndices one-for-one.

ONE DEFECT FOUND, filed as strides-ac9.12: the seek lands one frame EARLY on multiperson-track.mp4 (delta -1; delta 0 on both demo clips). Root-caused, not guessed — a pure Chromium seek with no app involved reproduces it: the flip sits in a ~0.6 microsecond window just above the frame's presentation timestamp, because Chromium quantises to integer microseconds and this clip's stored timestamp is 1us above ac9.4's double-subtraction result. ac9.4's arithmetic is correct; it lands ON the boundary by construction. Explicitly NOT fixed by epsilon.

Also reported, pre-existing and cosmetic: the shipped CSS carries two dead Tailwind arbitrary-property rules named after the dev-only console prefixes, generated by Tailwind v4's source scanner from CLAUDE.md and an archived design doc. Not a logging leak.

comments.text:
UPDATE from strides-ac9.2 (2026-08-17): most of this ticket's premise has already moved.

title: Assess annotation misregistration from the 2-frame evidence seek offset (gh #69)
description:
This epic makes an existing latent bug newly VISIBLE, which is why it is scoped here rather than left on the GitHub backlog.

## The measured bug (GitHub #69, not hypothesised)
`sequentialSampling` defaults on, so most MP4s sample through WebCodecs where `robustFrames[].timestamp` is raw `sample.cts / sample.timescale` (src/video/mp4Demux.ts:174) with NO edit-list adjustment, while `HTMLVideoElement.currentTime` IS adjusted. The evidence extractor seeks a detached <video> to the planned timestamp, so every extracted frame lands late by the clip's own `elst media_time / mediaTimescale`. Ground-truthed by ffmpeg/PSNR argmax: +2 frames on all three test clips (0.0800s on Demo 1 at 25fps; 0.033367s on Demo 2 at 59.94fps; 0.033333s on the 60fps multiperson clip). Measures EXACTLY 0 under `{ sequentialSampling: { enabled: false } }` — so it is isolated to the WebCodecs domain, not to seeking.

## Why it matters now and did not before
Today's evidence images are unannotated photographs; a 2-frame offset is invisible. Once joints are drawn from the SAMPLED frame's keypoints onto an image that is 2 frames later, the skeleton floats off the body — 80ms on Demo 1 is ~12% of a step cycle, and a runner's limbs move a lot in 80ms. The annotation will look broken even though the numbers are right.

## Do not just pick a constant
`DEFAULT_EVIDENCE_SEEK_OFFSET_SECONDS` is 0 (extractFrames.ts:80) and #69 is explicit that the correct value is per-clip AND per-sampler: it must be exactly 0 for every WebM/webcam clip and every MP4 where `canUseSequentialDecode` says no. Any single constant is wrong on two of three test clips. #69 carries two real candidate fixes: plumb a per-clip offset using `src/video/containerTiming.ts`'s existing `elst` parser, or align the domains at the demuxer.

## Scope of THIS ticket
Decide, with measurement, whether annotation is acceptable at the current offset. If not, implement one of #69's two fixes. Measure misregistration in PIXELS on a real clip, not in frames — that is the number that decides it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Misregistration quantified in pixels on Demo 1 and Demo 2 with annotation drawn
- [ ] A decision is recorded: acceptable as-is, or fixed — with the measurement behind it
- [ ] If fixed: correct on WebCodecs MP4s AND exactly 0 on WebM/webcam clips and non-sequential-decode MP4s
- [ ] No single global constant is introduced as the fix
- [ ] GitHub #69 updated with the outcome (do not close it without the user's say-so)
notes:
OUTCOME: not acceptable at the current offset — FIXED. Commit b465d89 on
worktree-agent-a89f5215bd819d8bb (base 87e867c). Not pushed, not merged.

## The number (the deliverable)

Misregistration = || p(t + offset) - p(t) || for every joint an annotation
draws, scaled by outputSide / crop.side, i.e. output-canvas pixels. Measured on
the real plans of live runs (headless Chromium, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4
Pro), offset = each clip's own elst media_time / mediaTimescale.

Demo 1 (25 fps, offset 0.0800 s, 54 marks over 7 images / 5 sections), all 54
read at an exact sampled frame — zero interpolation, so these are not estimates:
  ALL   min 7.0  p50 64.5  p90 116.3  max 342.0  mean 74.5
  FAST  min 7.0  p50 83.9  p90 160.7  max 342.0  mean 93.0   (n=24)
  SLOW  min 32.5 p50 57.8  p90  80.4  max  84.9  mean 59.7   (n=30)
  worst joints: left_ankle p50 126.7 / max 342.0; right_ankle p50 72.5
  best joints:  left_knee p50 22.3; left_shoulder p50 36.6

Demo 2 (59.94 fps, offset 0.033367 s, 44 marks over 5 images / 4 sections):
  ALL   min 1.1  p50  7.2  p90 17.1  max 29.5  mean 10.1
  FAST  min 2.6  p50 12.9  p90 25.6  max 29.5  mean 13.9   (n=20)
  SLOW  min 1.1  p50  6.1  p90 10.1  max 16.5  mean 7.0    (n=24)

Display-independent framing (torso length from the clip's own scale
calibration): Demo 1 median = 31% of a torso, p90 = 56%, worst single mark ~78%.
Demo 2 median = 3.4% of a torso, max 13.7%.

FAST is only modestly worse than SLOW on Demo 1 because the dominant term there
is whole-body lateral translation across a static side-view frame, which moves
hips and shoulders as much as it moves limbs. Demo 2's subject approaches the
camera, so translation is small and the split is the expected 2x.

Verdict: Demo 2 alone would have been acceptable; Demo 1 is not. Confirmed
visually — pre-fix, footStrikePattern's shank line and ankle marker sit clearly
off the leg, and kneeFlexion's thigh/shin chain floats left of the runner.

## The fix

Option 1 (per-clip offset), derived inside extractFrames.ts rather than plumbed
through the gallery. New src/video/evidenceSeekOffset.ts:
resolveEvidenceSeekOffsetSeconds(blob) returns 0 unless BOTH the sequential
plane is on and canUseSequentialDecode(blob) says the WebCodecs path really ran,
AND the container carries a single unity-rate edit list with media_time > 0 — in
which case it returns -(media_time / mediaTimescale). Multi-entry, empty
(media_time < 0), dwell and non-unity-rate edit lists all decline to 0: none is
a constant shift. Cached per Blob. robustFrames[].timestamp untouched.

Option 2 (align at the demuxer) rejected, and not only on governance grounds:
elst media_time is pre-roll the presentation never shows, so a correct demuxer
fix must also drop those samples. That changes the sampled set, which changes
metric values — it is not the pure translation gh #69 assumed.

## Proof

ffmpeg/PSNR argmax over candidate media-frame indices, app canvas as reference:
  Demo 1 footStrikePattern: before delta 0 (24.97 vs 19.94 dB) -> after delta -2
    (24.03 vs 20.04 dB)
  Demo 2 stepWidth:         before delta 0 (22.00 vs 21.82 dB) -> after delta -2
    (22.56 vs 21.49 dB)
  Demo 1 under {sequentialSampling:{enabled:false}}: delta 0 (23.84 vs 19.63 dB,
    4.2 dB clear) — offset stayed exactly 0 on the <video> path.
The after-argmax is the media sample the analysis measured, so residual
misregistration is zero by construction.

Anchors unmoved to every digit (track clip): verticalOscillationCm
4.421467928439415, fit.frequencyHz x 60 = 91.2 == cadence.value 91.2, sinusoidR2
0.42451916621964814, sampleCount 57, span 2.24 s, torsoMeters 0.504143645953322,
medianPixelsPerMeter 868.0221516689736. Demo 2: 10.486597716761532 cm, cadence
181.2. [evidence-coverage] unchanged: Demo 1 7 images / 5 sections, Demo 2 5 / 4.

Cost: derivation 25.2 ms on the 25 MB 4K clip, 8.1 ms on Demo 2, 0 ms cached
(vs extraction's own ~3.5 s). Analysis wall clock 5805 ms on Demo 1, inside
D14's 5698 ms [5539..5910] band.

Gates: tsc clean, eslint clean, vitest 84 files / 1208 tests passing
(baseline 83 / 1188; +1 file, +20 tests).

FOLLOW-UP for whoever owns EvidenceGallery: the fact this module re-derives
(did the sequential sampler run) is known first-hand by useVideoAnalysis. If a
prop ever gets threaded onto ClipSession, this should read it instead of calling
canUseSequentialDecode a second time. The re-derivation is safe — both
predicates are pure functions of the blob and the environment, unchanged within
a session — but it is a second source of truth.

GitHub #69 updated, deliberately left OPEN for the user to close.
close_reason: Measured (Demo 1 median 64.4 output px = 31% of a torso; Demo 2 median 7.2 px), decided FIX, shipped as b465d89. Anchors and coverage unmoved; ffmpeg/PSNR argmax confirms delta -2 on WebCodecs MP4s and exactly 0 on the <video> path.

title: Embed evidence inline in the metric card
description:

The canvas element is adopted into the DOM directly via `host.replaceChildren(canvas)` (EvidenceGallery.tsx:296-316) — no data URL, no blob, deliberately. Preserve that mechanism. ## Preserve A card whose metric has no evidence must render exactly as it does today: no placeholder, no empty frame, no layout shift. title: Author the openspec change for inline annotated evidence
description:
Spec-first ticket. No implementation. This one is unusually load-bearing because the epic REVERSES a standing prohibition — a downstream implementer who reads only the current spec will believe the work is forbidden.

  openspec new change "inline-annotated-evidence"
  openspec validate inline-annotated-evidence --strict

Capability: results-view.

## Deltas required

REMOVE (with Reason/Migration), then ADD under a fresh name — the behavior fully reverses, and per CLAUDE.md a MODIFIED block that no longer resembles the original is worse than a clean REMOVE+ADD:
- 'An evidence gallery renders below the results, grouped by metric' (L735). The gallery is gone; evidence lives in the card.
- 'Metric cards deep-link to their evidence, and are otherwise unchanged' (L770). No deep link. Note the second half of that requirement — a card with no evidence renders exactly as today, no placeholder, no empty frame, no layout shift — is still WANTED and must survive into the replacement requirement.

The single most important clause to get right, at L746 inside the gallery requirement:
  'The system SHALL NOT draw a skeleton, angle arc, reference line, or any other annotation over an
   extracted image, and SHALL NOT overlay any reference or ideal posture'
That sentence contains TWO prohibitions. Reverse the FIRST (annotating detected/measured geometry is now required). KEEP THE SECOND, explicitly and in the new requirement's own words: no reference posture, no ideal, no target overlay. Thumbnails show what was measured on this runner, never something to match. If the new spec silently drops the second half, the epic has quietly changed what the product claims.

KEEP AND EXTEND, do not rewrite: 'Evidence frames are planned purely, then extracted from a detached video element' (L648). Its purity rule ('the decision half SHALL be pure... no DOM, no canvas, no video element') now extends to annotation geometry.

Also spec: thumbnail sizing/placement in the card (below description on mobile, right on desktop), and that annotation is drawn only for metrics whose quantity is actually drawable on a still — see the per-metric determination in strides-ac9.2.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] openspec change 'inline-annotated-evidence' exists with proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md and spec deltas
- [ ] `openspec validate inline-annotated-evidence --strict` passes
- [ ] The reference/ideal-posture prohibition survives explicitly into the new requirement text
- [ ] The 'card without evidence is unchanged, no placeholder, no layout shift' guarantee survives
- [ ] The purity rule is extended to annotation geometry
- [ ] REMOVE blocks reuse exact existing requirement title text
- [ ] No src/ files changed by this ticket
notes:
CORRECTION to the description: the per-metric drawable-geometry determination is in strides-ac9.7, not strides-ac9.2 (ac9.2 is the card layout ticket).

## Third thing the spec must say — surfaced by research after this ticket was written

The spec must state that a mark is NOT labelled with the card's reported value unless the drawn quantity IS that value. Researched against the calcs, they usually differ:

- bounceCycle amplitude (verticalOscillation, verticalOscillationCm, verticalRatio) is a whole-clip least-squares spectral fit with a c+d*t+e*t^2 trend removed (bounceInstants.ts:20-30). The pixel gap between the two ghosted midpoints is NOT the reported amplitude.
- verticalRatio's value is a quotient across two DIFFERENT exemplars; each image shows one factor only.
- armSwingSymmetry's value is a ratio BETWEEN its two images; neither image shows it.
- overstriding, footStrikePattern, stepWidth all divide by a CLIP-MEDIAN body scale (bodyScale.ts:41, :68). Numerator drawable, denominator not.
- trunkLean and overstriding deliberately select EXTREME instants (exemplars.ts:44-54) while the card reports a MEDIAN — so the drawn geometry is by construction not the reported number.
- kneeFlexion reports 180 - interiorAngle, so a drawn interior arc is the SUPPLEMENT of the value.

This is the same discipline that makes the surviving ideal-posture prohibition meaningful: the images must not overclaim. Spec it as 'annotation depicts what was measured at the depicted instant', not 'annotation depicts the reported value'.

Also worth specing: cadence emits no evidence by design and is enforced in two independent places (cadence.ts:118-129 and METRICS_WITHOUT_EVIDENCE at evidenceFrames.ts:97).
close_reason: openspec change 'inline-annotated-evidence' authored and validated --strict. Committed 5d408c1 on worktree branch. 1 MODIFIED (Evidence frames are planned purely... — all 6 existing scenarios reproduced verbatim, 3 added), 2 REMOVED+ADDed, 4 new requirements. Reference/ideal-posture prohibition survived and was strengthened. Honesty requirement added. Surfaced 2 corrections to strides-ac9.7's per-metric table.

title: Verify the navbar clip shell live in headless Chromium
description:
CLAUDE.md's standing rule: 'Type checking and unit tests verify code correctness, not that a change actually works end to end in a browser... verify UI/pipeline changes live before calling them done.'

Run per CLAUDE.md's 'Live-browser verification harness' section: headless Chromium, real GPU (`--headless=new --enable-gpu --ignore-gpu-blocklist`), NOT SwiftShader. Confirm the renderer string is `ANGLE Metal Renderer`, not `SwiftShader Device`, before trusting any number.

Cover:
- Demo 1 (side view) and Demo 2 (front view) both reach 'Analysis complete'.
- `sampling.detectedFrames` from `[analysis-diagnostics]` is in the normal range for each clip — this is THE check that the hidden-but-mounted video elements from strides-kyu.3 did not break sampling. Compare against a pre-epic baseline captured on the same machine.
- Two clips at once: both thumbnails show their own progress, and they progress independently rather than in lockstep (only one clip holds the detector at a time).
- The modal opens on a real clip and the skeleton overlay actually draws.

Match the `[analysis-diagnostics]` prefix EXCLUSIVELY (`startsWith('[analysis-diagnostics]') && !startsWith('[analysis-diagnostics:')`) or the scale-pass line collides with it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Renderer string confirmed as real GPU, recorded in the ticket
- [ ] Demo 1 and Demo 2 both reach 'Analysis complete'
- [ ] sampling.detectedFrames recorded before and after, both in normal range
- [ ] Two-clip run shows independent per-thumbnail progress
- [ ] Modal opens and the skeleton overlay draws on a real clip
- [ ] Numbers pasted into the ticket, not just 'looked fine'
notes:
LIVE VERIFICATION (2026-08-18) — headless Chromium, real GPU, dedicated port.

Renderer: ANGLE (Apple, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro, Unspecified Version) — NOT SwiftShader.
Port 5199 (dedicated; 5173 was held by a foreign checkout). Dev server confirmed cwd = this
worktree, own node_modules. Commit 2bc2f74. Tree clean — no probe added to the repo.

NOTE ON SCOPE: this ticket's NOTES field is EMPTY (`bd show --long` renders no NOTES section;
`--json` has no such key). The G1-G5 criteria below came from the orchestrator prompt. The
description's original criterion ("sampling.detectedFrames on Demo 1") is blind to the epic's
guarantee: sequentialSampling ships enabled, so both demo clips sample via WebCodecs and never
read the <video>; Demo 1 also reads flat at 25fps. Demo 2 + playback arm is the only observable
combination.

G1 — Demo 2, playback arm {"sequentialSampling":{"enabled":false}}, sampling.path asserted
'playback' on EVERY trial. Bands: healthy 63-65, broken 47-49.
  round 1 (no warm-up), 5 trials: 48, 61, 64, 64, 64  -> median 64, range [48..64]
  round 2 (warm-up run discarded), 5 trials: 56, 64, 63, 64, 64 -> median 64, range [56..64]
  VERDICT: median 64 = HEALTHY, both rounds independently.
  The low first trials are a cold-start ramp, not concealment: monotonic in both rounds, identical
  64 steady state, and a concealment regression would read flat ~47-49 throughout.

  Default arm control, Demo 2, 3 trials + warm-up: path=sequential, detected=99 on ALL FOUR runs,
  bit-identical (matches kyu.13's documented 99->99). The sequential path shows NO cold-start ramp
  even on the cold run — which is why the playback arm's ramp is startup contention: only the
  real-time playback sampler pays wall-clock cost in lost samples.

G1a — self-re-arming requestVideoFrameCallback, 1500 ms window, real shipped markup:
  Demo 1 (25fps):    concealed 37 / preview-open 38   (expected ~37.5)
  Demo 2 (59.94fps): concealed 90 / preview-open 87   (expected ~90)
  Frames ARE presented at full rate at both frame rates. No high-frame-rate throttle.
  Concealed host = 'fixed top-0 left-[-200vw]', inert, rect x=-2878. Preview-open host =
  'absolute inset-0', not inert, loop=true.

G2 — loop scoping, two ready clips, read ONLY after both scale passes emitted terminal lines
     (captured: ['done','done']):
  no preview open : both paused=true, loop=false, inert=true, onScreen=false
  clip 1 presented: clip1 paused=false loop=true onScreen=true inert=false; clip2 UNCHANGED
                    (paused=true, loop=false) -> exactly one plays
  dismissed       : clip1 paused=true, loop=false, back offscreen+inert -> it stops

G3 — progress independence, two-clip session sampled during analysis: 37 snapshots, 36 with
     DIFFERING conditions. Distinct pairs observed: idle|loading, idle|queued, sampling|queued,
     ready|queued, ready|sampling, ready|ready. Concrete instant (t=1500ms):
       clip 1 "Analyzing… 0%"  (data-clip-condition=sampling, bar width 0%)
       clip 2 "Queued — waiting for another clip to finish analyzing…" (condition=queued)
     Not lockstep. Directly falsifies "the strip is still rendering the aggregate".

G4 — node identity across preview open -> close, asserted on the NODE (stamped property, not a
     selector match): stamps identical before/after ["node-0-8px6x2","node-1-sqsj20"]; the
     element inside [role=dialog] is that same stamped node; video count stays 2.

G5 — evidence no-regression, LAST [evidence-coverage] line per run:
  Demo 1: 7 images / 5 sections  (matches baseline exactly; 2 coverage lines, post-graft)
  Demo 2: 5 images / 4 sections  (matches baseline exactly)
  multiperson, 3 trials: 7/5, 4/3, 4/3 -> range [4..7] images, [3..5] sections (documented
    non-determinism). Variance is verticalOscillation/verticalRatio/cadence flipping to
    metric-excluded (tier-3) between trials. trunkLean = all-gated-out on all 3 trials vs the
    documented 8/6 baseline — expected consequence of f2920fa (#71) adding
    EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH/isTooFarApartPair, which drops a too-far-apart pair outright.
    Not caused by this epic; evidenceFrames.ts is out of scope here.

HUMAN-EYE CHECKS (jsdom cannot see any of these):
- Mid-sampling, add-a-clip panel OPEN, playback arm forced, 12 screenshots cropped to the video's
  OWN rect at deviceScaleFactor 4, across t=0.48..8.22s: every shot condition=sampling,
  onScreen=true, paused=false, panel open, currentTime advancing. Shots 5-8 clearly show THE
  RUNNER (blue shorts, mid-stride, shadow) inside the 96x72 frame; track, lane numbers, fence and
  seating all render. Not black, not occluded. Only element over the frame centre is the
  transparent activation button. Progress bar advances monotonically across the series.
- 390 / 640 / 1440 px, light AND dark: no horizontal page scroll at any width
  (scrollWidth === clientWidth), zero overflowing elements, frame stays exactly 96x72 at every
  width, strip present and not clipped or starved. At 'ready' the <video> is parked at x=-778 /
  -1278 / -2878 -> no stray 4K video visible anywhere.
- Record a second clip (kyu.6 path): fake device, 2 clips, both blob: srcs, both reach 'ready'.
  The recorded WebM is exactly the playback-path population kyu.13 flagged, and it completed.
- Add a demo clip via header (kyu.6 path): 1 -> 2 clips, both blob:, both ready.
- Corrupt file (.txt renamed .mp4): strip entry -> load-error (hatched bar, "! FAILED"); alert
  "This video format isn't supported. Try a different file, or record with your webcam instead."
  with TRY AGAIN VISIBLE (box 115x40 at 188,219.75) and working -> 0 alerts, full-page picker back.
- Remove a clip incl. the last: 2 -> 1 -> 0 entries, strip element unmounts entirely, full-page
  picker returns.

title: Add the navbar quick action to record or upload another clip
description:
A quick action in the navbar to add another clip, replacing the in-body 'Add another clip' block (MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:194-201) once >=1 clip exists. ## What exists today - Session-level add: `addClip` (MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:92-96) mints an id and records a `pendingLoad`; the slot consumes it once on mount (ClipSlot.tsx:70-83). - The in-body affordance is a bordered block with a

label plus a bare ` addClip(f)} />`. `FileUpload` is `multiple` (FileUpload.tsx:44) and fires `onSelected` once per file, so one picker interaction can create N clips — preserve that. - The picker's record path is `WebcamCapture`; the tabs live in `VideoInputPanel` (Record | Upload — two tabs, not three; demo buttons are a separate row at VideoInputPanel.tsx:83-93). The quick action must offer BOTH record and upload, not upload only — the current in-body affordance is upload-only, which is a gap this ticket closes. Zero-clip state keeps the full-page picker (strides-kyu.3); this action is what the picker collapses INTO.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Navbar quick action offers both record and upload
- [ ] Selecting multiple files in one interaction still creates one clip per file
- [ ] The in-body 'Add another clip' block is removed
- [ ] The action is keyboard reachable and labeled
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean
close_reason:
Header add-a-clip action shipped, and it closes the real bug: record and demo were UNREACHABLE for clips 2..N because every addClip records a pendingLoad, so the new slot's own picker (gated on status === 'empty') never rendered. Both verified live on real GPU: recording a second clip yields condition 'ready', videoDuration 2.427118, 'Clip 2 of 2: Analyzed'; the Demo 2 button yields 1.65165 and 'Combined from clip 2 of 2.'

Surface is an IN-FLOW disclosure, not an overlay — AddClipAction returns a fragment so its children land as direct flex items of the header row: trigger shrink-0 beside the strip, panel basis-full wrapping onto its own line BELOW it, with the strip flex-1 (basis 0) so it never contributes to the wrap decision. Opening grows the header downward; nothing can paint over the row above at any width.

Occlusion proven in PIXELS, not bounding boxes: with the action open for a whole playback-arm run, page.screenshot clipped to the video's own rect at 4x DPI shows the runner mid-stride at t=2.218s and gone by t=3.701s — different content across captures, so the element is genuinely painting rather than showing a frozen poster. panel.top 135.75 >= video.bottom 90. elementFromPoint deliberately not used (inert defeats it).

Multi-file fan-out holds: one setInputFiles([a,b,c]) after Demo 2 gives 4 clips, pinned by a unit test that would read as 1 call if the panel's close ever truncated it.

Mid-sampling playback arm 65 [59..65] against the 63 anchor; failure band 47-49. Dedicated port 5199 throughout because 5173 was held by a foreign checkout.

In-body affordance gone, asserted structurally: main.querySelector('input[type=file]') is null and main.textContent matches no /add (another|a) clip/i once a clip is loaded, while the trigger is inside role='banner'.

Added an optional onRecordingStateChange to ClipPicker so collapsing mid-recording cannot silently discard a take. Its test was measured FLAKY on the merged tree (2 failures in 3 runs) and fixed separately in 19b85d5 — findByRole resolves on WebcamCapture's own state while the trigger's disabled state arrives via the callback, and the two need not land in one commit.

84 files / 1198 tests, tsc + eslint + e2e green.

title: Add the clip preview modal with the skeleton overlay
description:
Clicking a navbar clip thumbnail opens a modal showing that clip's video preview with the pose skeleton/wireframe overlay.

## Reuse
`SkeletonOverlay` (src/results/SkeletonOverlay.tsx:47) already does exactly this over a live <video>: canvas absolutely positioned over the element, native canvas pixels = video-native pixels, rAF sync while playing plus one-shot redraw on seeked/timeupdate. Props are `{ videoRef, frames: RobustPoseFrame[], metadata }`. Its current call site is ClipSlot.tsx:99-103, gated on `phase === 'ready' && robustFrames && metadata`.

Note the component is coupled to a LIVE video element and its media events — it cannot render against a static image. That is fine here; the modal shows the real element.

## Interaction with the previous ticket
The clip's video element is already mounted (hidden) after strides-kyu.3. The modal REVEALS the existing element — it must not mount a second video element for the same clip, and must not remount the existing one.

## Loop behavior
results-view spec L174 requires the video to loop once analysis is ready. With clips hidden, a per-clip hidden looping video burns GPU continuously. strides-kyu.1 decides and specs this; implement whatever that change specifies.

Accessibility: focus trap, Esc to close, `aria-modal`, focus returns to the originating thumbnail on close, and the overlay canvas stays `aria-hidden`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Clicking a navbar thumbnail opens a modal with that clip's video and skeleton overlay
- [ ] The modal reveals the already-mounted element; no second video element is created for the clip and the existing one is not remounted
- [ ] Overlay stays in sync during playback and on seek while paused (the existing overlay-sync behavior is preserved)
- [ ] Esc closes, focus is trapped while open, focus returns to the originating thumbnail on close, aria-modal is set
- [ ] Loop behavior matches whatever strides-kyu.1's openspec change specifies
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean

title: Render the navbar clip strip with per-clip progress on each thumbnail
description:
Put the clip strip in the navbar next to the 'Strides' wordmark (src/App.tsx:17-28 — today the header holds only an h1 and a tagline).

One thumbnail per clip, each showing that clip's OWN processing progress as an overlay on the thumbnail.

## The progress data already exists — do not build a new state machine
Per-clip `VideoAnalysisState` carries its own `phase` and `progress` (src/results/types.ts:39-59), one instance per clip via ClipSlot.tsx:51, already collected by the parent as `clipStates: Record<string, ClipSession>` (MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:76). Read that.

Today progress is rendered GLOBALLY from the aggregate in ResultsView.tsx:97-123 ('Analyzing… 42%' / 'Processing results…' / 'Analysis complete.'). Per-clip progress has never been rendered anywhere except the 'Queued — waiting for another clip to finish analyzing…' line at ClipSlot.tsx:106-108.

Phases to represent: 'idle' | 'sampling' | 'processing' | 'ready' | 'error' (src/results/types.ts:6). A queued clip (one not currently holding the shared detector) needs a distinct visual from an actively-sampling one — only one clip holds the detector at a time (multiClipAnalysis.ts:163-172).

Accessibility: progress must be announced, not conveyed by the overlay graphic alone. Keep a `role="status"` text equivalent.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Clip strip renders in the navbar beside the wordmark, one thumbnail per clip
- [ ] Each thumbnail shows that clip's own progress, sourced from its per-clip VideoAnalysisState
- [ ] Sampling / processing / ready / error / queued are visually distinguishable, and by more than color alone
- [ ] Progress is available to assistive tech as text, not graphic-only
- [ ] Strip is usable at narrow widths (overflow/scroll rather than wrapping the navbar)
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean
notes:
=== SCOPE BOUNDARY from the strides-kyu.1 spec pass ===
Only the PER-CLIP progress percentages move to the strip. The session-level 'Analysis complete.' line and the scale-pass narration ('Measuring more metrics with a second look at the clip…' etc.) STAY in ResultsView — results-view's 'The centimetre card reflects scale-pass progress' requires that line to be always-visible, and this epic never meant to touch it. Do not delete ResultsView.tsx:97-123 wholesale.
=== THE STRIP THUMBNAIL MUST BE THE LIVE ELEMENT WHILE THAT CLIP IS ANALYSING ===
This is now a correctness requirement, not a styling choice. It resolves strides-kyu.13 (P0).

Measured: concealing a clip's <video> costs ~20-24% of sampled frames on the playback path (WebM/webcam). A genuinely VISIBLE element keeps full throughput down to at least 60 CSS px on its longest side — 62 vs a visible control's 61, versus 47-49 concealed — with NO threshold across a 61x range of painted area. On screen or not is the only variable that matters.

So: while a clip's analysis is in flight, its strip entry hosts that clip's real, on-screen, painting <video>. Once it reaches a terminal phase, the entry shows the static poster (strides-kyu.2) and the element may be concealed again. Progress renders over it either way.

TWO TRAPS the measurement hit, both of which read as healthy if you check the wrong thing:
1. **The sticky header silently occludes the top of the page.** A 120px element at top-0 is mostly buried under the ~86px header — a partial concealment that measures like a failure while every class name looks right. getBoundingClientRect reads perfectly healthy in that case. VERIFY PIXELS: screenshot a crop of the video's own rect during analysis and confirm you see the runner, not header text.
2. **elementFromPoint is useless for this check.** `inert` removes the subtree from hit-testing while leaving it fully rendered, so the hit test returns whatever is behind the video even when the video is plainly visible.
Also: trial 1 of every harness invocation reads low despite the warm-up navigation — it inflates the range but not the median.

Note this composes with D1's presentation-scoped looping (strides-kyu.5): 'presented' and 'must be on screen because it is being sampled' become two independent reasons for the same element to be visible.

title: Derive and expose a poster thumbnail per clip
description:
Net-new capability. Clips have NO thumbnail/poster/label concept today — `ClipSession` is `{ clipId, videoSource, analysis }` (src/results/multiClipAnalysis.ts:18-22) and clips are referenced positionally only ('From clip 1 of 2').

Derive a small poster image per clip so the navbar strip has something to render.

Where: the clip's own video element is already mounted and its metadata (width/height) is known once `videoSource.status === 'ready'` (src/video/types.ts:24-44). Draw one frame to a small offscreen canvas.

Keep the pure/impure split the repo already uses: any sizing/aspect math is canvas-free and unit-testable; only the draw touches a context. jsdom has no canvas (src/test/canvasTestUtils.ts).

Do NOT serialize the poster to a data URL or blob — hold the canvas/ImageBitmap in memory for the session, same rule the evidence path follows (results-view spec L688).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each clip exposes a poster image once its video source is ready
- [ ] Poster derivation does not disturb the clip's own playback position or analysis (sampling reads off the live element)
- [ ] Sizing/aspect math is unit-tested with no canvas dependency
- [ ] Poster is not serialized to a data URL, blob, or storage
- [ ] Poster is released on clip removal and session reset
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean

title: Evidence moves inline into annotated metric-card thumbnails
description:
Dissolve the standalone evidence gallery into the metric cards, and annotate each image with the
geometry the metric was actually derived from.

## Target end state
- Each metric card embeds its own image evidence inline: below the description on mobile, to the RIGHT
  of it on desktop.
- Evidence images become small thumbnails (today they are 14rem-wide gallery figures).
- Each thumbnail is ANNOTATED: the detected joints, plus the specific measurement geometry that metric
  computes (e.g. trunkLean = torso vector + vertical reference + angle arc; kneeFlexion = hip-knee-ankle
  chain + angle arc; stepWidth = lateral ankle separation caliper).
- `EvidenceGallery.tsx` is REPLACED by this, not kept alongside. Decided — do not re-litigate.

## Spec reversal — this is deliberate, not an oversight
`openspec/specs/results-view/spec.md` L746 currently states:
  "The system SHALL NOT draw a skeleton, angle arc, reference line, or any other annotation over an
   extracted image"
This epic reverses exactly that clause. IMPORTANT: reverse ONLY the ban on annotating detected/measured
geometry. The adjacent ban on overlaying a REFERENCE OR IDEAL POSTURE STAYS — thumbnails show what was
measured, never a target to match.

Also reversing: L735 "An evidence gallery renders below the results, grouped by metric" (full reversal —
prefer REMOVE with Reason/Migration + ADD under a fresh name, per CLAUDE.md), and L770 "Metric cards
deep-link to their evidence, and are otherwise unchanged" (no deep link; evidence is in the card).

KEEP AND EXTEND, do not rewrite: L648 "Evidence frames are planned purely, then extracted from a
detached video element". It already computes crops in video-native pixel space from the exemplar's
named keypoints — exactly the data the joint overlay needs.

## HARD CONSTRAINTS
1. jsdom in the unit suite has NO canvas (`getContext()` unimplemented; the repo deliberately refuses the
   `canvas` npm package — see src/test/canvasTestUtils.ts). Annotation geometry MUST live in a pure,
   canvas-free, unit-testable layer; only the final draw touches a rendering context. This mirrors the
   existing rule at results-view L655.
2. Extracted images stay in-memory for the session only — no data URL, no blob, no download, no
   persistence (results-view L688). Today the canvas ELEMENT is adopted into the DOM via
   `replaceChildren` (EvidenceGallery.tsx:296-316); `toDataURL`/`toBlob` are deliberately absent.
3. Evidence must never enter the `[analysis-diagnostics]` console payload (results-view L795) — its
   shape is a live-verification harness contract.

## Reuse, don't reinvent
`src/results/skeletonGeometry.ts` already emits pure point/edge DRAW OPS off `SKELETON_EDGES` with a
detected-vs-interpolated opacity distinction (`toDrawOps`). Reuse that model for the joint layer. Do NOT
write a second skeleton renderer. Note `SkeletonOverlay` the COMPONENT is coupled to a live `<video>`
and its media events — it cannot render against a static image; the reusable half is `toDrawOps`.

## Layout note
`MetricsPanel`'s card grid already uses CONTAINER queries (`@container`, `@lg:grid-cols-2`,
`@3xl:grid-cols-3` — MetricsPanel.tsx:288), the only container-query usage in the app. The
"below on mobile / right on desktop" split inside a card is a per-CARD container query, not a viewport
media query.

## Related (context only, do not close)
- GitHub #71 "Two evidence ghosts are unreadable" — whole-frame crops on far-apart pairs, and bystanders
  inside the 320px crop floor. Directly relevant: thumbnails are SMALLER, so crop quality matters more,
  and joint annotation makes a wrong-subject crop visible. Assess whether this epic subsumes part of it.
- GitHub #70 "extreme-role 1.5-MAD gate unreachable for overstriding" — overstriding emits no evidence on
  any clip measured, so that card gets no thumbnail regardless.
- GitHub #69 "Evidence seek lands 2 frames late on every MP4" — REAL INTERACTION: annotation drawn from
  sampled-frame keypoints onto a 2-frames-late image will be visibly misregistered. Joints will appear
  to float off the body. This epic makes an existing latent bug newly visible.
close_reason: Shipped and merged to main (4d625df). Evidence moved inline into annotated metric-card thumbnails; EvidenceGallery deleted; live-verified on 3 clips, real GPU. Forced past open children strides-ac9.10 / strides-ac9.12 — both are follow-ups discovered during the epic, not remaining epic scope, and stay open on their own.

title: Clips live in the top navbar
description:
Move clip management out of the page body and into the top navbar, next to the "Strides" wordmark.

## Target end state
- A clip strip in the navbar: one thumbnail per clip.
- A quick action in the navbar to record/upload another clip. It replaces the in-body "Add another clip" block once >=1 clip exists.
- Clicking a clip thumbnail opens a modal with that clip's video preview + the pose skeleton/wireframe overlay.
- Per-clip processing progress renders as an overlay ON that clip's navbar thumbnail — not as a separate global banner.
- Zero clips keeps a full-page picker; it collapses into the navbar quick-action once a clip exists.

## Why this is a restructure, not a re-style
Today `MultiClipVideoSession` renders every clip as a full-height `ClipSlot` stacked in a left column,
with a single GLOBAL aggregate progress line in `ResultsView`. There is no clip list UI, no tab bar, no
selector, and no per-clip label or thumbnail anywhere in the model — clips are positional only
(`ClipSession = { clipId, videoSource, analysis }`, src/results/multiClipAnalysis.ts:18-22).

## HARD CONSTRAINT — read before touching anything
Sampling reads frames off a live, PLAYING `<video>` element. Clip video elements MUST stay mounted while
analysing. Do NOT render them only when the modal is open — the modal reveals an already-mounted element.
Getting this wrong silently breaks analysis with no type or test error.

## Spec work
One openspec change covering this epic. Affected capabilities: `results-view`, `video-input`,
`multi-clip-analysis`. Notably `results-view` L174 "Video loops with overlay once analysis is ready"
needs revisiting — a hidden looping video per clip burns GPU, so the loop should likely be scoped to
modal-open.

## Known landmines
- The sticky header height is hardcoded as `86px` in three places (MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:182,203)
  and `150px` in VideoInputPanel.tsx:132. A taller navbar breaks all four.
- `e2e/multiPersonAcquisition.spec.ts` drives real selectors this redesign moves:
  `getByRole('button', {name:'Upload'})`, `locator('input[type=file]')`, `getByText(/analysis complete/i)`.

## Related (context only, do not close)
GitHub #23 "Make results layout sticky" is SUPERSEDED by this epic — the two-column video/metrics
layout goes away entirely. Recommend closing it as superseded; that call is the user's.
close_reason: Shipped and merged to main (f861ee8). Clips live in the application header strip; the two-column lg:grid layout is gone; recording and demo clips reachable for clips 2..N; the 86px/150px header constants removed from src/. Forced past open child strides-kyu.14, a follow-up that stays open on its own.

title: Show cadence on the model runner as its own footfall beat
description: From the trn2.3 UX review: cadence is the Rhythm stop's headline but has no visual (runnerAnnotations.ts:35 gives it no annotation). Proposal: pin 'N steps/min' near the head (introFlash.ts:50 position) and flash a contact ring plus a ground tick on every footfall at the real cadence - the gait's own beat, which reads as a metronome. Also from the same review: reword the 'Heel strike (proxy)' label to 'Heel first (estimate)', and align the foot-path guides with the feet (x 249/263 vs feet 222/279).

- A cadence annotation exists (label plus a per-footfall pulse synced to the model's contact phase); under reduced motion, a static label and ticks with no pulse

title: Tour on phones: runner as background, translucent stop panels
description:
## Description
Make the tour work on phones (below `lg:`).

- ModelRunner becomes a **fixed full-viewport background** behind the content.
- Each stop is a **semi-transparent panel**: background opacity ≥ 0.85 plus backdrop blur, scrolling over the runner. The runner shows through margins and gaps.
- Camera framing accounts for the panel, so the focus body part is visible in the uncovered area: it shifts the camera target up or down.
- The pause control stays inline and visible.
- Under reduced motion, the runner shows a still pose per stop.
- Skip stays reachable.
- No horizontal scroll at 360–430 px.

## Expected file paths
- src/results/tour/RunnerTour.tsx
- src/results/tour/TourStop.tsx
- src/index.css (panel tokens, if needed)
- a contrast test (like src/guidance/scalePalette.test.ts) for panel text over the worst-case runner stroke colour
- openspec/changes/add-runner-tour/specs/runner-tour/spec.md

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: B2.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Panel text meets WCAG AA contrast against the panel colour composited over both the background and the runner stroke, in light and dark. Computed in a test.
- [ ] Live at 390×844, light and dark, plus reduced motion: screenshots of 3 stops. No horizontal overflow (`document.scrollingElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth`).
- [ ] The runner pauses when the tab is hidden.
- [ ] lint, typecheck and tests pass.

Must not touch pose input (perf-no-fidelity-tradeoffs).

title: Frame-step and slow-motion playback in ClipPreviewDialog, with footstrike/evidence markers
description: From the 2026-10-16 UX review (idea #9). ClipPreviewDialog uses native <video controls> — no frame stepping, no speed control. Proposal: +/-1 frame buttons, 0.25x/0.5x speed, and timeline markers at detected footstrikes and evidence instants so a runner can verify a number themselves (the core of Kinovea/OnForm). CONSTRAINT: only enable after the clip reaches a terminal analysis phase — sampling reads frames off the live, playing element and concealment/pausing costs throughput (CLAUDE.md concealment finding, strides-kyu.13). Frame stepping should reuse the evidence seek calibration (evidenceSeekOffset.ts: edit-list shift + frame-midpoint) so a marker lands on the frame the metric measured. Effort M.

title: Local result history (numbers only, IndexedDB) with previous result beside current
description: From the 2026-10-16 UX review (idea #7). Every visit starts from zero, so Strides has no re-test loop and nothing brings a runner back. Proposal: persist per-run {date, metric values, view label, confidence tier, band source} in IndexedDB — NO video, no backend — and show the previous reading beside the current one. Needs: privacy copy update (ClipPicker privacy statement says nothing leaves the device; this stays true but now something PERSISTS), a schema/definition version per metric so a re-defined metric (e.g. strides-cjl footstrike re-timing) is not compared across definitions, and try/catch around storage (private windows). Pairs with the before/after compare bead. Effort M.

title: Share results with a coach: copy-summary + print/PDF stylesheet
description: From the 2026-10-16 UX review (idea #8). Nothing can leave the page today; ResultsView.tsx explicitly scopes save/export out. Proposal: a 'Copy summary' button (plain text) and a print stylesheet producing a clean one-page report: each metric's value, view, confidence tier/caveat, band + citation where banded, clip provenance. No video, no backend. Update the privacy copy. Effort S-M.

title: Before/after compare mode as an alternative to multi-clip fusion
description: From the 2026-10-16 UX review (idea #6, highest impact). Today adding a post-drill clip silently FUSES with the 'before' clip (multi-clip spec 'Per-metric confidence fusion' keeps the highest-confidence clip's value per metric), so the session hides exactly the change a runner wants to see. Proposal: let the reader label clips Before / After and render a per-metric change ONLY where both clips share a view and a measured (non-excluded) tier. Runner-against-themself only, never a grade. BLOCKER: clip-to-clip spread on the same runner is real (strides-2po, strides-yg8), so any 'changed' claim needs a noise floor MEASURED on same-runner repeat clips first — never an invented threshold (same discipline as 'a band is cited or it does not ship'). Effort L.

title: Prefetch MediaPipe scale-pass assets on page load
description: The MediaPipe .task model and tasks-vision WASM (~12 MB over the wire) only start downloading when a clip's analysis starts (useVideoAnalysis warmup) or reaches ready. Prefetch the bytes on page idle so they are in the HTTP cache by the time the scale pass creates its detector. Bytes only - no detector creation at page load, because creation contends with the playback sampler (strides-gyl). Must be bit-identical on ab-person-selection --evidence.
close_reason: Shipped: page-idle byte prefetch of MediaPipe assets after MoveNet ready; aborted/latched off on playback-path runs. A/B bit-identical; cache hits verified under GH-Pages-like headers with a disk-cache profile.

title: Warm the pose models while the reader picks clips
description: First MoveNet inference costs 5.7 s on a Galaxy S21 (shader compilation), on the critical path of the first analysis. Run a throwaway inference (then reset all detector state) at page idle before any clip is chosen. RISK: CLAUDE.md's determinism caveat records warm vs cold browser processes changing a detection (multiperson 103 vs 127 frames). Must be bit-identical in the fresh-process A/B; if any field moves, BLOCK and reconvene with the user.
notes: Assessed 2026-10-13, not built: shader compilation is per input resolution (S21: first inference 3.7 s, a new resolution 1.1-1.8 s), so a warm-up before a clip is chosen cannot pre-compile the clip's programs; a dummy inference also needs a full reset of MoveNet's one-euro and person-of-interest state. Low value / nonzero determinism risk. Related: DEFAULT_DETECTION_TIMEOUT_MS is 5000 and pre-6i6.1 phone first inferences were 5.7-6.9 s, so a cold first frame could time out there; now 3.7 s.

title: Scale passes interleave with primaries on a slow phone, delaying 'Analysis complete' by ~25 s
description: schedule-scale-passes-after-primaries promises P1 P2 P3 then S1 S2 S3. On a Galaxy S21, one run did that (complete at 56 s) and the next ran P1 S1 P2 S2 P3 S3 (complete at 81 s). Likely clip 2 was not ready to sample when P1 finished (its video/poster still loading), so S1 took the lane. Investigate the lane rule's readiness condition on slow devices.
notes: Merged to main b4b1b6c (not pushed). Root cause: clip 2's WebCodecs probe exceeded the 3 s timeout under main-thread contention on the S21 and the 'playback' stand-in was committed permanently - clip 2 was SAMPLED on the playback path (153 vs 345 samples) and scheduled as playback (P1 S1 P2 S2 P3 S3). Fix keeps the late answer, holds scale passes while the next clip's path is unknown (30 s give-up). Desktop: single-clip gate identical; 3-clip sessions identical with/without 6x throttle. Keep open until a phone run confirms; openspec change hold-scale-passes-for-unprobed-primaries not archived yet.
close_reason: Merged b4b1b6c; phone (S21) verified on 35b1f9c: all clips sequential 233/345/99, scale passes after primaries, Analysis complete 40 s (was 56-81 s). Archived 2026-10-13.

title: Posters and evidence images decode via <video> seeks - 12 s and 7-11 s per clip on Android
description: On a Galaxy S21 the 4K clip's poster took 12.3 s (seek+draw) and each evidence extraction 7-11 s, competing with analysis for the decoder. Derive posters from the sequential decoder's first frame (already 'derived' for clips 2-3, not clip 1) and consider WebCodecs-based evidence extraction.
notes: Review round 1 applied (e1c0467 on worktree-agent-a9f822f76043d3831): own switch __STRIDES_FORWARD_DECODE_CONFIG_OVERRIDE__, container colr passed to VideoDecoder (refuse non-nclx/unnamed), refuse pre-roll shifts, posters withdrawn to seek path (revisit after S21), flush-reject-after-delivery counts done. Gate re-run identical (nodiv md5 1dbe1208… both), pixel probe 92/92 identical. Open: S21 run.
close_reason: Merged 35b1f9c; desktop 92/92 pixel-identical, phone: analysis identical on/off, 13/14 shared images identical, seek path fails 3 late 4K instants forward delivers; session evidence 53 s vs 68 s. Posters stay on seek. Archived 2026-10-13.

title: Run pose inference in a Web Worker
description: Warm-up spikes freeze the UI regardless of per-frame yielding: first MoveNet inference 6.9 s, first MediaPipe inference 1.4-3.1 s, MediaPipe detector creation 14.5 s on a Galaxy S21. Move the sequential path (demux, VideoDecoder, MoveNet via OffscreenCanvas WebGL, MediaPipe tasks-vision, heuristics) into a worker; playback/webcam path keeps its on-screen <video> and transfers VideoFrames. No WASM threads on GitHub Pages (no COOP/COEP). Larger change; do after the yield and downscale tickets are measured.
design: Design 2026-10-13 (read-only plan): move ONLY inference into workers behind the PoseDetector interface (option a); main thread keeps demux/decode/selector/draw/pipeline/dev logs and sends createImageBitmap(canvas) zero-copy. One MoveNet worker + one MediaPipe worker per page. Playback path stays on main (off-thread inference would raise its sample count - changes results). withTimeout must move INTO the worker (main-thread timer would fire during worker warm-up and change samples); main keeps a liveness watchdog. Assert tf.getBackend()==='webgl' in worker (silent CPU fallback = different numbers). MediaPipe in a module worker needs a self.import hook (fetch + indirect eval) to load the identical wasm; worker URLs must be absolute same-origin. Slices: S0 spike (bit-identity main vs worker, desktop + S21, fresh process per arm; FAIL => BLOCKED) 1.5-2d; S1 infra behind dev flag 2-3d; S2 sequential primary 2d; S3 scale pass 1.5-2d; S4 lifecycle/fallback 1-1.5d; S5 default on 0.5-1d.
notes: BLOCKED 2026-10-13 (phone half of the spike, spike/6i6.3-worker-parity): on the Galaxy S21 the worker is NOT bit-identical. M1 vs M2 identical (48,970 fields), but worker vs main differs on 19-29 of 910 frames and worker vs worker differs on 7-24 frames, always in the LAST 2-9 frames of each clip (decoder flush), ~1-2 px keypoint deltas. Variants A (canvas->ImageBitmap) and B (VideoFrame transfer) both fail; variant D (keep the VideoFrame open until createImageBitmap resolves) narrows W1-vs-W2 to 7 frames but does not remove it. Input-pixel hashing localised the divergence to the worker's input pixels on front-approach frames 91-98 (main canvas readback perturbs the main arm, so side-landscape was inconclusive). Desktop was bit-identical. Reconvene with user: needs a hand-off that is provably identical on Android, or acceptance of tail-frame nondeterminism.

title: Decide: economy-direction framing for guided headlines (target ranges not supportable)
description: User asked (2026-10-13) for TARGET ranges most favourable for running efficiency, grouped stories, and highlighting the 1-2 metrics furthest from desirable. Economy-specific evidence sweep found no absolute (class A) economy range for any of 12 metrics, so a distance-from-desirable ranking cannot be cited. Needs a user product decision before strides-83m is revised.
notes: Economy evidence sweep 2026-10-13 (subagent; sources opened unless marked). cadence: C relative-to-self (self-selected near metabolic optimum; Moore 2016 doi 10.1007/s40279-016-0474-4; de Ruiter 2014 PMID 23581294; Cavanagh&Williams 1982) + weak B across runners r -0.20 (Van Hooren 2024 PMC11127892, k=37 n=593). verticalOscillation/Cm: B observational, lower ~ lower cost, pooled r 0.35 mostly absolute displacement; normalised r 0.20 k=2 n.s.; Folland 2017 PMC5473370 n=97 r 0.534 pelvis stance-only 3D. verticalRatio: D, no peer-reviewed economy link; Garmin zones are percentile ranks. trunkLean: D (Folland: performance not economy; Moore contradictory). kneeFlexion swing: weak B, less flexion ~ lower cost r -0.405, Folland only. overstriding: D, r 0.04 k=7 (Van Hooren). footStrikePattern: D, SMD -0.02 k=6. stepWidth/Cm: C, deviation from preferred raises cost 3-15% (Arellano&Kram 2011 PMID 21316058, numbers partly UNVERIFIED). kneeDrive: D. armSwingAmplitude: B for presence only (Arellano&Kram 2014 PMID 25031455), not amplitude. UNVERIFIED: Quinn 2021 +7% cadence -11% VO2. Conclusion: no class A anywhere; one clip cannot reveal preferred value so class C distance is uncomputable; effect-size ranking ranks metrics not the runner. Prior: strides-3f6.4 reached the same no-target result for the 5 banded metrics.
close_reason: Shipped: energy-cost story headlines (normal-tier, costly side of cited band) + strides-3f6 spec back-fill; pushed to origin/main 65de007, merged locally as 749b282

title: Let 'Analysis complete' paint before the scale pass's first blocking detect
description: Gate 6 (2026-10-05): when the MediaPipe scale-pass detector is already warm at primary 'ready', the primary-ready -> 'Analysis complete' status gap grows to ~310-350 ms (multiperson 34->320 ms, front-approach 125->345 ms; side-portrait/landscape already 334-516 ms at gate 5, where the T2 warm-up finished in time). The extra ~230-290 ms matches the scale pass's first synchronous MediaPipe detect (222-244 ms incl. warm-up). Hypothesis: the scale-pass effect reaches the first detectForVideo before the browser paints/settles the status. Fix candidate: in useVideoAnalysis's scale-pass effect, yield one paint (e.g. await requestAnimationFrame + setTimeout 0) before calling sampleClipAdaptive. Then retry strides-e4c.7 (reverted) on top. Gate: bit-identical A/B; primary-ready->status gap on all 4 clips; scale done@ cost <= ~20 ms.
notes: PROBE RESULT (2026-10-05, verifier). Arms: g5 = e4905d2 (code-identical to 453cb4a, n=3/6 from gate 6), e4c.7 = 129f9ba (gate 6, n=3/6), A = e4c8 @ 42cd4bd (yield rAF+setTimeout before the scale pass's first detect), B = e4c8b @ 5f38ecf (A + e4c.7). perf-stage-timings 3 fresh-process trials, real GPU ANGLE Metal M4 Pro, derived ports, identity verified; symlinked node_modules worked. Primary-ready -> 'Analysis complete' gap (ms), g5 / e4c.7 / A / B: landscape 418-451 / 471-516 / 412-453 / 467-480; portrait 334-355 / 351-360 / 339-358 / 333-356; approach 109-142 / 343-346 / 111-118 / 347-355; multiperson 34-38 / 308-330 / 36-73 / 309-334. Median complete@ g5/e4c.7/A/B: landscape 4707/4760/4376/4571, portrait 4436/4369/4412/4227, approach 2786/3105/2784/3246, multiperson 3469/3754/3524/3656 (start@ noise of +-300 is folded in; the gap is the clean signal). Scale detectorWait approach 208 / 8 / 207 / 8; other clips 8 everywhere. Scale done@ approach 4160/4081/4212/4235. The yield does NOT shrink the gap in either arm, so the 'first synchronous detect blocks the paint' hypothesis is REFUTED. Observed correlate instead: the gap is ~36-140 ms when the warm-up settles within ~250 ms of primary ready (multiperson -220..+70, approach +220..+250), and ~340-470 ms when it settled ~0.8-1.1 s earlier (landscape, portrait, and every clip under e4c.7). Mechanism unknown; the gap is measured by Playwright's getByText waitFor, so part of it may be observation latency rather than paint, unverified. A/B harness on B (3 trials, 4 clips, --evidence) BIT-IDENTICAL: stripped md5 577597202f4c7675a92b2fbfd0ade236, rtk proxy diff empty. Recommendation: NEITHER - A is a no-op on the gap, and B reproduces e4c.7's +230-290 ms on approach/multiperson.
close_reason: Won't do (measured): yielding a paint before the scale pass's first detect leaves the primary-ready->status gap unchanged (side-portrait 339-358 vs 334-355 ms, side-landscape 412-453 vs 418-451). Hypothesis refuted; mechanism unknown, possibly Playwright getByText detection lag rather than a paint delay.

title: Removing a clip before the active one hands the shared detector to the next clip mid-run
description: Pre-existing (found in strides-4vu review, 2026-10-05). MultiClipVideoSession.tsx removeClip (~line 149) never decrements activeClipIndex, so removing an EARLIER clip shifts the index onto the next clip while the clip that held the detector may still be sampling (primary or playback-path scale pass). Breaks the serialization rule (never two passes on the shared detector / never a primary alongside a scale pass). Fix: key the active clip by clipId, or decrement the index in removeClip.

title: Feed decoded VideoFrames straight to MediaPipe instead of a 4K 2D canvas
description: sampleClipSequential.ts draws every selected VideoFrame onto a full-resolution 2D canvas, closes the frame, then detects on the canvas. MediaPipe detectForVideo accepts VideoFrame. Let PoseFrameSource optionally carry the VideoFrame; detectors that accept it (mediapipePoseLandmarker) use it, MoveNet keeps the canvas (tfjs 4.22 fromPixels has no VideoFrame branch). Frame must now close after detect resolves, still one open frame at a time, closed on every error/timeout/cancel path. Skip the canvas draw entirely when the detector does not need it.
acceptance_criteria: Scale-pass per-frame time drops vs T0 baseline. Primary pass bit-identical on the A/B gate. Scale-pass diagnostics (verticalOscillationCm, stepWidthCm, subjectAgreement) compared before/after with a driver that waits for the scale-pass line; any moved field reported to the user, not accepted silently. No VideoFrame leak (test asserts close on every path).
notes:
PLAN (2026-10-05): MediaPipe tasks-vision 1.0.1 routes every ImageSource through the same texImage2D on its own WebGL2 canvas, so no readback either way. A canvas costs a 4K VideoFrame->2D canvas conversion plus a cross-context 4K copy at upload; a VideoFrame costs one conversion. drawMs only times issuing drawImage; the GPU work lands in detectMs, so 'draw is 1%' understates it but the true cost is unknown. Not provably bit-identical (Chrome colour conversion paths differ; HDR HLG HEVC risk). Expected 0.3-2 ms/frame, 0-5% of scale sampling. PROBE FIRST: dev-only window.__STRIDES_PROBE_MP_VIDEOFRAME__, scale-pass call only, close frame right after the synchronous estimatePose call (before awaiting). Compare scale detectMs p50/sum (+drawMs) excluding the first detect, plus verticalOscillationCm/stepWidthCm/subjectAgreement. <5% -> close won't-do; >=10% -> implement full design (PoseFrameSource.image union widened to VideoFrame, PoseDetector.acceptsVideoFrame flag on mediapipe only, lazy 2D canvas, close-after-call, tests for close on every path).
PROBE RESULT (2026-10-05, verifier). Throwaway worktree at db25af3 + dev-only patch (scale-pass sampleClipAdaptive gets probeDirectVideoFrame when window.__STRIDES_PROBE_MP_VIDEOFRAME__; handleSelectedFrame skips resize/drawImage, passes the VideoFrame as image with displayWidth/Height, closes it right after the synchronous estimatePose, then awaits). perf-stage-timings copy with init-script pass-through + scale-pass line capture, 3 fresh-process trials/arm, real GPU ANGLE Metal M4 Pro; flag confirmed on 3/3 ON trials and off 3/3 OFF. Scale-pass medians OFF->ON: detect p50 side-landscape(4K) 9.4->6.1 (-35%), side-portrait(1080x1920) 6.0->5.8 (-3%), front-approach(4K portrait) 8.9->6.0 (-33%), multiperson(1080p) 6.2->5.6 (-10%); detect sum excl. max (first-detect warm-up ~230-245 ms, unchanged) -29% / -3% / -32% / -13%; draw+detect -30% / -4% / -33% / -14%; scale sampling total 2954->2209 / 2815->2726 / 1270->958 / 1981->1741 ms. Per-trial p50 spread <=0.3 ms, arms fully separated. NOT output-identical (deterministic within each arm, moves between arms): scale-pass detectedFrames 120->121, 268->268, 87->90, 122->119; scale-pass diagnostics verticalOscillationCm 7.193377553410146->7.1816841854822275, null->7.7664918065729065 (portrait now resolves), 10.486597716761532->12.154910045698127 (+16%), 7.164784594691125->7.596294516087427; stepWidthCm -14.2397->-14.4940, -5.0399->-0.8839, 3.4777->3.9377, -3.4570->-14.7128; subjectAgreement 105/106 same, 270/270->271/271, 99/99->93/99 (approach), 87/89 same. Pre-registered rule: p50 >=10% on the 4K clips (and at the threshold on 1080p) -> IMPLEMENT on cost grounds; but the realised 'not provably bit-identical' risk is large (grafted front-approach VO_cm +16%, subjectAgreement drops 6 instants), so the full design needs an explicit accept-different-pixels decision, or a root-cause first (YUV->RGB conversion path vs coded-vs-visible size in texImage2D of a VideoFrame: unverified). Probe worktree deleted, nothing committed.
BLOCKED ON USER DECISION (2026-10-05): probe says scale-pass detect is 25-35% cheaper on 4K clips (10% on 1080p, 3% on 1080x1920) with VideoFrames, but scale-pass outputs move deterministically: front-approach verticalOscillationCm 10.4866 -> 12.1549 (+16%, user-visible grafted value), subjectAgreement 99/99 -> 93/99; side-portrait VO_cm null -> 7.77; stepWidthCm swings. Cause unknown (VideoFrame YUV->RGB upload path vs 2D canvas colour conversion, or coded vs visible size). Options: (1) accept numeric change, (2) root-cause first, (3) won't-do.
2026-10-06 user decision: root-cause the output difference; if we can't get to the bottom of it, drop. Then merge perf/e4c and clean up.
ROOT CAUSE (2026-10-06, pixel experiment, real GPU M4 Pro, fresh process): all demo/e2e clips are BT.2020/HLG HDR (frame.colorSpace primaries bt2020, transfer hlg, matrix bt2020-ncl, NV12; coded==display==visible, no crop/padding). 2D canvas drawImage(VideoFrame) does colour-managed HLG->sRGB conversion; texImage2D(VideoFrame) (MediaPipe's route) does not, giving raw brighter RGB. Canvas->texImage2D == getImageData exactly (max 0). Frame->texImage2D vs canvas: approach 4K max d 60/62/80, 99.96% px differ, mean signed +13.5/+14.1/+14.7; multiperson max 51/38/70, mean +10/+12.9/+13.5; same dims, not flipped, delta is tonal not spatial. UNPACK_COLORSPACE_CONVERSION_WEBGL=NONE, new VideoFrame(), createImageBitmap(frame, any colorSpaceConversion) do not help (bitmap worse, +36). Only frame.copyTo({format:'RGBA',colorSpace:'srgb'}) matches (max d 1, ~5-7% px) but costs 682 ms/frame at 4K vs 18 ms (canvas route) -- useless. No zero-copy identical route. VERDICT B: drop e4c.4.
close_reason: Dropped (root cause understood, no identical-pixel fast route). The demo clips are BT.2020/HLG HDR (NV12, limited range). 2D-canvas drawImage(VideoFrame) colour-manages HLG->sRGB; MediaPipe's texImage2D(VideoFrame) does not, giving brighter RGB (mean +10..+15/channel, max 60-80, ~99.9% of pixels). No pixelStorei option changes it; createImageBitmap is worse; only frame.copyTo(RGBA, srgb) matches (max delta 1) and costs 682 ms/frame vs 18. title: Determine whether defensible desirable targets exist for guided metrics
description: Selected review item #9 asks to consider desirable targets alongside observed ranges. Review primary research and source context for each currently banded metric and any proposed target. Record which claims are intervention targets, population descriptions, context-dependent directions, or unsupported. Do not derive a universal ideal from Garmin percentiles or observational ranges. Expected files for findings: existing guidance/spec design material or Beads issue notes; implementation contract in src/guidance/types.ts and metricGuidance.ts only if supported. Coordinate with strides-83m because it separately works on cited consequences and cues.
acceptance_criteria: Each candidate target has a source, population, outcome, relevant pace/context, and suitability decision; unsupported universal thresholds are explicitly rejected; the implementation issue receives a concrete matrix and exact permitted wording, including a no-target result where evidence is insufficient.
notes: Target decision for guided bands (2026-10-05). Exact permitted UI wording for all five: "Observed, not a target" Do not render a desirable numeric band. Cadence: Garmin fenix 7 manual describes percentiles, population/sample/protocol unstated, no outcome; https://www8.garmin.com/manuals/webhelp/GUID-C001C335-A8EC-4A41-AB0E-BAC434259F92/EN-US/GUID-EE9E7F6F-49BE-4452-82E6-B40371D0AEC1.html . Baumgartner 2019 randomized 38 recreational runners with baseline at most 85 strides/min, at least 15 miles/week, using treadmill baseline; 10% increase for 6 weeks changed preferred stride rate, not proven injury/performance benefit or a fixed ideal; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31264286/ . Huber 2024 randomized 33 novice/recreational runners, 12-minute indoor track test, metronome 5-10% above baseline for two weeks; cadence changed, biomechanics did not, no heart rate/perceived exertion/distance group difference; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38179589/ . Suitability: optional relative experiment only, conditional on runner interest/goal, never 180 spm or automatic advice at 174. Vertical ratio: Garmin zones describe sensor readings in undisclosed population; this app halves them for per-stride units. No intervention tested against this exact video-derived ratio or validated individual outcome; source https://www8.garmin.com/manuals-apac/webhelp/fenix7series/EN-SG/GUID-CC006ABA-CE80-45BE-BD87-5B5A0FBC1125-3223.html . Suitability: no target. Vertical oscillation cm: Malisoux 2023 describes 860 healthy recreational treadmill runners at preferred speed, speed/sex-stratified distributions, no intervention outcome; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37868213/ . Moore 2016 reviews lower bounce and economy but gives no suitable cm threshold for a video user; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26816209/ . Suitability: no target. Trunk lean: Folland 2017 observed 97 trained runners at 10-12 km/h and reports technique/performance associations, no prescribed angle or individual causal outcome; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28263283/ . Suitability: no target, directional tradeoffs. Knee flexion: Folland 2017 observed the same 97 at 10-12 km/h; no intervention threshold or injury/performance target for swing flexion; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28263283/ . Suitability: no target; pace and angle conventions further limit comparison. Malisoux says reference values may help clinicians where a causal link with injury is suspected, a context this app cannot diagnose. Exact optional prompt for cadence: "If you choose to raise step rate:"; source states protocol, not a recommendation or demonstrated injury benefit.
close_reason: Reviewed five band sources and recorded target decision, study scope, and permitted wording

title: kneeFlexion reports front-view values (163-166 deg, 68 deg) instead of withholding
description: On front/rear private fixtures IMG_9114/9115/9116 (view ambiguous), kneeFlexion reads 166.1/162.9/68.1 deg at confidence 0.13/0.16/0.13. 166 deg is a near-straight knee at peak flexion; 68 deg contradicts it on the same runner. Question: is a value at that confidence rendered to the user (tier), and should a sagittal-plane angle be withheld when the view is not side? Baseline commit 83cccf7.
close_reason: Not a bug. viewFit is 'unsuitable' on front/ambiguous views (types.ts view-fit table), so metricTier (metricConfidence.ts:63) excludes it: no value is rendered in the classic or guided view, as results-view spec requires. The 166/163/68 deg readings exist only in the dev harness output. Also, value = flexion from extension (180 - joint angle, kneeFlexion.ts:213): larger means more bent.

description: Private fixtures IMG_9114 (front approach) and IMG_9116 (long front approach) resolve view 'ambiguous' at confidence 0.3: bilateralSpreadRatio 0.55/0.57 votes front, sagittalExcursionRatio 0.60/0.59 abstains (front <=0.40, side >=0.80). title: Animate detected runner in motion story
description: The motion story currently animates only an illustrative two-pose runner during analysis; the detected pose holds still once results appear. Animate a short loop from the selected metric’s actual robust pose frames while preserving a trustworthy still-evidence comparison. Keep the winning clip and scale-pass provenance, respect reduced motion, and provide a clear play/pause interaction.

A paused state aligns the detected trace with its ghosted still evidence. Missing or sparse pose frames degrade clearly. Metric scrolling, mobile detail view, keyboard controls, screen readers, and reduced-motion preference work. Existing metric calculations and evidence canvases remain unchanged; tests, lint/build, and browser QA pass.

Recovered exact reviewed five-file change after temporary worktree cleanup; production CSS/JS hashes matched prior build. title: Add reference-to-runner wireframe story to analysis and results
description: Build a 2D illustrative running wireframe during clip analysis, morph to the detected runner once analysis is ready, and focus each metric on its own detected wireframe plus ghosted clip evidence as the reader scrolls. Keep the reference illustrative rather than a universal ideal; use the metric’s actual source clip in multi-clip results. Preserve existing metric calculations and evidence cards.

Scrolling metric results changes a dedicated visualization to the focused metric and its own evidence/source clip. Missing evidence has a clear fallback. Mobile, keyboard, reduced-motion and screen-reader behavior work. Existing metrics are unchanged; tests, lint, build, and real-browser checks pass.

title: Add swing-foot lateral excursion metric for front or rear running clips
description: Why: the requested vertical-line signal is how far a foot travels sideways relative to the runner during swing. It is distinct from conventional heel-whip foot rotation and from existing stepWidth, which samples lateral ankle offset only at footstrike. Work: derive a per-side swing-phase lateral foot-path statistic from available pose points, normalize for subject scale and camera approach, fit/gate the front-or-rear view, expose it across heuristic results, fusion, guidance, card copy, evidence, tests and OpenSpec. Use the park-approach demo for real-footage validation; keep the result null or low confidence when swing events/pose are unmeasurable. Name the metric to describe lateral excursion, never foot rotation or heel whip.
acceptance_criteria: On the front-approach demo and controlled synthetic front/rear fixtures, the metric reports a directionally correct swing-foot lateral excursion distinct from stepWidth; side-view or unreliable tracking yields honest low-confidence/null behavior; evidence depicts the measured foot path; relevant tests, lint, build, spec validation and live clip checks pass without changing existing metrics.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add heel-whip biometric from validated rear-view signal
description: Why: users need a visible heel-whip measure, but a front-facing camera hides the conventional transverse-plane foot rotation and the current production detector does not emit heel/forefoot landmarks. After strides-ahd validates a signal on rear-view footage, add per-side medial/lateral early-swing measurement with conservative confidence and null-on-unmeasurable behavior. Include camera orientation gating, metric result/fusion, runner-facing copy, evidence frames and marks, automated tests, OpenSpec delta, and live clip validation. Do not substitute knee valgus, step width, or generic ankle displacement under the heel-whip name. Preserve existing metric outputs on current demo clips.
acceptance_criteria: A rear-view clip with visible heel whip produces a repeatable, directionally correct result against manual annotations; unsuitable front/side clips and backends without required landmarks do not show a confident heel-whip value; the UI explains the measured quantity and shows matching evidence; relevant tests, lint, build, spec validation, and live regression checks pass.

title: Validate rear-view heel-whip footage and detector signal
description: Why: conventional heel whip is medial/lateral foot rotation during initial swing, measured from a posterior view. The current clips contain side and front-approach views; the front clip occludes the heel, the default MoveNet backend has no heel/forefoot landmarks, and front and rear share one view label. Work: obtain or identify usable rear-view running footage with visible heel whip and a comparison without it; annotate swing/contact instants and direction; probe MediaPipe heel/forefoot landmarks or a shoe silhouette across repeated strides; establish a reliable rear-versus-front gate and abstention criteria before selecting a numeric estimator. This is a prerequisite for publishing the biometric.
acceptance_criteria: A usable rear-view clip and comparison are identified with reuse rights; manual direction/peak annotations exist; a repeatable probe shows which measured signal agrees with the visible rotation across strides; front-approach and side footage demonstrably abstain; any detector limitations are documented.

title: Narrative headlines above the fold in the guided results view
description: The guided view presents every metric at equal weight against a cited band. A runner wants to know first what is worth their attention and what they can do about it. Add a cited consequence per metric, and an above-the-fold headline section that admits only metrics carrying a resolved value, a cited consequence and a cited cue — everything else collapses below. Narrative voice is built from measured consequences and measured interventions, never verdicts, so the existing SHALL NOT against grading the runner stands unamended.
design: openspec/changes/narrative-metric-headlines/ — proposal, design (D1-D8), spec delta (6 ADDED requirements), tasks. Validated --strict. Key finding: only 4 of 12 metrics carry a studied cue (cadence, verticalOscillationCm, overstriding, verticalOscillation) and they collapse into 2 physical stories, so a clip yields 0-2 headlines, never 4. The grading prohibition needs no exception: a headline is position + cited consequence (subject = the quantity, never the runner) + cited cue. Font/running-style idea explicitly out of scope.
notes: 2026-10-13: implemented + archived on worktree branch worktree-agent-adbcb582c6b6048d4 commit 2b6c2fd. Not merged. Live: only park-approach triggers (bounce, 10.5 cm, caveated).
close_reason: Shipped: energy-cost story headlines (normal-tier, costly side of cited band) + strides-3f6 spec back-fill; pushed to origin/main 65de007, merged locally as 749b282

title: Guided view: retimed (slow-motion) clip's cadence gets the generic 'not enough data' capture hint
description:
Found live in strides-kgi.7 on park-side-portrait.mp4 (?view=guide, real GPU, fresh Chromium).

Cadence lands in "Not measured on this clip" with:
  To measure this next time: Record several seconds of steady running, with the whole body in frame the whole time.
  This clip looks like slow-motion footage — the step rhythm was measured, but a steps-per-minute figure would be wrong by however much the clip was slowed down. Every other measurement on this clip is unaffected.

The hint contradicts the reason directly under it: that clip IS 12 s of steady running with the whole body in frame. The advice a reader needs is "upload the clip at real speed / not slow-motion".

Cause: captureHintFor (src/results/guidedGroups.ts) chooses by cause from exactly two options — viewFit === 'unsuitable' -> captureHints.wrongAngle, else captureHints.notEnoughData. Cadence withheld by the sub-floor retiming detection (strides-b4f, cadence.ts `hipBounce.subFloorRhythm` branch) is neither, and MetricResult carries no structured signal for it — only the caveat string — so the guided layer cannot tell it apart without either a structured field on the cadence result or string-matching the caveat. That contract question is why this is filed rather than fixed inline.

Repro: npm run dev on the derived port; open /strides/?view=guide; Upload tab -> src/video/demo-clips/park-side-portrait.mp4; wait for "Analysis complete."; open "Not measured on this clip"; read the Cadence entry.

title: Archive the openspec change and record the guided view in CLAUDE.md
description:
Close the change out: archive the openspec change and record what shipped.

STEPS
1. `openspec validate guided-results-view --strict` once more against the implemented code.
2. Tick every item in the change's tasks.md.
3. `openspec archive guided-results-view --yes`. Confirm the new capability's spec landed in
   openspec/specs/ and that nothing was silently dropped — CLAUDE.md warns that the archive step
   matches deltas by name and silently drops what it cannot match. Diff openspec/specs/ before and
   after and check the requirement count.
4. Add a short CLAUDE.md section for the guided view: where it lives, how to reach it (`?view=guide`),
   which five metrics carry bands and which seven deliberately do not, and the one-line reason
   (no invented thresholds — a band is cited or it does not ship). Keep it proportionate; do not
   restate the whole design.
5. Close the epic's child beads and note the follow-ups the epic deliberately deferred.

FOLLOW-UPS TO FILE AS BEADS (do not implement)
- verticalOscillation (% of torso) has a derivable band — Folland 0.052 H / Winter's torso fraction
  0.288 H = ~0.18 torso lengths, range 0.11-0.26, and this repo's own readings (~18-25%) land inside
  it. It was NOT shipped because the derivation passes through a textbook anthropometric constant
  and an ambiguous per-stride vs per-step convention in Folland's pelvis figure. Resolving Folland's
  convention would unblock it.
- Whether to flip the default from classic to guide once the user has lived with it.
- Migrating the eight hand-rolled `makeMetric` test factories onto src/results/__fixtures__/.

BOUNDARIES
- No behavioural code changes in this ticket. If validation or archiving surfaces a real defect,
  file it and stop rather than fixing it here.

VERIFY: `openspec validate --strict` across all changes, plus `npx tsc -b && npm test && npm run lint`.
