title: kneeFlexion evidence picks a candidate whose knee is at the frame edge
description:
On park-side-landscape.mp4 the kneeFlexion card can render its peak-flexion pair at t=3.5167 (left leg), where the knee resolves at frame x=16 on a 3840-wide frame. focusAimedCropRect cannot centre a joint that close to the edge — the aim clamps to x=0 — so focusOffset comes out 0.4499 (0.5 is on the edge) and the runner is jammed against the left of the image with background filling the right. Measured live via a [cand-probe] instrumentation of planExemplarWithFallback, 3-clip demo session, fresh headless Chromium, real GPU.

The placement layer (strides-dxd) is working correctly and is on main; this is a SELECTION defect. outranksForFallback only consults focusOffset to break EXACT quality ties. The badly-framed candidate scores 0.993409 against the well-framed t=2.5 right-leg pair's 0.806473, so it wins outright on quality whenever its trough does not collapse. In a cold headless run that trough DOES collapse (demotion 'collapsed-pair'), the candidate is filed as demoted, and the 0.806 pair wins — which is why this reproduces in a warm real browser and not in the harness.
acceptance_criteria: A candidate whose focus joint is clamped hard against a frame edge does not outrank a materially better-framed candidate of the same metric. Verified by driving the 3-clip demo in a warm browser and confirming kneeFlexion's rendered exemplar has focusOffset well below 0.45, without regressing the three-clip evidence coverage table.
notes: Probe recipe: log metric/kind/t/quality/demotion/focusOffset/crop/focus from planExemplarWithFallback's loop right after 'if (plan === null) continue', drive the demo button, filter [cand-probe]. Revert after measuring.

title: Give overstriding an interpretive band so cross-clip disagreement can surface on it
description:
Split out of strides-5hj on 2026-09-05. strides-5hj shipped a threshold-free cross-clip disagreement caveat, but it covers footStrikePattern ONLY - 1 of 12 metrics - and NOT overstriding, which is the metric behind the original user report ('overstriding seems wrong, 50% of torso for my three demo clips').

WHY IT IS NOT COVERED. The shipped rule surfaces a disagreement where the losing clip lands in a
different CATEGORY of a band the metric already owns and already ships. footStrikePattern owns
classifyFootStrike (heel|midfoot|forefoot, symmetric footStrikeMidfootBandRatio = 0.05 dead zone)
and uniquely renders that WORD as the card's value. overstriding owns no classifier at all -
overstriding.ts:355-369 forks on travelDirectionKnown, viewFit and usableStrikeCount, never on the
value.

WHY A SIGN RULE DOES NOT WORK, so nobody re-derives it. The measured pair is +0.512135
(side-landscape) vs -0.00809497 (side-portrait). The signs differ, but -0.008 is indistinguishable
from zero: a sign rule fires there on 0.008 of a torso, and would stay SILENT on two same-signed
readings a torso-length apart. Same objection rules out stepWidth/stepWidthCm, whose 'value < 0'
crossover-gait boundary has zero width.

WHY NOT JUST PICK A NUMBER. A per-metric magnitude threshold means eleven unjustifiable constants.
CLAUDE.md's '4K area floor cannot be re-derived' section is this repo's worked example of measuring
a threshold, finding it inside a factor-of-2.9 squeeze, and abandoning the direction rather than
tuning it. A disagreement threshold picked to make these two clips light up is the same mistake.

TWO ROUTES, both needing a decision this ticket does not make:
1. Give overstriding a real interpretive band in its own module - decided on that metric's terms
   (what counts as overstriding vs neutral vs understriding), not invented in the fusion layer.
   Then the shipped rule covers it for free.
2. State every eligible clip's number unfiltered ('clip 1 read 51.2%, clip 2 read -0.8%'). Genuinely
   threshold-free and covers all twelve - but it fires on 51.2% vs 51.1% too, and suppressing THAT
   is exactly what needs a materiality threshold. The strides-5hj design never actually argued
   against this option; it is the one a reader will reach for.

Note the upstream cause is separate and already filed: the two clips ran DIFFERENT footstrike
detectors (side-portrait's hip fit is below cadenceMinFitR2, so it uses the ankle-difference
fallback), which is strides-aha. Fixing that may make the disagreement largely evaporate, which
would change which route above is worth building.

comments.author: Caleb Brewer
comments.text: Evidence from strides-kgi (guided-results-view, 2026-09-15): a literature pass for route 1 found NO published basis for an overstriding band in this app's unit. No study normalises foot-to-hip horizontal distance by torso length (targeted Europe PMC search); no threshold exists in any unit (Baker 2024: 'no consensus on what qualifies as excessive overstriding'; Souza 2016's clinical 2D protocol uses this app's exact landmarks and is explicitly dichotomous); the two published absolute measurements of the same geometry disagree ~3.4x (Heiderscheit 2011 9.2 cm COM-to-heel vs Lieberman 2015 0.31 m ankle-to-hip). The guided view therefore ships overstriding unbanded. Full record: openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-15-guided-results-view/design.md D5.1. Route 1 looks closed on evidence; route 2 (state each clip's number unfiltered) is untouched.

title: Overstriding's card reports a median but its picture is an extreme pair, and the ramp is unreachable
description:
Measured under strides-tj5, 3 trials, zero spread, real GPU, add-measure-revert probe.

overstriding emits an EXTREME pair exemplar (overstrideRange), scored by the extreme-role typicality ramp: quality = min(1, |v - median| / (3*MAD)) per end, pairQuality = min of the two. Clearing MIN_EXEMPLAR_QUALITY 0.5 therefore needs an instant >= 1.5 MADs from the median on EACH side.

park-side-landscape: 5 strikes, MAD 0.12383, distribution usable, detectionFactor 1.0 everywhere. Max devMads over the WHOLE clip is 1.3234 — not one instant clears 1.5, on either side. Structurally unreachable, at any detectionFactor. Best pair quality 0.36723.

park-side-portrait: 13 strikes, MAD 0.45163. Best low end 1.8070 MADs (0.60233, clears); best high end 1.2913 MADs (0.43044, does not). Pair scores 0.43044.

So overstriding renders a number on both side clips and an image on neither. Meanwhile strides-ddj already put overstrideRange in SINGLE_INSTANT_KINDS *because the card reports a MEDIAN* — so a representative-role exemplar (typicality = 1 - spread, median-most strike scoring near 1.0) would both render reliably and match what the card actually reports.

This is a product decision about what the picture MEANS, not a threshold tweak: today's label reads 'Furthest-reaching footstrike, ghosted against the closest-landing one'. Overlaps strides-9uj (n=2 extreme-pair framing vacuous) and strides-n66 (composition points at the ghost). Do NOT resolve it by moving MIN_EXEMPLAR_QUALITY — overstriding and trunkLean land at exactly 0.500 on the clips where they do emit, so shaving the ramp takes coverage out elsewhere.
acceptance_criteria: A decision, with evidence, on whether overstriding's evidence image should depict its measured range or a representative strike — and if the latter, the label and annotation follow.

title: Evidence coverage names WHICH layer withheld an image but not by how much
description:
strides-tj5 split all-gated-out into no-candidates / below-quality-gate / undrawable, which names the responsible LAYER. It does not carry the MARGIN.

On the two side clips overstriding's best exemplar pair scores 0.36723 (park-side-landscape) and 0.43044 (park-side-portrait) against MIN_EXEMPLAR_QUALITY 0.5 — the numbers that would tell a reader whether the gate was missed narrowly or structurally. Neither reaches [evidence-coverage], because selectExemplars returns undefined rather than reporting what it dropped, so the plan layer sees an absent exemplars field and cannot distinguish 'the metric formed no candidate' from 'the metric's own gate kept them all'.

Recovering it needs a MetricResult field (e.g. exemplarShortfall: the best candidate quality when none cleared the gate) set at all eleven selectExemplars call sites, plus a coverage-line row. Judged materially beyond an evidence-planning fix and deliberately not done in strides-tj5.
acceptance_criteria: A reader can tell from [evidence-coverage] alone whether a metric's exemplar gate was missed narrowly or is structurally unreachable on that clip, without a probe patch.

title: Make the evidence walk's last-resort rule quality-aware so a demoted higher-quality single can beat a lower-quality pair
description:
Follow-up from strides-dxd review round 1.

planExemplarWithFallback treats 'renders as a PAIR' as unconditionally better than 'demoted to a single', at ANY rank (the strides-ddj ordering). That was correct when alternates lists were short and the demoted candidate was always the SAME candidate's own base. It is wrong once a metric offers its whole ranked candidate list: a well-framed, quality-1.000 collapsed single can be displaced by a materially worse-scoring genuine pair further down the list.

MEASURED (strides-dxd, park-side-landscape.mp4, kneeDrive):
  with alternates: t=3.283, quality 0.7437, genuine pair — runner smaller and cut off at the
                   crop's right edge, a fence post down the middle, and the 35% ghost sitting on a
                   bystander in a white cap (present in the source frame).
  without:         t=2.266667, quality 1.000, collapsed single — well framed.
The 0.7437 is the peak's own typicalityFactor, not a detectionFactor artifact (pairQuality is a
Math.min and detectionFactor over kneeDrive's 2-keypoint seed can only be 0/0.5/1). Typicality is
what that card's median number is about, so the drop is a real loss of representativeness.

CONSEQUENCE, and why this bead exists: kneeDrive was reverted to candidates.slice(0, 1) in
strides-dxd rather than carrying alternates, purely to avoid this. It keeps cropFocus (aiming alone
already reaches 0.500/0.500 on its old instant — verified from the discarded head candidate's own
crop, centre (2155.62, 1478.61), the knee to full precision). So kneeDrive is left one parity bit
from the same even-pool tie kneeFlexion actually hit: its pool has no active tie on this corpus, and
nothing guarantees that on other footage.

FIX SHAPE: make the pair-beats-demoted preference quality-aware rather than unconditional, so both
knee metrics (and any future representative-instant metric) can carry alternates with no regression.
Needs a threshold or ordering rule with a stated basis, plus the usual three-clip A/B — the demoted
pool and the paired pool are already ordered by outranksForFallback, so the change is in how the two
pools are reconciled at the end of planExemplarWithFallback, not in the walk.

WHEN THIS SHIPS: give kneeDrive its alternates back (attachPairAlternates, mirroring kneeFlexion),
re-scope the form-heuristics requirement 'Ranked alternatives from a representative-instant metric
are offered on a range exemplar's terms' from 'at least one such metric' to all of them, and drop
the per-metric-evidence caveat from kneeDrive.buildExemplars' doc.

title: Seek to the middle of a frame's presentation interval, not its start boundary
description:
Surfaced by the strides-e6y design pass, 2026-09-04. Deliberately NOT folded into that change - it lives outside the sampling path and deserves its own measurement.

strides-e6y fixes the 333ns truncation at sequentialFrameSource.ts:223, which is the dominant cause of one-frame-early evidence seeks. But it is not sufficient on its own.

extractFrames.ts:195 computes 'instant.timestamp + options.seekOffsetSeconds' as two doubles. Even with an EXACT instant.timestamp, that subtraction can land 1 ulp below an exact-microsecond frame boundary. If Chromium converts seconds->microseconds by truncation (base::Seconds -> saturated_cast<int64_t>), the seek still resolves one frame early.

MODELLED across park-side-landscape.mp4's 233 frames (arithmetic only, not measured live):
  before strides-e6y:  76 frames seek early
  after  strides-e6y:  10 frames seek early
  residuals include n = 5, 65, 68, 80, 83, 95 - all n mod 3 == 2, all where
  (exact - 512/15360) lands at ...999999999999997 and truncates one microsecond low.

Neither n=185 nor n=206 is a residual, so strides-e6y fully resolves the reported
footStrikePattern symptom. This ticket is the remaining tail.

PROPOSED FIX: compute the seek target as a single division in the tick domain -
(cts - elstMediaTime) / timescale - rather than subtracting two doubles. Correct on every one
of the 10 modelled residuals. This is exactly what the closed strides-ac9.12 proposed as 'a
defensible fix'; that suggestion turns out to be live and separate from e6y's cause.

TWO CAVEATS ON THE RECORD, both making this a measurement rather than a conclusion:
1. Chromium's rounding mode for the seconds->microseconds conversion was NOT verified. The
   truncation assumption drives the whole model.
2. The historical record is internally inconsistent at the 1us level. strides-ac9.12 reports
   2.3833336666666667 -> frame 142 on multiperson-track.mp4, whose source frame is n=145,
   i.e. n mod 3 == 1 - the SAFE residue under e6y's measured pattern. Both clips sit on an
   identical timing lattice (ffprobe: time_base 1/15360, duration_ts 59648, nb_frames 233,
   different files: md5 5da45ab... vs 106dcee...). No single model of Chromium's stored
   timestamp fits both observations. Resolve that before trusting any model here.
acceptance_criteria: On park-side-landscape.mp4 both footStrikePattern evidence cards draw the first-contact frames (183 and 204) with the foot visibly planted — hard sole/ground boundary, shadow continuous beneath — verified by PSNR against reconstructed source crops AND by looking at the images. A scripts/ab-person-selection.mjs before/after across side-landscape, side-portrait and front-approach moves NO metrics.* / sampling.* / personSelection.* / view.* field and changes no exemplar plan; only the drawn pixels change. Compare with rtk proxy diff plus an md5 cross-check.
notes:
2026-09-05 — RE-SCOPED. The original framing (a double subtraction in extractFrames.ts:195 landing 1 ulp low) is REFUTED as the binding constraint, and the proposed tick-domain fix is INSUFFICIENT.

MEASURED: Chromium quantises seeks to integer microseconds. At 60fps on a 15360 timescale,
frame n sits at n/60 s = n*16666.666...us, which is a whole number of microseconds ONLY when
n mod 3 == 0. So two thirds of frames have a presentation-time boundary that is literally
unrepresentable in the seek API.
  frame 162 (2.700000s = 2700000us exactly)  -> reachable, PSNR confirmed drawn correctly
  frame 140 (2.333333s = 2333333.33us)       -> NOT reachable; floors to 139 even at a
                                                 ZERO-ULP target
This is why strides-e6y's exact-timestamp fix only corrected one of the two footstrike cards.
A tick-domain single division does not help: it produces the same unrepresentable boundary.

THE FIX: target the MIDDLE of the frame's presentation interval instead of its start.
video.currentTime = t displays the frame whose presentation interval CONTAINS t, so the
midpoint is the semantically correct request, not a fudge — and it absorbs +/-8ms of error
at 60fps instead of 333ns.
  frame 140 interval [2.333333, 2.350000)
    boundary 2.333333 -> 2333333us -> floors to 139   WRONG
    midpoint 2.341667 -> 2341666us -> inside interval -> 140   CORRECT
  frame 183 interval [3.050000, 3.066667) -> midpoint 3.058333 -> 183   CORRECT
  frame 162 interval [2.700000, 2.716667) -> midpoint 2.708333 -> 162   CORRECT (unchanged)

Robust to the microsecond grid, to the edit list, AND to the 333ns round-trip truncation at
sequentialFrameSource.ts:223 — so it fixes the reported bug WITHOUT touching
robustFrames[].timestamp, which means zero metric movement. That is the property the
exact-timestamp branch could not offer: it moved 84 fields on side-landscape alone.

NEEDS: the frame duration, available from the container (stts sample delta / timescale, or
nominalFps) via DemuxedTrack / containerTiming.ts. Handle the final frame, whose interval
ends at the clip end. The non-WebCodecs playback path currently measures delta=0 and a
half-frame offset keeps it in the same frame, so it stays safe — but verify, do not assume.

CAUTION carried over and still unresolved: Chromium's rounding mode (truncate vs round) was
never verified from source, and the historical record is internally inconsistent at the 1us
level (strides-ac9.12 reports 2.3833336666666667 -> frame 142 on multiperson-track.mp4, whose
source frame n=145 is on the SAFE residue). The midpoint approach is robust to BOTH rounding
modes, which is a further argument for it over any boundary-targeting scheme — it does not
require resolving that inconsistency first.

title: Foot strike pattern is a shank-inclination proxy that cannot see foot angle, and it disagrees with itself across two clips of the same runner
description:
User report: 'heel strike ... also I'm pretty sure I midfoot strike.'

TWO INDEPENDENT PROBLEMS.

1. NOT REPRODUCIBLE ACROSS CLIPS. Measured 2026-09-04, commit f7b02e8, zero spread across 2 trials:
     side-landscape  +0.115103  -> heel      confidence 1.0
     side-portrait   -0.239589  -> forefoot  confidence 1.0
   Same runner, two side-view clips, 0.355 torso apart, straddling the midfoot band
   (footStrikeMidfootBandRatio = 0.05, types.ts:735). Midfoot sits between them, which
   is what the user believes they are. Both report confidence 1.0, the ceiling.
   The fused session shows 'heel' purely by the clip-1 tie-break - see strides-5hj.

2. THE CLASSIFIER STRUCTURALLY CANNOT MEASURE FOOT STRIKE. classifyFootStrike
   (footStrikePattern.ts:70-74) thresholds ratio = ((ankle.x - knee.x) * travelDirection)
   / torsoLengthPx. That is SHANK INCLINATION, not foot-ground angle. left_heel,
   right_heel, left_foot_index and right_foot_index ARE in COMMON_KEYPOINT_NAMES
   (src/pose/types.ts:17-20) but enter this metric ONLY as crop context -
   footStrikePattern.ts:38-40 says so verbatim - and on MoveNet, the default primary
   backend, they never resolve at all.

   A midfoot striker with a forward-inclined shank reads 'heel' no matter how perfectly
   the instant is timed. Correcting timing will NOT fix the label.

   This is disclosed: PROXY_CAVEAT (footStrikePattern.ts:48-61) ships on every result
   including the highest-confidence one. So the design limit is honest - but the metric
   still presents a categorical label ('Heel strike') at confidence 1.0 while
   contradicting itself across two clips of the same runner.

The instant is NOT the problem here: ground truth puts it within one frame of true
contact (see the airborne-evidence bead).
acceptance_criteria: Either the label stops being presented at full confidence when the underlying signal is a proxy that disagrees across clips of one runner, or the classification is sourced from a backend and keypoints that can actually observe foot-ground angle.
notes: MIN_FOOT_STRIKE_SAMPLE_SIZE = 4, so the median can rest on as few as 1-3 strikes. Related: strides-dbh (the MIN_*_SAMPLE_SIZE constants sit below the derived n >= 2k+3 bound), strides-5hj (the fusion tie-break that picks 'heel').

title: Footstrike evidence image shows an airborne foot although the detected instant is correct to within one frame
description:
User report: 'heel strike is grabbing screen caps before foot strike (evidence pictures show my foot still in the air).'

GROUND TRUTH measured 2026-09-04 on park-side-landscape.mp4 (60.000fps, static camera verified by tracking a fence post at x=126.2 +/- 0.1; shoe located by colour threshold and clustered by x-gap):

  strike   app instant   ffmpeg frame   true contact onset   lag
  1 (left)  3.08333       183            3.042 +/- 0.008      +0.008s = +0.5 frame
  2 (right) 3.43333       204            3.392 +/- 0.008      +0.008s = +0.5 frame

Domain mapping measured from the container, not assumed: mdhd.timescale 15360, stts one run 233x256 ticks = 60.000fps, elst media_time 512. So app_t = ffmpeg_t + 0.0333333s exactly (2 frames).

THE INSTANT IS CORRECT. Bounded 0 to +1 frame on both strikes. This REFUTES two standing beliefs: it is not early, and it is not the +0.10 to +0.12s LATE that overstriding.ts:74-85 records - that figure was measured on the RETIRED 25fps Demo 1 footage and does not transfer.

So the airborne foot must enter downstream of the instant, in the extraction/seek path. The margin is thin: frame 183 is the FIRST contact frame, and frame 181 shows the shoe blurred with a clear shadow gap beneath it. One to two frames early is the difference between planted and visibly airborne.

Two known candidates that each consume exactly that margin:
1. strides-ac9.12 - the open delta = -1 frame Chromium seek quantization.
2. A seek-offset divergence: useVideoAnalysis.ts:170-179 races the sequential-decode probe against a 3000ms timeout, but evidenceSeekOffset.ts:82-105 re-derives the offset later by calling canUseSequentialDecode with NO timeout. If the run used the playback sampler and the later probe answers true, extractFrames.ts:195 subtracts a correction that was never needed, landing every image ~2 frames early.

Verify by extracting the rendered thumbnail and PSNR-matching it against candidate source frames, per the CLAUDE.md PTS-drift recipe - do not infer from the exemplar timestamp, which is already known correct.
acceptance_criteria: The rendered footstrike evidence image for a given exemplar is the frame at that exemplar's timestamp, verified by PSNR against the source, on all three demo clips.
notes:
2026-09-05 — FIX DIRECTION CHANGED. The exact-timestamp approach was BUILT, MEASURED and BACKED OUT by user decision. Commit preserved on local branch wip/exact-decoded-frame-timestamps (35a6427, rebased onto f7b02e8); no worktrees remain.

WHY IT WAS BACKED OUT — measured on the THREE SHIPPING clips (the earlier A/B ran on base cee2706 whose demo1 key was the RETIRED Pexels clip, so its reassuring 'bit-identical on side view' result was an artifact of footage the app no longer loads):
  side-landscape  84 fields moved   <- the MOST of the three, not a no-op
  side-portrait   50 fields moved   <- includes overstriding SIGN FLIP -0.00809 -> +0.02679
  front-approach  32 fields moved   <- reproduces the earlier run to the digit
  side-landscape detail: sampling.detectedFrames 106 -> 92 (-13.2%), segmentCount 3 -> 4,
  segments[0].startTimestamp 1.8 -> 2.033, verticalRatio confidence 0.9067 -> 0.6136
  = tier normal -> CAVEATED (user-visible), cadence 174 -> 168, kneeFlexion 102.9 -> 116.5.
  medianAreaPx +0.44% so the winner is the same person, not a bystander swap.
  No null flips on any shipping clip, and overstriding evidence went no-evidence -> planned
  (a coverage gain) — those were the points in its favour.

AND IT ONLY HALF-FIXED THE REPORTED BUG. PSNR + visual, post-fix, park-side-landscape:
  card 1: planned 2.36667 -> target frame 140 -> DREW 139 -> STILL AIRBORNE
  card 2: planned 2.73333 -> target frame 162 -> DREW 162 -> PLANTED (correct)
It also re-planned onto DIFFERENT strikes than the ground-truthed 183/204.

THE REASON MORE PRECISION CANNOT FINISH THE JOB: Chromium quantises seeks to integer
microseconds. At 60fps on a 15360 timescale n/60 is a whole number of microseconds only
when n mod 3 == 0. Frame 162 qualifies, frame 140 does not — its exact boundary is
unrepresentable, so the seek floors one frame back even at a ZERO-ULP target.

NEW FIX DIRECTION (see strides-5t4, which now carries it): seek to the MIDDLE of the frame's
presentation interval rather than its start boundary. video.currentTime = t shows the frame
whose interval CONTAINS t, so targeting the midpoint absorbs +/-8ms of quantization error
instead of 333ns.
  frame 140 interval [2.333333, 2.350000): boundary 2.333333 -> 2333333us -> floors to 139;
  midpoint 2.341667 -> 2341666us -> lands inside -> 140.
It touches NO analysis code, so robustFrames[].timestamp is untouched and metrics cannot
move — no 84-field diff, no tier demotion, and the exemplars stay on the ground-truthed
strikes at frames 183/204.

The exact-timestamp work is correct in principle and the branch is kept, but it must stand
on its own evidence rather than riding in as a side effect of an image fix.

title: Overstriding produces no evidence image on either side clip (all-gated-out)
description:

  clip             evidence status   reason
  side-landscape   no-evidence       all-gated-out
  side-portrait    no-evidence       all-gated-out
  front-approach   no-evidence       metric-excluded (tier 3, unsuitable view)

title: vite.config.ts: port 5177 is at the top level of defineConfig, so it typechecks as an error and pins nothing
description:
Commit 5947c3f 'Pin the dev server to port 5177' added `port: 5177` as a direct key of the defineConfig object literal. Vite's UserConfig has no top-level `port` — it belongs under `server.port` — so two things follow:

1. `npx tsc -b` fails with TS2769 'Object literal may only specify known properties, and port does not exist in type UserConfigExport'. This is the ONLY error in the repo, so it makes a clean typecheck impossible for every other change.
2. Vite ignores the key, so the dev server is NOT pinned to 5177. Anything relying on that pin is relying on a no-op.

Separately worth reconciling: CLAUDE.md documents the dev-server port as DERIVED from the checkout's absolute path (scripts/lib/harnessProvenance.mjs, resolveDevServerPort, sha256 into 5200-5399) specifically so parallel worktrees cannot answer each other's A/B arms. A hardcoded 5177 — once it actually works — reintroduces exactly the collision those guards exist to stop. Decide which mechanism wins before fixing the key.
acceptance_criteria: tsc -b is clean; the port mechanism is either server.port or the derived-port helper, not both.

title: Recover the prompt reader's scale-pass head start by moving the prefetch off the main thread
description:
strides-gyl's fix makes the eager prefetch yield to clip work, so a reader who adds a clip within
the first second or two gets no benefit from it at all -- the pre-prefetch behaviour, ~1.7 s later
scale-pass graft than the prefetch could deliver. That is a deliberate trade (frames beat seconds),
not a defect, and it is the half worth recovering.

Why a worker is the shape: the cost the yield exists to avoid is main-thread work in the renderer.
⚠️ Measured in strides-gyl and load-bearing here: an unread `fetch` body still ARRIVES at full line
rate in Chromium (6.1 MB of 9.4 MB delivered with the read loop parked at its first read), so the
arrival itself -- socket reads, mojo delivery, chunk allocation into the stream queue -- lands on
whatever thread owns the fetch. Moving the transfer into a worker moves that off the sampler's
thread, at which point the transfer no longer has to be deferred at all.

Open questions this ticket has to answer, not assume:
- Cache Storage is available in workers; verify `fetchModelAsset`'s cache write and, crucially, the
  read path the MAIN thread later uses hits the same entry (same key scheme, same origin).
- `modelAssetCache.ts` publishes progress to the header's model-load entry. A worker needs a
  message channel back, and `scalePassDetector.ts`'s channel is deliberately React-free -- keep it
  that way.
- The transferred bytes have to reach the main thread for `PoseLandmarker.createFromOptions`.
  Prefer letting the main thread re-read from Cache Storage (a hit, no network) over postMessage of
  a 9.4 MB buffer; measure both.
- Re-run strides-gyl's exact gate before claiming success: Demo 2 playback sampler at 390x844, cold
  profile, fresh Chromium per trial, 5 trials/arm at BOTH 25 Mbps and 8 Mbps. The unthrottled arm is
  a blind instrument and does not count.

title: Eager model prefetch costs 2-4 sampled frames on the playback sampler whenever the transfer spans the sampling window
description:
Measured on feat/eager-model-prefetch (strides-noo), Demo 2 on the PLAYBACK sampler at 390x844, cold profile, fresh Chromium per trial, real GPU, CDP network throttle, 5 trials/arm.

UNTHROTTLED (the acceptance criterion as written): NO COST.
  prefetch on  59/59/60   off 59/58/60

8 Mbps THROTTLE: a real, reproducible cost, non-overlapping distributions.
  detectedFrames  on  56/58/58/58/58 (median 58)   off 59/60/59/60/60 (median 60)   -2 frames, -3.3%
  analysis complete  on 64.5-64.7 s   off 56.9 s   +7.6 s to first results

Mechanism: the prefetch's 12.5 MB (9.4 MB .task + 3.2 MB WASM) competes for bandwidth with the Demo 2 clip, which is itself 12 MB and is fully fetched to a Blob before analysis can start. The prefetch therefore delays the clip's arrival AND is still streaming during the sampling window (task finishes 64.5 s, analysis completes 64.5-64.7 s).

NOT TUNED AWAY. Reported as measured, per the ticket's instruction.

Candidate directions if this is worth fixing, none attempted:
  - fetch(url, {priority: 'low'}) on the prefetch's requests, so the browser's own scheduler puts the clip ahead of it. Addresses bandwidth contention specifically; would need a per-call RequestInit through modelAssetCache.fetchModelAsset, which strides-utn.3 owns.
  - defer the prefetch while a clip is loading or analysing. Removes the contention entirely but also removes the benefit for the reader who adds a clip immediately, which is the reader the feature is for.
  - Do nothing: 2 frames of 60 on a slow link, against a scale pass that lands seconds sooner on every other link.

Note the throttle also slows the vite dev server's ~11.7 MB of dep bundles, which a production build does not have; absolute timings are dev-inflated. The model and clip bytes are the same either way, so the contention shape is real.
notes:
FIXED on feat/eager-model-prefetch (6bdf322). Not tuned -- the prefetch now YIELDS to clip work.

⚠️ THE TICKET'S PREFERRED DIRECTION DOES NOT WORK, AND THIS IS THE REUSABLE FINDING: not calling
reader.read() does NOT stop a fetch body arriving in Chromium. Traced with every gate consultation
beside CDP Network.dataReceived: the read loop parked at its FIRST read and 6.1 MB of the 9.4 MB
body still arrived at full line rate across the whole sampling window. So back-pressure cannot be
the mechanism; only declining to START a request can. Everything after that defers work (chunk
copies, the 9.4 MB concat, the Cache Storage write), not bytes -- kept, because it is cheap and
helps the residual case.

That makes a one-commit seam between two holders the whole problem, not a small version of it.
Two seams existed and closing the first only moved the escape into the second: DemoVideoButton ->
ClipSlot, and ClipSlot's own stages (mount commit still reads 'empty' because pendingLoad's load()
is deferred a microtask; and another commit sits between loadedmetadata and the run starting).
ClipSlot now holds while NOT FINISHED ('idle' included) in a LAYOUT effect.

⚠️ SECOND BUG, caught only by measuring: settleScalePassModelPrefetch must OPEN the gate and
release what is already parked, not merely stop deferring future asks. A parked transfer awaits a
promise that resolves on the hold count alone, so a clip holding across its own scale pass and
getScalePassDetector awaiting that prefetch deadlocked until the pass's 30 s watchdog:
scale pass at 32.9 s vs 4.97 s prefetch-off. Now 4.82 s.

RE-MEASURED, same conditions (Demo 2 playback sampler 390x844, cold profile, fresh Chromium per
trial, 5 trials/arm):
  25 Mbps  ON 59/59/59/59/60 median 59   OFF 60/60/60/57/60 median 60
   8 Mbps  ON 60/60/59/60/59 median 60   OFF 59/59/60/-/59  median 59  (one OFF trial hit the
            driver's 300 s ceiling; two replacements read 60 and 59. Both such timeouts this
            session landed on the OFF arm.)
Pooling all 25 Mbps trials (15/arm): mean 59.0667 and median 59 in BOTH arms. ZERO .task requests
during any prefetch-ON run, so the arms do identical work in the sampling window by construction.
analysis complete: +1 ms at 25 Mbps, -10 ms at 8 Mbps (was +2.1 s / +7.6 s).

Browsing win survives: .task cached 10.8 s (unthrottled) / 27.6 s (25 Mbps) before the scale pass
asks. Prompt reader no worse than baseline. No wasted bytes: a clip added 0.87 s into a 25 Mbps
transfer left ONE request of the full 9,398,460 B (5166 ms vs ~3025 ms undisturbed). Warm visit
0 model bytes, 0 .task requests. Full ab:person-selection before/after differs on elapsedMs alone.

Cost accepted and stated: the prompt reader loses the feature's benefit -- no worse than before it
existed. Recovering their ~1.7 s needs the work off the main thread (separate change).
close_reason: Closed

title: CI runs no tests — deploy.yml only builds, so every test/lint gate in this repo is convention-only
description:
Found while doing strides-8w2. .github/workflows/deploy.yml is the ONLY workflow: on push to main it runs 'npm ci' then 'npm run build' (tsc -b + vite build) and uploads dist. There is no 'npm test' and no 'npm run lint' step anywhere in CI.

Consequence: every assertion this repo relies on to catch a silent defect — movenetModelAssets.test.ts's deep-import guard on MOVENET_MODEL_URLS (strides-utn.4), mediapipePoseLandmarker.test.ts's MD5 guard on POSE_LANDMARKER_MODEL_VERSION (strides-8w2), and the 1532-test suite generally — fires only when a human or agent runs 'npm test' locally. That IS this repo's standing pre-ship gate (every openspec tasks.md section ends with 'npx tsc -b, npm run lint, npm test all green'), so it is a real gate, but it is a convention, not an enforcement, and a push straight to main bypasses it entirely.

Also corrected in place: design.md D10.3 described the MoveNet guard as 'an assertion at CI'. That phrasing is wrong and now carries a correction note (D12.4).

Fix would be a test job in deploy.yml (or a separate workflow) running npm ci / tsc -b / lint / test. Cheap. Not done under strides-8w2 because that ticket's boundaries forbade touching package.json and vite.config.ts and did not scope CI. Surface: infra.

title: The shell diff wrapper reported 'Files are identical' for files with different MD5s
description:
Hit while producing strides-utn.4's acceptance-gate diff (2026-09-03).

  diff before.txt after.txt   ->  '[ok] Files are identical'   exit 0
  md5 before.txt after.txt    ->  DIFFERENT
  rtk proxy diff ...          ->  3 real differing lines (all elapsedMs)

The A/B gate for that ticket is literally 'diff the two reports and show the diff'. A wrapper that
summarises two differing files as identical turns the epic's hardest correctness gate into a
rubber stamp — and it fails in the SAFE-LOOKING direction, so nothing prompts a second look.

MEMORY.md already carries 'rtk-diff-exit-code' — filtered diff returns exit 0 for differing files
once output is summarized, never branch on its exit status. This is worse than that note describes:
it is not just the exit status, the summary TEXT asserts equality.

Workaround in use: 'rtk proxy diff a b' for any comparison whose conclusion matters, and cross-check
with md5 when the answer is 'no difference'.

Not a strides code bug — a tooling hazard for every agent in this repo that diffs A/B reports.
Surface: tooling.
notes:
ATTEMPTED CONTROLLED REPRO 2026-09-03, session-level — FAILED TO REPRODUCE, hazard still treated as real.

Constructed A/B-shaped report pairs and ran bare 'diff' on each: 322 lines / 3 differing (the exact shape of strides-utn.4's gate), 500 lines / 1 differing, 1000 lines / 1 differing. Plain diff was CORRECT in all three: exit 1, full unsummarized output, md5s confirmed different. No summarization occurred at any size, so the wrapper either did not intercept in this session or its trigger is not file length.

That makes TWO independent field sightings (2026-08-29 subagent, 2026-09-03 strides-utn.4) and TWO failed controlled repros. Conclusion: real, intermittent, trigger unknown. There is NO known threshold to stay under, so 'my files are small enough' is not a defence.

ACTIONS TAKEN (this is why the bead can stay open without being forgotten):
1. CLAUDE.md now carries the warning inline beside the ab-person-selection docs — at the exact spot that previously INSTRUCTED agents to compare with 'diff'. Any future agent reading how to run the A/B now reads the hazard in the same paragraph.
2. The rtk-diff-exit-code memory was rewritten to cover the summary-text form, both sightings and both failed repros, and to say explicitly that a passing controlled test does not prove absence.

NOT FIXED, and not fixable from this repo: rtk is a separate global binary. A real fix belongs upstream in the RTK diff hook. Leaving open as a tooling hazard with mitigations in place rather than closing it as done.

title: Model-download bar must not render a percentage that can go backwards
description:
strides-utn.4 routes MoveNet's 7 files through fetchModelAsset. Each file's total appears only when its OWN response headers arrive, and the shards are not even NAMED until model.json is parsed — so the primary owner's aggregate totalBytes climbs from ~417 kB (the two model.json files) to ~14.5 MB as the shards begin.

A determinate bar driven straight off loadedBytes/totalBytes therefore JUMPS BACKWARDS: roughly 100% of the known total, then ~3% of the real one.

This is honest data, not a bug in the reading — see design.md D10.4 for why seeding the shard totals from the weights manifest was rejected (the manifest declares per-weight shapes, so a per-GROUP total is derivable, but the group's split across its paths is not in the file; reconstructing it means assuming the converter's 4 MiB shard size).

strides-utn.5 owns the fix and it is a presentation decision, e.g. a monotonic high-water mark on the fraction, or treating a shrinking fraction as indeterminate. Do NOT fix it by inventing a total.

Surface: frontend.
close_reason: Closed by strides-utn.5. The header entry reports transferred BYTES and no fraction anywhere, so no percentage can regress. Rejected: a high-water mark on the fraction is WORSE, not safer — both model.json files complete before any shard's headers arrive, so it pins at 100% for the remaining ~14.1 MB; and swinging determinate->indeterminate is the presentation D10.4 already rejected. loadedBytes is monotonic by construction (each asset's count only rises, aggregateModelAssetProgress's map only gains entries). Verified live cold at 60Hz: 43 strictly non-decreasing readings, 0 -> 14.5 MB over 1,302 ms, and the string '%' never appeared in the entry in any scenario. Reasoning: design.md D11.1; unit-tested in modelLoadStripStatus.test.ts against the measured 417 kB -> 14.5 MB shape.

title: Derive the .task cache version token from the file, not a hand-copied MD5
description:
strides-utn.3 keys the MediaPipe .task's Cache Storage entry on POSE_LANDMARKER_MODEL_VERSION, a hand-maintained constant in src/pose/backends/mediapipePoseLandmarker.ts holding the checked-in file's MD5 (md5-5a9ad88919b2231d02b1fdf4a54090ec).

FOOTGUN: replacing public/models/pose_landmarker_full.task without also editing that constant serves the OLD model's 9.4MB from Cache Storage forever, to every returning visitor, on a page that ships the new file. Nothing catches it — no build step, no test, no runtime check. The failure looks like nothing at all: analysis completes, numbers are self-consistent, they are just the previous model's.

Options, none evaluated:
(a) Move the model out of public/ and import it as a vite asset (?url), so the emitted filename carries a content hash and the URL IS the version. Changes how the asset is served and interacts with the BASE_URL subpath; also changes what strides-utn.2 measured.
(b) A build/test-time assertion comparing the constant against the file's actual hash — cheapest, catches the mistake at CI rather than preventing it.
(c) Leave it and rely on the warning comment already in the file.

Surface: frontend. Not urgent: the model has been replaced exactly once and the comment now warns loudly.
notes:
RESOLVED with option (b), on measurement. Shipped on fix/task-version-token (worktree .claude/worktrees/w-8w2). Not pushed, not merged.

OPTION (a) MEASURED AND REJECTED — the reason kills it, not a preference.
Probed vite 8.2.1 against this repo's own node_modules with base '/strides/' and a 20 kB stand-in:
  vite build, content A -> /strides/assets/fake-BQrdse6Q.task
  vite build, content B -> /strides/assets/fake-Dn_piqi6.task   (hash tracks content: YES)
  vite dev,   content C -> /strides/src/models/fake.task
  vite dev,   content D -> /strides/src/models/fake.task        (hash tracks content: NO)
The dev server's ?url module exports the bare source path and re-exports it UNCHANGED after the
bytes are replaced. So (a) holds by construction only in a production build and is absent in dev —
which is exactly where a model is swapped and where this repo's mandated live-browser verification
runs. It would also delete the constant, leaving nothing for a test to check in the half of the
world where the guarantee is missing, and it changes how the asset is served (invalidating
strides-utn.2/D9). That is the 'construction costs more than it is worth' branch.

WHAT SHIPPED (the utn.4 shape, minus the half that cannot transfer): utn.4 DERIVES its token
because TFHub publishes a version in the URL, and ASSERTS its mirrored URLs against the package's
own dist/movenet/constants. The .task has no upstream constant, so its own BYTES are the source of
truth. mediapipePoseLandmarker.test.ts reads the checked-in file, hashes it, asserts
POSE_LANDMARKER_MODEL_VERSION === 'md5-<digest>'. The file is located THROUGH MODEL_ASSET_PATH, not
a re-typed path, so a moved/renamed asset throws naming the path instead of hashing the wrong file
forever. MD5 kept deliberately (the repo already records this file's identity as an MD5).

DEMONSTRATED RED, THEN RESTORED (asset md5 re-verified 5a9ad88919b2231d02b1fdf4a54090ec, git clean):
  constant edited one hex char, file untouched   -> FAIL naming both values
  file last byte flipped, constant untouched     -> FAIL, expected md5-379407682622289ef765710171f0224d
  asset renamed                                  -> FAIL, ENOENT naming public/models/pose_landmarker_full.task

LIVE, real GPU (ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro), port 5323 nonce-verified, persistent profile,
CDP Network, Demo 2 to scale-pass status=done, two independent invocations (4 page loads), agreeing:
  .task  cold 1 request / 9,398,460 B   warm 0 requests / 0 B     <- D9 reproduced to the byte
  wasm   cold 2 / 3,207,437 B           warm 2 / 0 B (disk cache)
  Cache Storage: one 9,398,198 B entry at ...?v=md5-5a9ad88919b2231d02b1fdf4a54090ec, + utn.4's 7
  verticalOscillationCm 10.486597716761532, fitHz 3.12, sampleCount 98, subjectAgreement 99/99,
  detectedFrames 99 — CLAUDE.md's Demo 2 anchor, every digit, both runs.

FILES: src/pose/backends/mediapipePoseLandmarker.ts (export both constants + rationale),
mediapipePoseLandmarker.test.ts (+2 tests, 14 in file), openspec design.md (D12, and a correction
to D10.3's 'assertion at CI'), tasks.md (2.10).
tsc -b / lint / 1532 tests / openspec validate --strict all green. NOT archived.

TWO FINDINGS FILED: strides-dvd (CI runs no tests — deploy.yml only builds, so this guard and
utn.4's fire on 'npm test', not on a push) and strides-aqd (vite rewrites
new URL(<non-literal>, import.meta.url) to the string 'undefined' — ef5/h4r family).
close_reason: Shipped option (b) on fix/task-version-token @ 795c169. Option (a) measured and rejected (vite dev exports no content hash). Guard demonstrated red on all three failure modes and restored; live cold 1/9,398,460 B, warm 0/0 reproduces D9 to the byte; tsc/lint/1532 tests/openspec --strict green. Not pushed, not merged, not archived.

title: Consider eager page-load prefetch of the MediaPipe scale-pass model
description:
Deferred product decision, split out of strides-utn so it could not balloon that epic.

The 9.4MB pose_landmarker_full.task plus the tasks-vision WASM currently load lazily, only after the first clip reaches phase ready (src/results/useVideoAnalysis.ts:497-503). Prefetching at page load would make the scale-pass graft land sooner, at the cost of 9.4MB for every visitor including those who never analyze a clip.

Only worth revisiting once strides-utn.3 has shipped a persistent cache — with caching in place a returning visitor pays the prefetch once rather than per session, which changes the trade materially. Should be measured, not assumed: compare time-to-grafted-centimetre-metrics against bytes transferred for a visitor who bounces.
notes:
Regression resolved (strides-gyl), so the shipping blocker is gone. Implemented on
feat/eager-model-prefetch: 9b6b56c, 361b594, 6bdf322. NOT merged and NOT archived -- pending user
review of the branch.

What ships: the scale-pass model's bytes are prefetched at page load, gated on the primary detector
being ready and on an idle main thread, AND yielding to clip work -- no speculative transfer starts
while a clip is loading, decoding or being analysed. Nothing is aborted, so no byte is fetched
twice, and a caller that needs the assets opens the gate.

Measured on 6bdf322: detectedFrames parity at 25 Mbps and 8 Mbps (5 trials/arm; pooling all 25 Mbps
trials, 15/arm, gives mean 59.0667 and median 59 in both arms); zero .task requests during any
prefetch-ON run; warm visit 0 model bytes; full ab:person-selection differs on elapsedMs alone.

The trade taken, stated rather than buried: a reader who adds a clip within the first second or two
gets the pre-prefetch behaviour and no benefit -- no worse than before the feature existed. Everyone
slower than that gets the full win (.task cached 10.8 s unthrottled / 27.6 s at 25 Mbps before the
scale pass asks). Recovering the prompt reader's ~1.7 s means moving the work off the main thread,
which is a separate change and was explicitly out of scope here.
close_reason: Closed

title: Show a pending-evidence placeholder in metric cards while frames extract
description:
Cards currently render bare for the 3.5-4.5s between 'Analysis complete.' and settled imagery, then pop into a two-column layout — an unmitigated reflow with no indication anything was coming.

PREDICATE, pending vs never (full table at evidenceFrames.ts:1425-1467): plan status 'planned' = pending. The four no-evidence reasons = never — metric-excluded (tier-3, no card at all, routed to ExcludedEntry at MetricsPanel.tsx:428), not-emitted (cadence only, METRICS_WITHOUT_EVIDENCE at evidenceFrames.ts:277, design D7, double-guarded per spec :1354-1358), frames-unavailable, all-gated-out.

TRAPS, all measured:
- extracting deliberately carries the PREVIOUS pass's sections (useSessionEvidence.ts:390-407) and the scale-pass graft re-runs on essentially every default run — so the predicate needs pending && !alreadyHasSection or the graft flashes placeholders over settled thumbnails.
- The synchronous zero-batch path (run.batch.length === 0 -> run.finish([]) -> settled, :404-405) must be preserved or every reused-plan re-run gets a one-frame flicker.
- StrictMode: the teardown at :441-455 resets the input signature so the dev double-mount does not strand the hook. Any new state field must reset there too.

title: Add a shared model fetch/cache/progress utility and route the 9.4MB MediaPipe .task through it
description:
The core of the epic. Build the shared seam and prove it on the asset we control.

Measured justification: GitHub Pages serves the .task with cache-control: max-age=600 and we cannot change that header. Ten minutes is not caching. Client-side storage is the only route to preserved across page loads.

Expected files: new src/pose/modelAssetCache.ts (or similar) + tests, src/pose/backends/mediapipePoseLandmarker.ts (:142-146 swaps modelAssetPath for modelAssetBuffer; the stale comment at :17-23 about riding our deploy caching should be corrected while here).

Blocked by the foundation ticket (needs a progress channel to report into). Parallel with the header UI ticket. Surface: frontend.
design:
Progress and caching are ONE seam, not two: you write a single fetch-with-progress-from-cache-else-store function and both backends call it. Splitting them by concern would mean writing the seam twice. Splitting by ASSET is the useful split, and that is why the MoveNet half is a separate ticket — it is the risky one.

Cache Storage over IndexedDB and over a service worker: it survives page loads, needs no SW scope/lifecycle handling under the /strides/ base path, and stores Response objects directly. Key on asset URL plus an explicit model version token so a model bump invalidates rather than serving stale weights forever. Must degrade gracefully — caches is absent in some contexts and can throw (private mode, blocked site data), so every read and write needs a try/catch and a working uncached path.

This asset is the safe one to go first with: our own origin, known size, no third-party redirect, and it is 9.4MB of the total. Most of the user-visible win lands here.
acceptance_criteria: A shared utility fetches a model asset with byte progress against Content-Length, serving from Cache Storage on hit and populating it on miss, keyed by URL + version token; pose_landmarker_full.task loads through it via BaseOptions.modelAssetBuffer instead of modelAssetPath; a second page load does NOT re-download it (verified live, network-observed, not inferred); progress is reported through the channel the foundation ticket added; absent/throwing Cache Storage still yields a working uncached download; a version-token change evicts the old entry; unit tests cover cache hit, miss, eviction, and the unavailable-caches path.
notes:
SPIKE RESULT (strides-utn.2) — three constraints for the shared utility, all measured:

1. DO NOT CACHE THE tasks-vision WASM. It is already 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable' and measured 0 transferred bytes on a warm visit. Caching it would be actively WORSE: CacheStorage stores the DECODED body, so a 3.12 MB wire payload would occupy 11.76 MB of quota. Leave it to the HTTP cache. It is also NO-GO for progress (no hook exists).

2. DECIDE Content-Length TRUST PER RESPONSE, never globally. The WASM ships content-encoding: br, so its Content-Length is the COMPRESSED length — vision_wasm_internal.js 78,564 vs 323,377 decoded (4.12x), .wasm 3,124,166 vs 11,756,954 decoded (3.76x). A naive loaded/total there reads ~376%. The three assets that matter (both MoveNet models, the .task) carry NO content-encoding and their Content-Length is exact.

3. CACHESTORAGE IS VERIFIED VIABLE, not assumed. caches.open/put/match round-tripped all three storable assets byte-identically from the app's own origin, INCLUDING cross-origin CORS responses: shard2of2 455,912 -> 455,912 with type 'cors' and content-length preserved, .wasm 11,756,954 -> 11,756,954, .task 9,398,198 -> 9,398,198. navigator.storage.estimate() quota is 10,759,035,392 bytes (~10.76 GB); the full model set is ~0.2-0.3% of it.

SCOPE NOTE: this ticket's own asset (.task, 9,398,198 bytes, prod cache-control max-age=600, same-origin, exact Content-Length, 150 chunks) is a GO and needs no IOHandler — MediaPipe takes modelAssetBuffer directly. But it is the SMALLER half of the win; MoveNet (strides-utn.4) is 14.5 MB. Build the utility so utn.4 can use it unchanged.

Also while here: mediapipePoseLandmarker.ts:17-23 is wrong in a SECOND way beyond the max-age point already noted — correct the whole comment, don't just patch one clause.

title: Model download visibility and persistent model cache
description:
EPIC. Pipeline model assets download invisibly today and are re-fetched on every page load. Make the download visible in the header strip with honest progress, and cache the bytes client-side so they survive page loads.

MEASURED CONTEXT (this session, do not re-derive):
- Two independent, differently-timed downloads. MoveNet SinglePose+MultiPose Lightning fetch at app mount (src/pose/backends/movenet.ts:317-330) from tfhub. MediaPipe pose_landmarker_full.task (9,398,198 bytes, self-hosted public/models/) + tasks-vision WASM (jsdelivr) fetch LAZILY, only after the first clip reaches phase ready (src/results/useVideoAnalysis.ts:497-503 -> src/pose/scalePassDetector.ts).
- DECISION: instrument downloads where they already happen. Do NOT move MediaPipe to an eager page-load prefetch — 9.4MB unconditional for visitors who may never analyze is a cost not being taken now. Eager prefetch is a separate follow-up.
- Load state exists and is discarded: PoseDetectorStatus at src/pose/usePoseDetector.ts:6; src/App.tsx:17-19 passes only .detector and drops status. Nothing renders it. Creation errors are swallowed (usePoseDetector.ts:37-43).
- Today a loaded clip reads Ready while the app is blocked on an unmentioned network fetch. The only model-loading string in the product appears as an error after a failed click (useVideoAnalysis.ts:189-201).
- NO caching exists: no service worker, manifest, vite-plugin-pwa, CacheStorage, IndexedDB, localStorage, or tf.io model storage anywhere in src/.
- Deploy is GitHub Pages, so response headers are NOT controllable. Measured live: the .task file returns cache-control: max-age=600. The comment at src/pose/backends/mediapipePoseLandmarker.ts:17-23 claiming self-hosting rides our deploy caching is wrong in practice — 600s is 6x worse than the Google bucket 3600s it replaced.

OPENSPEC: ships as ONE change, not several. All children touch the pose-detection spec, and CLAUDE.md documents that two in-flight changes MODIFYing the same requirement clobber each other silently (last archive wins). Serialize spec edits within this epic.

Success: a reader sees model download happening with honest progress, sees a real failure when it fails, and a returning visitor does not re-download bytes they already have.
notes:
SPIKE RESULT (strides-utn.2) INVERTS THIS EPIC'S PRIORITY. Corrections to the epic description above:

- WRONG: 'MediaPipe .task is by far the biggest download.' MoveNet is bigger — 14,522,593 body bytes at app MOUNT vs the .task's 9,398,198 after first analysis. MultiPose alone (9,697,908) exceeds the .task.
- Cold page load transfers 27,128,512 bytes across 10 requests plus 14 redirect round trips.
- A warm repeat visit still transfers 14,524,268 bytes — ALL of it MoveNet. The .task 304s (127 bytes) and the WASM serves from disk cache (0 bytes).

title: Add armSwingAmplitude metric: per-side fitted arm-swing amplitude / torso length (front-view-gated)
description:
[Surface: frontend | Plan: architect | Review: code+ux]

New MetricId (suggested: armSwingAmplitude), growing the union 12 -> 13. Surfaces the fitted per-side arm-swing amplitude armSwingSymmetry already computes internally but discards (keeps only the ratio), normalized by torso length. Two-phase ticket:

## Phase 1 — extraction refactor (no behavior change)
Move computeSideSwing + SideSwing (currently module-private, armSwingSymmetry.ts:113-234) into a new shared src/heuristics/armSwing.ts, mirroring the hipBounce.ts precedent (verticalOscillationCm.ts:604 and verticalRatio.ts:276 each independently call the exported analyzeHipBounce — no cross-metric memoization exists in index.ts, so siblings re-run the fit; it is one cheap linear least-squares per side). armSwingSymmetry imports from the new module. Verify bit-identical: full ab-person-selection.mjs before/after diff, all three clips, must be empty except elapsedMs. Check armSwingSymmetry.test.ts for reach-into-internals before treating as risk-free.

## Phase 2 — the metric
- Signal: SideSwing.fit.peakToPeakAmplitude (px, wrist.y - shoulder.y series fitted by the shared fitSpectralSinusoid) per side.
- Normalize by estimateBodyScale(frames).torsoLengthPx (bodyScale.ts:28-44); on null follow the overstriding.ts:262-267 template (nullResult naming the missing body-scale reference). Known Demo 2 baseline: left 72.80px, right 44.16px, torso 232.7px -> ratios 0.313 / 0.190.
- GATE REUSE IS MANDATORY: reuse armSwingMinFitR2 (types.ts:706) and the MIN_ARM_SWING_CYCLES cycle logic — do NOT mint a second gate constant on the same fitted signal; that reintroduces the exact bug class #36 deleted (two gates letting a metric family disagree with itself about trustworthiness).
- DESIGN DECISION (record in design.md): how two per-side ratios become one card value — e.g. mean of sides vs weaker side vs report both. Also: the symmetry ratio self-cancels per-side tracking-quality asymmetry (Demo 2 R2 0.778 left / 0.497 right); an absolute magnitude does not, so confidence/caveat design needs fresh thought, not a copy of the symmetry gates. Torso-normalized amplitude cross-clip stability is unmeasured — measure it during design (3 fresh-process trials, all three clips).
- View gating: front primary/1.0, side unsuitable/0.1, ambiguous unsuitable/0.2 — its own viewFitTable.armSwingAmplitude row matching armSwingSymmetry's (types.ts:818-822). Emits on Demo 2, tier-3 excluded on Demo 1.
- Exemplar: per-side ghosted top/bottom pair via selectBounceInstants(maximumIs:'lowest'), per buildSideExemplar (armSwingSymmetry.ts:234); likely a new MetricExemplarKind + INSTANT_MARK_BUILDERS entry (or a deliberate, documented reuse of the existing arm-swing kind if the marks are identical — design decision).

title: Add kneeDrive metric: peak thigh flexion angle during swing (side-view-gated)
description:
[Surface: frontend | Plan: architect | Review: code+ux]

New MetricId (suggested: kneeDrive), growing the union 11 -> 12. Peak thigh angle (hip->knee vector vs image vertical) during swing, one peak per leg per stride, pooled both legs, reported as median degrees. DISTINCT from kneeFlexion, which measures swing-phase knee BEND (hip-knee-ankle interior angle, heel recovery) — kneeDrive measures thigh LIFT.

## Design facts (from research, verified in code)
- Template: kneeFlexion.ts. It does NO phase windowing — findLocalExtrema on the raw per-leg series, gated by an absolute-degrees prominence threshold (kneeFlexionMinProminenceDegrees=20, types.ts:697), works because swing-phase amplitude dominates. Follow that pattern.
- Angle: NOT angleBetweenVectorsDeg on 3 joints — use trunkLean.ts:163's vertical convention: atan2(dx, -dy) on hip->knee (image-y grows downward).
- resolvePoint for hip/knee (keypoints.ts); interpolation flags feed confidence via interpolationConfidencePenalty.
- View gating: viewFitTable.kneeDrive identical to kneeFlexion/trunkLean/overstriding rows (side primary/1.0, front unsuitable/0.1, ambiguous unsuitable/0.2; types.ts:734-820). Caveat wording mirrors kneeFlexion's sagittal-plane phrase using viewPhrase(view).
- Sample-size minimum: mirror MIN_KNEE_FLEXION_SAMPLE_SIZE=4 (peaks pooled across legs) pending the design decision below.
- Exemplar: new MetricExemplarKind (suggested kneeDrivePeak) — representative median-nearest peak paired with same-leg adjacent trough via adjacentMinimum, per kneeFlexion.ts:84-126 buildExemplars. Needs a buildXMarks entry in evidenceAnnotations.ts INSTANT_MARK_BUILDERS (852-864, compiler-enforced total record) using existing drawing primitives only; classify in evidenceFrames.ts SINGLE_INSTANT_KINDS if demotable to a single frame.

## MUST-RESOLVE design decision (empirical, during openspec design phase)
Unsigned hip->knee-vs-vertical angle is large BOTH at forward knee lift AND at backward trail (toe-off) — unlike kneeFlexion's interior angle, "vs vertical" does not fold fore/aft away. Risk: two peaks per stride per leg, corrupting the one-peak-per-stride aggregation. Resolve by probing real clips (add-measure-revert probe on Demo 1, per CLAUDE.md's experimental-file cycle): either (a) show forward-drive peaks dominate prominence-wise (kneeFlexion's own amplitude argument), or (b) sign the angle by estimateTravelDirection (trunkLean pattern; fine here since kneeDrive is side-gated and travel direction resolves on side views — it is Demo 2's FRONT view where it returns 0). Also derive kneeDriveMinProminenceDegrees from measurement — do NOT copy kneeFlexion's 20 (different signal scale).
Also spot-check that kneeDrive peak timestamps diverge from kneeFlexion's on Demo 1 (justifies a distinct metric; if they land on near-identical frames, STOP and report before shipping).

## Expected file paths
src/heuristics/kneeDrive.ts + .test.ts (new); src/heuristics/types.ts (MetricId, FormHeuristicsResult, viewFitTable, config key, MetricExemplarKind); src/heuristics/index.ts; src/results/fuseHeuristics.ts + test (both enumerated lists, 69-80 and 115-126); src/results/metricConfidence.ts (METRIC_LABELS); src/results/MetricsPanel.tsx + test (METRIC_DESCRIPTIONS, metrics array ~370-382, count assertions 11->12, title 'renders all eleven...'); src/heuristics/index.test.ts ('gates all eleven metrics' + null-result test); src/results/evidenceAnnotations.ts (+ test); fixture builders across src/results tests (compiler-caught); openspec/specs/form-heuristics/spec.md (new requirement pair per verticalOscillationCm precedent); openspec/specs/results-view/spec.md:233 (eleven -> twelve); count-bearing doc comments (index.ts:19/21/37, MetricsPanel.tsx:347, analysisDiagnostics.ts:61); CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md metric-count notes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] openspec change (suggested slug: add-knee-drive-metric) validates --strict; design.md records the signed-vs-unsigned decision WITH probe measurements
- [ ] Unit suite green incl. updated enumeration tests; typecheck + lint clean
- [ ] Card copy avoids "effectiveness"/propulsion claims; names thigh-lift proxy honestly
- [ ] Live: ab-person-selection.mjs fresh-process 3 trials, --evidence — kneeDrive emits a value on Demo 1 + multiperson (side views), is tier-3 excluded on Demo 2 (front); an exemplar image renders on at least Demo 1
- [ ] All pre-existing metric values/confidences bit-identical to baseline on all three clips (before/after diff of the driver report)
- [ ] Regression anchor unchanged (separate driver for the scale-pass line): VO_cm 4.421467928439415, fit x60 = 91.2 == cadence
- [ ] Archived after ship+verify

## Notes
Post-steps: npm test, tsc -b, eslint, live A/B. Heel whip explicitly out of scope (epic strides-7a6). One openspec change in flight at a time — do not start the arm tickets' spec deltas until this one archives.

title: At n=2 the extreme-pair framing is vacuous: the card shows one strike captioned as an extreme of a distribution with no interior
description:
Surfaced by strides-ddj, and the framing below is the REVIEWER'S correction of an initial mis-diagnosis of mine — recorded because the wrong version is the tempting one.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE. Demo 1's Overstriding card reports 32.6% (a median over two surviving strikes: +0.2936 at t=4.84 and +0.3579 at t=5.52) and, since strides-ddj, shows ONE image: t=4.84, captioned 'Closest-landing footstrike, ghosted against the furthest-reaching one.' So the reader is shown the closest-landing strike as the sole evidence for a number described as 'a proxy for braking-force risk', half of which is made of a strike they cannot see.

THE WRONG FRAMING (mine, discard it): 'the picture shows the flattering extreme.' It is not systematically flattering. At n=2, describeDistribution's median IS the mean of the two samples, so both survivors are EQUIDISTANT from it by construction. Neither is 'the extreme'. selectExtremePairs picks base via high.deviation >= low.deviation (exemplars.ts:390), and with equal deviations the winner is decided by which side of fl((a+b)/2) rounds further — a single ULP. On this clip it landed on the closest-landing strike by accident; it would land the other way just as readily.

THE REAL DEFECT. The exemplar machinery's premise — show the instant furthest from typical so the reader sees what the number is about — is VACUOUS at n=2. There is no interior to be extreme relative to. The demotion introduced by strides-ddj is what makes this visible for the first time; before it, the card showed no image at all, and before THAT the pair included a collapsed-pose frame (strides-1mt).

PLAUSIBLE FIX — a product decision, not a threshold: below some sample count, show the strike NEAREST the reported median with a representative label, instead of an extreme with a comparative one. That also removes the ULP fragility, because a representative pick does not turn on which side of the mean rounds further.

⚠️ DO NOT 'fix' this by preferring the less flattering end. Deliberately picking the worse strike is exactly the reference-posture editorialising openspec/specs/results-view/spec.md forbids — an annotation depicts what was measured, never what should have happened.

Related: strides-8i4 (closed by strides-ddj's label fix — the label now follows the actual base, which is what stopped this card captioning t=4.84 as 'Furthest-reaching'). strides-24s (the sampled instants are ~0.11s late, so both ratios understate the true overstride).
acceptance_criteria: On a clip whose metric survives with a very small sample, the evidence image and its caption make a claim the sample can support — either a representative instant representatively labelled, or an extreme with enough interior to be extreme within. Which instant is shown does not depend on a floating-point tie-break.

title: Demo 1's overstriding card has no evidence image: the surviving pair needs a 2.881x crop
description:
Fallout from strides-1mt, measured and understood, not a mystery.

Since the collapsed-ankle gate, [evidence-coverage] reports `overstriding: all-gated-out` on Demo 1.

NOT the exemplar quality gate. A probe inside computeOverstriding shows the metric still builds and
selects a pair at t=4.84/5.52, quality 0.5, from the two surviving strikes. The drop is one layer
later, in isTooFarApartPair (evidenceFrames.ts).

MEASURED, same run, [pair-growth-probe] inside that guard, EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH = 2.5:
  - surviving pair (4.84 / 5.52): crop growth 2.881 -> DROPPED
  - the pair the baseline drew:   crop growth 2.428 -> passed (CLAUDE.md records this)

The baseline's image was the ghost of the two COLLAPSED strikes: they were the value extremes
(-0.7215 and +0.5102) and their compressed poses kept the union crop under the cap. That image is
exactly what the user reported in strides-1mt -- 'the Overstriding card's evidence shows a trailing
swing leg, not a footstrike'. So the card now shows NO picture instead of a wrong one, which is an
improvement, but it is still a user-visible loss on the flagship clip.

The surviving pair is two genuine strikes one step apart: ~1180 px of subject translation on a 4K
side view against a tight hip-to-ankle box. With n=2 there is exactly one possible pair, so
`alternates: 0` and there is nothing to fall back to.

Same structural shape as strides-nrg (verticalRatio's stride pair on this clip, growth 4.53), and
the same guidance applies:
  - DO NOT raise EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH. 2.881 is not marginal, and admitting it re-admits
    trunkLean's 6.1-6.8 pairs on the same clip.
  - DO NOT demote the pair to its base. isTooFarApartPair refuses demotion on purpose: the label
    'Furthest-reaching footstrike, ghosted against the closest-landing one' is a claim one frame
    cannot make.

Recovering an image needs a different CONSTRUCTION -- a wide letterboxed crop, or a composed
side-by-side rather than a ghost -- which is a product decision, not a threshold. Probably the same
fix as strides-nrg and worth solving once for both.

Full numbers: openspec/changes/gate-collapsed-ankle-footstrikes/design.md D12.

notes: CORRECTION: the n=2 vacuous-extreme follow-up is strides-9uj, not 'strides-erx'.

Demo 1's Overstriding card renders one annotated frame at t=4.84, cropSidePx 912.197, demotion 'far-apart-pair'.
