title: Overstriding evidence: the 'furthest-reaching' base shows a trailing folded foot — check against the +0.11s footstrike lag
description:
Found during UX review of strides-7v0 (pre-existing, not caused by it). NEEDS INVESTIGATION — this is an image observation, not a confirmed sign bug.

On Demo 1's Overstriding thumbnail the two calipers depict OPPOSITE hip-to-ankle relationships. The ghost's foot is ~48px AHEAD of its hip line; the base's is ~88px BEHIND its hip line. Both arrowheads point the same way, in the direction of travel (the runner clearly moves left-to-right; ghost at 5.52s is left, base at 6.16s is right). The caption calls the base the 'Furthest-reaching footstrike', but its foot is the trailing one, folded up in swing. Reading the picture alone, the labels look swapped.

HYPOTHESIS worth testing first: this may be a visible symptom of the already-filed +0.11s systematic footstrike lag (strides-24s), not a polarity bug. Since strides-cjl, touchdown is derived from the fitted hip-bounce low point minus T/4, and CLAUDE.md records a residual +0.11s systematic lag on Demo 1 that was shipped uncorrected on principle. An instant sampled 0.11s AFTER real touchdown catches the body already travelled over the planted foot — and at 0.66s per step, 0.11s is a sixth of a step. That could plausibly put the sampled 'strike' late enough for the foot to read as trailing.

If that is the explanation, the fix belongs to strides-24s and this ticket closes as a duplicate symptom. If it is not, then either horizontalPolarity/travelDirection or the furthest-vs-closest ranking has a sign problem, which would mean the card's 32.9% is attached to the wrong end of the range.

Do NOT assume; the ground truth for Demo 1's contact onsets is app-domain 4.08 / 4.74 / 5.40 / 6.06 (strides-dly, keyframe-confirmed), and the exemplar instants are 6.16 and 5.52 — both ~0.10-0.12s after a confirmed onset, which is itself consistent with the lag.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) demonstrated to be the strides-24s lag and closed against it, or (b) a sign/ranking defect identified with the corrected behaviour verified on Demo 1's keyframe-confirmed onsets.
notes:
EXPLAINED — and the hypothesis in the description is WRONG. This is not the strides-24s +0.11s lag.

Measured on Demo 1: the base exemplar at t=6.16 sits on a COLLAPSED pose — both ankles detected 3px apart (3409 and 3406) on the trailing swing foot, hip at 3711, runner nearly out of frame right. Ratio -0.7215. The picture shows a trailing folded foot because that is genuinely what the metric measured there; the caliper and the label are faithfully rendering a bad sample.

Root cause is strides-1mt (collapsed-pose frames admitted as footstrikes). The residual issue that belongs to THIS ticket is the label: buildExemplars hardcodes 'Furthest-reaching footstrike, ghosted against the closest-landing one', but selectExtremePairs chooses the base by largest deviation from the MEDIAN, which here is the most NEGATIVE ratio (-0.7215). So on any clip whose extreme deviation is below the median, the caption asserts the opposite of what the image shows. That is a label/selection mismatch independent of the collapse, and it survives fixing strides-1mt.

The +0.11s lag IS confirmed on all four strikes (+0.12/+0.10/+0.12/+0.10 against keyframe-confirmed onsets) but does not produce the negative ratio — at the true onset 6.06 the left foot is further behind still.
close_reason:
Closed by strides-ddj's label fix (c4e55b3). ExtremePair.baseIsHigh now carries which end selectExtremePairs actually chose, and overstriding/trunkLean pick their label from it instead of hardcoding one end. Demonstrated non-hypothetical on the very clip: baseIsHigh came out FALSE on Demo 1, so the card correctly reads 'Closest-landing footstrike, ghosted against the furthest-reaching one' at t=4.84 — without the fix it would have said 'Furthest-reaching' beside the closest-landing frame. Independently confirmed from probe data: t=4.84 ratio +0.2936, t=5.52 ratio +0.3579.

The earlier hypothesis in this ticket's description (that the trailing folded foot was the strides-24s lag) was WRONG and was corrected in the notes: that was strides-1mt's collapsed pose. What remained here was purely the label/selection mismatch, and that is what is now fixed.

title: Overstriding evidence: the captioned base instant is edge-cropped and motion-blurred, so composition points at the ghost
description:
Found during UX review of strides-7v0 (pre-existing, NOT caused by that change; crop and amber marks are byte-identical before and after it).

On Demo 1's Overstriding thumbnail the BASE instant — the one the caption names as the source of the number — sits hard against the right edge of the crop, and its subject is so heavily motion-blurred there that the torso is a faint smear; the drawn leg extends left over bare grass with no visible leg beneath it. The GHOST is central, larger and far more readable.

The 65/35 photographic weighting toward the base (EVIDENCE_GHOST_BLEND_ALPHA, strides-c37) is nominally applied but is defeated here by the base frame's own blur and edge placement. Composition therefore points the reader at the ghost while the caption names the base — the same mis-attribution risk the evidence feature exists to prevent, arriving by a different route than the joint-marker bug strides-7v0 fixed.

Measured by pixel sampling, not by eye: ghost strokes sample at exactly alpha=0.5 (#2A7989 over the dark track = 0.5*#22D3EE + 0.5*bg), base strokes at pure #22D3EE. That is how base/ghost were identified.

Context: this exemplar's crop is cropSidePx 2160 on a 3840x2160 frame — the frame-height cap — with cropGrowth 2.4277, so the crop is as zoomed-out as it can get and both bodies render small. Related: strides-nrg (a pair needing a construction other than a ghost), strides-mjw (verticalRatio's stride pair dropped for demanding a crop wider than the frame).
acceptance_criteria: On Demo 1's overstriding card, the instant the caption names is the one a reader's eye lands on — either by choosing a pair whose base is legible, by changing how the base is emphasised, or by captioning what the picture actually shows.

title: Evidence annotates BOTH feet at each instant of a mixed-foot pair
description:
On Demo 1's Overstriding card the thumbnail draws joint markers for both legs at both ghosted instants, so it reads as though the metric measured the trailing leg as well as the landing one.

THE NUMBER IS NOT AFFECTED. overstriding.ts measures only ANKLE_NAME[sample.side] against the hip midline (seedFor, overstriding.ts:47-49), and buildOverstrideMarks (evidenceAnnotations.ts:708-732) draws the amber caliper from instant.side alone and refuses to draw at all when that is null. Both are correct.

The defect is in the JOINT layer. evidenceFrames.ts:1100 resolves each instant's drawn keypoints from exemplar.cropKeypoints — and for a pair that is cropKeypoints([...seedFor(base), ...seedFor(ghost)], [KNEE[base.side], KNEE[ghost.side]], ...) (overstriding.ts:98). When the two strikes are opposite feet — which overstriding.ts:80-82 calls 'the usual case', since nothing constrains the furthest-reaching and closest-landing strikes to one foot — that union is {left_ankle, right_ankle, left_hip, right_hip, left_knee, right_knee}, and the SAME list is used for both instants. So each skeleton shows the ankle and knee of the leg its own caliper did not measure, in the same cyan, with nothing distinguishing it.

The crop set must stay unioned (the image has to contain both instants). What is wrong is reusing it as the annotation set. evidenceFrames.ts:376 states the intent as 'the metric that measured the instant is the only layer that knows which points its measurement is about' — which the union is not, per instant.

MEASURED on Demo 1 (fresh Chromium, real GPU, last [evidence-coverage] line):
  overstriding: kind overstrideRange, timestamp 6.16, pairedTimestamp 5.52, quality 0.5, cropSidePx 2160, cropGrowth 2.4277, and NO side key -> mixed-foot pair by that field's own contract.
  footStrikePattern independently reports t=5.52 as the RIGHT foot, so the solid base at 6.16 is the LEFT foot. Both skeletons nonetheless draw both legs.

Amplifier: cropSidePx 2160 is the frame-height cap on this 3840x2160 clip, so the crop is as wide as it can be and both bodies render small, crowding the four leg markers together.

SAME SHAPE IN stepWidth's paired exemplar (stepWidthExemplars.ts:110-114), whose comment says the two instants are 'deliberately opposite feet' — that is Demo 2's card. Note stepWidth's SINGLE exemplar adds the opposite ankle as context on purpose (width is read against the midline), so a fix must not flatten the two cases together.
acceptance_criteria: At each instant of a mixed-foot ghosted pair, the drawn joint markers are those of that instant's own measurement, while the crop still frames both instants. Verified on Demo 1 overstriding (base 6.16 left foot, ghost 5.52 right foot) and on Demo 2 stepWidth, without changing either metric's value.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in c022c0f + dff0259. Per-instant annotationKeypoints/pairedAnnotationKeypoints on MetricExemplar, resolved via resolveInstantAnnotationKeypoints, emitted by overstriding and stepWidth's pair path. Verified live on Demo 1: two leg-chains per body became one, both plumbs and calipers intact, coverage byte-identical (cropSidePx 2160, cropGrowth 2.42768425598781) proving the crop unchanged, overstriding.value 0.3257433216584835 and cadence.value 91.2 unchanged. Demo 2 stepWidth likewise. Follow-up strides-p11 covers the demoted-pair legibility question.

title: Evidence thumbnails blank session-wide when the scale-pass graft forces a re-extraction
description:
After analysis completes, every metric card's evidence thumbnails appear, then vanish, then reappear ~0.8-4s later.

ROOT CAUSE (live-reproduced 3/3):
1. The background MediaPipe scale pass grafts verticalOscillationCm/stepWidthCm and writes a NEW heuristics object plus scalePass.robustFrames in one setState (useVideoAnalysis.ts:645-667). graftScalePassResult always returns a fresh spread (scalePassGraft.ts:107-116), so heuristics changes identity even when 9 of 11 metrics are reference-identical.
2. sameClipInputs (useSessionEvidence.ts:112-122) compares heuristics and graftedFrames BY REFERENCE, so the whole clip's cache entry is discarded (line 222-225) - not just the two grafted metrics. planClipEvidence replans every metric and the full clip re-enters the extraction batch.
3. setState(EXTRACTING_STATE) (useSessionEvidence.ts:297-299) discards the previously settled sections, and MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:207 maps any non-'settled' status to NO_EVIDENCE - session-wide, for every clip, with no placeholder. Cards switch branches (MetricsPanel.tsx:273), so the canvas subtree unmounts and the layout collapses two-column to single-column and back.

MEASURED (headless Chromium, real GPU, ANGLE Metal Renderer, dev server on derived port 5262; 13.2s clip = park-approach concatenated 8x, uploaded):
  ANALYSIS COMPLETE       t=10.09s
  canvases 0 -> 4         t=11.78s   (first appear)
  [scale-pass] done       t=17.89s
  canvases 4 -> 0         t=17.94s   (50ms after the graft)
  canvases 0 -> 4         t=18.76s   (817ms blank)
  2x [evidence-coverage] lines, payloads BYTE-IDENTICAL

Blank window 815/816/817ms across three runs. The second extraction produced identical coverage on this clip - entirely wasted decode.

WHY THE DEMO CLIPS DON'T REPRODUCE IT: it is a race. Scale-pass wall clock scales with clip length; extraction wall clock is roughly constant. On Demo 1 (scale pass 2.1s vs extraction 3.8s) and Demo 2 (1.6s vs 3.3s) the graft lands BEFORE the first extraction settles, so run 1 is superseded before it ever paints - one appear, no flicker, one coverage line. Any fix must be verified on a longer clip.

NOT A REGRESSION: state machine dates to ced0f24 (evidence feature's first commit); trigger dates to the scale pass shipping. Moving evidence into the cards (6de154c, strides-ac9.2) widened the blast radius from one page section to every card. No design doc ever weighed the visual consequence - CLAUDE.md and the archived designs only record it as the 'take the LAST [evidence-coverage] line' harness gotcha.
acceptance_criteria: Evidence thumbnails do not disappear after the scale-pass graft on a clip where the first extraction settles before the graft lands (verify on a >10s clip, not Demo 1/Demo 2). No layout shift on the metric cards across the graft. Evidence for metrics the graft did not touch is not re-decoded.
notes:
FIXED in working tree (not yet committed). openspec change: hold-evidence-through-reextraction (validated --strict, all 10 tasks checked).

Two changes in src/results/useSessionEvidence.ts + one line in MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:
1. canReuseCachedEvidence compares the recomputed plan (JSON-structural) plus the source blob, instead of the heuristics/frames/graftedFrames object references. Sufficient by construction: extractSessionEvidence receives exactly { sourceBlob, plan }. sameClipInputs survives as the cheap every-render outer guard.
2. SessionEvidenceState's 'extracting' now carries sections, carried forward only while the clip id list is unchanged (clipIndex is a position, so add/remove must not carry). Consumer reads sections from both non-idle states; only 'idle' means no imagery.

LIVE VERIFIED, 13.2s clip, 2 runs: canvases go 0 -> 4 and never drop. Second [evidence-coverage] line now lands 4ms after scale-pass done (was ~800ms with a full re-decode behind it). Demo 1 still 8 canvases / 1 line, Demo 2 still 5 / 1, coverage payload lengths unchanged (2402 / 1949 / 1825).

Gates: tsc clean, eslint exit 0, vitest 1393 passed / 0 failed, incl. 4 new tests in src/results/useSessionEvidence.test.ts (the hook had none).

REMAINING: commit, then 'openspec archive hold-evidence-through-reextraction --yes'.
close_reason: Fixed and shipped in 4dbcce6. Plan-based reuse key plus a non-destructive extracting state; live-verified on a 13.2s clip (canvases never drop after first appear, second coverage line 4ms after the graft instead of ~800ms). Follow-up strides-zm8 covers per-metric re-extraction granularity.

title: stepWidth takes a median over as few as 5 strikes, where a median is not outlier-robust
description:
Found by strides-87x, 2026-08-31.

computeStepWidth reduces its per-strike offset ratios with median(offsetRatios). On Demo 2 usableStrikeCount is 5 for BOTH passes, and at n=5 a median is simply the third-largest value -- two high outliers promote the third-smallest into the middle slot.

MEASURED on Demo 2, scale pass:

  ratios sorted: [-0.00793, 0.16306, 0.40424, 0.84934, 1.38051]
  median of all five               = 0.40424   <- the reported value
  median of the three non-outliers = 0.16306
                              ratio  2.48x

Two of five samples move the reported value by 2.48x. That is the whole of the 1.79x primary/scale-pass disagreement plus some. Had the non-outlier median stood, it would sit BELOW the primary's 0.22531 rather than 1.79x above it.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE TWO-PASS COMPARISON: this is not a MediaPipe problem. The primary pass also has usableStrikeCount 5 on this clip, so a MoveNet-only run is one bad strike away from the same failure and nothing would flag it. stepWidth reports confidence 1.0 on Demo 2 today. computeMetricConfidence does take sampleSize, so the machinery exists -- the question is whether 5 strikes should be reaching confidence 1.0 at all.

Note the clip is short (~1.65s, ~2-3 strides), so a low strike count is intrinsic to it rather than a detection failure. A longer clip would not have this problem.

OPTIONS, none chosen: raise the sampleSize floor in stepWidth's confidence term; use a trimmed statistic that degrades gracefully at small n; or refuse to report below some minimum strike count. Note that strides-87x also found two of the scale pass's five strikes sit on contaminated frames (one at the clip-opening window's edge, one on the very last sampled frame), so a strike-eligibility rule at the clip boundaries would help independently -- filed separately.

Full measurement: openspec/changes/archive/*-explain-the-step-width-pass-gap/design.md D2c.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded on how stepWidth should behave at small strike counts, and Demo 2's stepWidth no longer reports confidence 1.0 from five samples of which two are outliers -- or it is documented why that is acceptable.
close_reason: Shipped together. Boundary footstrikes excluded in detectFootstrikes -- and, after review, BEFORE selectFootstrikes' amplitude ranking on the fallback path, because a contaminated boundary pivot outranks a real contact, suppresses it within minIntervalSeconds, and was then dropped, deleting the real contact (reproduced: [] where a contact existed). MIN_STEP_WIDTH_SAMPLE_SIZE 4 -> 7 from n >= 2k+3 (derived shape) with k=2 (labelled a judgment call). A/B on 3 clips: exactly three fields moved, all stepWidth.confidence -- demo1 0.0875->0.05, demo2 1.0->0.714286 (the pre-registered 5/7), multiperson 0.08->0.0457143. No value, no sampleSize, no tier moved. Two plan assumptions corrected by the new per-metric diagnostics: demo1 and multiperson sat at sampleSize 4, so the saturation defect was corpus-wide not Demo 2-specific; and sampleSize unchanged everywhere means the boundary filter removed zero strikes from any primary pass.

title: The 1.79x stepWidth gap between the two passes is still unexplained
description:
Split out of strides-boc, 2026-08-31. BLOCKS strides-wac.

On Demo 2 the primary (MoveNet) and scale pass (MediaPipe) report stepWidth 0.2253 (confidence 1.0) vs 0.4042 (confidence 0.2) -- 1.79x apart, same clip, same sampleSize 5.

strides-boc diagnosed the 4.8x SER gap fully (clip-opening detection failure amplified by interpolation) but that diagnosis does NOT obviously explain this one, and saying so is the point of this bead:

  - SER is a p95-p5 RANGE -- outlier-amplifying. stepWidth is a MEDIAN at footstrikes -- outlier-suppressing.
  - The SER damage is concentrated in ~15% of frames, all at t < 0.45s. A median should shrug that off.
  - Cross-backend MEDIAN ankle-to-ankle distance is only ~20 px. MediaPipe's ankles are mostly FINE; the damage is concentrated, not systematic.

So a concentrated clip-opening outlier cluster should not move a median by 1.79x. Something else is going on.

CANDIDATES, none tested: the different denominator (stepWidth normalises by hipWidthPx, not torsoLengthPx -- and hipWidthPx is derived from the same possibly-suspect hip keypoints); the two passes detecting footstrikes at DIFFERENT INSTANTS (stepWidth samples at footstrikes, and strides-cjl re-timed footstrike detection off the fitted hip-bounce phase, so a different bounce fit gives different instants); or a genuine further defect.

WHY IT BLOCKS strides-wac: strides-fn4 withheld the 'grafted metrics inherit the primary's view' fix on the grounds that stepWidthCm's VALUE is untrustworthy. strides-boc makes that more nuanced rather than simply confirming it -- MediaPipe's ankles look mostly fine at the median. Until this 1.79x is explained we do not know whether stepWidthCm's 4.53 cm is trustworthy, which is exactly what strides-wac needs to know.

WHERE TO START: dump both passes' footstrike instants and their per-strike ankle/hipMid positions on Demo 2 and compare directly. If the instants differ, that is the answer and it is not an ankle problem at all.
acceptance_criteria: The 1.79x stepWidth disagreement is explained with evidence, and a judgement is recorded on whether MediaPipe's stepWidthCm value on Demo 2 is trustworthy enough for strides-wac to render it.
close_reason: Explained. The two passes detect footstrikes at DIFFERENT INSTANTS (a different set, not an offset): the scale pass misses the primary's first strike and gains one at t=1.66833, the clip's final sampled frame. Both its outliers sit on contaminated frames. The bead's own premise was the error -- a median over FIVE is not outlier-robust: two of five outliers move it 2.48x, and stripping them puts the value BELOW the primary's. Denominator refuted (hipWidthPx ratio 0.968); interpolation not involved (interpolatedFraction 0.000 both sides). JUDGEMENT FOR strides-wac: stepWidthCm on Demo 2 is NOT trustworthy. Follow-ups strides-h6r and strides-aah.

title: viewDetection discards the .interpolated flag that stepWidth honours
description:
Found by strides-boc's root-cause investigation, 2026-08-31. This is the one genuine CODE defect the diagnosis found, and it is in SHARED, backend-agnostic code -- not MediaPipe's adapter.

resolvePoint (src/heuristics/keypoints.ts:29) returns { x, y, interpolated }. computeSagittalRange (src/heuristics/viewDetection.ts:30) reads .x and throws .interpolated away. resolveBilateralPair does not even return it, so BSR discards it too. stepWidth.ts:99 honours the identical flag and discounts confidence accordingly.

viewDetection.ts is the ONLY consumer in the repo that receives the robustness layer's own trust signal and ignores it -- and view detection GATES EVERY OTHER METRIC via the view-fit table.

MEASURED IMPACT on Demo 2 with MediaPipe primary, both arms detecting 87/99 so they differ only in what happens to the 12 missed frames:

  default (maxGapSeconds 0.5)      SER 1.59113
  {robustness:{maxGapSeconds:0.05}} SER 0.650297     -> 2.45x

Mechanism: interpolateChannel lerps across any gap <= maxGapSeconds (0.5s default). At clip-open MediaPipe misses 10 of 12 consecutive frames (0.33s, inside budget) and BOTH flanking anchors are bad detections, so every interpolated frame lands in the same extreme zone. The outlier population grows from ~4 raw frames (4.6%) to ~14 (16%). computeSagittalRange reduces by percentile(.95) - percentile(.05), which at n=87 trims only ~4 values -- its docstring claims robustness to 'a single wildly-off ankle sample', which is true for one and false for fourteen.

WHY THIS IS NOT MEDIAPIPE-SPECIFIC: MoveNet is exposed to the identical defect and simply has no gaps to fill on these three clips (99/99 on Demo 2). A clip where MoveNet drops frames -- occlusion, a subject leaving frame, a lower-quality recording -- would hit it too, silently, and corrupt the view label that gates every metric.

SCOPE NOTE, IMPORTANT: this touches shared code and its blast radius reaches MoveNet's view path. It must be A/B'd on all three clips before shipping, not landed as an obvious fix. Use scripts/ab-person-selection.mjs; view.diagnostics.sagittalExcursionRatio and view.view are already in the report.

NOT SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN: at SER 0.650 MediaPipe casts no SER vote at all (front needs <=0.4, side >=0.8), so Demo 2's label stays 'ambiguous' by abstention and stepWidthCm stays tier-3 excluded. This fix is necessary for correctness but does not by itself restore the front label.

Full evidence: openspec/changes/archive/2026-08-31-diagnose-mediapipe-front-view-ankles/design.md D1b.
acceptance_criteria: View detection either honours the interpolated flag or documents why it must not, verified by an A/B on all three clips showing what moves on the MoveNet path as well as the MediaPipe one.
close_reason: Fixed: computeSagittalRange now excludes interpolated samples and refuses a range below MIN_SAGITTAL_RANGE_SAMPLES=21 (a derivation: below 21 the p95/p5 interpolation points still touch the extreme samples, so the trim is not a trim). BSR untouched -- it reduces by median, 50% breakdown point. Two new per-side diagnostics. A/B on all 3 clips: demo2 MediaPipe-primary SER 1.59113 -> 0.675891, plausibility {ambiguous 1} -> {ambiguous 0.690, front 0.310}; demo1 and multiperson stay side; NO metric value, confidence or tier moved anywhere. Measured finding that refuted this change's own no-op premise: 15-20% of ankle samples feeding view detection were interpolated on ALL THREE clips on the default MoveNet path -- detectedFrames counts frames, but a keypoint inside a detected frame can still be interpolated.

title: A grafted metric should inherit the primary pass's view for view-fit gating
description:
Split out of strides-fn4, 2026-08-31. BLOCKED on the MediaPipe ankle-placement bead -- do not land this alone.

graftScalePassResult copies the scale pass's MetricResult wholesale, viewFit included, while explicitly discarding the scale pass's view ('Every other metric, and view, stay reference-identical to primary's'). The result on Demo 2, measured on the default path:

  displayed view          front (MoveNet's), confidence 0.5486
  grafted stepWidthCm     4.5309 cm, confidence 0.2, viewFit 'unsuitable' -> tier 3 EXCLUDED
  grafted verticalOscillationCm  10.4866 cm, viewFit 'tolerated' -> caveated, survives

The panel tells the reader this is a front view and simultaneously withholds a card because a different, hidden pass thinks the view is ambiguous. The generated caveat even names a view the panel never displays: 'Step width is a side-to-side measurement and is not reliable from a ambiguous view.'

THE PRINCIPLE: view is a property of the CLIP -- camera geometry -- not of a detector. Both passes sample the same clip on the same media clock. There is one camera angle. Two detectors disagreeing means one is mistaken, and strides-fn4 shows which. Gating a grafted metric by a second, hidden, contradicting view opinion is not a safety measure; it is an inconsistency the user cannot see the evidence for.

WHY THIS IS BLOCKED AND MUST NOT LAND ALONE: stepWidthCm is computed from ankle positions at footstrike, and that is exactly what MediaPipe gets wrong on this clip. The two passes' own stepWidth reads 0.2253 (MoveNet) vs 0.4042 (MediaPipe) -- 1.79x apart. So today's gate reaches a DEFENSIBLE OUTCOME (withhold a suspect number) for a FALSE REASON (bad camera geometry). Removing the false reason without addressing the suspect number would put 4.53 cm on screen as a rendered card. Fix the cause first.

SCOPE WHEN UNBLOCKED: resolve a grafted metric's viewFit and its view-fit confidence multiplier against the PRIMARY pass's view, since that is the view the panel commits to for everything else. Note verticalOscillationCm would also move (ambiguous 'tolerated' 0.6 -> front 'tolerated' 0.85 on Demo 2), so its confidence changes too -- that is in scope, not a side effect to ignore.
acceptance_criteria: A grafted metric's view-fit is resolved against the view the panel displays, stepWidthCm renders on Demo 2, and its rendered value is one the blocking bead has established as trustworthy.

title: Characterise MediaPipe's ankle placement on front-approach footage
description:
Split out of strides-fn4, 2026-08-31. This is the REAL defect behind the MediaPipe/MoveNet view disagreement on Demo 2, and it currently gates nothing.

MEASURED. On Demo 2 (park-approach.mp4, a dead-on front approach), the two passes' view signals:

                MoveNet    MediaPipe
  BSR           0.5510     0.5229      (agree within 5%)
  SER           0.3284     1.5911      (4.8x apart)

BSR and SER SHARE A DENOMINATOR -- both divide by estimateBodyScale's clip-wide torsoLengthPx. BSR agreeing within 5% means the torso estimates agree within ~5%, so the entire 4.8x lives in SER's numerator: percentile(ankle.x - hip.x, 0.95) - percentile(..., 0.05). MediaPipe's ankles range ~4.8x further from their own hips, horizontally, than MoveNet's, on a clip where the runner comes straight at the camera.

THE CONTROL MAKES IT CONCLUSIVE. On Demo 1 (side view) the two backends agree on BOTH signals within 10% (BSR 0.1335 vs 0.1207; SER 1.5744 vs 1.4147). And MediaPipe's FRONT-view SER (1.5911) is HIGHER than its own SIDE-view SER (1.4147) -- it reports more fore-aft ankle excursion on a dead-on approach than on a dead-on side pass. A front view hides the leg's fore-aft reach in depth; that is the whole premise of the signal. Anatomically impossible, so the fault is the ankle placement, not the scoring.

CORROBORATION FROM A DIFFERENT DIRECTION: the two passes' own stepWidth on Demo 2 reads 0.2253 (MoveNet, confidence 1.0) vs 0.4042 (MediaPipe, confidence 0.2) -- 1.79x apart on the same clip, same footstrike concept, same sampleSize 5. stepWidth is computed from ankle positions at footstrike, so it is measuring the same defect from another angle.

HYPOTHESIS, NOT MEASURED: MediaPipe Pose Landmarker predicts landmarks for occluded and foreshortened parts rather than letting them collapse, so on a front approach where the feet are foreshortened and periodically leave frame it extrapolates fore-aft positions MoveNet does not. Consistent with MediaPipe detecting 87/99 frames on this clip against MoveNet's 99/99.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is what SHOULD gate stepWidthCm. Today the metric is withheld on Demo 2 by a view-fit rule that names the wrong reason (camera geometry), and the actual unreliability is unmeasured and ungated. strides-wac is blocked on this.

WHERE TO START: pull keyframes at footstrike instants and overlay both backends' ankle keypoints, per CLAUDE.md's keyframe-review method, to see directly where MediaPipe is putting the feet. Then decide whether this is a per-clip confidence term, a keypoint-level gate, or a reason to stop using MediaPipe's lower-body landmarks for anything but scale.

Full measurement: openspec/changes/archive/*-diagnose-scale-pass-view-divergence/design.md D2 and D4.2.
acceptance_criteria: MediaPipe's front-view ankle error is characterised against keyframes, and a decision is recorded on how stepWidthCm should be gated by it -- rather than by a view opinion that names the wrong cause.
close_reason: Characterisation complete: root cause is two stacked defects (raw clip-open detection failure ~1.97x, interpolation amplification ~2.45x), verified end-to-end via the maxGapSeconds experiment (SER 1.59113 -> 0.650297). Four hypotheses refuted with evidence. The gating decision this bead also asked for has been correctly relocated to the beads that own it: strides-kxn (the viewDetection .interpolated defect) and strides-87x (the unexplained stepWidth gap, now blocking strides-wac). Full record: openspec/changes/archive/2026-08-31-diagnose-mediapipe-front-view-ankles/.

title: stepWidth reads 3x differently on Demo 2 under tracking crop, at confidence 1.0 both ways
description:
Found by strides-09k's fresh-process tracking-crop re-run, 2026-08-31. Out of that ticket's scope, which was the default-OFF adjudication.

On Demo 2 (park-approach.mp4), scripts/ab-person-selection.mjs --backend-arm, 3 fresh trials per arm, zero spread:

  metrics.stepWidth.value        off 0.225311   on 0.0717871    (3.1x)
  metrics.stepWidth.confidence   off 1.0        on 1.0

A metric the UI renders as a full-confidence NORMAL-tier card reads three times larger with the tracking crop off than on, on the same clip, and the confidence machinery reports 1.0 either way. Nothing flags it. There is no ground truth for which value is right.

Alongside it on the same clip and same runs, metrics.kneeFlexion.value goes 106.103 -> 177.686 degrees. 177.7 is a knee essentially straight at peak flexion -- anatomically implausible for a running stride. That one is at caveated confidence in both arms (0.0667 / 0.0886), so it does not carry the same weight, but it points the same way: the tracking crop mistracks the subject on this front-approach clip, where the subject's on-screen scale changes ~3x across ~1.65s.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE FLAG. trackingCrop ships enabled: false, so no user sees the 'on' number today -- and strides-09k kept it off partly BECAUSE of this cell. But the finding is really about stepWidth's confidence, not about the crop: a metric whose value moves 3x under an upstream perturbation while reporting confidence 1.0 is a metric whose confidence is not measuring what the tier system assumes it measures. If some other upstream change moves stepWidth the same way, the card will present the wrong number with full confidence and no caveat.

FIRST THING TO ESTABLISH: which arm is right. Pull keyframes at the exemplar instants and measure the ankle separation by hand against a grid overlay (CLAUDE.md's keyframe-review method), on both arms. Then decide whether stepWidth's confidence needs a term that can see this.

Full tables: openspec/changes/archive/*-remeasure-backend-abs-under-fresh-process/design.md D1.3.
acceptance_criteria: Which arm's stepWidth value is correct on Demo 2 is established against keyframes, and a decision is recorded on whether stepWidth's confidence needs a term sensitive to the disagreement.
notes:
ADDENDUM 2026-09-04 (from strides-je4's measurement session) — the same clip's kneeFlexion has the SAME shape of defect and the mechanism is now identified as INTERPOLATED ANKLES AT PEAK SWING.

On the PRE-FIX commit cee2706, demo2, fresh process, 2 trials, --backend-arm tracking-crop toggle
ONLY (no timestamp change anywhere):
  metrics.kneeFlexion.value               cropoff 106.103    cropon 177.686
  metrics.kneeFlexion.interpolatedFraction cropoff 0.666667  cropon 0.200
  metrics.kneeFlexion.sampleSize           cropoff 6         cropon 5
  metrics.kneeFlexion.viewFit              unsuitable both
Reproduces this ticket's 106.103 -> 177.686 exactly.

Collect the four readings of this one number on this one clip and the pattern is monotonic in
interpolatedFraction, not in anything else:
  pre-fix default          106.103   interpolatedFraction 0.667
  pre-fix warm (5 trials)  103.191 [103.191..106.103]  interpolatedFraction 0.5 [0.5..0.667]
  post-fix default         162.269   interpolatedFraction 0.286
  pre-fix + tracking crop  177.686   interpolatedFraction 0.200

MECHANISM. park-approach.mp4 is a front approach. At peak swing flexion the heel is up behind the
glute, so the ankle is OCCLUDED and the thigh and shin both project to ~80-120 px. When the ankle
is genuinely detected, the projected hip->knee and knee->ankle vectors are nearly ANTI-PARALLEL
(both point up in projection once the foot rises above the knee), so 180 - interior angle lands at
160-180 deg. When the ankle is interpolated, interpolate.ts fills it on a straight line between the
flanking detections, which flattens the excursion and pulls the projected flexion down to ~105.
So the two 'families' are detected-ankle and interpolated-ankle readings of the same instants, and
NEITHER is a knee flexion measurement — the pipeline already says so: viewFit 'unsuitable' ->
metricTier 'excluded' in every one of the four readings above, so no value is ever rendered.

CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY FUTURE A/B: kneeFlexion on a FRONT-view clip is not a usable comparison field.
It swings 70 deg on a config flag that touches no timestamp, and it is product-invisible. Judge
kneeFlexion on side-view clips only — where it is stable: demo1 120.690220593611 bit-identical
across the timestamp change, multiperson 104.311 -> 106.539 (2.1%).

title: Remove GRAFTED_METRICS polarity suppression, now that the seam is closed
description:
`strides-3a1` closed the seam: a grafted metric's evidence is now planned from the background
scale pass's OWN frames (`ScalePassState.robustFrames` -> `planClipEvidence`'s fourth argument),
so its joint positions and its hip polarity come from the detector that took the measurement.

That makes `GRAFTED_METRICS` in `evidenceAnnotations.ts` obsolete, not redundant-but-safe. Its
stated premise -- "their joint positions AND their hip polarity are therefore resolved off a
primary-pass frame snapped within tolerance -- never the MediaPipe frame the metric actually
measured" -- is now false. What it still does is withhold a polarity that is correct, so
`stepWidthCm`'s caliper draws as an unsigned span when it could honestly point, and
`verticalOscillationCm` pays nothing either way.

`strides-3a1` deliberately did not remove it: another agent held `evidenceAnnotations.ts` and
`drawEvidenceAnnotations.ts` in the same session, and deleting a set out from under an in-flight
annotation rework is how two correct changes clobber each other. It is a single-file change and
should be made deliberately rather than left as two mechanisms guarding one thing.

Scope:
- Delete `GRAFTED_METRICS` and the `polarityAllowed` flag threaded through `InstantContext` /
  `polaritySource` (`evidenceAnnotations.ts:73, 671, 970`). With the set gone, `polaritySource`
  becomes the identity function and should go with it.
- `evidenceAnnotations.test.ts:758` asserts the set's membership; it goes too.
- `evidenceAnnotations.ts:53`'s doc comment is stale on a second count: it says "`useSessionEvidence`
  hands `planClipEvidence` `clip.analysis.robustFrames`, MoveNet's", which is no longer true for
  the two grafted metrics.

Verification this needs that `strides-3a1` could not do: `stepWidthCm` is tier-3 excluded on all
three test clips (`strides-fn4` -- MediaPipe calls Demo 2 `ambiguous` where MoveNet calls it
`front`), so its caliper cannot be seen live today. Either land this behind `strides-fn4`, or verify
the re-enabled polarity on `verticalOscillationCm` (which carries no polarity, so the check is that
coverage and imagery are unchanged) plus unit tests until a clip exists that renders `stepWidthCm`.
acceptance_criteria: GRAFTED_METRICS, polarityAllowed and polaritySource are deleted; evidenceAnnotations.ts:53's stale doc is corrected; a grafted metric's directional marks orient from the plan; coverage unchanged on all three clips
close_reason: Closed

title: MediaPipe and MoveNet disagree on Demo 2's view: ambiguous vs front
description:
Found while verifying strides-b5o, 2026-08-31. Not investigated further there because it was outside that ticket.

Forcing MediaPipe as the PRIMARY backend on Demo 2 (park-approach.mp4, a genuinely dead-on front approach) classifies the clip as view 'ambiguous' with confidence 0.3, where MoveNet classifies the same clip 'front'. The run produced a real stepWidthCm measurement (4.53) that was then excluded anyway, because viewFit resolved 'unsuitable' -> tier 3. The same run newly excluded stepWidth too.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE TICKET:
1. The background scale pass IS MediaPipe. So every grafted centimetre metric arrives carrying MediaPipe's view opinion, and on this clip that opinion is 'ambiguous'. stepWidthCm is therefore structurally unable to render on the one clip it is designed for. verticalOscillationCm survives only because it is view-TOLERANT.
2. It means the two backends disagree about a clip whose camera angle is not marginal - CLAUDE.md describes Demo 2 as a dead-on front approach, and strides-2iw measured its BSR at 0.5507 against a central anatomical estimate of 0.5612, i.e. essentially textbook front.
3. strides-2iw changed view-detection scoring on 2026-08-29 (margins now ramp to what each signal can physically reach; frontViewMinBilateralSpreadRatio 0.55 -> 0.45). That change was verified on the MoveNet path. Whether it helps, hurts, or does nothing on the MediaPipe path is UNMEASURED.

FIRST THING TO ESTABLISH: is MediaPipe's BSR/SER genuinely different on this clip (a keypoint-placement difference between the two models - MediaPipe's hips and shoulders may sit differently), or is it the same geometry scoring differently? Read view.bilateralSpreadRatio and view.sagittalExcursionRatio off [analysis-diagnostics] under __STRIDES_POSE_BACKEND_OVERRIDE__ = { backend: 'mediapipePoseLandmarker' } and compare against the MoveNet numbers. Those two answers point at completely different fixes.
acceptance_criteria: The cause of the disagreement is identified with both backends' BSR/SER measured on Demo 2, and a decision recorded on whether the scale pass's view opinion should gate grafted metrics at all.
close_reason: Closed

title: verticalRatio's stridePair image no longer renders on any clip
description:
Found by the strides-h4u coverage re-measurement, 2026-08-31, not investigated.

verticalRatio drops from 2 evidence images to 1 on BOTH Demo 1 and multiperson. The exemplar that disappeared is the stridePair; the bounceCycle still renders. Measured fresh-process, 3 trials, bit-identical - this is not flakiness.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A COUNT: CLAUDE.md's own assessment was that 'Best image on any clip is verticalRatio's stridePair'. The app has lost the single image its documentation named as the best thing it produced, and nobody noticed until the coverage table was re-measured.

NOT the exemplar budget: MAX_EXEMPLARS_PER_METRIC is still 2 and the metric still resolves its value, so something upstream stops emitting or gates out the stride pair specifically.

TWO SUSPECTS, neither confirmed - the measuring agent deliberately did not guess:
- ceee2dc 'Gate stride pairs on the fitted step period' (strides-dy8). A gate placed directly on stride pairs is the obvious first place to look.
- strides-cjl's footstrike re-timing, which moved every footstrike instant by ~0.11s systematic and changed which frames a stride pair would span.

Both landed between the CLAUDE.md observation and this measurement, so bisecting across those two commits should settle it in one pass.

START BY MEASURING WHICH STAGE DROPS IT - [evidence-coverage] reports a per-metric status and reason, so read whether the stridePair is 'all-gated-out' (a quality/guard rejection) or simply never emitted by the metric (an upstream gate). Those point at different fixes.
acceptance_criteria: The stage that drops verticalRatio's stridePair is identified with evidence, and either the image returns or the loss is recorded as correct with the reason. If it is correct, CLAUDE.md's 'best image' claim must be retired rather than left pointing at an image nobody can produce.

title: Demo 1's recorded contact onsets are 1.5-4 frames early — correct them at archive time
description:
strides-da8 recorded Demo 1's contact onsets as ffmpeg 3.90/4.60/5.16/5.84 (app 3.98/4.68/5.24/5.92) and both strides-da8's design and strides-cjl's acceptance criterion are stated against them. Demo 1's corrected footstrike ground truth (4.00/4.66/5.32/5.98, against the earlier 3.90/4.60/5.16/5.84) is now recorded as a dated addendum in the archived detect-footstrike-contact-onsets design at D1, and again at the head of D15 where every quoted lag is stated against the wrong onsets. The D15 addendum notes the corrected mean lag is +0.03s with 0.340s of scatter, which STRENGTHENS D15.2 and invalidates only D15.1's percentages.
