title: Annotation makes GitHub #71's whole-frame crop defect unmistakable
description:
Measured by strides-ac9.8 across all three clips: 28 of 352 drawn ops land off-canvas, and 27 of those are trunkLean on e2e/fixtures/multiperson-track.mp4.

Cause is NOT a transform error — ac9.8 audited for exactly that. It is GitHub #71's known crop defect: trunkLean's two extreme instants are 1.25s apart, the runner crosses the frame between them, computeEvidenceCropRect unions both torso boxes and hits the min(frameWidth, frameHeight) cap, giving a 1080 crop side on a 1920x1080 clip. Base sits at x -21..18 and ghost at x 629..661 on a 640 canvas — the runner straddles BOTH crop edges.

The 28th is a thighExtensionRay ending at x -9: a construction ray leaving the crop, benign, clips gracefully.

Before annotation this read as 'a wide shot with two small runners'. With joints drawn on it, the image now visibly asserts that the analysis measured something at both edges of a picture that is mostly fence — so annotation converts a quiet crop defect into a loud one. That is an argument for fixing #71, not against annotating.

Design D12 demotes a pair that is too SIMILAR (IoU >= 0.98). Nothing guards a pair that is too FAR APART. That is the guard #71 has been waiting for.

comments.author: Caleb Brewer
comments.text:
Seen again at INLINE thumbnail size (strides-ac9.2, live, multiperson clip, 1440px): trunkLean's whole-frame crop is materially worse in a card than it was in the gallery. At the gallery's w-56 (224px) the runner was at least findable at both edges; at the card's w-28 (112px) the image reads as fence and skyline with no visible subject at all. The caption still says 'the two overlapping positions are the same runner at two instants', which now describes a picture in which neither position is discernible.

Not a regression from ac9.2 — same crop, same frames, half the display width. It does raise the priority: a crop defect that was a curiosity at gallery scale is an uninterpretable thumbnail at card scale.

comments.author: Caleb Brewer
comments.text:
Fixed on worktree-agent-a9e83bee49762e2db @ f2920fa (branched from feat/layout-redesign-w3 @ 76ae004). NOT pushed, NOT merged.

Criterion: crop GROWTH ratio (pair crop / better-framed instant's own crop) >= EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH 2.5 -> drop the pair. 2.5 is the reading of the existing 1.6 padding contract under which the subject still spans a quarter of the image side.

Live, real GPU (ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro), 3 trials x 3 clips, bit-identical. 13 pairs measured: 11 at 1.000-2.068, multiperson kneeFlexion 2.190 (legible, reviewed), multiperson trunkLean 3.375 (#71's broken crop). Nothing between the last two.

Rejected with evidence: elapsed time / absolute separation (Demo 1's legible stridePair unions to 1164 px vs the broken pair's 1144 - orders them backwards); the frame-cap test (binds on every crop on a small source, would delete every ghost on a webcam clip); box non-overlap (IoU already 0 on 8 of 13, all five on Demo 1).

Dropped, never demoted: every paired label in this repo is a two-instant statement ('ghosted against', 'Opposite-foot plants either side of', 'Top and bottom of'), so no survivor can carry its own caption.

Before -> after: Demo 1 7/5 -> 7/5 all PNGs byte-identical; Demo 2 5/4 -> 5/4 all byte-identical; multiperson 5/4 -> 4/3 with the four survivors byte-identical. Off-canvas ops 34/277 -> 0/241, all 34 were this image. No metric moved anywhere; track anchor verticalOscillationCm 4.421467928439415, fitHz x 60 = 91.2 == cadence 91.2.

Gates: tsc clean, eslint clean, 1203/1203 across 83 files (+11).

EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX left at 320 - that is strides-ac9.10. GitHub #71 commented, left OPEN (items 2 and 3 still live).

title: Grafted exemplars carry the scale pass's instants but not its frames
description:
The root cause behind strides-ac9.7's option-(a) workaround. Filed so the workaround is not mistaken for a fix.

scalePassGraft.ts:43-50 records the seam plainly: a grafted exemplar carries the SCALE PASS's instants, but 'the only frames any consumer holds are the primary pass's'. So stepWidthCm and verticalOscillationCm get their joint positions and hip polarity resolved off a MoveNet frame snapped within tolerance — never the MediaPipe frame that actually measured them.

At a near-frontal step-width strike the two hips sit a few pixels apart and the two detectors can order them oppositely, so the plan can carry the INVERSE polarity, labelling a crossover strike as landing on its own side — contradicting stepWidth.ts:273-277's own crossover caveat in the same viewport.

ac9.7 mitigated by suppressing POLARITY (not geometry) for GRAFTED_METRICS. That is correct and cheap, but it is a workaround at the consumer, not a fix at the seam.

The clean fixes, per ac9.7: either a grafted exemplar carries its own pass's frames, or the graft drops when no primary frame corroborates it. Both are scalePassGraft.ts's business, and both are larger than any ticket in epic strides-ac9.

Note this seam previously carried only a coarse crop box, where a few pixels are invisible. ac9.6 was the first change to push a polarity through it — so the seam got riskier without anyone widening it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A grafted metric's annotation geometry derives from the frames that measured it, or the graft is dropped when unsupported
- [ ] ac9.7's GRAFTED_METRICS polarity suppression can be removed, or is documented as permanently correct
- [ ] Live-verified on a front-view clip where the scale pass reports 'agreed'
close_reason: Seam closed: the scale pass's own frames now travel with the metrics it grafts (ScalePassState.robustFrames), and planClipEvidence plans those metrics against them. Defect confirmed reachable before fixing: the two passes order the hips oppositely on 15/57 instants of Demo 1, 15/87 of multiperson, 0/98 of Demo 2, and 3 of 12 grafted exemplar instants carry the inverse ordering. scalePassSubjectAgreement cannot see it (hulls are invariant under a left/right relabelling; Demo 1 reads 'agreed' 52/53 on the same run). ac9.7's GRAFTED_METRICS suppression is now obsolete rather than protective and is removed by strides-us3 — deferred only because another agent held evidenceAnnotations.ts. Live-verified 3 trials x 3 clips, real GPU: coverage 8/7, 5/4, 8/7 unchanged; anchor 4.421467928439415 / 91.2 == 91.2 / 52,53 unchanged. openspec: plan-grafted-evidence-from-its-own-pass (NOT archived).

title: No way to remove a clip once the strip replaces ClipSlot chrome
description:
Gap in epic strides-kyu, surfaced while planning kyu.3.

The 'Remove clip' button lives in ClipSlot (ClipSlot.tsx:114-122). kyu.3 deliberately leaves it in the page body (only the <video>+overlay stage moves offscreen), so removal keeps working through that ticket. But NO ticket in the epic re-adds a remove affordance to the navbar strip, and once the strip is the clip's only presentation surface the body chrome has no reason to exist.

Left unfiled, the epic would ship a navbar of clips you cannot remove, with two unit tests (MultiClipVideoSession.test.tsx:291, :366) still green because jsdom cannot see that the control is gone from the UI.

Decide where removal lives — on the strip entry, in the preview modal, or both — and spec it. Depends on kyu.4 (the strip) and kyu.5 (the modal) existing.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A reader can remove a clip from the new shell without the old ClipSlot chrome
- [ ] removeClip's existing teardown (analysis reset, poster release, active-clip advance) still runs
- [ ] Covered by a test that fails if the affordance is absent, not merely if the handler is unwired
close_reason:
Already satisfied by strides-kyu.4 — verified, not assumed. When kyu.4 moved the clip chrome into the header strip it carried Remove with it rather than leaving it behind: ClipStripEntry.tsx:207-211 renders the button with an sr-only 'Remove clip' label, ClipSlot.tsx:167 passes onRemove(clipId), and MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:296 wires it to removeClip.

Covered by tests that would fail if the affordance disappeared, not merely if the handler were unwired: MultiClipVideoSession.test.tsx queries getAllByRole('button', {name: /remove clip/i}) at :557, :563 and :594, and :671 exercises removing the currently-ACTIVE clip while it is genuinely mid-analysis — the teardown path this ticket was filed to protect.

The gap this ticket described (a navbar of clips you cannot remove, with two unit tests still green because jsdom cannot see a missing control) never materialised, because kyu.4 chose to keep Remove per-entry in clip order specifically so those raw-.click() synchrony tests kept passing.

title: Derive the header offset instead of hardcoding 86px and 150px
description:
The sticky header's height is hardcoded in four places and derived from nothing:
- MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:182 — `lg:top-[86px]`
- MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:203 — `lg:max-h-[calc(100vh-86px)]`
- VideoInputPanel.tsx:132 — `max-h-[calc(100vh-150px)]`
(plus whatever the restructure in strides-kyu.3 leaves behind)

Adding a clip strip to the navbar changes its height, so every one of these silently goes wrong. Either derive the offset from the actual rendered header, or single-source it as one token both the header and its dependents read.

Small ticket, but it is a real correctness bug the moment the navbar grows — worth isolating so it does not get lost inside a larger change.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] No hardcoded header-height pixel value remains in layout math
- [ ] The offset tracks the navbar's real height, including when the clip strip is present vs absent
- [ ] Verified at narrow and wide viewports
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean
notes:
Only ONE of the four values survived to this branch. grep for 86px/150px/100vh-/lg:top-[/max-h-[calc across src/ returns exactly VideoInputPanel.tsx's max-h-[calc(100vh-150px)]; kyu.3 took both MultiClipVideoSession values with the two-column grid, and the lg:col-span-2 that task 3.1 parked here went with EvidenceGallery.tsx when ac9.3 retired it.

The survivor was a FALSE dependency, not a stale one. The element it caps is the concealed clip host, fixed; top:0; left:-200vw since kyu.3 - anchored to the viewport top edge and out of flow, so the sticky header is never above it and never takes room from it. Subtracting a header height there is meaningless at ANY header height. Fix: max-h-screen (the viewport itself). Deriving it from a measured header would have mechanised the error.

Measured, real GPU (ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro), 390/640/1440:
- header height: zero clips 66 (390) / 86 (640,1440); strip populated 129.8 all widths; add-a-clip panel open 367.8 (390) / 327.8 (640,1440). The old hardcoded 86 was already wrong at 390 before the strip existed (tagline is hidden sm:block).
- opening the panel moves the header +238.0/+198.0/+198.0 px and the concealed box rect is bit-identical either side; max-height resolves to 900px == innerHeight.
- no ResizeObserver/custom property added: nothing consumes a header offset any more, and a token nothing reads is worse than none.

P0 (kyu.13) re-checked in pixels: panel OPEN, element mid-sampling on the playback path, screenshot of the video's own rect shows the runner painting (t=0.906, paused=false, 92x68 @302,22, longest side 92 > 60 floor). ab-person-selection playback arm, demo2, 5 trials, own server: sampling.path=playback, detectedFrames 64 [60..65], missingFrames 0 - healthy band 63-65, clear of broken 47-49.

Gates: tsc -b clean; npm test 84 files/1209 tests (baseline unchanged); eslint clean; playwright 1 passed/0 failed on dedicated port 5203 (5173 held by a foreign checkout).

Untouched per boundaries: strides-49e (MetricsPanel.tsx:364 container query) and strides-kyu.14.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lengthen the model runner's flight phase so large bounces animate smoothly
description: From ps19.4 review: with GAIT_PHASES.stanceEnd fixed at 0.38, flight is 0.12 of a cycle (~80 ms), and the knee-flexion prominence rule limits how much hip travel stance can absorb with the foot pinned. Bounce beyond STANCE_DROP must happen in flight, so at large pelvisBounce (b > 0.2) the hip moves 0.5-0.6 b per 30 fps frame and per-step peaks alias. Shortening stance (~0.30) would spread it but touches every key phase (KEY_LEG_PHASE, swing-arc window, toe-off key).
acceptance_criteria:
At b up to 0.3 and cadence 150-190, per-frame hip change at 30 fps is at most 1.3x the sinusoid floor b*sin(2*pi*dp)
Spread of per-step drawn hip peaks over 12 steps at 30 fps is at most 0.12 b
Every MEASURE_PARAM binding test and the stance-foot pin tests still pass
KEY_LEG_PHASE consumers (focusAreaCamera, still frames) re-verified in screenshots

title: Give stepWidth's percent value a denominator in words
description: Found in strides-trn2.5: the summary's Foot path row reads 'Step width 15.2%' because formatGuidedValue (src/results/formatGuidedValue.ts:50) has no denominator for stepWidth's percent unit. A runner can't tell 15.2% of what.
acceptance_criteria:
- stepWidth (and swingFootLateralExcursion if also percent) renders with its denominator in words wherever formatGuidedValue is used
- Word budgets in focusAreas/feedback tests still hold

title: Pin the model runner's stance foot to the ground in gaitModel
description: From ps19.2 UX review: gaitModel uses a fixed PELVIS_HEIGHT and an unpinned stance foot, so the still mid-stance figure floats ~15 CSS px above the ground (the renderer mitigates by drawing the ground at the lowest foot point over the cycle). A floating figure can read as a finding about the runner's own landing. Related: footSide preset shows the foot only near contact while animating.
design:
# Plan: strides-ps19.4, pinning the stance foot to the ground (base epic/ps19-model-runner 06e36518 == main) ## User constraints (hard) - Only `src/runner/**` and `openspec/changes/add-model-runner/` may change. The change is unarchived and its requirements are ADDED blocks, so edit them in place; never write MODIFIED deltas. - runnerParams' contract must not change: every bound value is exactly what is drawn, i.e. measuring the model with each metric's own formula returns `bound.value`. The tour (strides-trn2.3) depends on this. - ModelRunner's public API (props and exported types) must not change. Consumers outside src/runner: - `src/results/summary/ResultsSummary.tsx` uses ModelRunner and bindRunnerParams. - `src/results/focusAreaCamera.ts` uses RunnerFocus, KEY_LEG_PHASE, paramForMetric and CameraPreset. None of these may change shape. - `src/runner/runnerParams.ts`, including realizeParams' code and precedence, must not change. - No changes to `src/heuristics/**`. No new dependencies. ## Orchestrator decisions on the planner's open questions - **Q1:** AC "within 0.01 at neutral and range corners" cannot be met at the landingOffset 0.7 corners: pinning there needs a stance knee of at least 50°, which breaks kneeFlexion. Restate AC1 in the spec and tests as: - pinned within 0.01 at neutral, at all landingOffset −0.3 corners, and over a declared realistic domain (landing ≤ 0.35 across the other axes); - outside that domain the bindings outrank the pin, the mid-stance foot gives way by a bounded amount that a test checks, and contact stays exactly on the ground. The orchestrator reports this to the user. - **Q2:** the fallback lets the mid-stance foot sink; the contact stays exactly on y=0. Never raise the figure so that the contact floats. - **Q3:** restate the isolation tests openly. x and z stay bit-identical. Non-own joints may differ only by one shared vertical shift per phase, to 1e-12. cadence, torsoPitch, armSwing and swingFootArc stay bit-identical. Say this plainly in the spec. - **Q4:** STANCE_DROP = 0.04. Judge it in the screenshots; fall back to 0.07 if the flight hop looks wrong, and report which value you used. ## Probe evidence The planner's probes are self-contained copies of repo code, at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-caleb-dev-strides-epic-ps19/cf110a44-e5fd-4105-8652-089fa00dc951/scratchpad/probe/`: - `pinned.ts`: the candidate model. - `analyse.ts`: the checks. - `p1.ts`: the current code. - `p2.ts`, `p3.ts`: the 64 leg-relevant corners. - `p4.ts`: one-parameter sweeps. - `p6.ts`: a 4050-point realistic grid. Run them with `node .ts ''` (Node 22 strips types). Reuse them freely. Results: - **Current code:** the neutral foot is 0.079 up at contact, 0.081 at mid-stance and 0.120 at toe-off. - **Option (a), stance IK alone with the cosine bounce:** rejected. The stance knee becomes a prominent peak, kneeFlexion is off by 45°, and 959 of 1023 corners fail. - **Option (b), hip height derived from the stance leg:** rejected. VO is no longer exact on the 1/1000 sampling grid, and bounces smaller than the leg's own stance range can't be drawn. - **Chosen, the hybrid "design D" with STANCE_DROP 0.04, toe-off knee 28, the knee cap on both sides and the thigh clamp:** - neutral stance error 7e-16, kneeFlexion error 0, kneeDrive −0.0166 (tolerance 0.05); - on the 4050-point realistic grid, 653 failures, all with landing ≥ 0.45; worst sink 0.049, worst swing dip −0.056; no binding broke; - all 32 landing −0.3 corners pass; - the landing 0.7 corners fail, with a sink of 0.05–0.18. - The recommended variant has NOT been rerun on the corners. Probe it. ## Math (gaitModel.ts) **Notation.** T′, S′ = sagittalLegLengths(stepWidth); L = T′+S′; (θc, κc, σc) = solveContact(params); s_e = GAIT_PHASES.stanceEnd = 0.38; b = pelvisBounce. **Foot drop.** drop(f) = max(0.15·sin f + 0.1·cos f, −0.45·sin f + 0.1·cos f). Minimum 0.1; A_MAX = R = hypot(0.45, 0.1). **Bounce.** g(p) has period 0.5. Use periodicEase over the half-cycle u = p mod 0.5 (evaluate in half-cycle phase so the keys land exactly), with keys [0, c], [0.19, −1], [0.38, c], [0.44, +1]. - c = b > 0 ? −1 + 2·min(1, STANCE_DROP/b) : 1. - hipY(p) = H + (b/2)·g(p). - The minimum H − b/2 falls at 0.19 and the maximum at 0.44, both on keys, so VO = b exactly. **Figure height.** New export `pelvisHeight(params)`: H = drop(σc) + T′cos θc + S′cos σc − (b/2)·c. This puts the contact foot's lowest point exactly on y=0. **Toe-off target.** - κ_to = KNEE_TOE_OFF_DEG = 28 (illustrative; was 22). - d(κ) = √(T′² + S′² + 2T′S′cos κ). - v_to = hipY(s_e) − drop(FOOT_TOE_OFF_DEG). - x_to = −√max(0, d(κ_to)² − v_to²). **Stance ankle path.** x(q) = x_c + (x_to − x_c)·q/s_e, with x_c = T′sin θc + S′sin σc. **Stance solve, for q in (0, s_e].** At q === 0, return the contact geometry exactly (the overstriding binding needs 1e-9). 1. f = foot keyframe(q); a = drop(f). 2. Heel lift: aMin = hipY(q) − √max(0, L² − x²). If aMin > a, set a = min(aMin, A_MAX) and f = min(f, φ − asin(a/R)), where φ = atan2(0.1, 0.45). 3. v = a − hipY(q); d = clamp(hypot(x, v), d_cap, L). If either clamp engages, the pin gives way. 4. κ_cap = min(peakSwingKneeBend − 5, max(κ_to, κc) + 18); d_cap = d(κ_cap). 5. θ = atan2(x, −v) + acos((T′² + d² − S′²)/(2T′d)); κ = π − acos((T′² + S′² − d²)/(2T′S′)). The knee bends forward. 6. Thigh clamp: θ = min(θ, max(peakThighAngle, θc)). **Swing (q > s_e).** Existing FK periodicEase, with these keys: - thigh, knee and foot at s_e come from the stance solve at s_e; - late-swing knee key = max(KNEE_LATE_SWING_DEG, κc); - FOOT_MID_SWING_DEG changes −20 → −5 for swing clearance. **Constants.** STANCE_DROP = 0.04, STANCE_KNEE_PROMINENCE_MARGIN_DEG = 18, STANCE_KNEE_BELOW_SWING_DEG = 5, all documented as illustrative. Keep `PELVIS_HEIGHT = 1.8066` exported as the nominal framing height; pelvisHeight(neutral) ≈ 1.809, so the camera presets are unchanged. Rewrite the header doc: the stance foot is pinned by IK where feasible, and the bindings outrank the pin. **Optional.** Export `stancePinError(params)` for tests. **Invariants to hold.** - seam (phase 0 = 1 to 1e-9, and the 0.5 wrap); - mirrored half-cycle; - segment lengths; - z independent of the leg angles; - every relative-measure binding unaffected by the whole-figure shift; - realizeParams untouched; - continuity in params (each clamp is a min/max of continuous functions, and c(b) is continuous). ## Files - **`gaitModel.ts`:** as above. - **`runnerAnnotations.ts`:** - delete `footFloor` and the `floor` fields of AnnotationInput/BuildContext; the ground is GROUND_Y = 0; - landing builder y = −0.05 with its extension to 0.25; step-width builder −0.06 and 0.3; - bounce bracket uses pelvisHeight(values). - **`introFlash.ts`:** drop the `floor` parameter; the landing anchor y is 0. Grep useRunnerIntro.ts for callers. - **`ModelRunner.tsx`:** remove the floor memo and Scene.floor; draw the ground at projectPoint({x: target.x, y: 0, z: target.z}). Props and types do not change. - **`camera.ts`, `runnerParams.ts`:** no change. - **Tests:** `gaitModel.test.ts`, `runnerAnnotations.test.ts`, `introFlash.test.ts`, `ModelRunner.test.tsx`. - **`dev/ModelRunnerSandbox.tsx`:** add a big-landing (0.5) scenario so the fallback is visible. ## Tests **AC1, the pin:** - lowest left-foot point over q in (0, 0.38] at 1/1000 steps: |y| < 1e-9 at neutral; < 0.01 over the declared domain grid (the p6 axes with landing ≤ 0.35) and at all landing −0.3 corners; - the contact (q=0) lowest point satisfies |y| < 1e-12 at EVERY corner; - fallback at the landing 0.7 corners: bindings exact, pin error under a documented bound you measure, contact on the ground; - every held still phase (midStance and each KEY_LEG_PHASE) has a foot at y≈0 at neutral; - swing foot lowest point ≥ −0.01 over the domain; - |pelvisHeight(neutral) − PELVIS_HEIGHT| < 0.01. **AC2:** MEASURE_PARAM sweeps and their tolerances stay UNCHANGED. So do the always-exact corner tests, the knee-flexion reviewer cases, the swing-arc cases and every realizeParams test. **AC3:** - ModelRunner draws the ground at y=0; - annotation tests use 0 and pelvisHeight; - introFlash's FLOOR becomes 0; - delete the footFloor tests; - screenshots. **Restated tests (Q3):** - isolation: shared vertical shift allowed; - MOVED_JOINTS.pelvisBounce = the legs; - check whether peakSwingKneeBend moves the stance knee in the sweeps; - "neutral runner on the ground" is replaced by AC1. **Gates:** `npm run lint`, `npx tsc -b`, `npx vitest run src/runner`, full `npx vitest run`, `openspec validate add-model-runner --strict`, `npx vite build`. ## openspec (edit in place) **spec.md:** - edit the kinematics requirement that says no IK / unpinned foot; - edit the isolation wording ("apart from one whole-figure vertical shift that keeps the runner standing; no metric reads absolute height"); - edit the renderer ground requirement (lowest foot point → y=0); - add a requirement "The stance foot stands on the ground, and the bindings outrank it", with scenarios: neutral pinned through stance; contact on the ground for every parameter set; undrawable geometry gives way while bound values read back exactly; still frames show a planted foot. Grep for "ground", "lowest foot", "inverse kinematics", "unrelated" to find each one. Keep requirement titles unless the meaning changes. **design.md:** add D15, covering the hybrid approach, why (a) and (b) were rejected (with numbers), the domain, the fallback and the illustrative key changes. **tasks.md:** add a ps19.4 section. ## Screenshots **Setup.** Run `npm ci`. Get the port with `node -e "import('./scripts/lib/harnessProvenance.mjs').then(m=>console.log(m.resolveDevServerPort()))"` (never 5173), start `npm run dev -- --port

--strictPort`, and run `assertServesThisCheckout`. Use GPU Chromium (`--headless=new --enable-gpu --ignore-gpu-blocklist`) and check that the renderer reads ANGLE Metal. **Sandbox.** Load `/strides/src/runner/dev/sandbox.html`. Take 390×844 and 1280×900 shots, in light and dark, with reduced and normal motion, saved to `test-results/model-runner/ps19.4-*.png`. Read them and confirm: - the ground touches the planted foot in still frames; - footSide and feetFront show the foot on the line; - the big-landing fallback dip is small; - the swing toe never crosses the line. **Summary view (ONE shot, required by the user).** ResultsSummary is mounted from `src/results/MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:681`; find the routing (a view toggle or query param). Upload `src/video/demo-clips/park-side-landscape.mp4` through the Upload tab (`input[type=file]`, `setInputFiles`), wait for `/analysis complete/i`, open the summary view, and screenshot it at 1280 light, as `test-results/model-runner/ps19.4-summary-1280-light.png`. Read it and confirm the runner's foot is on the ground line. **Clean up.** Kill the server. Keep the driver uncommitted, in your own tmp dir.
acceptance_criteria:
Stance foot sits on y=0 through stance within 0.01 torso lengths at neutral and at range corners
Every 'measuring the model returns the bound value' test in src/runner still passes
Renderer ground line returns to y=0 with no floating figure in 390/1280 screenshots

title: Evidence forward decode on a 4K clip is paced by the main-thread scale pass on phones
description: S21, 2026-10-13: forward evidence decode of park-side-landscape.mp4 (4K, 233 frames) takes 17-19 s vs 7-14 s via seeks, because VideoDecoder output callbacks are delivered on the main thread between the MediaPipe scale pass's synchronous ~50 ms detectForVideo calls. Other clips are faster forward. Options: decode in a dedicated worker and transfer only wanted VideoFrames (must prove pixel identity on Android - see strides-6i6.3's tail-frame finding), or schedule the 4K clip's extraction after its scale pass. Not a measurement issue: evidence images never feed metrics.
