title: Start the scale-pass detector warm-up earlier on short sequential clips
description: Gate 2 (2026-10-05): the strides-e4c.2 warm-up (MediaPipe PoseLandmarker creation started at primary start()) takes 1.9-2.2 s, but with T1/T3 front-approach's primary now finishes in 1.65 s, so the scale pass waits 217-259 ms for the detector again (T2 alone measured 9-119 ms; pre-T2 ~264 ms). Candidate: kick the warm-up at sequential-probe resolution (true) instead of start(), or as soon as the primary detector is ready AND a sequential clip is loaded. Trade-off to measure: does concurrent MediaPipe creation slow the cold MoveNet load that gates primary start (~1.1 s)? Gate: bit-identical A/B; scale detector wait on front-approach; analysis-complete@ not worse.
notes:
Implemented on branch perf/e4c.7-earlier-warmup @ f72fb87 (base e4905d2), not pushed/merged. Warm-up (getScalePassDetector + trackScaleDetectorCreation + unchanged scale-detector-warmup perf line) now fires in the probe effect when the clip's sequential probe COMMITS true, instead of in start(). Same gates (scale pass enabled, backend != mediapipe). New guard: page-wide count of playback primaries sampling; probe-time warm-up skipped while >0 (strides-gyl), start() falls back. Single commit, revertable. Live gate pending: primary start@ (overlap with cold MoveNet load), scale detector wait on front-approach, analysis-complete@.
Review follow-up @ 80f2bb2: reset() clears warm-up marker + bumps generation; counter clamp -> dev console.assert; probe-time warm-up cancelled via generation + mounted ref (not a cleanup flag: StrictMode would disable it in dev); WebM+MP4 mixed-case note on the counter.
GATE 6 VERIFIED LIVE (2026-10-05, verifier) at int perf/e4c 129f9ba vs gate-5 e4905d2 (own worktree, same session) and ref c39a7a8; real GPU ANGLE Metal M4 Pro, fresh process/trial, derived ports, identity verified. (1) A/B BIT-IDENTICAL: stripped md5 577597202f4c7675a92b2fbfd0ade236 both, rtk proxy diff empty. (2) Pixel check 2 trials: 43/43 identical to ref. (3) Timing g5 -> g6 (3 trials all clips + 3 extra on multiperson/front-approach/side-portrait, i.e. n=6 there): warm-up starts at sequential-probe settle (73-142 ms after trigger, ~1.0-1.2 s BEFORE primary start; StrictMode guard fine), duration 2.2 s -> 0.26-0.62 s. MoveNet cold load not measurably slowed: P1 start@ median (n=6) multiperson 1173 -> 1241, approach 1020 -> 1105, within the 900-1500 per-trial noise. front-approach scale detectorWait 210 [197..231] -> 8 [8..8] (PASS); scale done@ 4512 -> 4101. BUT analysis complete@ regresses systematically on two clips: median (n=6) multiperson 3469 -> 3754 (+285), front-approach 2786 -> 3105 (+320); side-portrait 4436 -> 4369, landscape 4707 -> 4760, demo3 7799 -> 7751 flat. Cause is the primary-ready -> 'Analysis complete' gap, not start@: multiperson 34-38 ms (6/6) -> 308-330 (6/6), front-approach 109-142 -> 343-346; portrait 334-360 both arms; landscape 418-451 -> 471-516. Unverified hypothesis: the gap growth (~230-290) matches the scale pass's synchronous first detect (222-244 ms), which now lands before React commits the status. Pre-registered rule FAILS (complete@ worse beyond noise on multiperson and front-approach) -> recommend reverting e4c.7, or root-causing the gap before keeping it. (4) Mixed mp4+WebM: order P-seq S-seq P-webm S-webm on all trials at ref (6), g5 (4) and g6 (2); WebM primary 99/99 everywhere. WebM scale pass detected/total: ref 86/99 x5 + 86/98; g5 85/96, 86/99 x3; g6 86/98, 86/99. NOT consistently below 99: occasional 1-3 sample drops occur at reference too (1/6), so the gate-5 85/96 is playback-sampler jitter, not a regression.
REVERTED on perf/e4c (gate 6, pre-registered rule failed): analysis-complete@ +285 ms multiperson, +320 ms front-approach (primary-ready -> status gap 34->320 ms), although front-approach scale detector wait 210->8 ms and MoveNet cold load not measurably slowed. Hypothesis: with the detector already warm, the scale pass's first synchronous detect (~230 ms) runs before the 'Analysis complete' paint. Same gap already exists at gate 5 on side-portrait/landscape (334-451 ms). Retry e4c.7 only after the paint-yield fix (strides-e4c.8) lands.
close_reason: Won't do (measured, reverted): removes front-approach scale detector wait (208->8 ms) but reproduces a +230-290 ms primary-ready->'Analysis complete' gap on front-approach and multiperson (gate 6 and e4c.8 probe arm B, bit-identical outputs). Net loss on time-to-first-results; pre-registered rule failed twice.

title: Evidence calibration can apply the edit-list shift to a run that used the playback sampler
description: Pre-existing (found in strides-dt9 review, 2026-10-05). When useVideoAnalysis's 3 s sequential-decode probe timeout wins, the run samples on the playback path, but evidenceSeekOffset.ts (~line 193) asks canUseSequentialDecode, which later answers true, and applies the WebCodecs edit-list shift (-media_time/timescale) to a playback-path run whose timestamps are already in currentTime's domain -> evidence images land ~2 frames off. Fix: record the sampler path the run actually used (diagnostics.sampling.path) and have calibration read that instead of re-deriving it.

title: Seek each evidence instant once, in timestamp order
description: extractPlannedFrames (src/video/extractFrames.ts) seeks once per instant in metric order; instants repeat across metrics (kneeFlexion/kneeDrive share one, armSwingAmplitude pair, footstrike instants across overstriding/footStrikePattern/stepWidth). Group by timestamp, seek ascending, draw every crop needing that instant from one presented frame; preserve base-then-ghost compositing per canvas (EVIDENCE_GHOST_BLEND_ALPHA). Related: strides-zm8, strides-061.
acceptance_criteria: Evidence canvases pixel-identical before/after (hash every canvas on all four clips). Seek count and extraction time vs T0 baseline. Gate: scripts/ab-person-selection.mjs --arm base={} --clips side-landscape,side-portrait,front-approach,multiperson --trials 3 --evidence, before vs after, BIT-IDENTICAL outside elapsedMs (compare elapsedMs-stripped md5 via rtk proxy sh -c; never trust bare diff). npm test, tsc -b, eslint on touched files green. Wall-clock gain shown against the T0 [perf-timings] baseline.
notes:
Branch perf/e4c.5-evidence-seek-dedupe @ 25947b0 (on 5a2afbb). extractPlannedFrames visits each distinct seek target once (exact target incl. offsets+clamp), draws all images needing it directly from the <video> (no intermediate canvas/bitmap). Order = earliest target whose waiting instants are all drawable (base-before-ghost topological order, ascending where allowed); ghost-before-base costs a backward step; a base/ghost cycle (front-approach armSwingAmplitude) costs one revisit. Real kept-pass plans: 13->11, 14->11, 12->9, 15->12 seeks (54->43). [perf-timings] evidence adds 'seeks'. Unit tests only; live gate pending verifier.
VERIFIED LIVE (2026-10-05, verifier) at int perf/e4c db25af3 (5a2afbb + e4c.5) vs ref c39a7a8 and gate-2 5a2afbb; real GPU ANGLE Metal M4 Pro, fresh process per trial, derived ports, identity verified. A/B gate (4 clips x3 --evidence) BIT-IDENTICAL: stripped md5 577597202f4c7675a92b2fbfd0ade236 both sides, rtk proxy diff empty. Evidence pixel check (sha256 getImageData per main canvas, 4 singles + demo3, 2 trials): 43/43 canvases identical to ref x2, none missing, ref stable. Kept-pass seeks issued / planned / reused (seek+draw ms, g2 -> g3): landscape 8/10/2 (4192->3832), portrait 5/6/4 (747->590), approach 7/8/2 (981->1023), multiperson 10/13/1 (1277->1207); fresh no-reuse passes in demo3: portrait 11/14 (1895->1482), approach 9/12 (1682->1328), landscape kept 10/12/1 (6091->4725) - matches the unit expectations 14->11, 12->9. Evidence settled@ ref -> g2 -> g3: landscape 14497->11939->11503, portrait 9538->7840->7593, approach 6401->5342->5893, multiperson 7707->6590->6650; demo3 all-settled 25531->23930->21547 (all-complete 14186->13030->13026). Approach/multiperson settle regressions are primary start@ cold-load noise (approach start@ 1062->1601), not evidence: scale-done->settled went 1044->1128 approach, 1330->1213 multiperson, 4840->4259 landscape, 809->630 portrait. Reuse counts shifted vs g2 (multiperson reused 2->1, demo3 landscape 0->1): which metrics the aborted pre-graft pass completed is a race; stable within each run, pixels identical regardless.
close_reason: Merged to local perf/e4c (db25af3). Gate 3: A/B bit-identical, all 43 canvases pixel-identical; 3-clip demo evidence settled 23.9 -> 21.5 s; seeks per plan 14->11 / 12->9.

title: Investigate removing the separate poster-frame decode
description: posterFrame.ts opens its own detached <video> decode per clip (queueDetachedDecode). Measure its cost from T0; if material, reuse the evidence decode or capture during sampling. Only ship if the poster is pixel-identical. May close won't-fix with the measurement.
acceptance_criteria: Either: poster pixel-identical with one fewer decode and measured saving; or closed with the T0 number showing it is not worth it.
close_reason: Won't fix (measured). T0: poster 139-450 ms (4K seek+draw ~357). All posters are requested at clip-ready and drain within ~1.2 s of upload; evidence is first requested >=3.6 s (single) / ~14 s (3-clip demo) later, after all clips are analyzed, and queueDetachedDecode is FIFO -> 0 ms queue delay to analysis, scale pass or evidence (analysis/scale never use that queue). Capturing during WebCodecs sampling is not provably pixel-identical (different decode/colour path, edit-list clock offset, stride may skip the instant); reusing the evidence decoder delays posters 3-13 s. Unmeasured residual: poster <video> decode contending with clip 1's primary pass (0.5-1.1 s total work) - an A/B with useClipPoster stubbed would settle it.

title: estimateLocalTorsoLengths needs a minimum window population
description: Review of strides-cge (975118c): next to a torso gap a ±0.5 s window can hold only 1-2 resolvable torsos, so the local torso becomes a per-frame denominator (the jitter D3 rejected) and the unbounded clipTorso/localTorso factor can push one ankle sample into the p95. Gate on window population (>= N torso samples, else null), not a factor clamp (a clamp cuts real approach signal). Not observed on the 7-clip corpus; window sparsity never measured. Also: the skip-ordering test in viewDetection.test.ts has no interpolated ankles, so 'skip happens before the interpolated count' is not actually exercised. Optional hardening: return all-null instead of throwing RangeError on decreasing timestamps (production sorts first, but a throw ends the run in phase 'error').

title: Decide whether to flip the default results view from classic to guided (?view=guide)
description:
Deferred by epic strides-kgi. The guided results view shipped opt-in: resolveResultsViewMode (src/results/resultsViewMode.ts) selects guide only for exactly one ?view=guide, and everything else — including absent — resolves classic. This is a PRODUCT DECISION for the user to make after living with the guided view, not an engineering call; do not flip it without that decision.

If flipped, check before shipping:
- scripts/ab-person-selection.mjs and the e2e suite load the default page and wait on role=status 'Analysis complete.' — both views render it, but every A/B and e2e reading today is taken against classic, so a flip changes what the harness drives. Confirm the harness still reads [analysis-diagnostics]/[evidence-coverage] identically (those are view-independent console lines, but verify).
- resultsViewMode.ts's strict parse and searchWithResultsViewMode's 'classic removes view entirely' rule both encode classic-as-default; the address for classic would need a value (e.g. ?view=classic) and resultsViewMode.test.ts pins the current contract.
- openspec: openspec/specs/guided-results-view/spec.md carries 'Requirement: The classic results view remains the default' — a flip fully reverses it, so per CLAUDE.md's archive hazards REMOVE it (with Reason/Migration) and ADD a new requirement under a fresh name rather than MODIFY it.
- Open guided-view defects that a default flip would expose to every user: strides-31k (slow-motion capture hint), strides-366 (no error boundary; the toggle is inside the crashing tree), strides-ryi, strides-xyc.
notes: 2026-10-16: user decided to flip the default to guided.
close_reason: Shipped on feat/ux-round-1 (openspec results-ux-round-one): unit-tested, live-verified at 390/1280 px on real GPU, A/B bit-identical to main except elapsedMs.

title: Guided view: resolve Folland's per-step vs per-stride pelvis-oscillation convention to unblock a verticalOscillation (% torso) band
description:
Deferred by epic strides-kgi (guided-results-view design.md D5.2). verticalOscillation (percent of torso length) is the one unbanded metric where a band IS arithmetically derivable: Folland 2017 MSSE 49(7):1412-1423 pelvis oscillation 0.052 H divided by Winter's textbook torso fraction 0.288 H (after Drillis & Contini 1966) gives ~0.18 torso lengths, range 0.11-0.26. This repo's own readings (~18-25%) land inside it — which is exactly why it must not ship on that basis.

It was NOT shipped because the derivation passes through two unresolved steps, either of which moves the answer:
1. a textbook anthropometric constant standing in for a measured torso length, and
2. an ambiguous per-stride vs per-step convention in Folland's pelvis-oscillation figure (the same ambiguity D3 resolved for verticalRatio from Garmin's own manual; for Folland no stated definition was found).

TO UNBLOCK: find Folland's stated definition (paper methods / supplementary material / author correspondence) of whether 0.052 H is per step or per stride. If resolved, a band still has to be justified against the governing rule 'a band is cited or it does not ship' — the torso constant is a second, separate question; record whether it is acceptable rather than assuming. 'Our footage lands inside it' is not corroboration, because a band built to contain it proves nothing.

If a band ships: src/guidance/metricGuidance.ts verticalOscillation entry (band: null today), metricGuidance.test.ts names the seven unbanded entries explicitly so this is a visible change, and the openspec guided-results-view spec needs a MODIFIED/ADDED delta. Do not implement until the convention is resolved.

title: 'A second look at the clip added N more metrics' counts metrics the page lists as not measured
description: Found in live verification of strides-kgi.7 (2026-09-15). ResultsView.tsx's addedMetricCount (mirrored verbatim in GuidedResultsView) counts non-null verticalOscillationCm + stepWidthCm values, but a non-null value with viewFit 'unsuitable' is tier-3 excluded and listed as not measured. park-side-portrait: status says 'added 1 more metric' while both centimetre metrics are listed not measured; park-approach says 'added 2' while stepWidthCm is not measured. Pre-existing on main in the classic view. Fix: count metricTier(m) !== 'excluded' in both views; ResultsView.test.tsx and GuidedResultsView.test.tsx pin the current strings.
acceptance_criteria: The added-metric message counts only metrics shown as measured in both results views; park-side-portrait and park-approach demo states no longer report added metrics that the page lists as not measured.
notes: Selected review item #15 in epic strides-3f6. Apply the metricTier guard to both ResultsView.tsx and GuidedResultsView.tsx, with regression tests for excluded centimetre values.
close_reason: Implemented in isolated drive worktree; targeted results tests, lint, and build pass; ready for integration

title: No error boundary: a crash in either results view unmounts the whole app, toggle included
description: Surfaced by the strides-kgi.6 review (2026-09-15). There is no componentDidCatch/getDerivedStateFromError anywhere in src/. If GuidedResultsView throws, the root unmounts - header, clip strip, in-flight analysis, and the ResultsViewToggle that is the only way back. A shared ?view=guide link would reproduce it on every analysis. Low likelihood (guidedGroups is typed over Record<MetricId,...>), but the recovery path is inside the crashing tree. Suggested: an error boundary around the results-view slot in MultiClipVideoSession that falls back to classic and writes ?view back to classic.

title: Overstriding caveat says 'this pipeline' to runners
description: src/heuristics/overstriding.ts:~113 authors a user-facing caveat containing 'this pipeline', and src/results/metricDescriptions.ts's overstriding entry says 'the footstrike instant this pipeline can detect'. Both render verbatim to runners in the classic panel (and the caveat in the guided view too). Surfaced by the strides-kgi.5 UX review on 2026-09-15; left out of the guided-results-view change because src/heuristics/ is out of its scope and the shared description is the classic view's copy. Fix is wording only: say 'this app' or restate without the implementation noun. Check MetricsPanel.test.tsx / overstriding.test.ts for asserted strings.

title: Show evidence extraction in progress on metric cards
description: A metric whose evidence was planned but not yet decoded rendered the same empty space as a metric with no evidence, for the several seconds each of the two extraction passes takes. Cards now show a thumbnail-sized pulsing placeholder plus a text line, with the region marked aria-busy.
close_reason: Shipped as openspec change show-evidence-extraction-in-progress; live-verified on park-side-landscape: 6 placeholders on the first pass, 7 once the scale pass planned verticalOscillationCm, all 144x144, clearing to 8 canvases

title: Drop clip timestamps from evidence captions
description: Evidence thumbnail captions ended on a clip time the reader cannot act on (no player, no timeline, no seek affordance in a metric card). Caption is now the metric's own label, plus the demotion sentence where a pair was demoted. Instants unchanged on the plan and still on [evidence-coverage].
close_reason: Shipped as openspec change drop-timestamps-from-evidence-captions; live-verified on park-side-landscape (8 captions, no clip time, demotion sentence intact)

title: results-view annotation requirement has no armSwingAmplitude bullet
description:
openspec/specs/results-view/spec.md, 'An annotation depicts what was measured at the depicted instant, never the card's reported value', lists per-metric reasons the drawn quantity differs from the reported value. armSwingAmplitude is NOT listed, and arguably should be: its value is the MEAN of the two sides' fitted peak-to-peak amplitudes divided by a clip-median torso length, so it spans BOTH images and a denominator present in neither - the same structural gap the verticalRatio and stepWidth bullets record.

Pre-existing gap, not opened by strides-zhv. That change removed the armSwingSymmetry bullet ('reports a ratio BETWEEN its two images, one per side. Neither image shows it.') and deliberately did NOT add an amplitude one, to avoid widening an already-large MODIFIED block for a hole it did not create.

Verified while doing so: removing the symmetry bullet does NOT orphan '#### Scenario: A ratio between two images is labelled on neither' - that scenario is generic and still backed by the surviving verticalRatio bullet.

No code change expected; the annotation layer already draws no text at all (no fillText/strokeText anywhere in the annotation modules). This is a spec-completeness fix.

title: Hoist the duplicated arm-swing test fixture into __fixtures__
description:
buildArmSwingFrames + makeJitter + the geometry constants (SHOULDER_Y, LEFT_SHOULDER_X, BASE_WRIST_OFFSET_Y, TORSO_LENGTH_PX...) are now duplicated VERBATIM in three test files: src/heuristics/armSwing.test.ts, armSwingAmplitude.test.ts, and formerly armSwingSymmetry.test.ts (deleted by strides-zhv). ~100 lines x3.

strides-zhv deliberately left the third copy in place: hoisting is a refactor, and that change was a deletion. The right home is src/heuristics/__fixtures__/, beside syntheticGait.ts and testFrames.ts.

Care needed: the builder's scaleGrowthFactor doc explains WHY the growth is exponential (log g(t) linear in time, inside the stabilizer's log-quadratic trend space by construction, which is what makes the expected values exact rather than approximate). That reasoning must survive the move - two tests assert bit-exact no-ops (toBe, not toBeCloseTo) against it.

title: vite.config.ts has port: 5177 at the top level of defineConfig, where it is not a valid option
description:
Introduced by 5947c3f ('Pin the dev server to port 5177'). 'port' is not a member of UserConfig at the top level - it belongs under 'server'. Two consequences:

1. It is the repo's one standing 'npx tsc -b' error: vite.config.ts(10,1): error TS2769: No overload matches this call. ... Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'port' does not exist in type 'UserConfigExport'. Every subsequent typecheck has to be read past it, which is exactly how a real error gets missed.
2. It does not do what the commit says. Vite ignores the unknown key, so the dev server is not pinned to 5177 by it. resolveDevServerPort() still returns the derived per-checkout port (5284 in the agent worktree) and the harness still works - which is why nobody noticed.

Fix is either moving it under 'server' (if the pin is actually wanted, though note it would then fight scripts/lib/harnessProvenance.mjs's derived-port guard, which exists specifically to stop parallel worktrees colliding on a shared port) or deleting it (if the derived port is the intended mechanism, which the guard's own documentation says it is).

Found 2026-09-05 during strides-5t4; deliberately not fixed there on minimal-surface grounds - it is unrelated to the evidence seek and the right answer involves a decision about the port pin, not a typo fix.
close_reason: Deleted the inert top-level port key from vite.config.ts. npx tsc -b now reports 'No errors found' - the repo's one standing error is gone. Deleted rather than relocated under server: 5947c3f's stated intent is already achieved by the --port 5177 it added to package.json's dev script in the same commit, and playwright.config.ts overrides that with its own derived --port on the CLI, so a vite.config entry would be a redundant third place the port is decided. Verified live: npm run dev still answers on 5177, resolveDevServerPort() still derives per-checkout (5262 in the main checkout).

title: park-side-portrait: the whole vertical-oscillation family is null — hip-bounce fit fails on the 12.17 s side clip
description:
The new portrait side clip (src/video/demo-clips/park-side-portrait.mp4, 1080x1920, 345 frames, 12.17 s) analyzes well on every other axis but resolves NONE of the VO family, and no cadence.

Measured live, fresh Chromium, real GPU, via scripts/ab-person-selection.mjs --clips side-portrait --trials 1:
  view=side confidence 0.8366  <- the HIGHEST view confidence of the three demo clips
  totalSamples 345, detectedFrames 277 (80%, the best detection ratio of the three)
  trunkLean 10.3371 @ 0.9929 (sampleSize 280)
  overstriding -0.008 @ 1.00, kneeFlexion 114.665 @ 0.93, footStrikePattern -0.240 @ 1.00, kneeDrive 32.858 @ 0.96
  verticalOscillation / verticalRatio / verticalOscillationCm: value null, sampleSize 0, frameCoverage 0
  cadence: null

So this is not a tracking failure - the clip has the best keypoint coverage in the corpus. It is the shared spectral hip-bounce fit failing its quality gate (cadenceMinFitR2 / verticalOscillationMinFitR2, 0.30). Likely causes to check, in order: (a) the clip is 12.17 s and the runner is only in frame for part of it, so the presence-trimmed window may still span mostly-empty stretches that flatten the fit; (b) the source is variable frame rate - the container claimed 402 frames and only 345 decode, ~28.4 fps effective - so timestamps may be uneven enough to hurt a fixed-grid spectral fit.

Consequence today: the clip contributes nothing to the fused demo panel; fusion picks clip 1 (side-landscape) or clip 3 (front-approach) for every metric. Not a regression - this clip is new - but it means one third of the demo corpus is carrying no weight.
acceptance_criteria: Either the fit resolves on this clip, or the reason it structurally cannot is measured and recorded.
notes: Filed from strides-w2v's live verification. Not blocking that change: all three clips analyze and the fused demo renders 12 metrics.

title: Harness hazard: new URL(<non-literal>, import.meta.url) resolves to the string 'undefined' under vite/vitest
description:
Third member of the strides-ef5 / strides-h4r family: an instrument that returns a clean, plausible wrong answer instead of failing.

Hit for real writing strides-8w2's test. This, in a vitest module:

    const p = fileURLToPath(new URL(`../../../public/${runtimeValue}`, import.meta.url))

does not resolve a path. Vite's assetImportMetaUrl plugin rewrites 'new URL(x, import.meta.url)' into an asset lookup whenever x is not a string literal; with a template carrying a runtime value it becomes a glob that matches nothing, and the expression evaluates to the STRING 'undefined'. Observed symptom: ENOENT on '<test-dir>/undefined' — note the path is relative to the TEST file, with the '../../../public/' prefix gone entirely, which is what gives it away.

It failed loudly here only because the very next call was readFileSync. Anything that treats the result as an optional path, or feeds it to something that tolerates a miss, would have passed vacuously on a check that measured nothing.

Workaround used: path.resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), ...) — node's own path resolution, which vite does not rewrite. Recorded in mediapipePoseLandmarker.test.ts's own comment.

Action: worth a line in CLAUDE.md's harness section alongside the ef5 diff hazard and the h4r async-predicate hazard, since all three have the same failure signature. Surface: testing/infra.

title: At 390px the clip strip has only 158px, so a leading entry leaves a clip frame 50px visible while idle
description:
Measured during strides-utn.5's live check (design.md D11.4), 390x844, one clip loaded:

  strip box 158 px wide (wordmark + AddClipAction take the rest)
  model entry 96 px + 12 px gap
  clip frame [209,305] against a strip ending at 259 -> 50 of 96 px visible

HARMLESS TODAY and verified so: it only occurs while the clip's condition is 'loading'/'idle', where clipHostsLiveElement is false and nothing is reading frames off the element. Every window in which the element IS being read measured 96/96 px visible, because ClipStripEntry re-scrolls on both hostsLiveElement and (since utn.5) leadingEntryPresent.

The hazard is that the margin is thin and the invariant is implicit: anything that makes a clip host its live element earlier (at 'idle', or during load), or that adds a second leading entry, re-opens a concealment path that measures healthy through getBoundingClientRect. The concealment cost is ~20-24% of sampled frames on the playback path.

Options if it ever needs closing: narrow the model entry (it hosts no element, so the 96x72 floor does not apply to it — the floor is for an element the sampler reads), or scroll the strip on any leading-entry change rather than only when the clip is hosting. Surface: frontend.
acceptance_criteria: At 390px with three demo clips, the runner can discover and reach all entries with touch and keyboard; a clear overflow cue is present when clips extend beyond the strip; every actively sampled video frame remains fully visible and retains at least the existing 96x72 CSS px floor.
notes: Selected review item #14 in epic strides-3f6. In addition to the existing live-element visibility hazard, make horizontal overflow discoverable at 390px so Clip 2 and Clip 3 are evidently available. Do not shrink a live video frame below the measured painting floor.
close_reason: 390px header gives three clip frames full 96x72 visibility; four-clip overflow cue and scroll checked in Chrome; build/lint/tests pass

title: Decide whether a failed model download deserves an in-product retry
description:
strides-utn.5 DECLINED an in-product retry and shipped copy that names the recovery instead ('Reload the page to try again.'). Recorded in openspec/changes/model-load-visibility-and-cache/design.md D11.2.

The three reasons, so this is revisitable rather than re-argued from scratch:
1. The primary detector is created once on mount and cached for the app lifetime, so its failure window is BEFORE any clip exists — a page reload costs the reader no session state, and a Retry control would buy back exactly a reload. movenet.ts:313-316 makes the same argument from the other end.
2. The scale pass ALREADY retries: getScalePassDetector clears its pending promise on failure, so the next analysis run re-attempts. Its 'error' phase is transient by construction.
3. Cost: retry means reopening usePoseDetector (a strides-utn.1 file), adding an attempt counter and a detector transition (null -> non-null AFTER an error) that every consumer currently assumes happens at most once.

Revisit if telemetry or a report shows real users stuck on a failed model load — e.g. a flaky connection where a reload also fails but a retry would have succeeded, or if the primary detector ever stops being created at mount.

title: Playwright waitForFunction with an async predicate settles on the truthy Promise
description:
Hit while writing strides-utn.4's cached-bytes byte-identity probe (2026-09-03).

  await page.waitForFunction(async () => {
    const cache = await caches.open('strides-model-assets-v1')
    return (await cache.keys()).filter(r => r.url.includes('tfhub.dev')).length === 7
  })

resolved immediately against an EMPTY cache. The probe then enumerated nothing, compared nothing,
and printed '0/0 cached MoveNet files are byte-identical to a fresh network fetch' — exit 0, no
error, and a line that reads like a pass unless you notice the 0/0.

Same failure shape as the guards CLAUDE.md's harness section exists for: a clean, plausible number
instead of a crash.

Fix used: poll from Node with page.evaluate in a loop and throw with the observed keys on timeout.

Worth a line in CLAUDE.md's harness section if another agent trips it — do not use an async
predicate with waitForFunction; the value it awaits is not necessarily what gets tested.
Surface: tooling.

title: A screen-reader user gets no signal that evidence imagery is still arriving
description:
strides-8zv's placeholder is deliberately SILENT: the pending evidence block is aria-hidden in its entirety (box and captions), adds no live region and no aria-busy. Reasons in openspec/changes/pending-evidence-placeholder/design.md D9 — results-view requires at most ONE live region announcing clip analysis progress for the whole session (spec :1074-1075), Demo 1 plans seven sections so per-card announcement would be seven announcers racing the authoritative line, and captionFor/altFor describe a picture that is not there yet.

Verified live 2026-09-03: live-region count held at 2 across 1,320 snapshots on three clips.

What it leaves open: a reader who cannot see the page learns nothing about the 3.5-4.5 s window in which imagery is arriving. That is the STATUS QUO — they got no such signal before this change either, and the reflow being fixed is a visual one — so this is a gap, not a regression.

Closing it properly means deciding what the session's single live region should say about extraction, which is a change to 'Session status stays a single announced line while per-clip progress moves to the clips', not to the placeholder requirement. Do NOT close it by adding a second announcer per card. Surface: frontend.

title: A pending-evidence placeholder still shrinks by a row on a partial extraction
description:
extractPlannedFrames pushes only successfully-extracted items (`if (extracted !== null) items.push(extracted)`, src/video/extractFrames.ts), so a two-image plan can settle to one image. The placeholder reserved two rows, so the card shrinks by one when that happens.

CLAUDE.md records ZERO extraction-failed across all three reference clips, so the plan predicts accurately in practice and this was NOT observed live on Demo 1, Demo 2 or multiperson (verified 2026-09-03, strides-8zv). The residual shift is also one row where the pre-placeholder behaviour was the whole two-column re-wrap, so this is strictly better than before either way.

Deliberately not designed around: the requirement is written as 'reserves the space the plan calls for', because the space the RESULT will occupy is not knowable before extraction and claiming it would be a promise the planner cannot keep. See openspec/changes/pending-evidence-placeholder/design.md D8.

Fixing it properly means either a per-image failure signal the placeholder can consume as it arrives, or making a partial extraction a whole-metric failure (which would COST coverage, not gain it). Neither is obviously right. Surface: frontend.

title: tfhub.dev model URLs now redirect to Kaggle, which bot-gates non-browser clients
description:
Supply-chain fragility found while scoping strides-utn. MoveNet's model URLs are library constants pointing at tfhub.dev (node_modules/@tensorflow-models/pose-detection/dist/movenet/constants.js:24-26). Measured this session: https://tfhub.dev/google/tfjs-model/movenet/singlepose/lightning/4/model.json?tfjs-format=file returns 302 to www.kaggle.com, and Kaggle then serves a Google reCAPTCHA challenge page — HTTP 200, ~20KB of HTML, confirmed via file(1).

Real browsers evidently get through (CLAUDE.md documents many successful live runs), so this is not currently breaking the app. But the app's primary detector depends at page load on a third-party redirect chain ending at a host that actively challenges automated clients, with no fallback and no pinned copy.

Worth deciding: self-host the MoveNet weights alongside pose_landmarker_full.task in public/models/ the way MediaPipe already is. That would remove the redirect chain, the bot gate and the third-party dependency in one move, and would make strides-utn.4 (custom IOHandler over MoveNet) substantially simpler — possibly unnecessary.

Do NOT quote the cache-control: no-store or access-control-allow-origin headers observed on that response as facts about the model; they were the challenge page's headers. strides-utn.2 measures the real ones in a browser.

title: armSwing 'tracked noticeably better' caveat misattributes fit disparity to tracking
description: The SIDE_FIT_QUALITY_DISPARITY_R2 caveat (armSwingSymmetry.ts:210, armSwingAmplitude.ts:215) says one arm 'was tracked noticeably better'. Measured on Demo 2 (strides-101 probe): the weaker-FITTING right arm is detected slightly BETTER than the left (98/99 detected, 1 low-score frame vs 95/99, 7 low-score). The disparity is sinusoidR2 0.497 vs 0.778 — trend-dominated trace, not detection dropout. Reword toward fit/rhythm ('one arm's motion matched a steady swing rhythm much better'), like the sibling caveat at :214.
close_reason: Shipped in the same change: caveat reworded to name rhythm-fit disparity ('One arm's swing rhythm fit its trace much less cleanly...') in both armSwingSymmetry and armSwingAmplitude; tests updated.

title: Revive arm midline crossing: per-approach statistic + a clip that actually crosses
description:
Successor to strides-7a6.3, which STOPPED at its pre-registered probe gate (2026-09-02, openspec change add-arm-midline-crossing-metric, archived with spec deltas withdrawn per the #57 precedent). Do not re-litigate the pooled-p95 statistic — the record is in that change's design.md D4.

What the probe established (fresh-process, real GPU, bit-identical Demo 2 trials):
- Pooled p95 of signed medial wrist excursion FAILED the pre-registered noise-tail rule at BOTH rungs (p95 and p90): the entire upper tail is one clip-opening episode (~0.083-0.434s, 19/20 left-arm at p90), not a recurring reach. A whole-series order statistic reads a single window, so the successor needs per-approach aggregation (kneeDrive's per-cycle-extremum shape: extrema of the signed series per arm, median over approaches) or an explicit single-window-tail guard.
- THE CORPUS CANNOT VALIDATE THE POSITIVE BRANCH: no clip in the repo shows any actual midline crossing (Demo 2 fraction-past-midline 0.000 both arms, pooled max -0.276 shoulder widths). Any redesign ships a metric whose defining behavior has never been observed in test data.
- Useful measured facts that survive: Demo 2 strict-shoulder-pair pooled n=197 (sample gate passes comfortably); shoulderWidthPx 165.0 vs torsoLengthPx 232.7; direction-independence held on the direction-0 clip; per-side interpolated fractions L 0.031 / R 0.020.
- Full signed series preserved in the probe JSONs (scratchpad wave3/probe-*.json — session-local, regenerate via the probe recipe in the archived design.md if needed).

BLOCKED ON: a front-view clip where the runner's arms genuinely cross the midline (user-recordable; same shape as the heel-whip rear-view-footage gap). Once it exists: fresh openspec change, NEW pre-registered rules for the per-approach statistic (do not adjudicate on the old probe data alone), then the standard metric fan-out (which would be 13 -> 14 at that point).

title: Add armMidlineCrossing metric: wrist-x excursion past shoulder midline (front-view-gated)
description:
[Surface: frontend | Plan: architect | Review: code+ux]

New MetricId (suggested: armMidlineCrossing), growing the union 13 -> 14. The classic "arms crossing the body" coaching cue: per-side wrist-x excursion past the shoulder midline, front-view-gated. LOWEST PRIORITY of the epic — cuttable if the user deprioritizes.

## Design facts (from research)
- Template: stepWidth.ts — the closest front-view, sign-sensitive metric.
- Midline reference: STRICT resolveBilateralPair('left_shoulder','right_shoulder') (keypoints.ts:72-84), NOT the tolerant resolveMidpoint — stepWidth.ts:113-121 documents why: a single-side fallback silently collapses the midline onto one shoulder and falsifies exactly the crossing sign being measured (a documented regression class in this repo).
- Sign convention: per stepWidth.ts:105-111/176-189 — sign by the candidate wrist's OWN-side shoulder relative to shoulder-mid (outwardSign pattern), not a clip-wide travel constant; raw unflipped offsets cancel toward zero for symmetric motion. Positive = crossed past midline (medial), by analogy.
- DESIGN DECISION (record in design.md with measurement): denominator — shoulder width (estimateHipWidth's sibling; plausible since front view is primary here and shoulder width degenerates only in SIDE view, per bodyScale.ts:16-22 reasoning) vs torsoLengthPx vs hip width. Also: sampled at which instants — every resolvable frame (max or p95 medial excursion per side?) vs footstrike-anchored; no spectral fit needed.
- View gating: front primary/1.0, side unsuitable/0.1, ambiguous unsuitable/0.2 — own viewFitTable row matching stepWidth/armSwingSymmetry (types.ts:818-838). Emits on Demo 2, excluded on Demo 1/multiperson.
- Wrist tracking quality on Demo 2 is asymmetric (fit R2 0.778 left / 0.497 right) and unquantified beyond that one clip — confidence design must account for per-side quality.
- Exemplar: new MetricExemplarKind + INSTANT_MARK_BUILDERS entry; a max-crossing instant with a guide at the shoulder-midline x is the natural mark (existing guide/marker primitives suffice — drawEvidenceAnnotations needs no edit).
- Card copy: crossing proxy, no propulsive-effectiveness or injury claims.

## Expected file paths
src/heuristics/armMidlineCrossing.ts + .test.ts (new); the standard MetricId fan-out (types.ts, index.ts, fuseHeuristics.ts x2, metricConfidence.ts, MetricsPanel.tsx + count assertions 13->14, index.test.ts, evidenceAnnotations.ts, fixture builders); openspec/specs/form-heuristics/spec.md requirement pair; openspec/specs/results-view/spec.md count sentence; count-bearing doc comments; CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md counts.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] openspec change (suggested slug: add-arm-midline-crossing-metric) validates --strict; design.md records denominator + sampling decisions with measurements
- [ ] Unit suite green; typecheck + lint clean
- [ ] Live: fresh-process 3 trials --evidence — emits on Demo 2, excluded on Demo 1; an exemplar renders on Demo 2
- [ ] All pre-existing metrics bit-identical on all three clips
- [ ] Regression anchor unchanged (VO_cm 4.421467928439415, fit x60 = 91.2 == cadence)
- [ ] Archived after ship+verify

## Notes
Depends on the armSwingAmplitude ticket ONLY for shared-file/spec serialization (no code dependency; it does not use the spectral fit at all). Do not start this ticket's spec delta until strides-7a6.2's change archives.
close_reason: STOPPED at pre-registered probe gate and WITHDRAWN per #57 precedent (archived 2026-09-02-add-arm-midline-crossing-metric, skip_specs, e8305dd): pooled-p95 tail was a single clip-opening window at both rungs, and the corpus contains no positive crossing to validate the metric's defining branch (Demo 2 max -0.276 shoulder widths). src/ and main specs byte-untouched. Successor: strides-7a6.4 (blocked on a front-view clip with real crossing).

title: The four sibling MIN_*_SAMPLE_SIZE constants are below stepWidth's own derived n >= 2k + 3 bound
description:
Surfaced reviewing strides-1mt, and deliberately NOT fixed there.

stepWidth.ts:18-83 derives n >= 2k + 3 for a median over per-strike ratios with k same-biased
contaminants, and prices k = 2 from two measured mechanisms:
  - boundary strikes (strides-aah) -- since EXCLUDED in detectFootstrikes, so this one is gone;
  - detector-dropout windows collapsing both ankles onto one point (strides-boc) -- STILL PRESENT,
    and explicitly 'not fixable at this layer'.

strides-1mt removed a THIRD mechanism (collapsed ankle pairs at phase-path strikes) but cannot touch
strides-boc: there both ankles sit far from the HIP while remaining far from EACH OTHER, and a
mutual-separation predicate is blind to that at any threshold.

So on stepWidth's own accounting k = 1 today, giving n >= 5. The four siblings sit below it:
  MIN_OVERSTRIDE_SAMPLE_SIZE      4
  MIN_FOOT_STRIKE_SAMPLE_SIZE     4
  MIN_STEP_WIDTH_CM_SAMPLE_SIZE   4
  MIN_KNEE_FLEXION_SAMPLE_SIZE    (check)
(MIN_STEP_WIDTH_SAMPLE_SIZE is already 7.)

At n = 4, k = 1 the median is mean(clean median, clean MAX) -- half the reported number is the worst
clean sample.

Not swept with strides-1mt on purpose, for the reason stepWidth.ts itself gives: 'the same arithmetic
applies to each, but each has its own estimator and its own blast radius, and sweeping them is a
separate decision'. Raising them would ALSO compound with the discount strides-1mt's gate already
applies to the same thinning (Demo 1: 2/4 = 0.5 vs 2/7 = 0.143).

Two ways this closes:
  1. Address strides-boc's dropout mechanism -- k reaches 0, the bound becomes n >= 3, and 4 is
     correct on the arithmetic as well as on the gait cycle.
  2. Or take the sweep as its own decision, with an A/B for the confidence movement it causes.

Referenced from overstriding.ts's MIN_OVERSTRIDE_SAMPLE_SIZE docstring.

title: Demoted step-width pair draws one ankle where a genuine single draws two
description:
A stepWidthStrike PAIR can collapse to one drawn instant (stepWidthStrike is in SINGLE_INSTANT_KINDS, so planExemplarFrames demotes rather than drops). Since strides-7v0 that demoted image draws only the base instant's own ankle, because the plan reads annotationKeypoints for the base role. Before that change it drew the union, i.e. both ankles.

So two one-frame step-width images now differ purely by how they got there:
  - a GENUINE single (selectOppositeSidePair found no adjacent opposite pair) keeps the opposite ankle, deliberately: it is emitted as crop context because a width read against the hip midline is only legible with the other foot in frame, and there is no second instant for it to be misattributed to.
  - a DEMOTED pair loses it, while the caption still reads 'Opposite-foot plants either side of the hip midline' + 'Shown as one frame...'.

LEGIBILITY, NOT CORRECTNESS. Both hips and the base ankle survive the narrowing, so no measurement mark is lost - buildStepWidthMarks needs left_hip, right_hip and ANKLE[instant.side] only. Asserted in evidenceAnnotations.test.ts.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN strides-7v0: a blanket 'demoted -> fall back to cropKeypoints' rule in the plan layer would be actively WRONG for overstriding, whose union is both legs - that is precisely the bug strides-7v0 fixed. Making it right per-metric is a plan-layer redesign (the planner would need to know, per kind, which parts of a union are context-for-one-instant vs the-other-instant's-measurement), which is out of proportion to the symptom.

Options if picked up: (a) leave it, and reword the demoted caption so it does not promise a second plant; (b) let a producer state a separate 'demoted' annotation set alongside the pair's two; (c) refuse to demote a stepWidth pair at all and drop it, so the genuine single is the only one-frame step-width image.

Reproduce: needs a clip where selectOppositeSidePair finds a pair whose two instants then land on the same sampled frame, are near-identical in box, or sit inside EVIDENCE_MIN_PAIR_SEPARATION_INTERVALS. Not observed on demo1/demo2/multiperson - all three either produce a real pair or no stepWidth card at all.

title: Step width evidence: the measurement is a ~4px stub while the denominator is the boldest mark
description:
Found during UX review of strides-7v0 (pre-existing, not caused by it).

On Demo 2's Step Width thumbnail the boldest amber mark is the caliper spanning the hip pair — the NORMALIZER — while the step width itself renders as a ~4-5px amber stub beside the ankle. At the real inline size (w-36, 144 CSS px nominal / 142 measured) the stub disappears entirely and the hip caliper is the only amber a reader registers, so the picture invites reading hip width as the measured quantity.

Consistent with CLAUDE.md's recorded legibility limit: the gestalt reads at 142px but fine marks do not resolve.

Also noted, lower severity: two full-height dashed midlines (one per instant, ~15px apart) run edge to edge including through the head and well below the feet; at 142px they merge into a single heavy dashed double-column that is the loudest element in the image.

Related: strides-60w (evidence ghost can vanish against a bright background at 144px).
acceptance_criteria: At 142px, the measured step-width mark is more visually prominent than its hip-width denominator; the dashed midlines do not dominate the picture; enlarged and inline evidence remain consistent.
notes: Selected review item #12 in epic strides-3f6. Treat with strides-60w as the evidence legibility wave, but keep the step-width annotation fix separate.
close_reason: Step-width evidence now emphasizes the ankle displacement, omits the misleading per-frame hip-width segment, and uses short local midline references; verified at 142 px in Chrome and with full tests, lint, and build.

title: Footstrikes are detected on the first and last sampled frames, where they cannot be confirmed
description:
Found by strides-87x, 2026-08-31.

On Demo 2 the background scale pass detects a footstrike at t=1.66833 -- the clip's FINAL sampled frame -- and it carries the most extreme offset ratio of the five (+1.38051, against a primary-pass maximum of +0.37568). The primary pass does not detect a strike there at all.

A strike on the last sampled frame has no following frame to confirm it; a strike on the first has no preceding one. Since strides-cjl, detectFootstrikes derives touchdown from the fitted hip-bounce phase (low point minus T/4), and the fit extends to the ends of the series, so an instant can be placed at a boundary where the ankle evidence to support it does not exist on both sides.

Compounding it: strides-boc established that MediaPipe's clip-OPENING frames on this clip are contaminated (10 of 12 consecutive frames missed, t=0.033-0.267s, surviving detections collapsing both ankles onto one point). The scale pass's other outlier strike sits at t=0.41708, at the edge of that window.

So both of the scale pass's two outlier strikes are at or near a clip boundary, and together they move a median-of-5 by 2.48x (strides-87x D2c).

WORTH CHECKING FIRST: whether this is specific to the phase-derived detector or was also true of the ankle-difference fallback it replaced. strides-cjl retained that fallback verbatim, so both are testable on the same clip.

OPTIONS, none chosen: require a strike to have supporting frames either side; exclude the first and last sampled frames from strike eligibility; or weight boundary strikes down rather than excluding them. Note any of these interacts with strides-<median bead> -- dropping boundary strikes REDUCES the strike count, which is the other half of that problem.
acceptance_criteria: Either footstrikes at the sampled-series boundaries are excluded or discounted, or it is documented why a strike with one-sided evidence is trustworthy -- verified on Demo 2, where the scale pass's t=1.66833 strike currently carries the clip's most extreme ratio.
close_reason: Shipped together. Boundary footstrikes excluded in detectFootstrikes -- and, after review, BEFORE selectFootstrikes' amplitude ranking on the fallback path, because a contaminated boundary pivot outranks a real contact, suppresses it within minIntervalSeconds, and was then dropped, deleting the real contact (reproduced: [] where a contact existed). MIN_STEP_WIDTH_SAMPLE_SIZE 4 -> 7 from n >= 2k+3 (derived shape) with k=2 (labelled a judgment call). A/B on 3 clips: exactly three fields moved, all stepWidth.confidence -- demo1 0.0875->0.05, demo2 1.0->0.714286 (the pre-registered 5/7), multiperson 0.08->0.0457143. No value, no sampleSize, no tier moved. Two plan assumptions corrected by the new per-metric diagnostics: demo1 and multiperson sat at sampleSize 4, so the saturation defect was corpus-wide not Demo 2-specific; and sampleSize unchanged everywhere means the boundary filter removed zero strikes from any primary pass.

title: subjectAgreement reads 99/99 while the two passes disagree about the clip's view and about stepWidth by 1.79x
description:
Split out of strides-fn4, 2026-08-31.

On Demo 2, one default MoveNet-primary run, the [analysis-diagnostics:scale-pass] line reports:

  subjectAgreement  { status: 'agreed', reason: null, comparedInstants: 99, agreeingInstants: 99 }

A flawless score. In the SAME run the two passes disagree about the clip's view (front vs ambiguous), about its sagittal excursion ratio by 4.8x (0.3284 vs 1.5911), and about stepWidth by 1.79x (0.2253 vs 0.4042).

#56 built subjectAgreement to catch primary/scale-pass divergence, and it does exactly what it says on the tin: it compares WHICH PERSON each pass selected, at matched timestamps. It is structurally incapable of seeing the two passes disagree about the clip's CAMERA GEOMETRY or about a metric's VALUE, because both are entirely compatible with looking at the same runner for the whole clip -- which is what is happening here.

This is not a bug in subjectAgreement. It is a gap between what the check measures and what a reader will take a 99/99 to mean. CLAUDE.md currently describes it as 'the sole observable for the primary/scale-pass divergence check' and says 'a verdict landing anywhere near 0.5 means the winner may be half runner and half bystander' -- true, and it invites reading 1.0 as 'the two passes agree', which this clip disproves.

OPTIONS, none chosen: (a) document the limit beside the field, cheapest and probably sufficient; (b) add a second, separate agreement observable comparing the two passes' shared metrics where both resolve (stepWidth is the obvious one -- both passes compute it, from the same frames, and a 1.79x gap is a loud signal); (c) compare the two passes' view labels directly and caveat on disagreement.

Note (b) and (c) would both have caught the strides-fn4 defect immediately, and nothing did.
acceptance_criteria: Either CLAUDE.md and the field's own doc state what subjectAgreement can and cannot see, or a second divergence observable ships that would have caught the Demo 2 view/stepWidth disagreement.

title: 'Confidence tiers hold' does not reproduce for person-of-interest: cadence degrades a tier onto the CORRECT value
description:
Found by strides-09k's fresh-process person-of-interest re-run, 2026-08-31. The default is not under review -- it is a correctness fix for a live-confirmed bug -- and this does not change that.

The 2026-08-15 ship decision recorded 'confidence tiers hold'. Under the fresh-process regime that is not quite true. On Demo 1, 3 trials per arm, zero spread:

  metrics.cadence.value        off 93.6     on 91.2
  metrics.cadence.confidence   off 0.7176   on 0.6341     -> normal degrades to caveated

No other tier moves on either demo clip in either direction.

THE POINT IS NOT THE TIER, IT IS WHICH VALUE IS RIGHT. 91.2 is this repo's own standing regression anchor for Demo 1: CLAUDE.md asserts fit.frequencyHz x 60 = 91.2 == cadence.value 91.2, re-confirmed on 2026-08-12, 2026-08-18 and 2026-08-31. So the arm that scores HIGHER confidence (POI off, 0.7176) is the arm whose number disagrees with the established ground truth, and the arm that drops below the 0.7 tier boundary is the one that lands on it.

That is a confidence signal that is anti-correlated with correctness on this cell. It is the same shape as strides-h4u's note that confidence is a fit-quality proxy rather than an accuracy measure, but this is a concrete instance with a known-correct answer to check against, which is rare.

WORTH DOING: (1) confirm on multiperson, which strides-09k did not run -- it is the only fixture with a genuine second near-field person and therefore the clip where POI should matter most; (2) work out why the shared hip-bounce fit scores the 93.6 run higher, since cadence and verticalOscillation both read that one fit and verticalOscillation's tier does NOT move here.
acceptance_criteria: The cadence tier degradation is either explained (why the wrong value fits better) or reproduced on multiperson and recorded, and CLAUDE.md's 'confidence tiers hold' line for person-of-interest is corrected to match.

title: A stride-spanning evidence image needs a different crop construction, not a different threshold
description:
Split out of strides-mjw, 2026-08-31, after the cause was isolated.

verticalRatio's stridePair exemplar is dropped by isTooFarApartPair on every clip, and the drop is CORRECT: the pair demands a union crop side of 4132.8 px on Demo 1's 3840-px-wide frame (growth 4.5306 against EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH = 2.5). It is not an unlucky pair. A stride pair spans a full stride of subject translation BY DEFINITION, and verticalRatio is side-view-gated -- the one camera angle where that translation is fully in-plane and therefore maximal. Every stride pair on every side-view clip has the same shape, so alternates cannot help and buildStridePairExemplar emits none anyway (alternates: 0).

So the exemplar KIND is structurally unreachable for this metric under a square, subject-scaled, ghosted crop. Whether a stride-spanning image is wanted at all is a PRODUCT question, and if it is, it needs a different construction:

  - a wide letterboxed crop (aspect != 1) rather than a square one, so a stride fits without shrinking the subject to nothing; or
  - a composed side-by-side rather than a ghost, since the two instants never overlap anyway; or
  - accept the loss permanently and let the bounceCycle carry the metric alone.

DO NOT raise EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH. 4.53 is not marginally over 2.5, and admitting it would re-admit trunkLean's 6.1-6.8 pairs on the same clip plus the multiperson whole-frame crop the guard was filed for (gh #71). DO NOT demote the pair to its base either -- isTooFarApartPair refuses demotion deliberately, and this exemplar's label ('One stride: consecutive left-foot strikes, ghosted together') is precisely a claim a single frame cannot make.

Full measurement: openspec/changes/archive/*-retire-the-stride-pair-best-image-claim/design.md D3-D5.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded on whether a stride-spanning image is wanted for verticalRatio. If yes, it ships via a crop construction that fits a stride without shrinking the subject below legibility at the 144 px inline size, verified by looking at the image. If no, this is closed and the coverage table records 8/7 on Demo 1 as final.

title: CLAUDE.md's evidence coverage table is stale — Demo 1 and multiperson both emit more than it records
description:
Pre-existing drift, found while re-measuring for strides-e9b (not caused by it — it is present in the
unmodified-main baseline run).

CLAUDE.md's "Metric frame evidence" coverage table records Demo 1 at 7 images / 5 sections with
trunkLean and overstriding both `all-gated-out`, and multiperson as a 7/5..4/3 RANGE with trunkLean
`all-gated-out` on every trial. Measured today on main (headless Chromium, real GPU, fresh process per
clip, last [evidence-coverage] line):

  Demo 1       8 images / 7 sections — trunkLean AND overstriding both now emit
  Demo 2       5 images / 4 sections — matches the table exactly
  multiperson  7 images / 6 sections — trunkLean now emits (crop 732.6 px, readable)

The cause is downstream work the table predates: edb3f07 (fall back to the next-best croppable
exemplar pair), 9fa169c (rank exemplar candidates by quality) and 4fac355 (judge a pair on the crop it
demands). Those changes are exactly what the table said would move these cells, so this is expected
drift rather than a defect — but the table is now the wrong reference to check a coverage regression
against, and CLAUDE.md tells readers to use it for precisely that.

Also worth folding in at the same time: the "multiperson is a RANGE" caveat already carries a
strides-b0y addendum saying the range does not survive the fresh-process regime, so the per-metric
column and the range paragraph now disagree with each other as well as with the measurement.

Separate from strides-hcm (stale "gallery" wording).
close_reason: Fixed and merged (b55c69e), with the numbers re-measured rather than pasted. Fresh-process regime, 3 trials, bit-identical on all three clips: Demo 1 8 images / 7 sections, Demo 2 5/4, multiperson 8 images / 7 sections. Note multiperson came in at 8/7, NOT the 7/6 I briefed - strides-e9b and strides-cjl both moved it after that measurement, and the extra section is verticalRatio, which now resolves on that clip (0.0348) and plans a bounceCycle. Four cells moved versus the old table, all traceable: trunkLean and overstriding now emit on Demo 1 AND multiperson where both were all-gated-out, and two of those four sit at EXACTLY MIN_EXEMPLAR_QUALITY 0.500 - they clear the gate but not comfortably, which is now written down. trunkLean on multiperson is no longer the far-apart-pair rejection: EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH is untouched at 2.5 and the pair it now picks demands 2.289 rather than the old 3.375, so the guard did not weaken - a better pair became reachable. The 'record multiperson as a RANGE' instruction is retired as a reused-browser artifact, with the old table kept as the record and demoted with a forward pointer, and the caveat preserved that only the PRESENCE OR ABSENCE of a range is comparable across the intervening evidence changes, never the values.

title: stepWidthCm's paired exemplar omits measuredSide, so its caliper is never drawn
description:
stepWidthCm.ts's buildExemplars is a near-verbatim copy of stepWidth.ts's, but the paired
branch omits two fields the original supplies:

  stepWidth.ts:97-98    measuredSide: base.side,
                        pairedMeasuredSide: ghost.side,
  stepWidthCm.ts:88-90  (absent)

Neither module sets the pair-level `side` (deliberately -- the two instants are opposite feet),
so for a stepWidthCm PAIR, resolveInstantSide (evidenceFrames.ts:555) evaluates
`measured ?? exemplar.side ?? null` to null on both halves. buildStepWidthMarks
(evidenceAnnotations.ts:813) then hits `if (side === null) return` and returns BEFORE
builder.caliper -- so the ankle-offset caliper, the mark that IS the measurement, is never
drawn on either half of the ghost. The hip-width segment and the hip-midline plumb still draw,
so the image looks deliberate rather than broken.

stepWidth's single-strike branch sets `side`, and stepWidthCm's does too, so only the PAIRED
exemplar is affected -- and the paired branch is the common case.

Found while measuring strides-zp6 (which came back a clean null: the select-then-score shape
that ticket describes costs no clip an exemplar today). This is a DIFFERENT defect, and it is
the concrete evidence that deduplicating those two buildExemplars is worth doing on its own
merits: the copies have already diverged in a way nothing catches.

INVISIBLE TODAY. stepWidthCm is metric-excluded (tier 3, no card) on demo1, demo2 and
multiperson-track.mp4, measured 2026-08-29 on main @ 0b1b197, real GPU, fresh process per trial,
2 trials each. So there is no live repro on this repo's footage and the fix cannot be verified
by looking at an image without a clip where stepWidthCm reaches tier 1 or 2.

is the in-repo precedent for a helper across 3+ callers), so the two metrics cannot state
different facts about the same construction again. That folds the fix and the dedup into one
change. Do NOT simply reuse selectExtremePairs/selectRangePair -- the representative role

Behaviour change, so it needs an openspec change under form-heuristics and a test that asserts
stepWidthCm's paired exemplar names both feet the way stepWidth.test.ts:277-278 already asserts
for stepWidth. Do not move MIN_EXEMPLAR_QUALITY, EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX,
EVIDENCE_MAX_PAIR_CROP_GROWTH or the 3-MAD bound.
notes: Correction: the MediaPipe-vs-MoveNet view disagreement referenced in the close reason was filed as strides-fn4, not strides-p2q (the ID was written before the bead existed).

title: Demo 2 arm-swing asymmetry: disclosed, not resolved - needs constant-distance footage
description:
fit-arm-swing-amplitude establishes that Demo 2's arm-swing asymmetry is REAL (both arms fit the stride rhythm within one grid step, 1.48 vs 1.52 Hz, cross-side agreement 0.027) but is measured under materially unequal conditions: left fit R2 0.778, right 0.497, and the weaker-looking right arm is the one measured at t=0.43-0.62 when the runner is furthest from the camera.

That change stops OVERSTATING it - confidence 0.980 -> 0.385, tier normal -> caveated, plus a caveat naming the disparity - but it cannot adjudicate how much of the 0.607 ratio is form and how much is measurement. Nothing in this clip's footage can: the runner's on-screen scale roughly triples across it.

Closing this needs a front-view clip filmed at roughly constant subject distance, where both arms are measured under comparable keypoint conditions for the whole window. Same shape of footage gap as the slow-motion and rear-view investigations already record.

Related: strides-e9b owns the EVIDENCE_CROP_MIN_SIDE_PX (320) half of the same confound - the crop floor that inflates the far-arm crop until it swallows a bystander. That was deliberately untouched here.
notes: RE-POINTED 2026-09-05 by strides-zhv (drop-arm-swing-symmetry), NOT closed. Only the RATIO half of this ticket dies with the metric. The footage gap it names is unresolved and still binding on armSwingAmplitude: that metric reads the identical per-side fits from the shared armSwing.ts, aggregates every confidence input from the WORSE side, and fires the same SIDE_FIT_QUALITY_DISPARITY_R2 caveat on Demo 2's left R2 0.778 vs right 0.497. Its own suite records that the disparity 'matters MORE here, not less' (armSwingAmplitude.test.ts): a magnitude does not self-cancel per-side tracking asymmetry the way a ratio partially does, so the worse arm's measurement error lands undiluted in the mean. Closing this still needs a front-view clip filmed at roughly constant subject distance. Measured for reference on ffd1ea1: armSwingAmplitude on front-approach reads value 0.233555 at confidence 0.412742, sampleSize 2 - the same confidence the withdrawn ratio carried, from the same worse-side fit.

title: armSwing frequency band floor excludes cadences below ~144 spm
description:
One arm swing spans one STRIDE, so its frequency is half the step rate, but armSwingSymmetry fits over the SHARED spectralFitMinFrequencyHz/Max band (1.2-4.0 Hz) which was sized for the per-step hip bounce. A runner below roughly 144 spm therefore has their true arm-swing frequency below the band floor entirely and cannot be fitted correctly.

Demo 1 is exactly that case: cadence 91.2 spm implies a 0.76 Hz arm swing; its fits land at 1.70 Hz (left) and 1.54 Hz (right) with R2 0.385/0.383. It is side-view/tier-3 excluded so nothing is shown, but a slow front-view clip would hit this in the UI.

Halving the band to 0.6-2.0 Hz was measured and REJECTED in fit-arm-swing-amplitude (design D3): on Demo 2 it is a wash (agrees within one grid step, 0.3% of amplitude) but its secondPeakRatio is strictly worse (0.13->0.25 left, 0.31->0.69 right), and on BOTH side-view clips it lands on its own grid FLOOR at 0.60 Hz with barely one observed cycle - a grid-edge artifact that looks like an answer. Do not re-litigate by just picking a wider band.

A next attempt needs either a per-metric band that is bounded BELOW by observed cycles rather than by a fixed floor, or a real slow-cadence front-view clip to calibrate against. Neither exists today.
notes: RE-POINTED 2026-09-05 by strides-zhv (drop-arm-swing-symmetry), NOT closed. The armSwingSymmetry metric is withdrawn, but this defect is NOT its property: the band floor belongs to the SHARED computeSideSwing (src/heuristics/armSwing.ts), which armSwingAmplitude still calls on every clip through the identical spectralFitMinFrequencyHz/Max grid. Read every reference to armSwingSymmetry in the description above as armSwingAmplitude; the Demo 1 measurements (1.70/1.54 Hz at R2 0.385/0.383 against a 0.76 Hz true swing), the rejected 0.6-2.0 Hz halving with its worse secondPeakRatio and its grid-floor artifact on both side clips, and the stated next step (a band bounded below by observed cycles, or real slow-cadence front-view footage) all transfer verbatim. Nothing about this ticket was resolved by the withdrawal.

title: Two async callers have no rejection handler, so a throw surfaces as an unhandled rejection
description:
Flagged by strides-k03's agent, deliberately not fixed there because it is a behaviour change in files that refactor otherwise did not touch.

useClipPoster.ts:41 and useSessionEvidence.ts:280 both call an async derivation with no rejection handler. Neither derivation is supposed to throw - every failure they know about resolves to null - so a throw is by definition a bug, and today it surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection rather than anywhere a developer will see it.

Note strides-k03 CORRECTED the related doc rather than adding a catch, and the reasoning transfers: an existing test deliberately pins deriveClipPoster REJECTING when URL.createObjectURL throws, and pins that the shared queue survives it. Swallowing the rejection at the call site would leave the poster null either way while erasing the only signal the bug exists.

So the question here is not 'add a catch' but 'where should an unexpected throw become visible' - a dev-only console line, an error boundary, or leaving it as an unhandled rejection on purpose and documenting that. It is a repo-wide pattern (two sites, and EvidenceGallery.tsx had a third before it was deleted), so decide once and apply to both.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded on where an unexpected derivation throw becomes visible, applied consistently at both sites. The existing test pinning deriveClipPoster's rejection and queue survival still passes.
notes: Decided and applied on branch worktree-agent-af6209a235e18201b (commit 402dfc2), NOT merged. DECISION: leave both as unhandled rejections, deliberately, and record why at both sites. Rationale: (1) a React error boundary structurally CANNOT catch a rejection raised inside a .then callback -- it is not on React's call stack -- so that option is a non-option, not a trade-off; (2) this app has no error channel to catch into: no telemetry, no boundary, and zero console.error/console.warn anywhere in shipped src/ (only three DEV-gated console.log diagnostics lines), so a handler could only write a log line while SUPPRESSING the browser's unhandled-rejection report, which carries a stack, is marked an error, and is the only machine-detectable signal (page.on('pageerror'), vitest unhandled-rejection failure, window.onunhandledrejection) -- strictly less visible, not more; (3) both sites are already bounded (poster stays null; an abort is a VERDICT not a rejection, extractFrames.ts:117). posterFrame.test.ts's rejection + queue-survival test still passes (1343/1343 green). No openspec change filed: no behaviour changes, and the deliverable is a recorded decision.
close_reason:
Decided and documented (402dfc2), no catch added, at both sites. LEFT AS UNHANDLED REJECTIONS DELIBERATELY, with the reasoning recorded at useClipPoster.ts and cross-referenced at useSessionEvidence.ts:280.

Three reasons, and the first is decisive rather than a preference: an error boundary STRUCTURALLY CANNOT catch a rejection raised inside a .then callback - it is not on React's call stack. That is a non-option, not a trade-off. Second, there is no error channel to catch INTO: no telemetry, no boundary, and zero console.error/console.warn in shipped src/. A handler could therefore only write a log line while SUPPRESSING the browser's unhandled-rejection report - which carries a stack, is marked an error, and is the only machine-detectable signal (page.on('pageerror'), vitest, window.onunhandledrejection). Quieter and machine-invisible is the wrong trade for a defect. Third, both sites are already bounded, verified rather than assumed: an abort is not a rejection on either path (extractFrames.ts:117, 'Abandonment is a VERDICT, never a rejection').

Consistent with strides-k03's earlier call on the same pattern, which corrected the doc rather than adding a catch. The existing posterFrame.test.ts test pinning deriveClipPoster's rejection AND the shared queue's survival still passes.
